Thou didst create the stars of night:
Yet thou hast vailed in flesh thy light—
Hast deigned a mortal form to wear,
A mortal’s painful lot to bear.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When thou didst hang upon the tree,
The quaking earth acknowledged thee;
When thou didst there yield up thy breath,
The world grew dark as shades of death.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Now in the Father’s glory high,
Great Conqueror, never more to die,
Us by thy mighty power defend,
And reign through ages without end!

title: Saviour, I lift my trembling eyes
author: The lowliest spirit share thy throne

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour, I lift my trembling eyes,
To that bright seat, where, placed on high,
The great, the atoning sacrifice,
For me, for all, is ever nigh.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
For what is earthly change or loss?
Thy promises are still my own:
The feeblest frame may bear thy cross,

title: Thee we adore, O gracious Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thee we adore, O gracious Lord!
We praise thy name with one accord;
Thy saints, who here thy goodness see,
Through all the world do worship thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To thee aloud all angels cry,
And ceaseless raise their songs on high,
Both cherubim and seraphim,
The heavens and all the powers therein:

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thee, holy, holy, holy King!
Thee, O Lord God of hosts, they sing:
Thus earth below, and heaven above,
Resound thy glory and thy love.

title: Hail to the Prince of Life and Peace
author: Sublimer anthems near thy throne

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail to the Prince of Life and Peace,
Who holds the keys of death and hell;
The spacious world unseen is his,
The sovereign power becomes him well.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Live, live for ever, glorious Lord,
To crush thy foes and guard thy friends,
While all thy chosen tribes rejoice
That thy dominion never ends.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Worthy thy hand to hold the keys,
Guided by wisdom and by love;
Worthy to rule our mortal lives,
O’er worlds below and worlds above.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: I know that my Redeemer lives

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I know that my Redeemer lives;
What comfort this sweet sentence gives!
He lives, he lives who once was dead,
He lives, my ever-living Head!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He lives to bless me with his love,
He lives to plead for me above,
He lives my hungry soul to feed,
He lives to bless in time of need.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He lives to grant me rich supply,
He lives to guide me with his eye,
He lives to comfort me when faint,
He lives to hear my soul’s complaint.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He lives, my kind, wise, heavenly friend,
He lives, and loves me to the end;
He lives, and while he lives I’ll sing,
He lives, my Prophet, Priest, and King!

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
He lives, all glory to his name!
He lives, my Jesus, still the same!
O the sweet joy this sentence gives—
I know that my Redeemer lives!

title: Jesus, the spring of joys divine
author: Where perfect joy for ever reigns

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, the spring of joys divine,
Whence all our hopes and comforts flow:
Jesus, no other name but thine
Can save us from eternal woe.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In vain would boasting reason find
Thy way to happiness and God;
Her weak directions leave the mind
Bewildered in a dubious road.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No other name will heaven approve;
Thou art the true, the living way,
Ordained by everlasting love,
To the bright realms of endless day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here let our constant feet abide,
Nor from the heavenly path depart;
O let thy Spirit, gracious Guide!
Direct our steps, and cheer our heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Safe lead us through this world of night,
And bring us to the blissful plains—
The regions of unclouded light

title: Let everlasting glories crown
author: And bind the gospel to my heart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let everlasting glories crown
Thy head, my Saviour and my Lord;
Thy hands have brought salvation down,
And stored the blessings in thy word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In vain the trembling conscience seeks
Some solid ground to rest upon;
With long despair the spirit breaks,
Till we apply to Christ alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How well thy blesséd truths agree!
How wise and holy thy commands!
Thy promises, how firm they be!
How firm our hope and comfort stands!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Should all the forms that men devise
Assault my faith with treacherous art,
I’d call them vanity and lies,

title: Thou only Sovereign of my heart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou only Sovereign of my heart,
My Refuge, my almighty Friend—
And can my soul from thee depart,
On whom alone my hopes depend?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Whither, ah! whither shall I go,
A wretched wanderer from my Lord?
Can this dark world of sin and woe
One glimpse of happiness afford?

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Let earth’s alluring joys combine;
While thou art near, in vain they call!
One smile, one blissful smile of thine,
My dearest Lord, outweighs them all.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6

title: Thou art the way; and he who sighs

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou art the way; and he who sighs,
Amid this starless waste of woe,
To find a pathway to the skies,
A light from heaven’s eternal glow,
By thee must come, thou gate of love,
Through which the saints undoubting trod,
Till faith discovers, like the dove,
An ark, a resting-place in God.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou art the Life, the blesséd Well
With living waters gushing o’er,
Which those that drink shall ever dwell
Where sin and thirst are known no more,
Thou art the mystic Pillar given,
Our Lamp by night, our Light by day;
Thou art the sacred Bread from heaven;
Thou art the Life, the Truth, the Way.

title: Still nigh me, O my Saviour, stand

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
In suffering be thy love my peace,
In weakness be thy love my power;
And when the storms of life shall cease,
O, Saviour, in that trying hour,
In death, as life, be thou my guide,
And save me, who for me hast died.

title: Jesus, thou source of calm repose

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3

title: My Prophet thou, my heavenly Guide

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Prophet thou, my heavenly Guide,
Thy sweet instructions I will hear;
The words that from thy lips proceed,
O how divinely sweet they are!
Thee, my great Prophet, I would love,
And imitate the blest above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My great High Priest, whose precious blood
Did once atone upon the cross,
Who now dost intercede with God,
And plead the friendless sinner’s cause:
In thee I trust, thee would I love,
And imitate the blest above.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Jesus! the very thought is sweet

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, the hope of souls forlorn!
How good to them for sin that mourn;
To them that seek thee, O how kind!
But what art thou to them that find?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No tongue of mortal can express,
No letters write its blessedness;
Alone, who hath thee in his heart,
Knows, love of Jesus, what thou art.

title: With joy we meditate the grace
author: In each distressing hour

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With joy we meditate the grace
Of our High Priest above:
His heart is full of tenderness;
His bosom glows with love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Touched with a sympathy within,
He knows our feeble frame;
He knows what sore temptations mean,
For he has felt the same.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He in the days of feeble flesh,
Poured out his cries and tears;
And in his measure feels afresh
What every member bears.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Bright was the guiding star that led
author: Shall reign with him in heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bright was the guiding star that led,
With mild, benignant ray,
The Gentiles to the lowly shed
Where the Redeemer lay.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But, lo! a brighter, clearer light
Now points to his abode;
It shines through sin and sorrow’s night
To guide us to our God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O haste to follow where it leads;
The gracious call obey,
Be rugged wilds or flowery meads
The Christian’s destined way.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O gladly tread the narrow path
While light and grace are given:
Who meekly follow Christ on earth,

title: Come, you that love the Saviour’s name
author: To celebrate thy praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, you that love the Saviour’s name,
And joy to make it known;
The Sovereign of your heart proclaim,
And bow before his throne.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Behold your King, your Saviour, crowned
With glories all divine;
And tell the wondering nations round
How bright these glories shine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Infinite power and boundless grace
In him unite their rays;
You that have seen his lovely face,
Can you forbear his praise?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When in the earthly courts we view
The beauties of our King,
We long to love as angels do,
And wish like them to sing.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And shall we long and wish in vain?
Lord, teach our songs to rise!
Thy love can animate our strain,
And bid it reach the skies.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O for the day, the glorious day!
When heaven and earth shall raise,
With all their powers, the raptured lay,

title: Thou dear Redeemer, dying Lamb
author: When all things else decay

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou dear Redeemer, dying Lamb,
I love to hear of thee;
No music’s like thy charming name,
Nor half so sweet can be.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, may I ever hear thy voice
In mercy to me speak;
In thee, my Priest, will I rejoice,
And thy salvation seek.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: We bless the Prophet of the Lord
author: By his almighty hands

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We bless the Prophet of the Lord,
That comes with truth and grace;
Jesus, thy Spirit and thy Word,
Shall lead us in thy ways.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We reverence our High Priest above,
Who offered up his blood,
And lives to carry on his love
By pleading with our God.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Come, let us join in songs of praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us join in songs of praise
To our ascended Priest;
He entered heaven with all our names
Engraven on his breast.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On earth he washed our guilt away
By his atoning blood;
Now he appears before the throne,
And pleads our cause with God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
What though while here we oft must feel
Temptation’s keenest dart;
Our tender High Priest feels it too,
And will appease the smart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Clothed with our nature still, he knows
The weakness of our frame,
And how to shield us from the foes
Which he himself o’ercame.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Nor time nor distance e’er shall quench
The fervor of his love;
For us he died in kindness here,
For us he lives above.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O may we ne’er forget his grace,
Nor blush to wear his name!
Still may our hearts hold fast his faith,
Our lips his praise proclaim!

title: Hosanna! raise the pealing hymn
author: We’ll sing to harps of gold

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hosanna! raise the pealing hymn
To David’s Son and Lord;
With cherubim and seraphim
Exalt th’ incarnate Word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hosanna! Lord, our feeble tongue
No lofty strains can raise:
But thou wilt not despise the young
Who meekly chant thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hosanna! Sovereign, Prophet, Priest,
How vast thy gifts, how free!
Thy Blood, our life; thy Word, our feast;
Thy Name, our only plea.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hosanna! Master, lo! we bring
Our offerings to thy throne;
Not gold, nor myrrh, nor mortal thing,
But hearts to be thine own.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Hosanna! once thy gracious ear
Approved a lisping throng;
Be gracious still, and deign to hear
Our poor but grateful song.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O Saviour, if, redeemed by thee,
Thy temple we behold,
Hosannas through eternity

title: Now let our cheerful eyes survey
author: To endless ages borne

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now let our cheerful eyes survey
Our great High Priest above,
And celebrate his constant care
And sympathetic love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though raised to heaven’s exalted throne
Where angels bow around,
And high o’er all the hosts of light,
With matchless honors crowned—

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The names of all his saints he bears
Deep graven on his heart;
Nor shall the weakest Christian say
That he has lost his part.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Those characters shall fair abide,
Our everlasting trust,
When gems, and monuments, and crowns,
Have moldered down to dust.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
So, gracious Saviour, on my breast
May thy loved name be worn—
A sacred ornament and guard,

title: Behold the glories of the Lamb
author: And we shall reign with thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold the glories of the Lamb
Amidst his Father’s throne;
Prepare new honors for his name,
And songs before unknown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let elders worship at his feet,
The church adore around,
With vials full of odors sweet,
And harps of sweeter sound.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Now to the Lamb that once was slain,
Be endless blessings paid;
Salvation, glory, joy, remain
For ever on thy head!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou hast redeemed our souls with blood,
Hast set the prisoners free,
Hast made us kings and priests to God,

title: Infinite excellence is thine
author: Through all eternity

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Infinite excellence is thine,
Thou lovely Prince of Grace!
Thy uncreated beauties shine
With never-fading rays.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sinners from earth’s remotest end
Come bending at thy feet;
To thee their prayers and praise ascend,
In thee their wishes meet.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy name, as precious ointment shed,
Delights the church around;
Sweetly the sacred odors spread,
And purest joys abound.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Millions of happy spirits live
On thy exhaustless store;
From thee they all their bliss receive,
And still thou givest more.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Jesus, in thy transporting name

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, in thy transporting name
What blissful glories rise!
Jesus, the angels’ sweetest theme—
The wonder of the skies!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Well might the skies with wonder view
A love so strange as thine!
No thought of angels ever knew
Compassion so divine!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, and didst thou leave the sky
To bear our sins and woes?
And didst thou bleed, and groan, and die,
For vile rebellious foes?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Victorious love! can language tell
The wonders of thy power,
Which conquered all the force of hell
In that tremendous hour!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
What glad return can I impart
For favors so divine?
O take this heart, this worthless heart,
And make it only thine!

title: The Saviour! O what endless charms
author: My Saviour and my all

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Saviour! O what endless charms
Dwell in the blissful sound!
Its influence every fear disarms,
And spreads sweet peace around.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here pardon, life, and joys divine,
In rich profusion flow;
For guilty rebels, lost in sin,
And doomed to endless woe.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Th’ almighty Former of the skies
Stooped to our vile abode;
While angels viewed, with wondering eyes,
And hailed th’ incarnate God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O the rich depths of love divine!
Of bliss a boundless store!
Blest Saviour, let me call thee mine;
I can not wish for more.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Alas! and did my Saviour bleed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Alas! and did my Saviour bleed?
And did my Sovereign die?
Would he devote that sacred head
For such a worm as I?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Was it for crimes that I had done
He groaned upon the tree?
Amazing pity! grace unknown!
And love beyond degree!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Well might the sun in darkness hide,
And shut his glories in,
When God’s own son was crucified
For man the creature’s sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus might I hide my blushing face
While his dear cross appears,
Dissolve my heart in thankfulness,
And melt mine eyes to tears.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But drops of grief can ne’er repay
The debt of love I owe:
Here, Lord, I give myself away;
’Tis all that I can do.

title: Jesus, thou art the sinner’s friend

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Remember thy pure word of grace,
Remember Calvary;
Remember all thy promises,
And then remember me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou mighty Advocate with God!
I yield myself to thee;
While thou art sitting on thy throne,
O Lord, remember me!

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Howe’er forsaken or distressed,
Howe’er oppressed I be,
Howe’er afflicted here on earth,
Do thou remember me!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
And when I close my eyes in death,
And creature helps all flee,
Then, O my great Redeemer, Lord,
I pray, remember me!

title: Jesus, in thee our eyes behold
author: Who by him come to God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, in thee our eyes behold
A thousand glories more
Than the rich gems and polished gold
The sons of Aaron wore.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
They first their own burnt-offerings brought
To purge themselves from sin:
Thy life was pure, without a spot,
And all thy nature clean.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fresh blood, as constant as the day,
Was on their altar spilt;
But thy one offering takes away
For ever all our guilt.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Their priesthood ran through several hands,
For mortal was their race;
Thy never-changing office stands
Eternal as thy days.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Once, in the circuit of a year,
With blood, but not his own,
Aaron with the vail appeared
Before the golden throne;

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
But Christ, with his own precious blood,
Ascends above the skies,
And in the presence of our God
Shows his own sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Jesus, the King of glory, reigns
On Zion’s holy hill;
Looks like a lamb that had been slain,
And wears his priesthood still.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
He ever lives in heaven to plead
The cause which cost his blood,
And saves unto the utmost those

title: Hosanna to our conquering King
author: The triumphs thou hast won

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hosanna to our conquering King!
All hail incarnate Love!
Ten thousand songs and glories wait
To crown thy head above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy victories and thy deathless fame
Through all the world shall run,
And everlasting ages sing

title: O Jesus! King most wonderful
author: The image of thine own

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Jesus! King most wonderful!
Thou Conqueror renowned!
Thou Sweetness most ineffable!
In whom all joys are found.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
May every heart confess thy name,
And ever thee adore;
And seeking thee, itself inflame
To seek thee more and more.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Jesus, immortal King! arise
author: Hosannas to the Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, immortal King! arise,
Assert thy rightful sway,
Till earth, subdued, its tribute brings,
And distant lands obey.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ride forth, victorious Conqueror! ride,
Till all thy foes submit,
And all the powers of hell resign
Their trophies at thy feet.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Send forth thy word, and let it fly
The spacious earth around,
Till every soul beneath the sun
Shall hear the joyful sound.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
From sea to sea, from shore to shore,
May Jesus be adored!
And earth, with all her millions, shout

title: He who on earth as man was known
author: And crowns them at the end

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
He who on earth as man was known,
And bore our sins and pains,
Now seated on th’ eternal throne,
The Lord of glory reigns.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His hands the wheels of nature guide
With sure, unerring skill,
And countless worlds, extended wide,
Obey his sovereign will.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While harps unnumbered sound his praise
In yonder worlds above,
His saints on earth admire his ways,
And glory in his love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
This land through which his pilgrims go,
Is desolate and dry;
But streams of grace from him o’erflow,
Their thirst to satisfy.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When troubles, like a burning sun,
Beat heavy on their head,
To this high Rock for rest they run,
And find a pleasing shade.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
How glorious he, how happy they
In such a generous friend,
Whose love secures them all the way,

title: How sweet the name of Jesus sounds

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sweet the name of Jesus sounds
In a believer’s ear;
It soothes his sorrows, heals his wounds,
And drives away his fear!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It makes the wounded spirit whole,
And calms the troubled breast;
’Tis manna to the hungry soul,
And to the weary rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By thee my prayers acceptance gain,
Although with sin defiled;
Satan accuses me in vain,
And I am owned a child.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, my Shepherd, Guardian, Friend,
My Prophet, Priest, and King,
My Lord, my Life, my Way, my End,
Accept the praise I bring.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Weak is the effort of my heart,
And cold my warmest thought;
But when I see thee as thou art,
I’ll praise thee as I ought.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Till then, I would thy love proclaim
With every fleeting breath;
And may the music of thy name
Refresh my soul in death!

title: Thou art the Way—to thee alone
author: Whose joys eternal flow

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou art the Way—to thee alone
From sin and death we flee;
And he who would the Father seek,
Must seek him, Lord, by thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou art the Truth—thy word alone
True wisdom can impart;
Thou only canst inform the mind,
And purify the heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou art the Life—the rending tomb
Proclaims thy conquering arm;
And those who put their trust in thee,
Nor death nor hell shall harm.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: My Saviour! my almighty Friend
author: Shall thy salvation sing

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Saviour! my almighty Friend!
When I begin thy praise,
Where will the growing numbers end—
The numbers of thy grace?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
My feet shall travel all the length
Of the celestial road;
And march, with courage, in thy strength,
To see my Father God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
How will my lips rejoice to tell
The victories of my King!
My soul, redeemed from sin and hell,

title: Majestic sweetness sits enthroned

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Majestic sweetness sits enthroned
Upon the Saviour’s brow;
His head with radiant glories crowned,
His lips with grace o’erflow.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No mortal can with him compare
Among the sons of men;
Fairer is he than all the fair
Who fill the heavenly train.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He saw me plunged in deep distress,
And flew to my relief;
For me he bore the shameful cross,
And carried all my grief.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To him I owe my life and breath,
And all the joys I have!
He makes me triumph over death,
And saves me from the grave.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To heaven, the place of his abode,
He brings my weary feet;
Shows me the glories of my God,
And makes my joys complete.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Since from thy bounty I receive
Such proofs of love divine,
Had I a thousand hearts to give,
Lord, they should all be thine.

title: Jesus, I love thy charming name
author: The antidote of death

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Yes, thou art precious to my soul,
My transport and my trust;
Jewels to thee are gaudy toys,
And gold is sordid dust.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
All that my ardent soul can wish
In thee doth richly meet;
Nor to my eyes is light so dear,
Nor friendship half so sweet.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy grace shall dwell upon my heart,
And shed its fragrance there;
The noblest balm of all its wounds,
The cordial of its care.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Plunged in a gulf of dark despair
author: His love can ne’er be told

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Plunged in a gulf of dark despair,
We wretchéd sinners lay,
Without one cheerful beam of hope,
Or spark of glimmering day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With pitying eyes the Prince of grace
Beheld our helpless grief;
He saw, and—O! amazing love!
He ran to our relief.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Down from the shining seats above,
With joyful haste he fled,
Entered the grave in mortal flesh,
And dwelt among the dead.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O! for this love let rocks and hills
Their lasting silence break;
And all harmonious human tongues
The Saviour’s praises speak.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: There is a fountain filled with blood
author: I’ll sing thy power to save

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a fountain filled with blood
Drawn from Immanuel’s veins;
And sinners plunged beneath that flood,
Loose all their guilty stains.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The dying thief rejoiced to see
That fountain in his day;
And there have I, as vile as he,
Washed all my sins away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Lamb of God, thy precious blood
Shall never lose its power,
Till all the ransomed Church of God
Be saved to sin no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
E’er since by faith I saw the stream
Thy flowing wounds supply,
Redeeming love has been my theme,
And shall be till I die.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And when this lisping, stammering tongue
Lies silent in the grave,
Then, in a nobler, sweeter song,

title: Salvation! O the joyful sound
author: Conspire to raise the sound

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Buried in sorrow and in sin,
At hell’s dark door we lay;
But we arise by grace divine,
To see a heavenly day.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Let earth, with every isle and sea
author: And a rich harvest bear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let earth, with every isle and sea,
Rejoice; the Saviour reigns:
His word, like fire, prepares his way,
And mountains melt to plains.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His presence sinks the proudest hills
And makes the valleys rise;
The humble soul enjoys his smiles,
The haughty sinner dies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Adoring angels, at his birth,
Made our Redeemer known;
Thus shall he come to judge the earth,
And angels guard his throne.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His foes shall tremble at his sight,
And hills and seas retire;
His children take their upward flight,
And leave the world on fire.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The seeds of joy and glory sown
For saints in darkness here,
Shall rise and spring in worlds unknown,

title: O North, with all thy vales of green

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O North, with all thy vales of green,
O South, with all thy palms,
From peopled towns, and fields between,
Uplift the voice of psalms;
Raise, ancient East, the anthem high,
And let the youthful West reply.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lo! in the clouds of heaven appears
God’s well-belovéd Son;
He brings a train of brighter years—
His kingdom is begun:
He comes, a guilty world to bless
With mercy, truth and righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Father, haste the promised hour
When at his feet shall lie
All rule, authority, and power,
Beneath the ample sky,
When he shall reign from pole to pole,
The Lord of every human soul.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When all shall heed the words he said,
Amid their daily cares,
And by the loving life he led
Shall strive to pattern theirs;
And he who conquered Death shall win,
The mighty conquest over Sin.

title: Had I ten thousand gifts beside
author: Eternal life is mine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Had I ten thousand gifts beside,
I’d cleave to Jesus crucified,
And build on him alone;
For no foundation is there given
On which to place my hopes of heaven,
But Christ, the corner-stone.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Possessing Christ I all possess,
Wisdom, and strength, and righteousness,
And holiness complete;
Bold in his name, I dare draw nigh
Before the Ruler of the sky,
And all his justice meet.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is no path to heavenly bliss,
To solid joy or lasting peace,
But Christ, th’ appointed road;
O may we tread the sacred way,
By faith rejoice, and praise, and pray,
Till we sit down with God!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The types and shadows of the word
Unite in Christ, the Man, the Lord,
The Saviour kind and true;
O may we still his word believe,
And all his promises receive,
And all his precepts do.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
As he above for ever lives,
And life to dying mortals gives,
Eternal and divine;
O may his Spirit in me dwell!
Then, saved from sin, and death, and hell,

title: Like sheep we went astray
author: To recompense his pain

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Like sheep we went astray,
And broke the fold of God;
Each wandering in a different way,
But all the downward road.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How dreadful was the hour
When God our wanderings laid,
And did at once his vengeance pour
Upon the Shepherd’s head.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How glorious was the grace
When Christ sustained the stroke!
His life and blood the Shepherd pays,
A ransom for the flock.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But God hath raised his head
O’er all the sons of men,
And made him see a numerous seed

title: Beyond the starry skies

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Beyond the starry skies,
Far as th’ eternal hills,
Yon heaven of heavens, with living light,
Our great Redeemer fills.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Around him angels fair,
In countless armies shine;
And ever, in exalted lays,
They offer songs divine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
“Hail, Prince of life!” they cry,
“Whose unexampled love
Moved thee to quit those glorious realms
And royalties above.”

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when he stooped to earth,
And suffered rude disdain,
They cast their honors at his feet,
And waited in his train.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
They saw him on the cross,
While darkness vailed the skies;
And when he burst the gates of death,
They saw the Conqueror rise.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
They thronged his chariot wheels,
And bore him to his throne;
Then swept their golden harps and sung—
“The glorious work is done.”

title: Sing of Jesus, sing for ever
author: Him they serve and love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sing of Jesus, sing for ever
Of the love that changes never!
Who, or what, from him can sever
Those he makes his own?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With his blood the Lord hath bought them,
When they knew him not, he sought them,
And from all their wanderings brought them;
His the praise alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Through the desert Jesus leads them,
With the bread of heaven he feeds them,
And through all their way he speeds them
To their home above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There they see the Lord who bought them,
Him who came from heaven and sought them,
Him who by his Spirit taught them,

title: Rock of ages, cleft for me

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
While I draw this fleeting breath,
When my heart-strings break in death,
When I soar to worlds unknown,
See thee on thy judgment throne,
Rock of ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in thee.

title: Jesus, lover of my soul
author: Rise to all eternity

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, lover of my soul,
Let me to thy bosom fly,
While the billows near me roll,
While the tempest still is high;
Hide me, O my Saviour, hide,
Till the storm of life is past,
Safe into the haven guide,
O receive my soul at last.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Other refuge have I none,
Hangs my helpless soul on thee!
Leave, O leave me not alone,
Still support and comfort me:
All my trust on thee is stayed,
All my help from thee I bring,
Cover my defenseless head
With the shadow of thy wing.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou, O Christ, art all I want,
Boundless love in thee I find;
Raise the fallen, cheer the faint,
Heal the sick, and lead the blind.
Just and holy is thy name,
Prince of Peace and Righteousness;
Most unworthy, Lord, I am,
Thou art full of love and grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Plenteous grace with thee is found,
Grace to pardon all my sins;
Let the healing streams abound,
Make and keep me pure within.
Thou of life the fountain art,
Freely let me take of thee;
Spring thou up within my heart,

title: One there is above all others
author: He rejoices in the same

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Which of all our friends to save us,
Could or would have shed his blood?
But this Saviour died, to have us
Reconciled in him to God.
Hallelujah!
Reconciled in him to God.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: In seasons of grief to my God I’ll repair
author: To praise the great Rock that is higher than I

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In seasons of grief to my God I’ll repair,
When my heart is o’erwhelmed with sorrow and care:
From the end of the earth unto thee will I cry,
Lead me to the Rock that is higher than I!
Higher than I, higher than I,
Lead me to the Rock that is higher than I.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When Satan the tempter comes in like a flood
To drive my poor soul from the fountain of good,
I’ll pray to the Lord who for sinners did die—
Lead me to the Rock that is higher than I.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And when I have finished my pilgrimage here,
Complete in Christ’s righteousness I shall appear,
In the swellings of Jordan, all dangers defy,
And look to the Rock that is higher than I.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when the last trumpet shall sound thro’ the skies,
And the dead from the dust of the earth shall arise,
Transported I’ll join with the ransomed on high,
To praise the great Rock that is higher than I!
Higher than I, higher than I,

title: Cling to the mighty One, Ps. lxxxix. 19

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Cling to the mighty One, Ps. lxxxix. 19.
Cling in thy grief; Heb. xii. 11.
Cling to the Holy One, Heb. vii. 26.
He gives relief; Ps. cxvi. 8.
Cling to the Gracious One, Ps. cxvi. 5.
Cling in thy pain, Ps. lv. 4.
Cling to the Faithful One, 1 Thess. v. 24.
He will sustain. Ps. xxviii. 8.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Cling to the Living One, Heb. vii. 25.
Cling in thy woe, Ps. lxxxvi. 7.
Cling to the Loving One 1 John iv. 16.
Through all below; Romans viii. 38, 39.
Cling to the Pardoning One, Is. lv. 7.
He speaketh peace; John xiv. 27.
Cling to the Healing One, Exod. xv. 26.
Anguish shall cease. Ps. cxvi. 8.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Cling to the Bleeding One, 1 John i. 7.
Cling to his side; John xx. 27.
Cling to the Risen One, Rom. vi. 9.
In him abide; John xv. 4.
Cling to the Coming One, Rev. xxii. 20.
Hope shall arise; Titus ii. 13.
Cling to the Reigning One, Eph. i. 20-23.
Joy lights thine eyes. Ps. xvi. 11.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: THE GOSPEL—THE PROCLAMATION.

title: The Christian banner! dread no loss
author: Above a blest but conquered world

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Christian banner! dread no loss
Where that broad ensign floats unrolled;
But let the fair and sacred cross
Blaze out from every radiant fold:
Stern foes arise, a countless throng,
Loud as the storms of Kara’s sea,
But though the strife be fierce and long,
That cross shall wave in victory.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sound the shrill trumpet, sound, and call
The people of the mighty King,
And bid them keep that standard all
In martial thousands gathering:
Let them come forth from every clime
That lies beneath the circling sun,
Various, as flowers in that sweet clime
Where flowers are, in heart, but one.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Soldiers of heaven! take sword and shield,
Look up to him who rules on high,
And forward to the glorious field,
Where noble martyrs bleed and die;
Press onward, scorning flight or fear,
As deep waves burst on Norway’s coast,
And let the startled nations hear
The war-shout of the Christian host.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lift up the banner: rest no more,
Nor let this righteous warfare cease,
Till man’s last tribe shall bow before
The Lord of lords—the Prince of Peace:
Go! bear it forth, ye strong and brave;
Let not those bright folds once be furled,
Till that high sun shall see them wave

title: Fling out the banner! let it float
author: We conquer only in that sign

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Fling out the banner! let it float
Sky-ward and sea-ward, high and wide:
The sun, that lights its shining folds,
The cross, on which the Saviour died.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Fling out the banner! angels bend,
In anxious silence, o’er the sign;
And vainly seek to comprehend
The wonder of the love divine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fling out the banner! heathen lands
Shall see, from far, the glorious sight,
And nations, crowding to be born,
Baptize their spirits in its light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fling out the banner! sin-sick souls,
That sink and perish in the strife,
Shall touch in faith its radiant hem,
And spring immortal into life.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6

title: God, in the gospel of his Son

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God, in the gospel of his Son,
Makes his eternal counsels known;
’Tis here his richest mercy shines,
And truth is drawn in fairest lines.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here sinners of a humble frame
May taste his grace and learn his name;
’Tis writ in characters of blood,
Severely just—immensely good.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here Jesus, in ten thousand ways,
His soul-attracting charms displays;
Recounts his poverty and pains,
And tells his love in melting strains.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
May this blest volume ever lie
Close to my heart, and near my eye—
Till life’s last hour my soul engage,
And be my chosen heritage!

title: Great was the day, the joy was great

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great was the day, the joy was great,
When the beloved disciples met;
And on their heads the Spirit came,
And sat like tongues of cloven flame.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What gifts, what miracles he gave!
The power to kill, the power to save,
Furnished their tongues with wondrous words,
Instead of shields, and spears, and swords.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thus armed, he sent the champions forth,
From east to west, from south to north;
Go, and assert your Saviour’s cause—
Go, spread the mystery of the cross!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
These weapons of the holy war,
Of what almighty force they are
To make our stubborn passions bow,
And lay the proudest rebel low!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Greeks and Jews, the learned and rude,
Are by these heavenly arms subdued;
While Satan rages at his loss,
And hates the doctrine of the cross.

title: How beauteous are their feet
author: Their Saviour and their God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How beauteous are their feet
Who stand on Zion’s hill!
Who bring salvation on their tongues,
And words of peace reveal!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How charming is their voice!
How sweet the tidings are!
“Zion, behold thy Saviour King,
He reigns and triumphs here.”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How happy are our ears
That hear this joyful sound,
Which kings and prophets waited for,
And sought, but never found!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
How blesséd are our eyes
That see this heavenly light!
Prophets and kings desired it long,
But died without the sight.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The watchmen join their voice,
And tuneful notes employ;
Jerusalem breaks forth in songs,
And deserts learn the joy.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Behold, the morning sun
author: But find the path to heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold, the morning sun
Begins his glorious way;
His beams through all the nations run,
And light and life convey.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But where the gospel comes,
It spreads diviner light;
It calls dead sinners from their tombs,
And gives the blind their sight.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How perfect is thy word!
And all thy judgments just!
For ever sure thy promise, Lord,
And we securely trust.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My gracious God, how plain
Are thy directions given!
O, may I never read in vain,

title: Hark! how the gospel trumpet sounds
author: In endless day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark! how the gospel trumpet sounds!
Through all the world the echo bounds!
And Jesus, by redeeming blood,
Is bringing sinners back to God,
And guides them safely by his word
To endless day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hail, Jesus! all victorious Lord!
Be thou by all mankind adored!
For us didst thou the fight maintain,
And o’er our foes the victory gain,
That we with thee might ever reign
In endless day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fight on, ye conquering souls, fight on,
And when the conquest you have won,
Then palms of victory you shall hear,
And in his kingdom have a share,
And crowns of glory ever wear,
In endless day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There we shall in full chorus join,
With saints and angels all combine
To sing of his redeeming love,
When rolling years shall cease to move,
And this shall be our theme above,

title: Blow ye the trumpet, blow

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye slaves of sin and hell,
Your liberty receive,
And safe in Jesus dwell,
And blest in Jesus live:
The year of jubilee is come;
Return, ye ransomed sinners, home.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Hear the royal proclamation

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hear the royal proclamation,
The glad tidings of salvation,
Publishing to every creature,
To the ruined sons of nature,
Jesus reigns—he reigns victorious,
Over heaven and earth most glorious!
Jesus reigns.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See the royal banners flying,
Hear the heralds loudly crying:
“Rebel sinners, royal favor
Now is offered by the Saviour.”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here is wine, and milk, and honey,
Come and purchase without money,
Mercy like a flowing fountain
Streaming from the holy mountain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Shout, you tongues of every nation,
To the bounds of the creation,
Shout the praise of Judah’s Lion,
The almighty King of Zion.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Shout, O saints! make joyful mention,
Christ has purchased our redemption;
Angels, shout the joyful story,
Through the brighter worlds of glory.

title: Sound, sound the truth abroad
author: INVITATIONS

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sound, sound the truth abroad!
Bear ye the word of God
Through the wide world;
Tell what our Lord has done,
Tell how the day is won,
Tell from his lofty throne
Satan is hurled.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Far over sea and land,
Go at your Lord’s command,
Bear ye his name;
Bear it to every shore,
Regions unknown explore,
Enter at every door;
Silence is shame.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
When on the mighty deep,
He will their spirits keep,
Stayed on his word;
When in a foreign land,
No other friend at hand,
Jesus will by them stand,

title: Haste, traveler, haste! the night comes on

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Haste, traveler, haste! the night comes on,
And many a shining hour is gone;
The storm is gathering in the west,
And thou art far from home and rest:
Haste, traveler, haste!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Haste, while a shelter you may gain—
A covert from the wind and rain;
A hiding-place, a rest, a home—
A refuge from the wrath to come:
Haste, traveler, haste!

sections.label: Verse 5

title: While life prolongs its precious light
author: While yet a pardoning God is found

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
While life prolongs its precious light,
Mercy is found, and peace is given;
But soon, ah! soon, approaching night
Shall blot out every hope of heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
While God invites, how blest the day!
How sweet the gospel’s charming sound!
Come, sinners, haste, O haste away,
While yet a pardoning God is found.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Soon, borne on time’s most rapid wing,
Shall death command you to the grave,
Before his bar your spirits bring,
And none be found to hear or save.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
In that lone land of deep despair,
No Sabbath’s heavenly light shall rise;
No God regard your bitter prayer,
Nor Saviour call you to the skies.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Now God invites, how blest the day!
How sweet the gospel’s charming sound!
Come, sinners, haste, O haste away,

title: With tearful eyes I look around

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
It tells me of a place of rest;
It tells me where my soul may flee:
O! to the weary, faint, opprest,
How sweet the bidding, Come to me!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
O voice of mercy, voice of love!
In conflict, grief, and agony,
Support me, cheer me from above,
And gently whisper, Come to me!

title: To-day, if you will hear his voice

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To-day, if you will hear his voice,
Now is the time to make your choice;
Say will you to Mount Zion go?
Say, will you come to Christ or no?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Say, will you be for ever blest,
And with this glorious Jesus rest?
Will you be saved from guilt and pain?
Will you with Christ for ever reign?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Make now your choice, and halt no more;
He now is waiting for the poor:
Say, now, poor souls, what will you do?
Say, will you come to Christ or no?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fathers and sons for ruin bound,
Amidst the gospel’s joyful sound,
Come, go with us, and seek to prove
The joys of Christ’s redeeming love.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Matrons and maids, we look to you;
Are you resolved to perish, too?
To rush in carnal pleasures on,
And sink in flaming ruin down?

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Once more we ask you in his name,
(We know his love remains the same),
Say, will you to Mount Zion go?
Say, will you come to Christ or no?

title: O, do not let the word depart

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
To-morrow’s sun may never rise
To bless thy long deluded sight;
This is the time; O, then be wise!
Thou wouldst be saved; why not to-night?

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Our blesséd Lord refuses none
Who would to him their souls unite;
Then be the work of grace begun:
Thou wouldst be saved; why not to-night?

title: Come, weary souls, with sin distressed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, weary souls, with sin distressed,
Come and accept the promised rest;
The Saviour’s gracious call obey,
And cast your gloomy fears away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oppressed with guilt, a heavy load,
O! come and bow before your God;
Divine compassion, mighty love,
Will all the painful load remove.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here mercy’s boundless ocean flows
To cleanse your guilt and heal your woes;
Pardon, and life, and endless peace—
How rich the gift, how free the grace!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord, we accept with thankful heart
The hope thy gracious words impart:
We come with trembling, yet rejoice,
And bless thy kind inviting voice.

title: Why will ye waste on trifling cares

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why will ye waste on trifling cares
That life which God’s compassion spares;
While, in the various range of thought,
The one thing needful is forgot?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Shall God invite you from above?
Shall Jesus urge his dying love?
Shall troubled conscience give you pain?
And all these pleas unite in vain?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Not so your eyes will always view
Those objects which you now pursue:
Not so will heaven and hell appear
When death’s decisive hour is near.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Broad is the road that leads to death
author: This false apostates never knew

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
“Deny thyself, and take thy cross,”
Is the Redeemer’s great command;
Nature must count her gold but dross,
If she would gain this heavenly land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The fearful soul that tires and faints,
And walks the ways of God no more,
Is but esteemed almost a saint,
And makes his own destruction sure.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Life is the time to serve the Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Life is the time to serve the Lord,
The time t’ insure the great reward;
And while the lamp holds out to burn,
O hasten, sinner, to return!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Life is the hour that God has given
To ’scape from hell and fly to heaven,
The day of grace, when mortals may
Secure the blessings of the day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The living know that they must die,
Beneath the clods their dust must lie;
Then have no share in all that’s done
Beneath the circle of the sun.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then what my thoughts design to do,
My hands, with all your might pursue:
Since no device nor work is found,
Nor faith, nor hope, beneath the ground.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
There are no acts of pardon passed
In the cold grave to which we haste;
O may we all receive thy grace,
And see with joy thy smiling face.

title: Come, sinners, to the gospel feast

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Hark! ’tis the Saviour’s gracious call,
The invitation is to all;
Come, all the world—come, sinner, thou—
All things in Christ are ready now.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, all you souls by sin oppressed,
You weary wanderers after rest;
You poor and maimed, and halt and blind,
In Christ a hearty welcome find.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The message, as from God, receive—
You all may come to Christ and live;
O let his love your hearts constrain,
Nor suffer him to call in vain.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
This is the time—no more delay;
The Saviour calls you all to-day:
O may his call effectual prove!
Accept the offers of his love!

title: Let every mortal ear attend
author: And drive our wants away

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let every mortal ear attend,
And every heart rejoice;
The trumpet of the gospel sounds
With an inviting voice:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ho! all you hungry, starving souls,
Who feed upon the wind,
And vainly strive with earthly toys
To fill an empty mind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Eternal wisdom has prepared
A soul-reviving feast,
And bids your longing appetites
The rich provision taste.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ho! you that pant for living streams,
And pine away and die,
Here may you quench your raging thirst
With springs that never dry.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Rivers of love and mercy here
In a rich ocean join;
Salvation in abundance flows,
Like floods of milk and wine.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Great God! the treasures of thy love
Are everlasting mines,
Deep as our helpless miseries are,
And boundless as our sins.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The happy gates of gospel grace
Stand open night and day:
Lord, we are come to seek supplies,

title: How free and boundless is the grace
author: And soothe your fears away

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How free and boundless is the grace
Of our redeeming God!
Extending to the Greek and Jew,
And men of every blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come, all you wretched sinners, come,
He’ll form your souls anew;
His gospel and his heart have room
For rebels such as you.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His doctrine is almighty love;
There’s virtue in his name
To turn a raven to a dove,
A lion to a lamb.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Return, O wanderer, now return

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Return, O wanderer, now return,
And seek thy Father’s face;
Those new desires which in thee burn
Were kindled by his grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Return, O wanderer, now return!
He hears thy humble sigh!
He sees thy softened spirit mourn,
When no one else is nigh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Return, O wanderer, now return!
Thy Saviour bids thee live;
Go to his feet, and grateful learn
How freely he’ll forgive.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Return, O wanderer, now return!
And wipe the falling tear;
Thy Father calls—no longer mourn,
’Tis love invites thee near.

title: The Saviour calls; let every ear

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
For every thirsty, longing heart,
Here streams of bounty flow,
And life, and health, and bliss impart,
To banish mortal woe.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Dear Saviour, draw reluctant hearts;
To thee let sinners fly,
And take the bliss thy love imparts,
And drink, and never die.

title: O what amazing words of grace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O what amazing words of grace
Are in the gospel found,
Suited to every sinner’s case
Who hears the joyful sound!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come, then, with all your wants and wounds
Your every burden bring;
Here love, unchanging love, abounds—
A deep celestial spring.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This spring with living water flows,
And heavenly joy imparts;
Come, thirsty souls! your wants disclose,
And drink with thankful hearts.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Millions of sinners, vile as you,
Have here found life and peace;
Come then, and prove its virtues too,
And drink, adore, and bless.

title: Come, humble sinner, in whose breast
author: I must for ever die

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, humble sinner, in whose breast
A thousand thoughts revolve;
Come, with your guilt and fear oppressed,
And make this last resolve:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I’ll go to Jesus, though my sin
Has like a mountain rose;
His kingdom now I’ll enter in,
Whatever may oppose.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Humbly I’ll bow at his command,
And there my guilt confess;
I’ll own I am a wretch undone,
Without his sovereign grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Surely he will accept my plea,
For he has bid me come;
Forthwith I’ll rise, and to him flee,
For yet, he says, there’s room.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Come to the ark, come to the ark
author: Is now about to close

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Come to the ark; the waters rise,
The seas their billows rear:
While darkness gathers o’er the skies,
Behold a refuge near!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come to the ark, all, all that weep
Beneath the sense of sin:
Without, deep calleth unto deep,
But all is peace within.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Ye wretched, hungry, starving poor

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye wretched, hungry, starving poor,
Behold a royal feast,
Where mercy spreads her bounteous store
For every humble guest.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Room in the Saviour’s bleeding heart;
There love and pity meet:
Nor will he bid the soul depart
That trembles at his feet.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O come, and with his children taste
The blessings of his love,
While hope attends the sweet repast
Of nobler joys above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
There, with united heart and voice,
Before th’ eternal throne,
Ten thousand thousand souls rejoice
In ecstasies unknown.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: The King of heaven his table spreads
author: And bless the Founder’s name

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The King of heaven his table spreads,
And dainties crown the board;
Not paradise, with all its joys,
Could such delights afford.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Pardon and peace to dying men,
And endless life are given,
Through the rich blood that Jesus shed,
To raise our souls to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
You hungry poor, that long have strayed
In sin’s dark mazes, come;
Come from your most obscure retreat,
And grace shall find you room.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Millions of souls in glory now
Were fed and feasted here;
And millions more still on the way
Around the board appear.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yet are his heart and house so large
That millions more may come:
Nor could the whole assembled world
O’erfill the spacious room.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Jesus, thy blessings are not few
author: The lion to a lamb

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thy blessings are not few,
Nor is thy gospel weak;
Thy grace can melt the stubborn Jew,
And heal the dying Greek.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Wide as the reach of Satan’s rage
Doth thy salvation flow;
’Tis not confined to sex nor age,
The lofty nor the low.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While grace is offered to the prince,
The poor may take his share;
No mortal has a just pretense
To perish in despair.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, all ye wretched sinners, come,
He’ll form your souls anew;
His gospel and his heart have room
For rebels such as you.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Return, O wanderer, to thy home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Return, O wanderer, to thy home,
Thy Father calls for thee;
No longer now an exile roam,
In guilt and misery:
Return, return!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Return, O wanderer, to thy home,
’Tis madness to delay;
There are no pardons in the tomb,
And brief is mercy’s day:
Return, return!

title: Now is th’ accepted time
author: Declares there yet is room

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now is th’ accepted time,
Now is the day of grace;
Now, sinners, come, without delay,
And seek the Saviour’s face.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now is th’ accepted time,
The Saviour calls to-day;
To-morrow it may be too late—
Then why should you delay?

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Now is the day of grace
author: May shine upon your grave

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Give to the Lord thine heart
author: Can never take away

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Give to the Lord thine heart;
In him all pleasures meet:
O, come and choose the better part,
Low at the Saviour’s feet.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: And will the Judge descend
author: We live with God in heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And will the Judge descend?
And must the dead arise?
And not a single soul escape
His all-discerning eyes?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How will my heart endure
The terrors of that day,
When earth and heaven before his face,
Astonished, shrink away?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But ere the trumpet shakes
The mansions of the dead;
Hark! from the Gospel’s cheering sound,
What joyful tidings spread.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ye sinners! seek his grace,
Whose wrath you can not bear;
Flee to the shelter of his cross,
And find salvation there.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Come! take his offers now,
From every sin depart,
Perform thy oft-repeated vow,
And render him thy heart.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Ye trembling captives! hear
author: In glorious triumph lead

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
’Tis not the trump of war,
Nor Sinai’s awful roar;
Salvation’s news it spreads afar,
And vengeance is no more.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Forgiveness, love, and peace,
Glad heaven aloud proclaims;
And earth, the jubilee’s release,
With eager rapture claims.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: To-morrow, Lord! is thine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To-morrow, Lord! is thine,
Lodged in thy sovereign hand;
And if its sun arise and shine,
It shines by thy command.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The present moment flies,
And bears our life away;
O, make thy servants truly wise,
That they may live to-day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Since on this fleeting hour
Eternity is hung,
Awake, by thine almighty power,
The agéd and the young.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
One thing demands our care;
O, be it still pursued!
Lest, slighted once, the season fair
Should never be renewed.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To Jesus may we fly,
Swift as the morning light,
Lest life’s young, golden beams should die
In sudden, endless night.

title: From the cross, uplifted high

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From the cross, uplifted high,
Where the Saviour deigns to die,
What melodious sounds we hear,
Bursting on the ravished ear!
“Love’s redeeming work is done;
Come and welcome, sinner, come.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
“Spread for thee the festal board,
See with richest dainties stored;
To thy Father’s bosom pressed,
Yet again a child confessed,
Never from his house to roam—
Come and welcome, sinner, come.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Sinners, turn—why will you die

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sinners, turn—why will you die?
God, your Maker, asks you why:
God, who did your being give,
Made you with himself to live.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sinners, turn—why will you die?
Christ, your Saviour, asks you why;
He, who did your souls retrieve,
He, who died that you might live.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Will you let him die in vain?
Crucify your Lord again?
Why, you ransomed sinners, why,
Will you slight his grace and die?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Will you not his grace receive?
Will you still refuse to live?
O! you dying sinners, why—
Why will you for ever die?

title: What could your Redeemer do

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What could your Redeemer do
More than he has done for you?
To procure your peace with God,
Could he more than shed his blood?
After all this flow of love,
All his drawings from above,
Why will you your Lord deny?
Why will you resolve to die?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Turn, he cries, O sinner, turn!
By his life your God hath sworn
He would have you turn and live,
He would all the world receive:
If your death were his delight,
Would he thus to life invite?
Would he ask, beseech and cry,
Why will you resolve to die?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sinners, turn, while God is near!
He has left you naught to fear;
Now, e’en now, your Saviour stands,
All day long he spreads his hands:
Cries, “You will not happy be,
No, you will not come to me:
Me who life to none deny—
Why will you resolve to die?”

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Can you doubt that God is love,
Who thus calls you from above?
Will you not his word receive?
Will you not his oath believe?
See, the suffering Lord appears;
Jesus weeps—believe his tears!
Mingled with his blood, they cry,
“Why will you resolve to die?”

title: Haste, O sinner, to be wise
author: Ere the morrow is begun

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Haste, O sinner, to be wise,
Stay not for the morrow’s sun;
Wisdom warns thee from the skies,
All the paths of death to shun.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Bleeding hearts, defiled by sin

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bleeding hearts, defiled by sin,
Jesus Christ can make you clean;
Contrite souls, with guilt oppressed,
Jesus Christ can give you rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
You that mourn o’er follies past,
Precious hours and years laid waste;
Turn to God, O turn and live,
Jesus Christ can still forgive.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
You that oft have wandered far
From the light of Bethlehem’s star,
Trembling, now your steps retrace,
Jesus Christ is full of grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Souls benighted and forlorn,
Grieved, afflicted, tempest-worn,
Now in Israel’s rock confide,
Jesus Christ for man has died.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Fainting souls, in peril’s hour,
Yield not to the tempter’s power;
On the risen Lord rely,
Jesus Christ now reigns on high.

title: Sinner, art thou still secure
author: Scorn the world’s pretended joys

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sinner, art thou still secure?
Wilt thou still refuse to pray?
Can thy heart or hands endure
In the Lord’s avenging day?
See his mighty arm made bare!
Awful terrors clothe his brow!
For his judgment now prepare,
Thou must either break or bow.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Then the great, the rich, the wise,
Trembling, guilty, self-condemned,
Must behold the wrathful eyes
Of the Judge they once blasphemed.
Where are now their haughty looks?
O! their horror and despair,
When they see the opened books,
And their dreadful sentence hear!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord, prepare us by thy grace:
Soon we must resign our breath,
And our souls be called to pass
Through the iron gate of death.
Let us now our days improve,
Listen to the gospel voice;
Seek the things that are above;

title: Ye who in his courts are found

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye who in his courts are found
Listening to the joyful sound,
Lost and hopeless as ye are,
Sons of sorrow, sin and care,
Glorify the King of kings;
Take the peace the gospel brings.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Weeping sinners, dry your tears

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Peace he brings you by his death,
Peace he speaks with every breath;
Can you slight such heavenly charms?
Flee, O flee to Jesus’ arms.

title: Sinner, seek the priceless treasure

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sinner, seek the priceless treasure,
Offered without price from God;
Here is mercy without measure,
Flowing in the Saviour’s blood.
Come, then, to the fount of healing,
Come, and prove its virtues true;
Turn not from love’s sweet appealing,
Jesus shed his blood for you!

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Come, you sinners, poor and needy
author: Sinners now his love proclaim

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, you weary, heavy laden,
Bruised and mangled by the fall;
If you tarry till you’re better,
You will never come at all:
Not the righteous—
Sinners Jesus came to call.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Agonizing in the garden,
Lo! your Saviour prostrate lies!
On the bloody tree behold him!
Hear him cry before he dies,
“It is finished!”
Sinners, will not this suffice?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lo! the rising Lord, ascending,
Pleads the virtue of his blood:
Venture on him, venture freely,
Let no other trust intrude:
None but Jesus
Can do helpless sinners good.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Saints and angels, joined in concert,
Sing the praises of the Lamb,
While the blissful seats of heaven
Sweetly echo to his name,
Hallelujah!

title: We are on the ocean sailing
author: Safe at home beyond the tide

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We are on the ocean sailing,
Homeward bound we sweetly glide;
We are on the ocean sailing,
To a home beyond the tide.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
All the storms will soon be over,
Then we’ll anchor in the harbor;
We are out on the ocean sailing
To a home beyond the tide.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Come on board, O ship for glory,
Be in haste, make up your mind,
For our vessel’s weighing anchor—
You will soon be left behind.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
When we all are safely landed,
Over on the shining shore,
We will walk about the city,
And we’ll sing for evermore.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
All the storms of life are over,
Landed in the port of glory:
Now no more on the ocean sailing—

title: Sinners, will you scorn the message
author: Glad the message will obey

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Will you not receive the message—
Listen to the joyful word;
And embrace the news of pardon
Offered to you by the Lord?
Can you slight it—
Offered to you by the Lord?

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Listen to the gospel, telling

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Listen to the gospel, telling
How the Lord was crucified;
How upon the cross he suffered,
When he bowed his head and died,
All for sinners!
Come, then, to his bleeding side.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Hear, O sinner! mercy hails you
author: You must perish if you stay

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

title: Stop, poor sinner, stop and think

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Stop, poor sinner, stop and think,
Before you further go;
Will you sport upon the brink
Of everlasting woe!
On the verge of ruin stop—
Now the friendly warning take—
Stay your footsteps—ere you drop
Into the burning lake.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Say, have you an arm like God,
That you his will oppose?
Fear ye not that iron rod
With which he breaks his foes?
Can you stand in that dread day
Which his justice shall proclaim—
When the earth shall melt away
Like wax before the flame?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ghastly death will quickly come,
And drag you to his bar;
Then, to hear your awful doom,
Will fill you with despair!
All your sins will round you crowd—
You shall mark their crimson dye—
Each for vengeance crying loud;
And what can you reply?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though your heart were made of steel,
Your forehead lined with brass,
God at length will make you feel—
He will not let you pass:
Sinners then in vain will call—
Those who now despise his grace—
“Rocks and mountains, on us fall,
And hide us from his face.”

title: Burdened with guilt, wouldst thou be blest
author: Thy Saviour bids thee come

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Burdened with guilt, wouldst thou be blest?
Trust not the world; it gives no rest:
I bring relief to hearts oppressed;
O, weary sinner, come!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, hither bring thy boding fears,
Thine aching heart, thy bursting tears;
’Tis mercy’s voice salutes thine ears:
O, trembling sinner, come!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
“The Spirit and the Bride say, Come;”
Rejoicing saints re-echo, Come!
Who faints, who thirsts, who will, may come:

title: Sinner! come, ’mid thy gloom
author: Eternity is dawning

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sinner! come, ’mid thy gloom,
All thy guilt confessing;
Trembling now, contrite bow,
Take the offered blessing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sinner! come, while there’s room—
While the feast is waiting;
While the Lord, by his word,
Kindly is inviting.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sinner! come, ere thy doom
Shall be sealed for ever;
Now return, grieve and mourn,
Flee to Christ, the Saviour.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sinner! come to thy home,
High in heaven gleaming;
To the sky lift thine eye,
With true sorrow streaming.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: We’re traveling home to heaven above

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
The way to heaven is straight and plain,
Will you go?
Believe, repent, be born again;
Will you go?
The Saviour cries aloud to thee
“Take up thy cross, and follow me,
And thou shalt my salvation see;
Come to me.”

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O, could I hear some sinner say,
I will go,
I’ll start this moment, clear the way,
Let me go!
My old companions, fare you well,
I will not go with you to hell,
With Jesus Christ I mean to dwell,
Let me go! fare you well.

title: All you that are weary and sad—come
author: And drink of the fountain of life

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All you that are weary and sad—come!
And you that are cheerful and glad—come!
In robes of humility clad—come!
The Saviour invites you to-day.
CHORUS.
Let youth in its freshness and bloom—come!
Let man in the pride of his noon—come!
Let age on the verge of the tomb—come!
Let none in his pride stay away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let the halt, and the maimed, and the blind—come!
Let all who are freely inclined—come!
With an humble and peaceable mind—come!
Away from the waters of strife.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Spirit and Bride freely say—Come!
And let him that heareth it, say—Come!
And let him that thirsteth to-day—come!

title: Child of sin and sorrow, filled with dismay

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Child of sin and sorrow, filled with dismay,
Wait not for to-morrow, yield thee to-day;
Heaven bids thee come
While yet there’s room:
Child of sin and sorrow,
Hear and obey.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Child of sin and sorrow, why wilt thou die?
Come, while thou canst borrow help from on high:
Grieve not that love,
Which from above—
Child of sin and sorrow—
Would bring thee nigh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Child of sin and sorrow, where wilt thou flee?
Through that long to-morrow, eternity!
Exiled from home,
Darkly to roam—
Child of sin and sorrow,
Where wilt thou flee?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Child of sin and sorrow, lift up thine eye!
Heirship thou canst borrow in worlds on high!
In that high home,
Graven thy name;
Child of sin and sorrow,
Swift homeward fly!

title: To-day the Saviour calls

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To-day the Saviour calls.
Ye wanderers, come:
O, ye benighted souls
Why longer roam?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Come—come—come to the Saviour
author: Jesus is rich to redeem

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Hark—hark, angels are singing,
Love—love—love is their theme;
Peace—peace joyfully bringing,
Mercy from God the Supreme:
Come—come—come—come,

title: O come in life’s gay morning
author: Throughout eternity

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O come in life’s gay morning,
Ere in thy sunny way
The flowers of hope have withered,
And sorrow end thy day.
Come, while from joy’s bright fountain
The streams of pleasure flow,
Come ere thy buoyant spirits
Have felt the blight of wo.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
“Remember thy Creator”
Now in thy youthful days,
And he will guide thy footsteps
Through life’s uncertain maze.
“Remember thy Creator,”
He calls in tones of love,
And offers deathless glories
In brighter worlds above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And in the hour of sadness,
When earthly joys depart,
His love shall be thy solace,
And cheer thy drooping heart.
And when life’s storm is over,
And thou from earth art free,
Thy God will be thy portion

title: Fair shines the morning star

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Fair shines the morning star,
The silver trumpets sound,
Their notes re-echoing far,
While dawns the day around:
Joy to the slave; the slave is free;
It is the year of jubilee.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye, who yourselves have sold
For debts to justice due,
Ransomed, but not with gold,
He gave himself for you!
The blood of Christ hath made you free;
It is the year of jubilee.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Sinner, go; will you go

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sinner, go; will you go
To the highlands of heaven?
Where the storms never blow,
And the long summer’s given;
Where the bright, blooming flowers
Are their odors emitting;
And the leaves of the bowers
In the breezes are flitting.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Where the rich golden fruit
Is in bright clusters pending,
And the deep laden boughs,
Of life’s fair tree are bending;
And where life’s crystal stream
Is unceasingly flowing,
And the verdure is green,
And eternally growing.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Where the saints robed in white—
Cleansed in life’s flowing fountain—
Shining beauteous and bright,
They inhabit the mountain;
Where no sin, nor dismay,
Neither trouble nor sorrow,
Will be felt for a day,
Nor be feared for the morrow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He’s prepared thee a home—
Sinner, canst thou believe it?
And invites thee to come,
Sinner, wilt thou receive it?
O come, sinner, come,
For the tide is receding,
And the Saviour will soon,
And for ever, cease pleading.

title: Hail, ransomed world! awake to glory
author: On glorious victory

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail, ransomed world! awake to glory!
For God, the Saviour, bids you rise;
Angelic hosts proclaim the story,
And speed the tidings from the skies:
Shall then the Prince of Darkness reigning,
Oppress the earth from pole to pole,
And bind in chains the immortal soul—
His hands all sacred things profaning?
Awake! O Church, awake!
The tyrant’s fetters break!
In God’s right arm of strength resolved
On glorious victory.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Far let the gospel-trump be sounding—
O’er sea, and continent, and isle;
While the sweet voice of grace abounding,
Shall make the burdened captive smile.
Yes! to a world in bondage lying,
Go teach a bleeding Saviour’s name—
Freedom from sin and death proclaim,
On every breeze salvation flying—
And seize the gospel sword!
And with our mighty Lord,
March on, march on, all hearts resolved

title: O turn you! O turn you, for why will you die

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O turn you! O turn you, for why will you die,
When God in his mercy is coming so nigh?
Now Jesus invites you, the Spirit says Come,
The brethren are waiting to welcome you home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How vain the delusion, that while you delay
Your hearts may grow better by staying away;
Come wretched, come starving, come just as you be,
Here streams of salvation are flowing most free.

sections.label: Verse 3
