sections.text:
Here Jesus is ready your souls to receive;
O, how can you question, since now you believe?
Since sin is your burden, why will you not come?
He now bids you welcome—he now says there’s room.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
In riches, in pleasure, what can you obtain,
To soothe your affliction, or banish your pain;
To bear up your spirit when summoned to die,
Or waft you to mansions of glory on high?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Why will you be starving and feeding on air?
There’s mercy in Jesus, enough and to spare;
If still you are doubting, make trial and see,
And prove that his mercy is boundless and free.

title: Delay not, delay not, O sinner, draw near

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Delay not, delay not, O sinner, draw near,
The waters of life are now flowing for thee;
No price is demanded, the Saviour is here,
Redemption is purchased—salvation is free.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Delay not, delay not! why longer abuse
The love and compassion of Jesus our Lord!
A fountain is opened; how canst thou refuse
To wash and be cleansed in his pardoning blood?

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Delay not, delay not! the Spirit of grace,
Long grieved and resisted, entreats thee to come;
Beware, lest in darkness thou finish thy race,
And sink to the vale of eternity’s gloom.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Delay not, delay not! the hour is at hand,
The earth shall dissolve and the heavens shall fade;
The dead, small and great, in the judgment shall stand:
What power, then, O sinner, shall lend thee its aid?

title: We’re bound for the land of the pure and the holy

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We’re bound for the land of the pure and the holy,
The home of the happy, the kingdom of love,
Ye wanderers from God, in the broad road of folly,
O say, will you go to the Eden above,
Will you go, will you go,
O say, will you go to the Eden above?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In that blesséd land neither sighing nor anguish
Can breathe in the fields where the glorified move.
Ye heart-burdened ones, who in misery languish,
O say, will you go to the Eden above?
Will you go, etc.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Nor fraud, nor deceit, nor the hand of oppression,
Can injure the dwellers in that holy grove;
No wickedness there, not a shade of transgression:
O say, will you go to the Eden above?
Will you go, etc.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Each saint has a mansion, prepared and all furnished,
Ere from this clay house he is summoned to move;
Its gates and its towers with glory are burnished,
O say, will you go to the Eden above?
Will you go, etc.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
And yet, guilty sinner, we would not forsake thee,
We halt yet a moment as onward we move;
O come to thy Lord, in his arms he will take thee,
And bear thee along to the Eden above.
Will you go, will you go,
O say, will you go to the Eden above?

title: The voice of free grace cries, “Escape to the mountain!”

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The voice of free grace cries, “Escape to the mountain!”
For Adam’s lost race Christ hath opened a fountain;
For sin and uncleanness, and every transgression,
His blood flows most freely in streams of salvation.
CHORUS.
Hallelujah to the Lamb! he hath purchased our pardon;
We’ll praise him again when we pass over Jordan.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O Jesus! ride onward, triumphantly glorious,
O’er sin, death, and hell, thou art more than victorious;
Thy name is the theme of the great congregation,
While angels and saints raise the shout of salvation.

title: Restless thy spirit, poor wandering sinner
author: Shall waft thee at last to the regions of day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Restless thy spirit, poor wandering sinner,
Restless and roving: O, come to thy home!
Return to the arms, to the bosom, of mercy;
The Saviour of sinners invites thee to come.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Darkness surrounds thee, and tempests are rising,
Fearful and dangerous the path thou hast trod;
But mercy shines forth in the rainbow of promise,
To welcome the wanderer home to his God.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Hark, sinner, while God from on high doth entreat thee

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
How oft of thy danger and guilt he hath told thee!
How oft still the message of mercy doth send!
Haste, haste, while he waits in his arms to enfold thee;
“The harvest is passing, the summer will end.”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Despised and rejected, at length he may leave thee:
What anguish and horror thy bosom will rend!
Then, haste thee, O sinner, while he will receive thee;
“The harvest is passing, the summer will end.”

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Sinners, come; no longer wander
author: FAITH AND REPENTANCE

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Christ for you his life has offered,
What can you excusing say,
If you slight the pardon proffered?
Come, come away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hold not back in hesitation,
There is danger in delay,
Haste, secure your soul’s salvation,
Come, come away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
You may feel regret and sorrow,
If you fail to come to-day,
God may grant you no to-morrow,
Come, come away.

title: Though all the world my choice deride
author: Nor count it worthy of a tear

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Sweet is the vision of thy face,
And kindness o’er thy lips is shed;
Lovely art thou, and full of grace,
And glory beams around thy head.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy sufferings I embrace with thee,
Thy poverty and shameful cross;
The pleasure of the world I flee,
And deem its treasures only dross.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: When human hopes and joys depart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When human hopes and joys depart,
I give thee, Lord, a contrite heart;
And on my weary spirit steal
The thoughts that pass all earthly weal.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I cast above my tearful eyes,
And muse upon the starry skies;
And think that he who governs there
Still keeps me in his guardian care.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I gaze upon the opening flower,
Just moistened with the evening shower;
And bless the love which made it bloom,
To chase away my transient gloom.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I think, whene’er this mortal frame
Returns again to whence it came,
My soul shall wing its happy flight
To regions of eternal light.

title: Let thoughtless thousands choose the road

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let thoughtless thousands choose the road
That leads the soul away from God;
This happiness, blest Lord, be mine,
To live and die entirely thine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On Christ, by faith, my soul would live,
From him my life, my all receive;
To him devote my fleeting hours,
Serve him alone with all my powers.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: God calling yet! shall I not hear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God calling yet! shall I not hear?
Earth’s pleasures shall I still hold dear?
Shall life’s swift passing years all fly,
And still my soul in slumbers lie?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
God calling yet! shall I not rise?
Can I his loving voice despise,
And basely his kind care repay?
He calls me still: can I delay?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God calling yet! and shall he knock,
And I my heart the closer lock?
He still is waiting to receive,
And shall I dare his Spirit grieve?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
God calling yet! and shall I give
No heed, but still in bondage live?
I wait, but he does not forsake;
He calls me still! my heart, awake!

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Now to the Lord, who makes us know
author: Nor let the chariot long delay

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now to the Lord, who makes us know
The wonders of his dying love,
Be humble honors paid below,
And strains of nobler praise above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
’Twas he who cleansed us from our sins,
And washed us in his precious blood;
’Tis he who makes us priests and kings,
And brings us, rebels, near to God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To Jesus, our atoning Priest,
To Jesus, our eternal King,
Be everlasting power confessed;
Let every tongue his glory sing.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Behold, on flying clouds he comes,
And every eye shall see him move;
Though with our sins we pierced him once,
Now he displays his pardoning love.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The unbelieving world shall wail,
While we rejoice to see the day:
Come, Lord, nor let thy promise fail,

title: Ah! wretched, vile, ungrateful heart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ah! wretched, vile, ungrateful heart!
That can from Jesus thus depart;
Thus fond of trifles, widely rove,
Forgetful of a Saviour’s love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Dear Lord! to thee I would return,
And at thy feet, repentant, mourn;
There let me view thy pardoning love,
And never from thy sight remove.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O let thy love, with sweet control,
Bind every passion of my soul;
Bid every vain desire depart,
And dwell for ever in my heart.

title: Awaked from sin’s delusive sleep

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awaked from sin’s delusive sleep,
My heavy guilt I feel, and weep;
Beneath a weight of woes oppressed,
I come to thee, my Lord, for rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now, from thy throne of grace above,
Look down upon my soul in love;
That smile shall sweeten all my pain,
And make my soul rejoice again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By thy divine, transforming power,
My ruined nature now restore;
And let my life and temper shine,
In blest resemblance, Lord! to thine.

title: Just as I am—without one plea

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Just as I am—without one plea,
But that thy blood was shed for me,
And that thou bidd’st me come to thee,
O Lamb of God, I come.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Just as I am, and waiting not
To rid my soul of one dark blot—
To thee, whose blood can cleanse each spot,
O Lamb of God, I come.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Just as I am, though tossed about
With many a conflict, many a doubt,
With fears within, and foes without—
O Lamb of God, I come.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Just as I am, poor, wretched, blind;
Sight, riches, healing of the mind,
Yea, all I need, in thee to find,
O Lamb of God, I come.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Just as I am, thou wilt receive,
Wilt welcome, pardon, cleanse, relieve,
Because thy promise I believe—
O Lamb of God, I come.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Just as I am—thy love unknown,
Has broken every barrier down;
Now to be thine, yea, thine alone,
O Lamb of God, I come.

title: Hear, gracious God! a sinner’s cry

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
To thee I come, a sinner lost,
Nor have I aught wherein to trust,
But where thou art, Lord, I would be,
O God, be merciful to me!

title: Lord, when my thoughts delighted rove

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, when my thoughts delighted rove
Amid the wonders of thy love,
Sweet hope revives my drooping heart,
And bids intruding fears depart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For mortal crimes a sacrifice,
The Lord of life, the Saviour dies;
What love! what mercy! how divine!
Jesus, and can I call thee mine?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Repentant sorrows fill my heart,
But mingling joy allays the smart;
O, may my future life declare
This sorrow and the joy sincere.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Be all my heart and all my days
Devoted to my Saviour’s praise;
And let my glad obedience prove
How much I owe, how much I love.

title: Show pity, Lord; O Lord forgive

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O, wash my soul from every sin,
And make my guilty conscience clean;
Here, on my heart, the burden lies,
And past offenses pain my eyes.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My lips, with shame, my sins confess,
Against thy law, against thy grace;
Lord, should thy judgment grow severe,
I am condemned, but thou art clear.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Should sudden vengeance seize my breath,
I must pronounce thee just in death;
And if my soul were sent to hell,
Thy righteous law approves it well.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Yet save a trembling sinner, Lord,
Whose hope, still hovering round thy word,
Would light on some sweet promise there,
Some sure support against despair.

title: A broken heart, my God, my King

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A broken heart, my God, my King,
Is all the sacrifice I bring;
The God of grace will ne’er despise
A broken heart for sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My soul lies humbled in the dust,
And owns thy dreadful sentence just;
Look down, O Lord, with pitying eye,
And save the soul condemned to die.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
O, may thy love inspire my tongue!
Salvation shall be all my song;
And all my powers shall join to bless
The Lord, my Strength and Righteousness.

title: Here is my heart—I give it thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Here is my heart—I give it thee!
My God, I heard thee call, and say,
“Not to the world, my child—to me!”
I heard thy voice and will obey;
Here is love’s offering to my King,
Which in glad sacrifice I bring.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here is my heart! so hard before,
But now by thy rich grace made meet;
Yet bruised and sad, it can but pour
Its tears and anguish at thy feet:
It groans beneath the weight of sin,
It sighs salvation’s joy to win.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here is my heart! its longings end
In Christ as near his cross it draws;
It says, “Thou art my rest, my Friend,
Thy precious blood my ransom was;”
In thee, the Saviour, it has found
That peace and blessedness abound.

title: Around Bethesda’s healing wave

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Around Bethesda’s healing wave,
Waiting to hear the rustling wind
Which spoke the angel nigh, who gave
Its virtue to that holy spring,
With patience and with hope endued,
Were seen the gathered multitude.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Bethesda’s pool has lost its power!
No angel, by his glad descent
Dispenses that diviner dower
Which with its healing waters went;
But he, whose word surpassed its wave,
Is still omnipotent to save.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Saviour! thy love is still the same
As when that healing word was spoke;
Still in thine all-redeeming name
Dwells power to burst the strongest yoke!
O, be that power, that love, displayed,
Help those whom thou alone canst aid.

title: Peace, troubled soul, whose plaintive moan

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Peace, troubled soul, whose plaintive moan
Hath taught each scene the notes of woe;
Cease thy complaint, suppress thy groan,
And let thy tears forget to flow:
Behold, the precious balm is found
To lull thy pain, to heal thy wound.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: When marshaled on the nightly plain

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When marshaled on the nightly plain,
The glittering host bestud the sky,
One star alone, of all the train,
Can fix the sinner’s wandering eye.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hark! hark! to God the chorus breaks,
From every host, from every gem;
But one alone the Saviour speaks—
It is the Star of Bethlehem.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Once on the raging seas I rode;
The storm was loud, the night was dark,
The ocean yawned, and rudely blowed
The wind that tossed my foundering bark.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Now safely moored, my perils o’er,
I’ll sing, first in night’s diadem,
For ever, and for evermore,
The Star—the Star of Bethlehem.

title: Faith adds new charms to earthly bliss
author: To endless glory rise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Faith adds new charms to earthly bliss,
And saves us from its snares;
It yields support in all our toils,
And softens all our cares.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The wounded conscience knows its power
The healing balm to give;
That balm the saddest heart can cheer,
And make the dying live.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Unvailing wide the heavenly world,
Where endless pleasures reign,
It bids us seek our portion there,
Nor bids us seek in vain.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: O for a faith that will not shrink
author: Of an eternal home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O for a faith that will not shrink,
Though pressed by every foe,
That will not tremble on the brink
Of any earthly woe!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That will not murmur nor complain
Beneath the chastening rod,
But, in the hour of grief or pain,
Will lean upon its God;

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
That bears, unmoved, the world’s dread frown,
Nor heeds its scornful smile;
That seas of trouble can not drown,
Nor Satan’s arts beguile.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
A faith that keeps the narrow way
Till life’s last hour is fled,
And with a pure and heavenly ray,
Lights up a dying bed.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Mistaken souls, that dream of heaven
author: In death’s approaching hour

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Mistaken souls, that dream of heaven,
And make their empty boast
Of inward joys, and sins forgiven,
While they are slaves to lust!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How vain are fancy’s airy flights,
If faith be cold and dead!
None but a living power unites
To Christ, the living Head.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Faith must obey our Father’s will,
As well as trust his grace;
A pardoning God requires us still
To walk in all his ways.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
This faith shall every fear control
By its celestial power,
With holy triumph fill the soul

title: Didst thou, Lord Jesus, suffer shame
author: And glory in thy cross

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Didst thou, Lord Jesus, suffer shame,
And bear the cross for me?
And shall I fear to own thy name,
Or thy disciple be?

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Repent! the voice celestial cries

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Repent! the voice celestial cries,
No longer dare delay:
The soul that scorns the mandate dies,
And meets a fiery day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No more the sovereign eye of God
O’erlooks the crimes of men;
His heralds now are sent abroad
To warn the world of sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O sinners! in his presence bow,
And all your guilt confess;
Accept the offered Saviour now
Nor trifle with his grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Soon will the awful trumpet sound,
And call you to his bar;
His mercy knows the appointed bound,
And yields to justice there.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Amazing love—that yet will call,
And yet prolong our days!
Our hearts, subdued by goodness, fall,
And weep, and love, and praise.

title: Come, let us to the Lord our God
author: The sorrows of the night

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us to the Lord our God,
With contrite hearts return!
Our God is gracious, nor will leave
The desolate to mourn.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His voice commands the tempest forth,
And stills the stormy wave;
And though his arm be strong to smite,
’Tis also strong to save.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
As dew upon the tender herb,
Diffusing fragrance round;
As showers that usher in the spring,
And cheer the thirsty ground:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
So shall his presence bless our souls,
And shed a joyful light
That hallowed morn shall chase away

title: O how divine, how sweet the joy
author: And strike the sounding lyre

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O how divine, how sweet the joy,
When but one sinner turns,
And, with a humble, broken heart,
His sins and errors mourns!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Pleased with the news, the saints below,
In songs their tongues employ;
Beyond the skies the tidings go,
And heaven is filled with joy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Well pleased the Father sees, and hears
The conscious sinner’s moan;
Jesus receives him in his arms,
And claims him for his own.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Welcome, O Saviour! to my heart
author: I give it all to thee

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The world and Satan I forsake—
To thee, I all resign;
My longing heart, O Jesus! take,
And fill with love divine.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: And must I part with all I have
author: I’ll glory in my gain

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And must I part with all I have,
Jesus, my Lord! for thee?
This is my joy, since thou hast done
Much more than this for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yes, let it go; one look from thee
Will more than make amends
For all the losses I sustain
Of credit, riches, friends.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ten thousand worlds, ten thousand lives,
How worthless they appear,
Compared with thee, supremely good,
Divinely bright and fair.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Saviour of souls! while I from thee
A single smile obtain,
Though destitute of all things else,

title: Mercy alone can meet my case

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Mercy alone can meet my case,
For mercy, Lord, I cry;
Jesus, Redeemer, show thy face
In mercy, or I die.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

title: When I sink down in gloom or fear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When I sink down in gloom or fear,
Hope blighted or delayed,
Thy whisper, Lord, my heart shall cheer,
“’Tis I: be not afraid!”

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Or, startled at some sudden blow,
If fretful thoughts I feel,
“Fear not, it is but I!” shall flow
As balm my wound to heal.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Nor will I quit thy way, though foes
Some onward pass defend;
From each rough voice the watchword goes,
“Be not afraid! ... a friend!”

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And O! when judgment’s trumpet clear
Awakes me from the grave,
Still in its echo may I hear,
“’Tis Christ! he comes to save.”

title: Desponding soul, O cease thy woe

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
No works of thine can e’er impart
A balm to heal thy wounded heart,
Or solid comfort give;
Turn, then, to him who freely gave
His precious blood thy soul to save:
E’en now he bids thee live.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Ah! what avails my strife
author: And give up all for thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ah! what avails my strife,
My wandering to and fro?
Thou hast the words of endless life;
Ah! whither should I go?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy condescending grace
To me did freely move;
It calls me still to seek thy face,
And stoops to ask my love.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: And can I yet delay
author: No other good below

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And can I yet delay
My little all to give?
To tear my soul from earth away
For Jesus to receive?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, and possess me whole,
Nor hence again remove;
Settle and fix my wavering soul
With all thy weight of love.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Sweet is the friendly voice
author: From paths which thou hast blessed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet is the friendly voice
Which speaks of life and peace;
Which bids the penitent rejoice,
And sin and sorrow cease.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No balm on earth like this
Can cheer the contrite heart;
No flattering dreams of earthly bliss
Such pure delight impart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Still merciful and kind,
Thy mercy, Lord, reveal;
The broken heart thy love can bind,
The wounded spirit heal.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Love for all! and can it be

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Love for all! and can it be?
Can I hope it is for me?
I, who strayed so long ago,
Strayed so far, and fell so low!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I, the disobedient child,
Wayward, passionate and wild;
I, who left my Father’s home
In forbidden ways to roam!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I, who spurned his loving hold,
I, who would not be controlled;
I, who would not hear his call,
I, the willful prodigal!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I, who wasted and misspent
Every talent he had lent;
I, who sinned again, again,
Giving every passion rein!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To my Father can I go?
At his feet myself I’ll throw,
In his house there yet may be
Place, a servant’s place, for me.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: People of the living God
author: Light thy burden now to me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
People of the living God!
I have sought the world around,
Paths of sin and sorrow trod,
Peace and comfort nowhere found.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now to you my spirit turns,
Turns, a fugitive unblessed;
Brethren! where your altar burns,
O receive me into rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lonely I no longer roam,
Like the cloud, the wind, the wave:
Where you dwell shall be my home,
Where you die shall be my grave.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Mine the God whom you adore,
Your Redeemer shall be mine;
Earth can fill my heart no more,
Every idol I resign.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Tell me not of gain or loss,
Ease, enjoyment, pomp, and power;
Welcome! poverty and cross,
Shame, reproach, affliction’s hour.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Does the gospel word proclaim

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Does the gospel word proclaim
Rest for those that weary be?
Then, my soul, put in thy claim—
Sure that promise speaks to thee:
Marks of grace I can not show,
All polluted is my best;
But I weary am, I know,
And the weary long for rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Burdened with a load of sin,
Harassed with tormenting doubt,
Hourly conflicts from within,
Hourly crosses from without;
All my little strength is gone,
Sink I must without supply;
Sure upon the earth is none
Can more weary be than I.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: When we can not see our way

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When we can not see our way,
Let us trust, and still obey;
He who bids us forward go,
Can not fail the way to show.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though the sea be deep and wide,
Though a passage seem denied;
Fearless let us still proceed,
Since the Lord vouchsafes to lead.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though it seems the gloom of night,
Though we see no ray of light;
Since the Lord himself is there,
’Tis not meet that we should fear.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Be it ours, then, while we’re here,
Him to follow without fear;
Where he calls us, there to go,
What he bids us, that to do.

title: O holy Saviour! Friend unseen

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O holy Saviour! Friend unseen,
Since on thine arm thou bidd’st me lean,
Help me, throughout life’s changing scene,
By faith to cling to thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Blest with this fellowship divine,
Take what thou wilt, I’ll not repine;
For, as the branches to the vine,
My soul would cling to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though far from home, fatigued, oppressed,
Here have I found a place of rest;
An exile still, yet not unblest,
Because I cling to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
What though the world deceitful prove,
And earthly friends and hopes remove;
With patient, uncomplaining love,
Still would I cling to thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Though oft I seem to tread alone
Life’s dreary waste, with thorns o’ergrown,
Thy voice of love in gentlest tone,
Still whispers, “Cling to me!”

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Though faith and hope are often tried,
I ask not, need not aught beside;
So safe, so calm, so satisfied,
The soul that clings to thee!

title: Cling to the Crucified
author: BAPTISM

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Cling to the Crucified!
His eye shall guard thee well—
For thee, fast from his side,
The crimson current fell.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Cling to the Crucified!
My weary feet in peace
His tender hand shall guide
Till all thy wanderings cease.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Cling to the Crucified!
His love the golden door
For thee shall open wide,

title: Jesus, and shall it ever be

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, and shall it ever be,
A mortal man ashamed of thee:
Ashamed of thee, whom angels praise,
Whose glory shines through endless days.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ashamed of Jesus! Sooner far
Let evening blush to own a star!
He sheds the beams of light divine
O’er this benighted soul of mine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ashamed of Jesus! Just as soon
Let morning be ashamed of noon;
’Tis midnight with my soul, till he,
Bright Morning Star, bid darkness flee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ashamed of Jesus! that dear friend,
On whom my hopes of heaven depend!
No! when I blush, be this my shame,
That I no more revere his name.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ashamed of Jesus! Yes, I may,
When I’ve no guilt to wash away,
No tear to wipe, no good to crave,
No fears to quell, no soul to save.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Till then—nor is my boasting vain—
Till then I’ll boast a Saviour slain!
And O! may this my glory be,
That Christ is not ashamed of me!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
His institutions would I prize,
Take up my cross, the shame despise—
Dare to defend his noble cause,
And yield obedience to his laws.

title: We love thy name, we love thy laws

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We love thy name, we love thy laws,
And joyfully embrace thy cause;
We love thy cross, the shame, the pain,
O Lamb of God, for sinners slain.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
And as we rise, with thee to live,
O, let the Holy Spirit give
The sealing unction from above,
The breath of life, the fire of love.

title: Jesus my all to heaven has gone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus my all to heaven has gone,
He whom I fix my hopes upon;
His path I see, and I’ll pursue
The narrow way, till him I view.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The way the holy prophets went,
The road that leads from banishment,
The King’s highway of holiness—
I’ll go, for all his paths are peace.

title: Our Saviour bowed beneath the wave

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our Saviour bowed beneath the wave,
And meekly sought a watery grave;
Come see the sacred path he trod,
A path well-pleasing to our God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His voice we hear, his footsteps trace,
And hither come to seek his face,
To do his will, to feel his love,
And join our songs with songs above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hosanna to the Lamb divine!
Let endless glories round him shine!
High o’er the heavens for ever reign,
O Lamb of God! for sinners slain!

title: Come, happy souls, adore the Lamb

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, happy souls, adore the Lamb,
Who loved our race ere time began,
Who vailed his Godhead in our clay,
And in an humble manger lay.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To Jordan’s stream the Spirit led,
To mark the path his saints should tread;
With joy they trace the sacred way,
To see the place where Jesus lay.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Baptized by John in Jordan’s wave,
The Saviour left his watery grave;
Heaven owned the deed, approved the way,
And blessed the place where Jesus lay.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: The great Redeemer we adore
author: And rise and triumph at thy side

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The great Redeemer we adore,
Who came the lost to seek and save—
Went humbly down from Jordan’s shore
To find a tomb beneath its wave!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With thee into thy watery tomb,
Lord, ’tis our glory to descend;
’Tis wondrous grace that gives us room
To share the grave of such a friend.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yet, as the yielding waves give way
To let us see the light again,
So, on the resurrection day,
The bands of death proved weak and vain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus, when thou shalt again appear,
The gates of death shall open wide:
Our dust thy mighty voice shall hear,

title: See how the willing converts trace
author: In concert join their loud Amen

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
See how the willing converts trace
The path their great Redeemer trod:
And follow through his liquid grave
The meek, the lowly Son of God!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here they renounce their former deeds,
And to a heavenly life aspire,
Their rags for glorious robes exchanged,
They shine in clean and bright attire.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O sacred rite, by thee the name
Of Jesus we to own begin;
This is our resurrection pledge,
Pledge of the pardon of our sin.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: In all my Lord’s appointed ways
author: I’ll gladly go with thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In all my Lord’s appointed ways,
My journey I’ll pursue;
Hinder me not, you much-loved saints,
For I must go with you.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Through floods and flames, if Jesus lead,
I’ll follow where he goes;
Hinder me not, shall be my cry,
Though earth and hell oppose.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Through trials and through sufferings too,
I’ll go at his command;
Hinder me not, for I am bound
To my Immanuel’s land.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when my Saviour calls me home,
Still this my cry shall be—
Hinder me not—come, welcome death—

title: Ashamed of Christ! our souls disdain
author: Shall reign with him in bliss

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ashamed of Christ! our souls disdain
The mean, ungenerous thought;
Shall we disown that friend whose blood
To man salvation brought?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With the glad news of love and peace,
From heaven to earth he came;
For us endured the painful cross,
For us despised the shame.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To his command let us submit
Ourselves without delay;
Our lives—yea, thousand lives of ours,
His love can ne’er repay.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Each faithful follower Jesus views
With infinite delight;
Their lives to him are dear—their death
Is precious in his sight.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To bear his name—his cross to bear—
Our highest honor this!
Who nobly suffers for him now,

title: Buried beneath the yielding wave
author: Our lives shall be thy praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Buried beneath the yielding wave,
The great Redeemer lies;
Faith views him in the watery grave,
And thence beholds him rise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With joy we in his footsteps tread,
And would his cause maintain,
Like him be numbered with the dead,
And with him rise and reign.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: O Lord, and will thy pardoning love
author: In thy delightful ways

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord, and will thy pardoning love
Embrace a wretch so vile?
Wilt thou my load of guilt remove,
And bless me with thy smile?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hast thou the cross for me endured,
And all its shame despised?
And shall I be ashamed, O Lord,
With thee to be baptized?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Didst thou the great example lead,
In Jordan’s swelling flood!
And shall my pride disdain the deed,
That’s worthy of my God!

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Meekly in Jordan’s flowing stream
author: In melody our tongues

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Meekly in Jordan’s flowing stream
The great Redeemer bowed;
Bright was the glory’s sacred beam
That hushed the wondering crowd.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thus God descended to approve
The deed that Christ had done;
Thus came the emblematic Dove,
And hovered over the Son.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So may the Spirit come to-day
To our baptismal scene;
Let thoughts of earth be far away,
And every mind serene.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: “I come,” the great Redeemer cries
author: Our souls to things above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
“I come,” the great Redeemer cries,
“To do thy will, O Lord!”
At Jordan’s flood, behold! he seals
The sure prophetic word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
“Thus it becomes us to fulfill
All righteousness,” he said;
He spake obedient, and beneath
The yielding wave was laid.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hark! a glad voice—the Father speaks,
From heaven’s exalted hight;
“This is my Son, my well beloved,
In whom I do delight.”

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, the Saviour, well beloved!
His name we will profess,
Like him, desirous to fulfill
Each law of righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Come and behold the place
author: And bid us go in peace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come and behold the place
Where once your Saviour lay;
Confess that he is Lord of all,
And humble homage pay.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Laid in the watery grave,
He quickly rose again;
Buried with him, we too shall rise,
And endless life obtain.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Now may the Spirit crown,
With tokens of his grace,
The solemn service of this day,

title: Saviour, thy law we love
author: We humbly offer here

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour, thy law we love,
Thy pure example bless,
And with a firm, unwavering zeal,
Would in thy footsteps press.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not to the fiery pains
By which the martyrs bled;
Not to the scourge, the thorn, the cross,
Our favored feet are led—

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But, at this peaceful tide,
Assembled in thy fear,
The homage of obedient hearts,

title: Here, Saviour, we would come
author: Our strength shall also be

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Here, Saviour, we would come,
In thine appointed way;
Obedient to thy high commands,
Our solemn vows we pay.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: With willing hearts we tread
author: To life and bliss in thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With willing hearts we tread
The path the Saviour trod;
We love th’ example of our Head,
The glorious Lamb of God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On thee, on thee alone,
Our hope and faith rely;
O thou who didst for sin atone,
Who didst for sinners die.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Jesus, Lamb of God, for me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, Lamb of God, for me
Thou, the Lord of life, didst die;
Whither—whither, but to thee,
Can a trembling sinner fly?
Death’s dark waters o’er me roll,
Save, O save, my sinking soul!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Never bowed a martyred head,
Weighed with equal sorrow down;
Never blood so rich was shed,
Never king wore such a crown!
To thy cross and sacrifice,
Faith now lifts her tearful eyes.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Jesus, to thy wounds I fly

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Purge me in that sacred flood,
In that fountain of thy blood;
Then thy Father’s eye shall see
Not a spot of guilt in me.

title: Weary souls that wander wide

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Humble souls, who seek salvation

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Humble souls, who seek salvation
Through the Lamb’s redeeming blood,
Hear the voice of revelation;
Tread the path that Jesus trod.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Plainly here his footsteps tracing,
Follow him without delay,
Gladly his command embracing;
Lo! your Captain leads the way.

title: Gracious Saviour, we adore thee
author: REMISSION OF SINS

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Gracious Saviour, we adore thee;
Purchased by thy precious blood
We present ourselves before thee,
Now to walk the narrow road:
Saviour guide us—
Guide us to our heavenly home.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Forgiveness! ’tis a joyful sound

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
For this stupendous love of heaven,
What grateful honors shall we show!
Where much transgression is forgiven,
Let love in equal ardors glow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By this inspired, let all our days
With gospel holiness be crowned;
Let truth and goodness, prayer and praise
In all abide, in all abound.

title: Earth has a joy unknown in heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Earth has a joy unknown in heaven—
The new-born joy of sins forgiven!
Tears of such pure and deep delight,
O angels! never dimmed your sight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
You saw of old on chaos rise
The beauteous pillars of the skies;
You know where morn exulting springs,
And evening folds her drooping wings.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Bright heralds of th’ Eternal Will,
Abroad his errands you fulfill;
Or, throned in floods of beamy day,
Symphonies in his presence play.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Loud is the song—the heavenly plain
Is shaken with the choral strain;
And dying echoes, floating far,
Draw music from each chiming star.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But I amid your choirs shall shine,
And all your knowledge shall be mine;
You on your harps must lean to hear
A secret chord that mine shall bear.

title: Lord, I am thine, entirely thine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, I am thine, entirely thine,
Purchased alone by blood divine;
With full consent I yield to thee,
And own thy sovereign right to me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Grant me, in mercy, now a place
Among the children of thy grace;
A wretched sinner, lost to God,
But ransomed by Immanuel’s blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thee, my new Master, now I call,
And consecrate to thee my all:
Lord, let me live and die to thee;
Be thine through all eternity.

title: O happy day, that fixed my choice
author: And bless in death a bond so dear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O happy day, that fixed my choice
On thee, my Saviour and my God!
Well may this glowing heart rejoice,
And tell its raptures all abroad.
CHORUS.
Happy day, happy day,
When Jesus washed my sins away;
He taught me how to watch and pray,
And live rejoicing every day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O happy bond, that seals my vows
To him who merits all my love!
Let cheerful anthems fill his house,
While to that sacred shrine I move.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Now rest, my long divided heart!
Fixed on this blissful center rest;
Here have I found a nobler part,
Here heavenly pleasures fill my breast.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: O sweetly breathe the lyres above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O sweetly breathe the lyres above,
When angels touch the quivering string,
And wake, to chant Immanuel’s love,
Such strains as angel-lips can sing!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And sweet, on earth, the choral swell,
From mortal tongues, of gladsome lays;
When pardoned souls their raptures tell,
And, grateful, hymn Immanuel’s praise.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Our hearts, by dying love subdued,
Accept thine offered grace to-day;
Beneath the cross, with blood bedewed,
We bow, and give ourselves away.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Now I have found the ground wherein

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
With faith I plunge me in this sea,
Here is my hope, my joy, my rest;
Hither, when hell assails, I flee,
I look into my Saviour’s breast.
Away, sad doubt, and anxious fear!
Mercy is all that’s written here.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Tho’ waves and storms go o’er my head,
Tho’ strength, and health, and friends, be gone:
Tho’ joys be withered all, and dead;
Tho’ every comfort be withdrawn—
Steadfast on this my soul relies:
Father, thy mercy never dies.

title: Redeemed from guilt, redeemed from fears

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Redeemed from guilt, redeemed from fears,
My soul enlarged, and dried my tears,
What can I do, O Love Divine,
What to repay such gifts as thine?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What can I do, so poor, so weak,
But from thy hands new blessings seek,
A heart to feel thy mercies more,
A soul to know thee, and adore?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O teach me at thy feet to fall,
And yield thee up myself, my all!
Before thy saints my debts to own,
And live and die to thee alone!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy Spirit, Lord, at large impart,
Expand, and raise, and fill my heart!
So may I hope my life shall be
Some faint return, O Lord, to thee.

title: How happy is the Christian’s state
author: To everlasting day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How happy is the Christian’s state!
His sins are all forgiven;
A cheering ray confirms the grace,
And lifts his hopes to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though in the rugged path of life
He heaves the pensive sigh;
Yet, trusting in his God, he finds
Delivering grace is nigh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If, to prevent his wandering steps,
He feels the chastening rod,
The gentle stroke shall bring him back
To his forgiving God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when the welcome message comes
To call his soul away,
His soul in raptures shall ascend

title: Amazing grace! (how sweet the sound!)
author: A life of joy and peace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Amazing grace! (how sweet the sound!)
That saved a wretch like me!
I once was lost, but now am found;
Was blind, but now I see.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Through many dangers, toils, and snares,
I have already come;
’Tis grace has brought me safe thus far,
And grace will lead me home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Lord has promised good to me,
His word my hope secures;
He will my shield and portion be
As long as life endures.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Yes, when this heart and flesh shall fail,
And mortal life shall cease,
I shall possess within the vail

title: How happy every child of grace
author: Through all eternity

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How happy every child of grace,
Who knows his sins forgiven!
This earth, he cries, is not my place—
I seek my home in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A country far from mortal sight,
Yet O, by faith I see
The land of rest, the saint’s delight,
The heaven prepared for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O what a blesséd hope is ours!
While here on earth we stay,
We more than taste the heavenly powers,
And antedate that day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We feel the resurrection near,
Our life in Christ concealed,
And with his glorious presence here,
Our earthen vessels filled.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O, would he all of heaven bestow!
Then like our Lord we’ll rise;
Our bodies, fully ransomed, go
To take the glorious prize.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
On him with rapture then I’ll gaze,
Who bought the bliss for me,
And shout and wonder at his grace,

title: Grace! ’tis a charming sound
author: And well deserves our praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Grace! ’tis a charming sound,
Harmonious to the ear;
Heaven with the echo shall resound,
And all the earth shall hear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Grace first contrived the way
To save rebellious man;
And all the steps that grace display,
Which drew the wondrous plan.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Grace led our wandering feet
To tread the heavenly road;
And new supplies each hour we meet,
While pressing on to God.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Blest Saviour! Friend divine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest Saviour! Friend divine!
Thou source of boundless love!
The hope of all thy saints on earth,
The joy of all above!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How can I tell thy worth!
How make thy glories known!
No language can thy goodness speak,
No tongue thy mercies own!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My words can not express
The sweetness of thy name!
Nor can my feeble lips declare
The wonders of thy fame!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then take my trusting heart,
I can not give thee more;
Make rich my soul’s deep poverty,
From thine unwasting store!

title: Since first thy word awaked my heart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Since first thy word awaked my heart,
Like light new dawning o’er me,
Where’er I turn my eyes, thou art
All light and love before me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Naught else I feel, or hear, or see,
All bonds of earth I sever;
Thee, O my Lord, and only thee,
I live for, now, and ever.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Like him whose fetters dropped away
When light shone o’er his prison,
My soul now touched by mercy’s ray,
Hath from its chains arisen.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And shall the soul thou bidd’st be free,
Return to bondage? Never;
Thee, O my God, and only thee,
I live for, now, and ever.

title: How happy are they who their Saviour obey
author: SPIRIT OF ADOPTION

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How happy are they who their Saviour obey,
And have laid up their treasures above!
Tongue can not express the sweet comfort and peace
Of a soul in its earliest love!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This comfort is mine, since the favor divine
I have found in the blood of the Lamb:
Since the truth I believed what a joy I’ve received,
What a heaven in Jesus’ blest name!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
’Tis a heavén below my Redeemer to know,
And the angels can do nothing more
Than to fall at his feet, and the story repeat,
And the lover of sinners adore!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus all the day long is my joy and my song;
O that all to this refuge may fly!
He has loved me, I cried, he has suffered and died
To redeem such a rebel as I!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
On the wings of his love I am carried above
All my sin, and temptation, and pain;
O why should I grieve, while on him I believe!
O why should I sorrow again!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O the rapturous hight of that holy delight,
Which I find in the life-giving blood!
Of my Saviour possessed, I am perfectly blessed,
Being filled with the fullness of God!

sections.label: Verse 7
Verse 8
sections.text:
What a mercy is this! what a heaven of bliss!
How unspeakably happy am I!
Gathered into the fold, with believers enrolled—
With believers to live and to die!

title: Like morning—when her early breeze

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Like morning—when her early breeze
Breaks up the surface of the seas,
That, in their furrows, dark with night,
Her hand may sow the seeds of light—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy grace can send its breathings o’er
The spirit dark and lost before;
And, freshening all its depths, prepare
For truth divine to enter there.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Till David touched his sacred lyre,
In silence lay the unbreathing wire;
But when he swept its chords along,
Then angels stooped to hear the song.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
So sleeps the soul, till thou, O Lord,
Shall deign to touch its lifeless chord;
Till, waked by thee, its breath shall rise,
In music worthy of the skies.

title: O Lord! and shall thy Spirit rest
author: Sweet earnest of the joys above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord! and shall thy Spirit rest
In such a wretched heart as mine!
Unworthy dwelling! glorious guest!
Favor astonishing, divine!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When sin prevails, and gloomy fear,
And hope almost expires in night,
Lord, can thy Spirit then be here,
Great Spring of comfort, life, and light?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sure the blest Comforter is nigh!
’Tis he sustains my fainting heart;
Else would my hopes for ever die,
And every cheering ray depart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When some kind promise glads my soul,
Do I not find his healing voice
The tempest of my fears control,
And bid my drooping powers rejoice!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Let thy kind Spirit in my heart
For ever dwell, O God of love!
And light and heavenly peace impart—

title: Blessed are the humble souls that see

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blessed are the humble souls that see
Their emptiness and poverty;
Treasures of grace to them are given,
And crowns of joy laid up in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Blessed are the men of broken heart,
Who mourn for sin with inward smart;
The blood of Christ divinely flows,
A healing balm for all their woes.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blessed are the souls who thirst for grace,
Hunger and thirst for righteousness;
They shall be well supplied, and fed
With living streams and living bread.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blessed are the men of peaceful life,
Who quench the glowing coals of strife;
They shall be called the heirs of bliss,
The sons of God, the God of peace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Blessed are the sufferers who partake
Of pain and shame for Jesus’ sake;
Their souls shall triumph in the Lord:
Glory and joy are their reward.

title: God of my life! thy boundless grace

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, my Hope, my Rock, my Shield!
Whose precious blood was shed for me,
Into thy hands my soul I yield;
Saviour! I come, I come to thee.

title: Honor and happiness unite

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Honor and happiness unite
To make the Christian’s name a praise;
How fair the scene, how clear the light,
That fills the remnant of his days!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A kingly character he bears,
No change his priestly office knows;
Unfading is the crown he wears,
His joys can never reach a close.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Adorned with glory from on high,
Salvation shines upon his face;
His robe is of the ethereal dye,
His steps are dignity and grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Inferior honors he disdains,
Nor stoops to take applause from earth,
The King of kings himself maintains
The expenses of his heavenly birth.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The noblest creature seen below,
Ordained to fill a throne above;
God gives him all he can bestow,
His kingdom of eternal love!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
My soul is ravished at the thought!
Methinks from earth I see him rise!
Angels congratulate his lot,
And shout him welcome to the skies!

title: Lord, in whose might the Saviour trod
author: Since thou art present there

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, in whose might the Saviour trod
The dark and stormy wave,
And trusted in his Father’s arm,
Omnipotent to save;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When thickly round our footsteps rise
The floods and storms of life,
Grant us thy Spirit, Lord, to still
The dark and fearful strife.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Strong in our trust, on thee reposed,
The ocean path we’ll dare,
Though waves around us rage and foam,

title: Father! I wait before thy throne
author: With an unwavering tongue

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

title: There is a name I love to hear
author: That leads me up to God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a name I love to hear,
I love to speak its worth;
It sounds like music in mine ear,
The sweetest name on earth.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It tells me of a Saviour’s love,
Who died to set me free;
It tells me of his precious blood,
The sinner’s perfect plea.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It tells me of a Father’s smile,
Beaming upon his child;
It cheers me through this “little while,”
Through desert, waste, and wild.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus! the name I love so well,
The name I love to hear!
No saint on earth its worth can tell,
No heart conceive how dear.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
This name shall shed its fragrance still
Along this thorny road,
Shall sweetly smooth the rugged hill

title: Lord, let thy Spirit penetrate
author: Filled with the light of God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, let thy Spirit penetrate
This heart and soul of mine;
And my whole being with thy grace
Pervade, O Life divine!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As this clear air surrounds the earth,
Thy grace around me roll;
As the fresh light pervades the air,
So pierce and fill my soul.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
As from these clouds drops down in love
The precious summer rain,
So from thyself pour down the flood
That freshens all again.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
As these fair flowers exhale their scent
In gladness at our feet,
So from thyself let fragrance breathe,
More heavenly and more sweet.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Great source of life and light
author: Where sin and sorrow cease

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Long as my trials last,
Long as the cross I bear,
O, let my soul on thee be cast
In confidence and prayer!
Conduct me to the shore
Of everlasting peace,
Where storm and tempest rise no more,

title: Thy Spirit shall unite
author: He’ll fix his members there

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy Spirit shall unite
Our souls to thee our Head;
Shall form us to thine image bright,
That we thy paths may tread.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Death may our souls divide
From these abodes of clay;
But love shall keep us near thy side
Through all the gloomy way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Since Christ and we are one,
Why should we doubt or fear!
If he in heaven hath fixed his throne,

title: Blesséd are the sons of God

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Call Jehovah thy salvation
author: Crown with life beyond the grave

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

title: Our blest Redeemer, ere he breathed
author: And speaks of heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our blest Redeemer, ere he breathed
His tender, last farewell,
A Guide, a Comforter, bequeathed
With us to dwell.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He came in tongues of living flame,
To teach, convince, subdue;
All powerful as the wind he came,
As viewless too.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He came, sweet influence to impart,
A gracious, willing guest,
While he can find one humble heart
Wherein to rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And his that gentle voice we hear,
Soft as the breeze of even,
That checks each fault, that calms each fear,

title: We ask for peace, O Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We ask for peace, O Lord!
Thy children ask thy peace;
Not what the world calls rest,
That toil and care should cease,
That through bright sunny hours
Calm life should fleet away,
And tranquil night should fade
In smiling day—
It is not for such peace that we would pray.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We ask for peace, O Lord!
Yet not to stand secure,
Girt round with iron pride,
Contented to endure:
Crushing the gentle strings,
That human hearts should know,
Untouched by others’ joys
Or others’ woe;
Thou, O dear Lord, wilt never teach us so.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We ask thy peace, O Lord!
Through storm, and fear, and strife,
To light and guide us on,
Through a long struggling life:
While no success or gain
Shall cheer the desperate fight,
Or nerve, what the world calls,
Our wasted might:
Yet pressing through the darkness to the light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
It is thine own, O Lord!
Who toil while others sleep,
Who sow with loving care
What other hands shall reap:
They lean on thee entranced
In calm and perfect rest:
Give us that peace, O Lord!
Divine and blest,
Thou keepest for those hearts who love thee best.

title: O Thou that hearest prayer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Thou that hearest prayer,
Attend our humble cry,
And let thy servants share
Thy blessings from on high:
We plead the promise of thy word;
Grant us thy Holy Spirit, Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If earthly parents hear
Their children when they cry—
If they, with love sincere,
Their varied wants supply—
Much more wilt thou thy love display,
And answer when thy children pray.

title: Let others boast their ancient line
author: THE HOPE OF ETERNAL LIFE

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let others boast their ancient line,
In long succession great;
In the proud list let heroes shine,
And monarchs swell the state,
Descended from the King of kings,
Each saint a nobler title sings.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Pronounce me, gracious God, thy son,
Own me an heir divine;
I’ll pity princes on the throne,
When I can call thee mine:
Scepters and crowns unenvied rise,
And lose their luster in my eyes.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Content, obscure, I pass my days,
To all I meet unknown,
And wait till thou thy child shalt raise,
And seat me near thy throne:
No name, no honors here I crave,
Well pleased with those beyond the grave.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
When he, in robes divinely bright,
Shall once again appear,
Thou, too, my soul, shalt shine in light,
And his full image bear:
Enough!—I wait th’ appointed day—
Blessed Saviour, haste, and come away!

title: How vain is all beneath the skies
author: Though passing through a vale of tears

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How vain is all beneath the skies!
How transient every earthly bliss!
How slender all the fondest ties
That bind us to a world like this!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The evening cloud, the morning dew,
The withering grass, the fading flower,
Of earthly hopes are emblems true,
The glory of a passing hour.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But though earth’s fairest blossoms die,
And all beneath the skies is vain,
There is a brighter world on high,
Beyond the reach of care and pain.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Stand up, my soul, shake off thy fears
author: Join in my glorious Leader’s praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Stand up, my soul, shake off thy fears,
And gird the gospel armor on;
March to the gates of endless joy,
Where Jesus, the great Captain’s gone.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Then let my soul march boldly on,
Press forward to the heavenly gate;
There peace and joy eternal reign,
And glittering robes for conquerors wait.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There shall I wear a starry crown,
And triumph in almighty grace,
While all the armies of the skies

title: There is a land of pure delight
author: Should fright us from the shore

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a land of pure delight,
Where saints immortal reign,
Infinite day excludes the night,
And pleasures banish pain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There everlasting spring abides,
And never withering flowers;
Death, like a narrow sea, divides
This heavenly land from ours.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sweet fields, beyond the swelling flood,
Stand dressed in living green;
So to the Jews old Canaan stood,
While Jordan rolled between.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But timorous mortals start and shrink
To cross this narrow sea,
And linger, shivering on the brink,
And fear to launch away.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O! could we make our doubts remove,
Those gloomy doubts that rise,
And see the Canaan that we love,
With unbeclouded eyes;

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Far from these narrow scenes of night
author: Spreads everlasting day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Far from these narrow scenes of night,
Unbounded glories rise;
And realms of infinite delight,
Unknown to mortal eyes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Celestial land! could our weak eyes
But half thy charms explore,
How would our spirits long to rise;
And dwell on earth no more:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There pain and sickness never come,
And grief no place obtains;
Health triumphs in immortal bloom,
And endless pleasure reigns!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No cloud these blissful regions know,
For ever bright and fair!
For sin, the source of every woe,
Can never enter there.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Hail, sweetest, dearest tie, that binds
author: We all shall meet in heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hail, sweetest, dearest tie, that binds
Our glowing hearts in one;
Hail, sacred hope, that tunes our minds
To harmony divine.
It is the hope, the blissful hope,
Which Jesus’ grace has given—
The hope, when days and years are past,
We all shall meet in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What though the northern wintry blast
Shall howl around our cot;
What though beneath an eastern sun
Be cast our distant lot;
Yet still we share the blissful hope,
Which Jesus’ grace has given—
The hope, when days and years are past,
We all shall meet in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
From eastern shores, from northern lands,
From western hill and plain,
From southern climes, the brother-bands
May hope to meet again;
It is the hope, the blissful hope,
Which Jesus’ grace has given—
The hope, when life and time are o’er,
We all shall meet in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
From Burmah’s shores, from Afric’s strand,
From India’s burning plain,
From Europe, from Columbia’s land,
We hope to meet again;
It is the hope, the blissful hope,
Which Jesus’ grace has given—
The hope, when days and years are past,
We all shall meet in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
No lingering look, nor parting sigh,
Our future meeting knows;
There friendship beams from every eye,
And love immortal glows.
O sacred hope! O blissful hope!
Which Jesus’ grace has given—
The hope, when days and years are past

title: On Jordan’s stormy banks I stand
author: Fearless I’d launch away

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
On Jordan’s stormy banks I stand,
And cast a wishful eye
To Canaan’s fair and happy land,
Where my possessions lie.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O the transporting, rapturous scene,
That rises to my sight!
Sweet fields arrayed in living green,
And rivers of delight!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There generous fruits that never fail
On trees immortal grow;
There rocks and hills, and brooks and vales,
With milk and honey flow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
All o’er these wide, extended plains,
Shines one eternal day;
There God, the Son, for ever reigns,
And scatters night away.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
No chilling winds nor poisonous breath
Can reach that healthful shore;
Sickness and sorrow, pain and death,
Are felt and feared no more.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
When shall I reach that happy place,
And be for ever blest!
When shall I see my Father’s face,
And in his bosom rest!

sections.label: Verse 7

title: When musing sorrow weeps the past
author: My Saviour’s bliss to share

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When musing sorrow weeps the past,
And mourns the present pain,
’Tis sweet to think of peace at last,
And feel that death is gain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
’Tis not that murmuring thoughts arise,
And dread a Father’s will;
’Tis not that meek submission flies,
And would not suffer still.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It is that heaven-born faith surveys
The path that leads to light,
And longs her eagle plumes to raise,
And lose herself in sight.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
It is that troubled conscience feels
The pangs of struggling sin,
And sees, though far, the hand that heals,
And ends the strife within.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O, let me wing my hallowed flight
From earth-born woe and care,
And soar above these clouds of night,

title: O there’s a better world on high
author: But there ’tis heaven to be

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Anguish may rend each vital part;
Poor man, thy strength how frail!
Yet heaven’s own strength shall shield thy heart,
When flesh and heart shall fail.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy God—and with the tenderest hand—
Shall guard the traveler through;
“Hail!” shalt thou cry: “hail! promised land!
And, wilderness, adieu!”

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Since I can read my title clear
author: Across my peaceful breast

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Since I can read my title clear
To mansions in the skies,
I bid farewell to every fear,
And wipe my weeping eyes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Should earth against my soul engage,
And fiery darts be hurled,
Then I would smile at Satan’s rage,
And face a frowning world.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let cares, like a wild deluge, come,
And storms of sorrow fall,
May I but safely reach my home,
My God, my heaven, my all.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: When reft of all, and hopeless care
author: His power alone can heal

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When reft of all, and hopeless care
Would sink us to the tomb,
What power shall save us from despair,
What dissipate the gloom?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No balm that earthly plants distill
Can soothe the mourner’s smart,
No mortal hand, with lenient skill,
Bind up the broken heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But One alone, who reigns above,
Our woe to joy can turn,
And light the lamp of life and love,
That long has ceased to burn.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: My soul! triumphant in the Lord
author: To be removed no more

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My soul! triumphant in the Lord,
Proclaim thy joys abroad,
And march with holy vigor on,
Supported by thy God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Through every winding maze of life,
His hand has been my guide;
And in his long-experienced care,
My heart shall still confide.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His grace through all the desert flows,
An unexhausted stream;
That grace, on Zion’s sacred mount,
Shall be my endless theme.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Beyond the choicest joys of time,
Thy courts on earth I love;
But O! I burn with strong desire
To view thy house above.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: When for eternal worlds we steer
author: I’m safe at home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When for eternal worlds we steer,
And seas are calm, and skies are clear,
And faith, in lively exercise,
Sees distant fields of Canaan rise,
The soul for joy then spreads her wings,
And loud her lovely sonnet sings,
Vain world, adieu.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With cheerful hope, her eyes explore
Each land-mark on the distant shore,
The trees of life, the pastures green,
The golden streets, the crystal stream;
Again for joy she spreads her wings,
And loud her lovely sonnet sings,
I’m going home.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: The world may change from old to new
author: To cheer us on our way

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The world may change from old to new,
From new to old again;
Yet hope and heaven, for ever true,
Within our hearts remain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hope leads the child to plant the flower,
The man to sow the seed;
Nor leaves fulfillment to her hour—
But prompts again to deed.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And ere upon the old man’s dust
The grass is seen to wave,
We look through falling tears, to trust
Hope’s sunshine on the grave.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O, no, it is no flattering lure,
No fancy weak or fond,
When hope would bid us rest secure
In better life beyond.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: If life’s pleasures charm you, give them not your heart
author: The Rock of your Salvation

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Let not death alarm you, shrink not from his blow;
For your God shall arm you, and victory bestow,
For death shall bring to you no sting,
The grave no desolation:
’Tis sweet to die with Jesus nigh,

title: Now I have found a friend

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Though I grow poor and old,
Jesus is mine;
He will my faith uphold,
Jesus is mine;
He shall my wants supply,
His precious blood is nigh,
Nought can my hope destroy,
Jesus is mine!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When earth shall pass away,
Jesus is mine.
In the great Judgment day,
Jesus is mine.
O! what a glorious thing
Then to behold my King,
On tuneful harp to sing,
Jesus is mine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Farewell mortality!
Jesus is mine.
Welcome eternity!
Jesus is mine,
He my Redemption is,
Wisdom and Righteousness,
Life, Light and Holiness,
Jesus is mine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text: THE CHURCH—DIVINE CONSTITUTION.

title: Happy the church, thou sacred place

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy the church, thou sacred place,
The seat of thy Creator’s grace!
Thine holy courts are his abode,
Thou earthly palace of our God!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy walls are strength, and at thy gates
A guard of heavenly warriors waits;
Nor shall thy deep foundations move,
Fixed on his counsels and his love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy foes in vain designs engage;
Against his throne in vain they rage:
Like rising waves, with angry roar,
That dash and die upon the shore.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
God is our shield, and God our sun;
Swift as the fleeting moments run,
On us he sheds new beams of grace,
And we reflect his brightest praise.

title: God is the refuge of his saints

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God is the refuge of his saints,
When storms of sharp distress invade;
Ere we can offer our complaints,
Behold him present with his aid.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Zion enjoys her monarch’s love,
Secure against a threatening hour;
Nor can her firm foundations move,
Built on his truth, and armed with power.

title: Thy kingdom, Lord, for ever stands
author: In one eternal song

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy kingdom, Lord, for ever stands,
While earthly thrones decay;
And time submits to thy commands,
While ages roll away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy sovereign bounty freely gives
Its unexhausted store;
And universal nature lives
On thy sustaining power.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Holy and just in all thy ways,
Thy providence divine;
In all thy works, immortal rays
Of power and mercy shine.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Behold the sure foundation-stone
author: And wondrous in our eyes

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold the sure foundation-stone,
Which God in Zion lays,
To build our heavenly hopes upon,
And his eternal praise!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Chosen of God, to sinners dear,
And saints adore the name;
They trust their whole salvation here,
Nor shall they suffer shame.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The foolish builders, scribe, and priest,
Reject it with disdain;
Yet on this rock the church shall rest,
And envy rage in vain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
What though the gates of hell withstood,
Yet must this building rise:
’Tis thy own work, almighty God,

title: How did my heart rejoice to hear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How did my heart rejoice to hear
My friends devoutly say,
“In Zion let us all appear,
And keep the solemn day.”

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love her gates, I love the road:
The church, adorned with grace,
Stands like a palace, built for God,
To show his milder face.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Up to her courts, with joys unknown,
The holy tribes repair;
The Son of David holds his throne,
And sits in judgment there.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He hears our praises and complaints;
And while his awful voice
Divides the sinners from the saints,
We tremble and rejoice.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Peace be within this sacred place,
And joy a constant guest!
With holy gifts and heavenly grace,
Be her attendants blest!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
My soul shall pray for Zion still,
While life or breath remains;
There my best friends, my kindred, dwell,
There God, my Saviour reigns.

title: A mother may forgetful be
author: Dwell in thy Saviour’s breast

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A mother may forgetful be,
For human love is frail;
But thy Creator’s love to thee,
O Zion! can not fail.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No! thy dear name engraven stands,
In characters of love,
On thy almighty Father’s hands,
And never shall remove.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Before his ever watchful eye
Thy mournful state appears;
And every groan, and every sigh,
Divine compassion hears.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: The Lord of glory is my light
author: Within thy temple sound

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord of glory is my light,
And my salvation too;
God is my strength, nor will I fear
What all my foes can do.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
One blessing, Lord, my heart desires;
O, grant me my abode
Among the churches of thy saints,
The temples of my God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There shall I offer my requests,
And see thy glory still;
Shall hear thy messages of love,
And learn thy holy will.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When troubles rise, and storms appear,
There may his children hide;
God has a strong pavilion, where
He makes my soul abide.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Now shall my head be lifted high
Above my foes around,
And songs of joy and victory

title: There is a little, lonely fold

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a little, lonely fold,
Whose flock one Shepherd keeps,
Through summer’s heat and winter’s cold,
With eye that never sleeps.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
By evil beast, or burning sky,
Or damp of midnight air,
Not one in all that flock shall die
Beneath that Shepherd’s care.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For if, unheeding or beguiled,
In danger’s path they roam,
His pity follows through the wild,
And guards them safely home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O, gentle Shepherd, still behold
Thy helpless charge in me;
And take a wanderer to thy fold,
That, trembling, turns to thee.

title: Not to the terrors of the Lord
author: Must be for ever blessed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Not to the terrors of the Lord,
The tempest, fire, and smoke—
Not to the thunder of that word
Which God on Sinai spoke;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But we are come to Zion hill,
The city of our God,
Where milder words declare his will,
And spread his love abroad.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Behold the great, the glorious host
Of angels clothed in light!
Behold the spirits of the just,
Whose faith is turned to sight!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Behold the blest assembly there,
Whose names are writ in heaven!
And God, the Judge, who doth declare
Their vilest sins forgiven!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Saints here, and those in Jesus dead,
But one communion make;
All join in Christ, their living head,
And of his grace partake.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Our Christ hath reached his heavenly seat

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our Christ hath reached his heavenly seat,
Through sorrows and through scars;
