The golden lamps are at his feet,
And in his hand the stars.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O God of life, and truth, and grace,
Ere nature was begun!
Make welcome to our erring race
Thy Spirit and thy Son.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We hail the Church, built high o’er all
The heathens’ rage and scoff;
Thy providence its fenced wall,
“The Lamb the light thereof.”

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O, may he walk among us here,
With his rebuke and love—
A brightness o’er this lower sphere,
A ray from worlds above!

title: O where are kings and empires now
author: A fane unbuilt by hands

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O where are kings and empires now,
Of old that went and came?
But holy Church is praying yet,
A thousand years the same.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Mark ye her holy battlements,
And her foundations strong:
And hear within, the solemn voice,
And her unending song.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For not like kingdoms of the world,
The Holy Church of God!
Though earthquake shocks are rocking her,
And tempests are abroad;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Unshaken as eternal hills,
Unmovable she stands—
A mountain that shall fill the earth,

title: Great is the Lord our God
author: And seek deliverance there

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great is the Lord our God,
And let his praise be great;
He makes his churches his abode,
His most delightful seat.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
These temples of his grace,
How beautiful they stand!
The honors of our native place,
And bulwarks of our land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In Zion God is known,
A refuge in distress;
How bright has his salvation shone,
Through all her palaces!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When kings against her joined,
And saw the Lord was there,
In wild confusion of the mind,
They fled with hasty fear.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oft have our fathers told,
Our eyes have often seen,
How well our God secures the fold
Where his own sheep have been.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: I Love thy kingdom, Lord
author: And brighter bliss of heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I Love thy kingdom, Lord—
The house of thine abode,
The church our blest Redeemer saved
With his own precious blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love thy Church, O God!
Her walls before thee stand,
Dear as the apple of thine eye,
And graven on thy hand.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For her my tears shall fall,
For her my prayers ascend;
To her my cares and toils be given,
Till toils and cares shall end.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Beyond my highest joy
I prize her heavenly ways,
Her sweet communion, solemn vows,
Her hymns of love and praise.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus, thou Friend divine,
Our Saviour and our King,
Thy hand from every snare and foe
Shall great deliverance bring.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Sure as thy truth shall last,
To Zion shall be given
The brightest glories earth can yield,

title: How charming is the place
author: The servants of my God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How charming is the place
Where my Redeemer God
Unvails the beauties of his face,
And sheds his love abroad!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not the fair palaces
To which the great resort,
Are once to be compared with this,
Where Jesus holds his court.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here on the mercy-seat,
With radiant glory crowned,
Our joyful eyes behold him sit,
And smile on all around.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To him their prayers and cries
Each humble soul presents;
He listens to their broken sighs,
And grants them all their wants.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Give me, O Lord, a place
Within thy blessed abode,
Among the children of thy grace,

title: Thy kingdom, gracious Lord
author: And fill our hearts with peace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy kingdom, gracious Lord,
Shall never pass away;
Firm as thy truth it still shall stand,
When earthly thrones decay.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy people here have found,
Through many weary years,
The sweet communion, joy and peace,
To banish all their fears.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Like Noah’s weary dove
author: Then rest on Zion’s hill

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Like Noah’s weary dove,
That soared the earth around,
But not a resting-place above
The cheerless waters found;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O cease, my wandering soul,
On restless wing to roam;
All the wide world, to either pole,
Has not for thee a home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Behold the ark of God,
Behold the open door;
Hasten to gain that dear abode,
And rove, my soul, no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There safe thou shalt abide,
There sweet shall be thy rest,
And every longing satisfied,
With full salvation blest.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: How honored is the place
author: Eternal as his years

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How honored is the place,
Where we adoring stand!
Zion, the glory of the earth,
And beauty of the land.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Bulwarks of grace defend
The city where we dwell;
While walls of strong salvation made,
Defy th’ assaults of hell.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lift up th’ eternal gates,
The doors wide open fling;
Enter, ye nations, that obey
The statutes of our King.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here taste unmingled joys,
And live in perfect peace;
You that have known Jehovah’s name,
And ventured on his grace.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Far as thy name is known
author: And ours above the sky

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Far as thy name is known
The world declares thy praise;
The saints, O Lord, before thy throne
Their songs of honor raise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With joy, thy people stand
On Zion’s chosen hill,
Proclaim the wonders of thy hand,
And counsels of thy will.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let strangers walk around
The city where we dwell,
Compass and view thy holy ground,
And mark the building well.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
How comely and how wise!
How glorious to behold!
Beyond the pomp that charms the eyes,
And rites adorned with gold.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Far down the ages now
author: The kingdom in our view

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Far down the ages now,
Much of her journey done,
The pilgrim church pursues her way,
Until her crown be won.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The story of the past
Comes up before her view:
How well it seems to suit her still—
Old, and yet ever new!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It is the oft-told tale
Of sin and weariness—
Of grace and love yet flowing down
To pardon and to bless.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No wider is the gate,
No broader is the way,
No smoother is the ancient path,
That leads to life and day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
No sweeter is the cup,
Nor less our lot of ill:
’Twas tribulation ages since,
’Tis tribulation still.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
No slacker grows the fight,
No feebler is the foe,
Nor less the need of armor tried,
Of shield, and spear, and bow.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Thus onward still we press,
Through evil and through good—
Through pain, and poverty, and want,
Through peril and through blood.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Still faithful to our God,
And to our Captain true,
We follow where he leads the way,

title: Glorious things of thee are spoken
author: None but Zion’s children know

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glorious things of thee are spoken,
Zion, city of our God!
He, whose word can not be broken,
Formed thee for his own abode:
On the Rock of ages founded,
What can shake thy sure repose?
With salvation’s wall surrounded,
Thou mayst smile at all thy foes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See the streams of living waters,
Springing from Eternal Love,
Well supply thy sons and daughters,
And all fear of drought remove:
Who can faint while such a river
Ever flows their thirst t’ assuage!
Grace, which like the Lord, the giver,
Never fails from age to age.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Round each habitation hovering,
See the cloud and fire appear,
For a glory and a covering,
Showing that the Lord is near:
Thus deriving from their banner
Light by night, and shade by day,
Safe they feed upon the manna
Which he gives them when they pray.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest inhabitants of Zion,
Washed in the Redeemer’s blood,
Jesus, whom their souls rely on,
Makes them kings and priests to God:
’Tis his love his people raises
With himself to reign as kings;
And, as priests, his solemn praises
Each for a thank-offering brings.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Saviour, since of Zion’s city,
I through grace a member am,
Let the world deride or pity,
I will glory in thy name:
Fading is the worldling’s treasure,
All his boasted pomp and show!
Solid joys and lasting pleasure

title: Restore, O Father! to our times restore

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Restore, O Father! to our times restore
The peace which filled thine infant Church of yore,
Ere lust of power had sown the seeds of strife,
And quenched the new-born charities of life.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, never more may different judgments part
From kindled sympathy a brother’s heart!
But, linked in one, believing thousands kneel,
And share with each the sacred joy they feel.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
From soul to soul, quick as the sunbeam’s ray,
Let concord spread one universal day;
And faith by love lead all mankind to thee,
Parent of peace, and Fount of harmony!

title: See, from Zion’s sacred mountain
author: Sings for joy where’er it flows

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Through ten thousand channels flowing,
Streams of mercy find their way:
Life, and health, and joy bestowing,
Waking beauty from decay.
O, ye nations,
Hail the long-expected day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Gladdened by the flowing treasure,
All-enriching as it goes,
Lo! the desert smiles with pleasure,
Buds and blossoms as the rose;
Lo! the desert

title: You may sing of the beauty of mountain and dale

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
You may sing of the beauty of mountain and dale,
Of the silvery streamlets and flowers of the vale;
But the place most delightful this earth can afford,
Is the place of devotion, the house of the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
You may boast of the sweetness of day’s early dawn,
Of the sky’s softening graces when day is just gone;
But there’s no other season or time can compare,
With the hour of devotion, the season of prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
You may value the friendships of youth and of age,
And select for your comrades the noble and sage;
But the friends that most cheer me on life’s rugged road,
Are the friends of my Master, the children of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
You may talk of your prospects, of fame, or of wealth,
And the hopes that oft flatter the favorites of health;
But the hope of bright glory, of heavenly bliss—
Take away every other, and give me but this.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ever hail, blessed temple, abode of my Lord!
I will turn to thee often, to hear from his word;
I will walk to thine altar with those that I love,
And rejoice in the prospects revealed from above.

title: Zion stands with hills surrounded
author: OFFICERS

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Zion stands with hills surrounded—
Zion kept by power divine;
All her foes shall be confounded,
Though the world in arms combine:
Happy Zion,
What a favored lot is thine.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
In the furnace God may prove thee,
Thence to bring thee forth more bright,
But can never cease to love thee;
Thou art precious in his sight:
God is with thee—
God, thine everlasting light.

title: Ye Christian heralds! go, proclaim

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye Christian heralds! go, proclaim
Salvation through Immanuel’s name;
To distant climes the tidings bear,
And plant the rose of Sharon there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He’ll shield you with a wall of a fire,
With holy zeal your hearts inspire,
Bid raging winds their fury cease,
And hush the tempest into peace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And when our labors all are o’er,
Then we shall meet to part no more—
Meet with the blood-bought throng, to fall,
And crown our Jesus—Lord of all!

title: Go—messenger of peace and love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Go—messenger of peace and love!
To nations plunged in shades of night;
Like angels sent from fields above,
Be thine to shed celestial light.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Go—to the hungry food impart;
To paths of peace the wanderer guide,
And lead the thirsty, panting heart,
Where streams of living water glide.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Go—bid the bright and morning-star
From Bethlehem’s plains resplendent shine,
And, piercing through the gloom afar,
Shed heavenly light and love divine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
From north to south, from east to west,
Messiah yet shall reign supreme;
His name by every tongue confessed—
His praise—the universal theme.

title: Father of mercies, bow thine ear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of mercies, bow thine ear,
Attentive to our earnest prayer:
We plead for those who plead for thee;
Successful pleaders may they be.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How great their work! how vast their charge!
Do thou their anxious souls enlarge:
Their best endowments are our gain;
We share the blessings they obtain.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Let thronging multitudes around,
Hear from their lips the joyful sound,
In humble strains thy grace implore,
And feel thy Spirit’s living power.

title: Vouchsafe, O Lord, thy presence now
author: With such thy people bless

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Vouchsafe, O Lord, thy presence now,
Direct us in thy fear;
Before thy throne we humbly bow,
And offer fervent prayer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Give us the men whom thou shalt choose,
Thy house on earth to guide;
Those who shall ne’er their power abuse,
Or rule with haughty pride.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
These are the men we seek of thee,
O God of righteousness:
Such may thy servants ever be,

title: With joy we own thy servant, Lord
author: The reign of truth and love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With joy we own thy servant, Lord,
Thy minister below,
Ordained to spread thy truth abroad,
That all thy name may know.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O may he now, and ever, keep
His eye intent on thee:
Do thou, great Shepherd of the sheep,
His bright example be.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With plenteous grace his heart prepare
To execute thy will;
And give him patience, love, and care,
And faithfulness and skill.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Inflame his mind with ardent zeal,
Thy flock to feed and teach;
And let him live, and let him feel,
The truths he’s called to preach.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
As showers refresh the thirsty plain,
So let his labors prove:
By him extend thy righteous reign—

title: You messengers of Christ
author: Will your endeavors bless

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
You messengers of Christ,
His sovereign voice obey;
Arise and follow where he leads—
And peace attend your way.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The master whom you serve
Will needful strength bestow;
Depending on his promised aid,
With sacred courage go.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Mountains shall sink to plains,
And hell in vain oppose;
The cause is God’s, and must prevail
In spite of all his foes.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Go, spread a Saviour’s fame,
And tell his matchless grace,
To the most guilty and depraved
Of Adam’s numerous race.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Go with thy servant, Lord
author: O may we meet above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Go with thy servant, Lord,
His every step attend;
All needful help to him afford,
And bless him to the end.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Preserve him from all wrong;
Stand thou at his right hand:
And keep him from the slanderous tongue
And persecuting band.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
May he proclaim aloud
The wonders of thy grace;
And do thou, to the listening crowd,
His faithful labors bless.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Ye servants of the Lord
author: And be with honor crowned

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye servants of the Lord,
Each in his office wait;
With joy obey his heavenly word,
And watch before his gate.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
O happy servant he,
In such a posture found!
He shall his Lord with rapture see,

title: Lord of the harvest! hear
author: That thou hast died for all

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Convert and send forth more
Into thy Church abroad;
And let them speak thy word of power,
As workers with their God.
Give the pure gospel-word,
The word of general grace;
Thee let them preach, the common Lord,
The Saviour of our race.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, let them spread thy name;
Their mission fully prove;
Thy universal grace proclaim,
Thy all-redeeming love.
On all mankind, forgiven,
Empower them still to call,
And tell each creature under heaven,

title: You servants of God
author: For infinite love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
You servants of God,
Your Master proclaim,
And publish abroad
His wonderful name:
The name all victorious
Of Jesus extol;
His kingdom is glorious,
And rules over all.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Christ ruleth on high,
Almighty to save:
And still he is nigh—
His presence we have:
The great congregation
His triumph shall sing,
Ascribing salvation
To Jesus our King.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Salvation to him,
Who sits on the throne—
Let all cry aloud,
And honor the Son;
Our Saviour’s praises
The angels proclaim,
They fall on their faces
And worship the Lamb.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Him let us adore,
And give him his right;
All glory and power,
And wisdom and might;
All honor and blessing
With angels above,
And thanks never ceasing,

title: Son of God, our glorious Head

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Son of God, our glorious Head!
On us now thy blessing shed;
From thy throne let mercy flow
To thy waiting flock below.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Taught by thee, with prayer sincere,
We have called thy servants here,
For thy needy ones to care,
And thy holy feast to bear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
May the Spirit from above
Fill their hearts with faith and love;
Make them humble, zealous, wise,
Strife to shun, and good devise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When their earthly work is done,
When the crown of life is won,
May they, with thy favor blest,
Pass from labor into rest.

title: Ho, reapers of life’s harvest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ho, reapers of life’s harvest,
Why stand with rusted blade,
Until the night draws round thee,
And day begins to fade?
Why stand ye idle, waiting
For reapers more to come?
The golden morn is passing,
Why sit ye idle, dumb?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thrust in your sharpened sickle,
And gather in the grain:
The night is fast approaching,
And soon will come again.
Thy Master calls for reapers;
And shall he call in vain?
Shall sheaves lie there ungathered,
And waste upon the plain?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come down from hill and mountain,
In morning’s ruddy glow,
Nor wait until the dial
Points to the noon below;
And come with the strong sinew,
Nor faint in heat or cold;
And pause not till the evening
Draws round its wealth of gold.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text: LOVE, UNITY AND FELLOWSHIP.

title: Kindred in Christ, for his dear sake
author: When we shall meet to part no more

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Kindred in Christ, for his dear sake
A hearty welcome here receive;
May we together now partake
The joys which only he can give.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
May he, by whose kind care we meet,
Send his good spirit from above;
Make our communications sweet,
And cause our hearts to burn with love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Forgotten be each worldly theme,
When Christians meet together thus;
We only wish to speak of him
Who lived, and died, and reigns for us.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We’ll talk of all he did, and said,
And suffered for us here below;
The path he marked for us to tread,
And what he’s doing for us now.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Come in, thou blesséd of our God
author: Around the throne of God above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come in, thou blesséd of our God,
In Jesus’ name we bid thee come;
No more thy feet shall roam abroad,
Henceforth a brother—welcome home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Those joys which earth can not afford,
We’ll seek in fellowship to prove,
Joined in one spirit to our Lord,
Together bound by mutual love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And while we pass this vale of tears
We’ll make our joys and sorrows known;
We’ll share each other’s hopes and fears,
And count a brother’s cares our own.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: How blest the sacred tie that binds

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How blest the sacred tie that binds,
In sweet communion, kindred minds!
How swift the heavenly course they run,
Whose hearts, whose faith, whose hopes are one!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To each the soul of each how dear!
What tender love, what holy fear!
How doth the generous flame within
Refine from earth, and cleanse from sin!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Their streaming eyes together flow
For human guilt and mortal woe;
Their ardent prayers together rise
Like mingling flames in sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Nor shall the glowing flame expire,
When dimly burns frail nature’s fire;
Then shall they meet in realms above,
A heaven of joy, a heaven of love.

title: Had I the tongues of Greeks and Jews

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Had I the tongues of Greeks and Jews,
And nobler speech than angels use,
If love be absent, I am found,
Like tinkling brass, an empty sound.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Were I inspired to preach and tell
All that is done in heaven and hell—
Or could my faith the world remove—
Still I am nothing without love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Should I distribute all my store
To feed the hungry, clothe the poor—
Or give my body to the flame,
To gain a martyr’s glorious name—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
If love to God and love to men
Be absent, all my hopes are vain;
Nor tongues, nor gifts, nor fiery zeal,
The work of love can e’er fulfill.

title: Come, you that love the Lord indeed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, you that love the Lord indeed,
Who are from sin and bondage freed,
Submit to all the ways of God,
And walk the narrow, happy road.
CHORUS.
We’re all united heart and hand,
Joined in one band completely;
We’re marching through Immanuel’s land,
Where waters flow most sweetly.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Great tribulation you shall meet,
But soon shall walk the golden street;
Though hell may rage and vent its spite,
Yet Christ will save his heart’s delight.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
That happy day will soon appear
When Michael’s trumpet you shall hear
Sound through the earth—yea, down to hell,
And call the nations, great and small.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Behold the righteous marching home,
And all the angels bid them come,
While Christ the Judge these words proclaims,
“Here come my saints—I own their names!”

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
“You everlasting gates, fly wide,
Make ready to receive my bride;
You harps of heaven, now sound aloud,
Here come the ransomed by my blood!”

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
In grandeur see the royal line,
In glittering robes the sun outshine!
See saints and angels join in one,
And march in splendor to the throne.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
They stand, and wonder, and look on:
They join in one eternal song,
Their great Redeemer to admire,
While rapture sets their souls on fire.

title: Jesus, thou Shepherd of the sheep

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thou Shepherd of the sheep,
Thy little flock in safety keep;
These lambs within thine arms now take,
Nor let them e’er thy fold forsake.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Secure them from the scorching beam,
And lead them to the living stream;
In verdant pastures let them lie,
And watch them with a shepherd’s eye!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, teach them to discern thy voice,
And in its sacred sound rejoice!
From strangers may they ever flee,
And know no other guide but thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord, bring thy sheep that wander yet,
And let their number be complete;
Then let the flock from earth remove,
And reach the heavenly fold above.

title: Lord, bless thy saints assembled here
author: And fruits of thy blessed Spirit grow

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, bless thy saints assembled here,
In solemn covenant now to join;
Unite them in thy holy fear,
And in thy love their hearts combine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O give this church a large increase
Of such as thou wilt own and bless;
Lord, fill their hearts with joy and peace,
And clothe them with thy righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Still one in life and one in death
author: But soon we’ll meet to part no more

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Still one in life and one in death,
One in our hope of rest above;
One in our joy, our trust, our faith,
One in each other’s faithful love,

sections.label: Verse 2

title: My Christian friends in bonds of love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Christian friends in bonds of love,
Whose hearts the sweetest union prove;
Your friendship’s like the strongest band,
Yet we must take the parting hand.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Your presence sweet, our union dear,
What joys we feel together here!
And when I see that we must part,
You draw like chords around my heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How sweet the hours have passed away,
Since we have met to sing and pray;
How loath are we to leave the place
Where Jesus shows his smiling face!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O could I stay with friends so kind,
How would it cheer my fainting mind!
But pilgrims in a foreign land,
We oft must take the parting hand.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
My Christian friends, both old and young,
I trust you will in Christ go on;
Press on, and soon you’ll win the prize—
A crown of glory in the skies.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
A few more days, or years at most,
And we shall reach fair Canaan’s coast:
When, in that holy, happy land,
We’ll take no more the parting hand.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O blesséd day! O glorious hope!
My soul rejoices at the thought,
When, in that holy, happy land,
We’ll take no more the parting hand.

title: Go on, you pilgrims, while below
author: To sing redeeming grace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Go on, you pilgrims, while below,
In the sure path of peace,
Determined nothing else to know
But Jesus and his grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Observe your leader, follow him;
He through this world has been
Often reviled; but like a lamb
Did ne’er revile again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O! take the pattern he has given,
And love your enemies;
And learn the only way to heaven
Through self-denial lies.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Remember, you must watch and pray
While journeying on the road,
Lest you should fall out by the way,
And wound the cause of God.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Go on rejoicing night and day;
Your crown is yet before,
Defy the trials of the way,
The storm will soon be o’er.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Soon we shall reach the promised land,
With all the ransomed race,
And join with all the glorious band,

title: Planted in Christ, the living vine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Planted in Christ, the living vine,
This day, with one accord,
Ourselves, with humble faith and joy,
We yield to thee, O Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
In prayer, in effort, tears, and toils,
One wisdom be our guide;
Taught by one Spirit from above,
In thee may we abide.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Around this feeble, trusting band,
Thy sheltering pinions spread,
Nor let the storms of trial beat
Too fiercely on our head.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then, when, among the saints in light,
Our joyful spirits shine,
Shall anthems of immortal praise,
O Lamb of God, be thine.

title: Blessed be the dear uniting love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blessed be the dear uniting love,
That will not let us part;
Our bodies may far off remove—
We still are one in heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Joined in one Spirit to our Head,
Where he appoints, we go;
And still in Jesus’ footsteps tread,
And show his praise below.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Partakers of the Saviour’s grace,
The same in mind and heart;
Nor joy, nor grief, nor time, nor place,
Nor life, nor death, can part.

title: Ye men and angels, witness now
author: Turn thou our prayers to praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye men and angels, witness now—
Before the Lord we speak,
To him we make our solemn vow—
A vow we dare not break:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That, long as life itself shall last,
Ourselves to Christ we yield;
Nor from his cause will we depart,
Or ever quit the field.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We trust not in our native strength,
But on his grace rely;
May he, with our returning wants,
All needful aid supply.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Think gently of the erring one
author: As God hath dealt with thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Think gently of the erring one!
O, let us not forget,
However darkly stained by sin,
He is our brother yet.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Heir of the same inheritance,
Child of the self-same God,
He hath but stumbled in the path
We have in weakness trod.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Speak gently to the erring ones!
We yet may lead them back,
With holy words and tones of love,
From misery’s thorny track.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Happy the souls to Jesus joined
author: Shall meet thee in the skies

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy the souls to Jesus joined,
And made in spirit one:
Walking in all his ways, they find
Their heaven on earth begun.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The church triumphant in thy love,
Their mighty joys we know;
They sing the Lamb in hymns above,
And we in hymns below.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: O happy they who know the Lord
author: To worship thee above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O happy they who know the Lord,
With whom he deigns to dwell!
He feeds and cheers them by his word,
His arm supports them well.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To them, in each distressing hour,
His throne of grace is near;
And when they plead his love and power,
He stands engaged to hear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His presence sweetens all our cares,
And makes our burdens light;
A word from him dispels our fears,
And gilds the gloom of night.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord, we expect to suffer here,
Nor would we dare repine;
But give us still to find thee near,
And own us still for thine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Let us enjoy and highly prize
These tokens of thy love,
Till thou shalt bid our spirits rise

title: How sweet, how heavenly is the sight
author: His bosom glow with love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sweet, how heavenly is the sight,
When those that love the Lord,
In one another’s peace delight,
And so fulfill the word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When each can feel his brother’s sigh,
And with him bear a part;
When sorrow flows from eye to eye,
And joy from heart to heart:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When free from envy, scorn, and pride,
Our wishes all above,
Each can his brother’s failing hide,
And show a brother’s love:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When love in one delightful stream
Through every bosom flows,
When union sweet and dear esteem
In every action glows.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Love is the golden chain that binds,
The happy souls above,
And he’s an heir of heaven that finds

title: Come, let us join our friends above
author: And land us safe in heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, let us join our friends above,
Who have obtained the prize,
And on the eagle wings of love,
To joy celestial rise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let saints below in concert sing
With those to glory gone;
For all the servants of our King,
In heaven and earth are one:

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
One army of the living God,
To his command we bow;
Part of the host have crossed the flood,
And part are crossing now.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Even now to their eternal home
Some happy spirits fly;
And we are to the margin come,
Expecting soon to die!

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Blest be the tie that binds
author: Through all eternity

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest be the tie that binds
Our hearts in Christian love;
The fellowship of kindred minds
Is like to that above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Before our Father’s throne
We pour our ardent prayers;
Our fears, our hopes, our aims, are one,
Our comforts and our cares.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We share our mutual woes,
Our mutual burdens bear;
And often for each other flows
The sympathizing tear.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though often called to part,
Amid these scenes of pain;
Yet, we shall still be joined in heart,
And hope to meet again.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
This glorious hope revives
Our courage by the way;
While each in expectation lives,
And longs to see the day.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: All you that have confessed
author: You’ll reign with him above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All you that have confessed
That Jesus is the Lord,
And to his people joined yourselves,
According to his word:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In Zion you must dwell,
Her altar ne’er forsake;
Must come to all her solemn feasts,
Of all her joys partake.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
She must employ your thoughts,
And your unceasing care;
Her welfare be your constant wish,
And her increase your prayer.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
With humbleness of mind,
Among her sons rejoice;
A meek and quiet spirit is
With God of highest price.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Never offend, nor grieve
Your brethren by the way;
But shun the dark abodes of strife,
Like children of the day.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Let party names no more
author: And every heart is love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let party names no more
The Christian world o’erspread,
Gentile and Jew, and bond and free,
Are one in Christ, their Head.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Among the saints on earth
Let mutual love be found;
Heirs of the same inheritance,
With mutual blessings crowned.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thus will the church below
Resemble that above,
Where streams of pleasure ever flow,

title: Children of the heavenly King

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Children of the heavenly King,
As ye journey, sweetly sing;
Sing your Saviour’s worthy praise,
Glorious in his works and ways.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ye are traveling home to God,
In the way the fathers trod:
They are happy now—and ye
Soon there happiness shall see.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Shout, ye little flock, and blest;
You on Jesus’ throne shall rest:
There your seat is now prepared—
There your kingdom and reward.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fear not, brethren, joyful stand
On the borders of your land;
Jesus Christ, your Father’s Son,
Bids you undismayed go on.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord, submissive make us go,
Gladly leaving all below;
Only thou our leader be,
And we still will follow thee.

title: Jesus, Lord, we look to thee

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
By thy reconciling love,
Every stumbling-block remove:
Each to each unite, endear;
Come, and spread thy banner here.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Make us of one heart and mind—
Courteous, pitiful and kind;
Lowly, meek, in thought and word—
Altogether like our Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Free from anger and from pride,
Let us thus in God abide;
All the depths of love express—
All the hights of holiness.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Say, whence does this union arise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Say, whence does this union arise,
Where hatred is conquered by love?
It fastens our souls with such ties,
That distance nor time can remove.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It can not in Eden be found,
Nor yet in a Paradise lost;
It grows on Immanuel’s ground,
And Jesus’ life’s blood it has cost.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My friends so endeared unto me,
Our souls so united in love;
Where Jesus is gone we shall be,
In yonder blest mansions above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Why then so unwilling to part,
Since there we shall soon meet again;
Engraved on Immanuel’s heart,
At distance we can not remain.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And then we shall see that bright day,
And join with the angels above,
Set free from our prisons of clay,
United in Jesus’ kind love.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
With Jesus we ever shall reign,
And all his bright glory shall see;
Then sing hallelujahs—Amen!
Amen! Even so let it be!

title: Come, dear friends, we all are brethren

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, dear friends, we all are brethren,
Bound for Canaan’s happy land;
Come, unite and walk together,
Christ, our Leader, gives command.
Cease to boast of party merit,
Wound the cause of God no more,
Be united by his spirit;
Zion’s peace again restore.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now our hand, our heart and spirit,
Here in fellowship we give;
Let us love and peace inherit,
Show the world how Christians live.
We’ll be one in Christ our Saviour,
Male and female, bond and free!
Christ is all in all for ever,
In him we shall blesséd be.

title: When shall we all meet again

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When shall we all meet again?
When shall we all meet again?
Oft shall glowing hope expire,
Oft shall wearied love retire,
Oft shall death and sorrow reign,
Ere we all shall meet again.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though in distant lands we sigh,
Parched beneath a hostile sky;
Though the deep between us rolls—
Friendship shall unite our souls:
And in fancy’s wide domain,
Oft shall we all meet again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When the dreams of life are fled,
And its wasted lamp is dead:
When in cold oblivion’s shade,
Beauty, wealth, and fame are laid;
Where immortal spirits reign,
There may we all meet again.

title: We shall meet no more to part

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We shall meet no more to part;
Cease thy sorrows, mourning heart!
Weary days will soon depart—
Then we may rest for ever!
When the work of life is done,
When the victor’s crown is won,
Then, immortal life begun,
We no more shall sever.
We shall meet, no more to part;
Cease thy sorrows, mourning heart!
Weary days will soon depart—
Then we may rest for ever!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In the house of peace and bliss,
In the world where Jesus is,
When we bid adieu to this,
Then we may love for ever.
Purified from every stain,
Through the Lamb that once was slain,
Brethren, we shall meet again,
And be parted never!

title: When shall we meet again

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When shall we meet again?
Meet ne’er to sever?
When will Peace wreathe her chain
Round us for ever?
Our hearts will ne’er repose
Safe from each blast that blows
In this dark vail of woes,
Never—no, never!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When shall love freely flow,
Pure as life’s river?
When shall sweet friendship glow,
Changeless for ever?
Where joys celestial thrill,
Where bliss each heart shall fill,
And fears of parting chill,
Never—no, never!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Up to that world of light
Take us, dear Saviour;
May we all there unite,
Happy for ever:
Where kindred spirits dwell,
There may our music swell,
And time our joys dispel,
Never—no, never!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Soon shall we meet again,
Meet ne’er to sever:
Soon shall Peace wreathe her chain
Round us for ever:
Our hearts will then repose
Secure from worldly woes;
Our songs of praise shall close,
Never—no, never!

title: O love divine, how sweet thou art
author: My everlasting rest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O love divine, how sweet thou art!
When shall I find my wandering heart
All taken up in thee!
O may I daily live to prove
The sweetness of redeeming love,
The love of Christ to me.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O that I could for ever sit
With Mary at the Master’s feet!
Be this my happy choice;
My only care, delight, and bliss,
My joy, my heaven on earth, be this,
To hear the Bridegroom’s voice.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O that I might, with happy John,
Recline my weary head upon
The blessed Redeemer’s breast!
From care, and fear, and sorrow free,
Give me, O Lord, to find in thee

title: Peacefully, tenderly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Peacefully, tenderly,
Here, as we part,
The farewell that lingers
Be breathed from the heart:
No place more fitting,
O house of the Lord—
Here be it spoken,
That last prayerful word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thoughtfully, carefully,
Solemn and slow!
Tears are bedewing
The path that we go;
Perils before us
We know not to-day—
Kindly and safely,
O Lord, lead the way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Upwardly, steadfastly,
Gaze on that brow:
Jesus, our Leader,
Reigns conqueror now.
His steps let us follow,
His sufferings dare,
Go up to glory,
His blessedness share.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Patiently, cheerfully,
Up, and depart
To labor and duty
With gladness of heart;
The ransomed, with triumph,
To Zion we’ll bring,
Shouting salvation
To Jesus, our King.

title: Farewell, my friends, time rolls along

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Farewell, my friends, time rolls along,
Nor waits for mortal care or bliss;
I leave you here to travel on,
Till I arrive where Jesus is.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Farewell, farewell, farewell,
My Christian friends, farewell.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Farewell, my brethren in the Lord,
To you I’m bound in cords of love,
Yet we believe his gracious word,
That we ere long shall meet above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Farewell, old soldiers of the cross,
You’ve struggled long and hard for heaven,
You’ve counted all things here but dross,
Fight on, the crown will soon be given.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Farewell, poor careless sinners, too,
It grieves my soul to leave you here.
Eternal sorrow waits for you,
O turn, and find salvation near.

title: O happy children who follow Jesus

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O happy children who follow Jesus
Into the house of prayer and praise,
And join in union while love increases,
Resolved this way to spend our days:
Although we’re hated by the world and Satan,
By the flesh and such as love not God;
Yet happy moments and joyful seasons
We ofttimes find on Canaan’s road.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Since we’ve been waiting on lovely Jesus,
We’ve felt some strength come from above,
Our hearts have burned with holy rapture,
We long to be absorbed in love:
Let us sing praises for what is given,
And trust in God for time to come;
Sure we shall find the way to heaven;
So farewell, brethren—we’re going home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And as we go let us praise our Saviour,
And pray for those who spurn his grace,
Lest they should lose love’s richest treasure,
And ne’er enjoy his smiling face.
Now here’s my hand and my best wishes,
In token of my Christian love;
In hopes with you to praise my Jesus:
So farewell, brethren,—we’ll meet above.

title: Come on, my partners in distress

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come on, my partners in distress,
My comrades in the wilderness,
Who feel your sorrows still;
A while forget your griefs and fears
And look beyond this vale of tears
To that celestial hill.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Beyond the bounds of time and space,
Look forward to that heavenly place,
The saint’s secure abode;
On faith’s strong eagle pinions rise,
And force your passage to the skies,
And scale the mount of God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Who suffer with our Master here,
Shall there before his face appear,
And by his side sit down:
To patient faith the prize is sure;
And all that to the end endure
The cross, shall wear the crown.

title: ’Mid scenes of confusion and creature complaints

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
’Mid scenes of confusion and creature complaints,
How sweet to my soul is communion with saints;
To find at the banquet of mercy there’s room,
And feel in the presence of Jesus at home.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
While here in the valley of conflict I stray,
O give me submission and strength as my day;
In all my afflictions to thee would I come,
Rejoicing in hope of my glorious home.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: One baptism and one faith
author: THE LORD’S SUPPER

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
One baptism and one faith,
One Lord below, above,
The fellowship of Zion hath
One only watchword—Love.
From different temples though it rise,
One song ascendeth to the skies.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our sacrifice is One;
One priest before the throne—
The crucified, the risen Son,
Redeemer, Lord alone!
And sighs from contrite hearts that spring,
Our chief, our choicest offering.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O why should they who love
One gospel to unfold,
Who look for one bright home above,
On earth be strange and cold?
Why, subjects of the Prince of Peace,
In strife abide, and bitterness?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O may that holy prayer—
His tenderest and his last,
The utterance of his latest care
Ere to the cross he passed—
No longer unfulfilled remain,
The World’s offense, thy people’s stain!

title: When I survey the wondrous cross

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When I survey the wondrous cross,
On which the Prince of glory died,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Forbid it, Lord, that I should boast,
Save in the death of Christ, my Lord:
All the vain things that charm me most,
I sacrifice them to his blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See from his head, his hands, his feet,
Sorrow and love flow mingled down;
Did e’er such love and sorrow meet—
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Were the whole realm of nature mine,
That were a present far too small;
Love so amazing, so divine,
Demands my soul, my life, my all!

title: Jesus, thou Joy of loving hearts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, thou Joy of loving hearts!
Thou Fount of Life! thou Light of men!
From the best bliss that earth imparts,
We turn unfilled to thee again.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
We taste thee, O thou Living Bread,
And long to feed upon thee still;
We drink of thee, the Fountain Head,
And thirst our souls from thee to fill.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our restless spirits yearn for thee,
Where’er our changeful lot is cast;
Glad, when thy gracious smile we see,
Blest, when our faith can hold thee fast.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O Jesus, ever with us stay!
Make all our moments calm and bright,
Chase the dark night of sin away—
Shed o’er the world thy holy light!

title: Soft be the gently breathing notes
author: To him who bled upon the tree

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Soft be the gently breathing notes
That sing the Saviour’s dying love;
Soft as the evening zephyr floats,
Soft as the tuneful lyres above:
Soft as the morning dews descend,
While warbling birds exulting soar;
So soft to our almighty Friend
Be every sigh our bosoms pour.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: How pleasing to behold and see

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How pleasing to behold and see
The friends of Jesus all agree—
To sit around the sacred board
As members of one common Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here we behold the dawn of bliss—
Here we behold the Saviour’s grace—
Here we behold his precious blood,
Which sweetly pleads for us with God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While here we sit, we would implore
That love may spread from shore to shore,
Till all the saints, like us, combine
To praise the Lord in songs divine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To all we freely give our hand,
Who love the Lord in every land;
For all are one in Christ our head,
To whom be endless honors paid.

title: Welcome, ye hopeful heirs of heaven
author: Ere we exhaust the theme of love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Welcome, ye hopeful heirs of heaven,
To this rich feast of gospel love—
This pledge is but the prelude given
To that immortal feast above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How great the blessing, thus to meet
According to our Saviour’s word,
And hold by faith communion sweet,
With our unseen yet present Lord.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And if so sweet this feast below,
What will it be to meet above,
Where all we see, and feel, and know,
Are fruits of everlasting love!

sections.label: Verse 4

title: ’Twas on that night when doomed to know

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
’Twas on that night when doomed to know
The eager rage of every foe,
That night in which he was betrayed,
The Saviour of the world took bread;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And, after thanks and glory given
To him that rules in earth and heaven,
That symbol of his flesh he broke,
And thus to all his followers spoke:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My broken body thus I give
To you, my friends; take, eat, and live;
And oft the sacred feast renew,
That brings my wondrous love to view.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then in his hands the cup he raised,
And God anew he thanked and praised;
While kindness in his bosom glowed,
And from his lips salvation flowed.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
My blood I thus pour forth, he cries,
To cleanse the soul in sin that lies;
In this the covenant is sealed,
And heaven’s eternal grace revealed.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Away from earth my spirit turns
author: Forever firm on Zion’s hill

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Away from earth my spirit turns—
Away from every transient good:
With strong desire my bosom burns
To feast on heaven’s diviner food.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
What though temptations oft distress,
And sin assails, and breaks my peace;
Thou wilt uphold, and save, and bless,
And bid the storms of passion cease.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Lord, may the spirit of this feast
author: Have thus remembered thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, may the spirit of this feast—
The earnest of thy love—
Maintain a dwelling in our breast
Until we meet above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The healing sense of pardoned sin,
The hope that never tires,
The strength a pilgrim’s race to win,
The joy that heaven inspires:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Still may their light our duties trace
In lines of hallowed flame,
Like that upon the prophet’s face,
When from the mount he came.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But if no more with kindred dear
The broken bread we share,
Nor at the banquet board appear
To breathe the grateful prayer;

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Forget us not—when on the bed
Of dire disease we waste,
Or to the chambers of the dead,
And bar of judgment haste.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Forget not—thou who bore the woe
Of Calvary’s fatal tree—
Those who within these courts below

title: If human kindness meets return
author: But His recorded there

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
If human kindness meets return,
And owns the grateful tie—
If tender thoughts within us burn
To feel a friend is nigh;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, shall not warmer accents tell
The gratitude we owe
To him who died our fears to quell,
And save from endless woe?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While yet his anguished soul surveyed
Those pangs he would not flee,
What love his latest words displayed—
“Meet and remember me.”

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Remember thee! thy death, thy shame,
The griefs which thou didst bear!
O memory, leave no other name

title: O God, unseen yet ever near
author: Renewed with strength divine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God, unseen yet ever near!
Reveal thy presence now,
While we, in love that hath no fear,
Before thy glory bow.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here may obedient spirits find
The blessings of thy love—
The streams that through the desert wind,
The manna from above.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Awhile beside the fount we stay,
And eat this bread of thine,
Then go, rejoicing, on our way,

title: Come in, thou blesséd of the Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come in, thou blesséd of the Lord;
Stranger nor foe art thou:
We welcome thee with warm accord,
Our friend, our brother now.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The hand of fellowship, the heart
Of love, we offer thee:
Leaving the world, thou dost but part
From lies and vanity.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The cup of blessing which we bless,
The heavenly bread we break—
Our Saviour’s blood and righteousness,
Freely with us partake.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Come with us, we will do thee good,
As God to us hath done;
Stand but in him, as those have stood,
Whose faith the victory won.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
And when, by turns, we pass away
As star by star grows dim,
May each, translated into day,
Be lost, and found in him.

title: Lord, at thy table we behold
author: No Saviour is like ours

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, at thy table we behold
The wonders of thy grace;
But most of all admire that we
Should find a welcome place.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What strange, surprising grace is this,
That we, so lost, have room!
Jesus our weary souls invites,
And freely bids us come!

sections.label: Verse 3

title: In memory of the Saviour’s love
author: The heavenly feast above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In memory of the Saviour’s love,
We keep the sacred feast,
Where every humble, contrite heart
Is made a welcome guest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Under his banner thus we sing
The wonders of his love,
And thus anticipate by faith

title: Shepherd of souls, refresh and bless
author: Be our immortal food

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Shepherd of souls, refresh and bless
Thy chosen pilgrim flock,
With manna from the wilderness,
With water from the rock.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hungry and thirsty, faint and weak
(As thou when here below),
Our souls the joys celestial seek,
That from thy sorrows flow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We would not live by bread alone,
But by thy word of grace—
In strength of which we travel on
To our abiding place.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Be known to us in breaking bread,
But do not then depart—
Saviour abide with us, and spread
Thy table in our heart.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Jesus, the Friend of man
author: With kind affections grow

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, the Friend of man,
Invites us to his board;
The welcome summons we obey,
And own our gracious Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here we show forth his love,
Which spake in every breath,
Prompted each action of his life,
And triumphed in his death.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here let our powers unite
His honored name to raise;
Let grateful joy fill every mind,
And every voice be praise.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Now let each happy guest
author: Of peace and pardon too

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now let each happy guest
The sacred concert raise,
To close the honors of the feast,
And sing the Master’s praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His condescending love
First calls our wonder forth;
He left the blesséd realms above,
To dwell with men on earth.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His precepts, how divine!
How suited to our state!
How bright his acts of mercy shine
His promises how great!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Redemption’s glorious plan,
How wondrous in our view!
The salutary source to man

title: Our heavenly Father calls
author: In nobler scenes above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our heavenly Father calls,
And Christ invites us near;
With both, our friendship shall be sweet,
And our communion dear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
God pities all our griefs:
He pardons every day;
Almighty to protect our souls,
And wise to guide our way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How large his bounties are!
What various stores of good,
Diffused from our Redeemer’s hand,
And purchased with his blood!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus, our living Head,
We bless thy faithful care;
Our Advocate before the throne,
And our forerunner there.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Here fix my roving heart!
Here wait my warmest love!
Till the communion be complete,

title: Jesus invites his saints
author: And every voice be praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus invites his saints
To meet around his board;
Here pardoned rebels sit, and hold
Communion with their Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This holy bread and wine
Maintain our fainting breath,
By union with our living Lord,
And interest in his death.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: A parting hymn we sing
author: And know as we are known

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A parting hymn we sing,
Around thy table, Lord;
Again our grateful tribute bring,
Our solemn vows record.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here have we seen thy face,
And felt thy presence here;
So may the savor of thy grace
In word and life appear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The purchase of thy blood—
By sin no longer led—
The path our dear Redeemer trod
May we rejoicing tread.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
In self-forgetting love
Be Christian union shown,
Until we join the Church above,

title: Not all the blood of beasts
author: And sing his dying love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Not all the blood of beasts,
On Jewish altars slain,
Could give the guilty conscience peace,
Or wash away its stain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But Christ, the heavenly Lamb,
Bears all our sins away;
A sacrifice of nobler name
And richer blood than they.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My faith would lay her hand
On that dear head of thine,
While like a penitent I stand,
And there confess my sin.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Blest feast of love divine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest feast of love divine!
’Tis grace that makes us free
To feed upon this bread and wine,
In memory, Lord, of thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That blood which flowed for sin,
In symbol here we see,
And feel the blesséd pledge within,
That we are loved of thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, if this glimpse of love
Be so divinely sweet,
What will it be, O Lord, above,
Thy gladdening smile to meet!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To see thee face to face—
Thy perfect likeness wear—
And all thy ways of wondrous grace
Through endless years declare!

title: It is finished! Man of Sorrows

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
It is finished! Man of Sorrows!
From thy cross our frailty borrows
Strength to bear and conquer thus.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Bread of heaven, on thee we feed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bread of heaven, on thee we feed,
For thy flesh is meat indeed;
Ever let our souls be fed
With this true and living bread.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Day by day with strength supplied,
Through the life of him who died,
Lord of life, O let us be
Rooted, grafted, built on thee.

title: From the table now retiring

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From the table now retiring,
Which for us the Lord hath spread,
May our souls, refreshment finding,
Grow in all things like our Head.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His example by beholding,
May our lives his image bear;
Him our Lord and Master calling,
His commands may we revere.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Love to God and man displaying,
Walking steadfast in his way,
Joy attend us in believing,
Peace from God, through endless day.

title: Near the cross our station taking

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Near the cross our station taking,
Earthly cares and joys forsaking,
Meet it is for us to mourn:
’Twas for us he came from heaven,
’Twas for us his heart was riven;
All his griefs for us were borne.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When no eye its pity gave us,
When there was no arm to save us,
He his love and power displayed:
By his stripes our help and healing,
By his death our life revealing,
He for us the ransom paid.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, may thy love constrain us,
That from sin we may refrain us,
In thy griefs may deeply grieve;
Thee our best affections giving,
To thy praise and honor living,
May we in thy glory live!

title: Lamb of God! whose bleeding love

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
By thine agonizing pain,
And bloody sweat, we pray—
By thy dying love to man,
Take all our sins away:
By thy passion on the tree,
Let our griefs and troubles cease:
O, remember Calvary,
And bid us go in peace!

title: Sweet the moments, rich in blessing
author: And thy face in glory see

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet the moments, rich in blessing,
Which before the cross I spend;
Life, and health, and peace possessing,
From the sinner’s dying friend.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here I’ll sit, for ever viewing
Mercy streaming in his blood;
Precious drops! my soul bedewing,
Plead they now my peace with God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Truly blesséd is this station,
Here unfolds his wondrous grace;
While I see divine compassion
Beaming in his lovely face.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here it is I find my heaven,
While upon the cross I gaze;
Here the joy of sins forgiven
Shall inspire my songs of praise.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Love and grief my heart dividing,
While his feet I bathe with tears;
Constant still in faith abiding—
Hope triumphant o’er my fears.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Lord! in ceaseless contemplation,
Fix my trusting heart on thee,
Till I know thy full salvation,

title: Here I sink before thee lowly

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Here I sink before thee lowly,
Filled with gladness deep and holy,
As with trembling awe and wonder
On thy mighty work I ponder—
On this banquet’s mystery,
On the depths we can not see:
Far beyond all mortal sight
Lie the secrets of thy might.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sun, who all my life dost brighten!
Light, who dost my soul enlighten!
Joy, the sweetest man e’er knoweth!
Fount, whence all my being floweth!
Humbly draw I near to thee;
Grant that I may worthily
Take this blesséd heavenly food,
To thy praise, and to my good.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: While in sweet communion feeding
author: Wean our hearts from all below

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
While in sweet communion feeding
On this earthly bread and wine,
Saviour may we see thee bleeding
On the cross to make us thine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though unseen, now be thou near us,
With the still small voice of love,
Whispering words of peace to cheer us—
Every doubt and fear remove.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Bring before us all the story,
Of thy life, and death of woe!
And with hopes of endless glory,

title: Jesus has died for me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus has died for me,
Glory to God!
From sin he set me free,
Glory to God!
And, if I trust his grace,
I soon shall win the race;
Then see his lovely face,
Glory to God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon, I shall sing above,
Glory to God!
Tell of his wondrous love,
Glory to God:
Free from all death and wrong,
Then shall my notes prolong
One loud, triumphant song,
Glory to God!

title: My faith looks up to thee
author: A ransomed soul

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My faith looks up to thee,
Thou Lamb of Calvary:
Saviour divine,
Now hear me while I pray;
Take all my guilt away;
O, let me, from this day,
Be wholly thine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
May thy rich grace impart
Strength to my fainting heart;
My zeal inspire;
As thou hast died for me,
O may my love to thee
Pure, warm, and changeless be—
A living fire.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While life’s dark maze I tread,
And griefs around me spread,
Be thou my guide;
Bid darkness turn to day,
Wipe sorrow’s tears away,
Nor let me ever stray
From thee aside.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: I saw the cross of Jesus
author: And death is known no more

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
I love the cross of Jesus—
It tells what I am;
A vile and guilty creature,
Saved only through the Lamb.
No righteousness, no merit,
No beauty can I plead;
Yet in the cross I glory,
My title there I read.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I clasp the cross of Jesus
In every trying hour,
My sure and certain refuge,
My never-failing tower.
In every fear and conflict,
I more than conqueror am;
Living I’m safe, or dying,
Through Christ the risen Lamb.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sweet is the cross of Jesus!
There let my weary heart
Still rest in peace and safety
Till life itself depart;
And then in strains of glory
I’ll sing thy wondrous power,
Where sin can never enter,

title: Here, O my Lord, I see thee face to face
author: The Lamb’s great bridal feast of bliss and love

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Too soon we rise; the symbols disappear;
The feast, though not the love, is passed and gone:
The bread and wine remove, but thou art here—
Nearer than ever—still my Shield and Sun.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Ye saints, your music bring

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The cross, the cross alone,
Subdued the powers of hell;
Like lightning from his throne
The prince of darkness fell,
The triumphs of the cross we sing,
Awake, ye saints, each joyful string.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Once the angel started back
author: PRAYER AND SOCIAL MEETINGS

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Once the angel started back,
When he saw the blood-stained door,
Pausing on his vengeful track,
And the dwelling passing o’er.
Once the sea from Israel fled,
Ere it rolled o’er Egypt’s dead.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now our Passover is come,
Dimly shadowed in the past,
And the very Paschal Lamb,
Christ, the Lord, is slain at last.
Then with hearts and hands made meet,
Our unleavened bread we’ll eat.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blesséd Victim sent from heaven,
Whom all angel hosts obey,
To whose will all earth is given,
At whose word hell shrinks away.
Thou hast conquered death’s dread strife,
Thou hast brought us light and life.

title: From every stormy wind that blows

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From every stormy wind that blows,
From every swelling tide of woes,
There is a calm, a sure retreat—
’Tis found beneath the Mercy Seat.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There is a place where Jesus sheds
The oil of gladness on our heads,
A place than all besides more sweet—
It is the blood-bought Mercy Seat.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is a scene where spirits blend,
Where friend holds fellowship with friend;
Though sundered far, by faith they meet
Around one common Mercy Seat.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ah! whither could we flee for aid,
When tempted, desolate, dismayed;
Or how the host of hell defeat,
Had suffering souls no Mercy Seat?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
There! there on eagle wings we soar,
And sin and sense seem all no more,
And heaven comes down our souls to greet,
And glory crowns the Mercy Seat!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O let my hand forget her skill,
My tongue be silent cold and still,
This bounding heart forget to beat,
Ere I forget the Mercy Seat!

title: How sweet to leave the world awhile
author: And let thy presence fill this place

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sweet to leave the world awhile
And seek the presence of our Lord!
Dear Saviour! on thy people smile,
And come according to thy word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
From busy scenes we now retreat,
That we may here converse with thee:
Ah! Lord! behold us at thy feet—
Let this the “gate of heaven” be.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
“Chief of ten thousand!” now appear,
That we by faith may see thy face:
O! grant that we thy voice may hear,

title: Benignant God of love and power

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Benignant God of love and power,
Be with us in this solemn hour;
Smile on our souls; our plans approve,
By which we seek to spread thy love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let each discordant thought be gone,
And love unite our hearts in one;
Let all we have and are combine
To forward objects so divine.

title: Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer,
That calls me from a world of care,
And bids me at my Father’s throne,
Make all my wants and wishes known!
In seasons of distress and grief,
My soul has often found relief,
And oft escaped the tempter’s snare,
By thy return, sweet hour of prayer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer!
The joy I feel, the bliss I share,
Of those whose anxious spirits burn
With strong desires for thy return.
With such I hasten to the place
Where God my Saviour shows his face,
And gladly take my station there,
And wait for thee, sweet hour of prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer!
Thy wings shall my petition bear
To him whose truth and faithfulness
Engage the waiting soul to bless;
And since he bids me seek his face,
Believe his word and trust his grace,
I’ll cast on him my every care,
And wait for thee, sweet hour of prayer.

title: Jesus, where’er thy people meet

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
For thou, within no walls confined,
Inhabitest the humble mind;
Such ever bring thee where they come,
And, going, take thee to their home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Dear Shepherd of thy chosen few,
Thy former mercies here renew;
Here to our waiting hearts proclaim
The sweetness of thy saving name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here may we prove the power of prayer
To strengthen faith and banish care;
To teach our faint desires to rise,
And bring all heaven before our eyes.

title: Where two or three, with sweet accord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Where two or three, with sweet accord,
Obedient to their sovereign Lord,
Meet to recount his acts of grace,
And offer solemn prayer and praise;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
“There,” says the Saviour, “will I be,
Amid the little company;
To them unvail my smiling face,
And shed my glories round the place.”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We meet at thy command, O Lord,
Relying on thy faithful word;
Be present in each waiting heart,
And strength and heavenly peace impart.

title: My precious Lord, for thy dear name

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
No other name but thine is given
To cheer my soul in earth or heaven;
No other wealth will I require:
No other friend can I desire.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: O thou pure light of souls that love
author: In death our everlasting prize

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou pure light of souls that love,
True joy of every human breast,
Sower of life’s immortal seed,
Our Saviour and Redeemer blest!

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Thou, Saviour, from thy throne on high
author: Of hearts that love the tranquil hour

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou, Saviour, from thy throne on high,
Enrobed with light, and girt with power,
Dost note the thought, the prayer, the sigh,
Of hearts that love the tranquil hour.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oft thou thyself didst steal away,
At eventide, from labor done,
In some still peaceful shade to pray,
Till morning watches were begun.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou hast not, dearest Lord, forgot
Thy wrestlings on Judea’s hills;
And still thou lovest the quiet spot
Where praise the lowly spirit fills.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now to our souls, withdrawn awhile
From earth’s rude noise, thy face reveal,
And, as we worship, kindly smile,
And for thine own our spirits seal.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: What various hindrances we meet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What various hindrances we meet
In coming to a mercy-seat!
Yet who, that knows the worth of prayer,
But wishes to be often there?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Prayer makes the darkened clouds withdraw;
Prayer climbs the ladder Jacob saw,
Gives exercise to faith and love,
Brings every blessing from above.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Have you no words? Ah, think again;
Words flow apace when we complain,
And fill a fellow-creature’s ear
With the sad tale of all our care.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Were half the breath thus vainly spent,
To heaven in supplication sent,
Our cheerful song would oftener be,
“Hear what the Lord has done for me!”

title: My only Saviour! when I feel

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My only Saviour! when I feel
O’erwhelmed in spirit, faint, oppressed,
’Tis sweet to tell thee, while I kneel
Low at thy feet, thou art my rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O! sweet will be the welcome day,
When from her toils and woes released,
My parting soul in death shall say,
“Now, Lord! I come to thee for rest.”

title: Father, whate’er of earthly bliss
author: And crown my journey’s end

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, whate’er of earthly bliss
Thy sovereign will denies,
Accepted at thy throne of grace,
Let this petition rise:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Give me a calm, a thankful heart,
From every murmur free;
The blessings of thy grace impart,
And make me live to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: O Jesus, Saviour of the lost
author: To hide myself in thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Jesus, Saviour of the lost,
My Rock and Hiding-place,
By storms of sin and sorrow tost,
I seek thy sheltering grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
And when I stand before thy throne
And all thy glory see,
Still be my righteousness alone

title: How sweet to be allowed to pray

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How sweet to be allowed to pray
To God, the Holy One;
With filial love and trust to say,
“O God, thy will be done.”

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We in these sacred words can find
A cure for every ill;
They calm and soothe the troubled mind,
And bid all care be still.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O let that Will which gave me breath,
And an immortal soul,
In joy or grief, in life or death,
My every wish control.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O, could my heart thus ever pray,
Thus imitate thy Son!
Teach me, O God, with truth to say,
Thy will, not mine, be done.

title: While thee I seek, protecting Power
author: That heart shall rest on thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
While thee I seek, protecting Power,
Be my vain wishes stilled;
And may this consecrated hour
With better hopes be filled.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
In each event of life, how clear
Thy ruling hand I see!
Each blessing to my soul more dear,
Because conferred by thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
In every joy that crowns my days,
In every pain I bear,
My heart shall find delight in praise,
Or seek relief in prayer.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When gladness wings my favored hour,
Thy love my thoughts shall fill;
Resigned, when storms of sorrow lower,
My soul shall meet thy will.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: I love to steal awhile away
author: And lead to endless day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I love to steal awhile away
From every cumbering care,
And spend the hours of setting day
In humble, grateful prayer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love in solitude to shed
The penitential tear;
And all his promises to plead,
Where none but God can hear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I love to think on mercies past,
And future good implore,
And all my cares and sorrows cast
On him whom I adore.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I love, by faith, to take a view
Of brighter scenes in heaven;
The prospect doth my strength renew,
While here by tempests driven.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thus, when life’s toilsome day is o’er,
May its departing ray
Be calm as this impressive hour,

title: Thou art my hiding-place, O Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou art my hiding-place, O Lord,
In thee I fix my trust,
Encouraged by thy holy word,
A feeble child of dust.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I have no argument beside,
I urge no other plea,
And ’tis enough—the Saviour died,
The Saviour died for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When storms of fierce temptation beat,
And furious foes assail,
My refuge is the mercy-seat,
My hope within the vail.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
From strife of tongues and bitter words,
My spirit flies to thee;
Joy to my heart the thought affords—
My Saviour died for me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And when thy awful voice commands
This body to decay,
And life, in its last lingering sands,
Is ebbing fast away—

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
