title: Blest hour, when mortal man retires

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest hour, when mortal man retires
To hold communion with his God,
To send to heaven his warm desires,
And listen to the sacred word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Blest hour, when earthly cares resign
Their empire o’er his anxious breast,
While, all around, the calm divine,
Proclaims the holy day of rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blest hour, when God himself draws nigh,
Well pleased his people’s voice to hear,
To hush the penitential sigh,
And wipe away the mourner’s tear.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest hour! for, where the Lord resorts,
Foretastes of future bliss are given,
And mortals find his earthly courts
The house of God, the gate of heaven.

title: Great God, attend while Zion sings

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great God, attend while Zion sings
The joy that from thy presence springs;
To spend one day with thee on earth,
Exceeds a thousand days of mirth.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Might I enjoy the meanest place
Within thy house, O God of grace,
Not tents of ease, nor thrones of power,
Should tempt my feet to leave thy door.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God is our sun, he makes our day;
God is our shield, he guards our way
From all th’ assaults of hell and sin,
From foes without and foes within.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
All needful grace will God bestow,
And crown that grace with glory too:
He gives us all things, and withholds
No real good from upright souls.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O God, our King, whose sovereign sway,
The glorious hosts of heaven obey,
And devils at thy presence flee;
Blest is the man that trusts in thee.

title: Ye nations round the earth, rejoice
author: His truth from age to age endure

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: O come, loud anthems let us sing

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O come, loud anthems let us sing,
Loud thanks to our almighty King!
For we our voices high should raise,
When our salvation’s Rock we praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Into his presence let us haste,
To thank him for his favors past;
To him address in joyful songs
The praise that to his name belongs.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, let us to his courts repair,
And bow with adoration there!
Down on our knees, devoutly, all
Before the Lord, our Maker, fall.

title: While now thy throne of grace we seek

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
While now thy throne of grace we seek,
O God! within our spirits speak;
For we will hear thy voice to-day,
Nor turn our hardened hearts away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Speak in thy gentlest tones of love,
Till all our best affections move;
We long to hear thy gentle call,
And feel that thou art all in all.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To conscience speak thy quickening word,
Till all its sense of sin is stirred;
For we would leave no stain of guile,
To cloud the radiance of thy smile.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Speak, Father, to the anxious heart,
Till every fear and doubt depart;
For we can find no home or rest,
Till with thy Spirit’s whispers blest.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Speak to convince, forgive, console:
Childlike we yield to thy control;
These hearts, too often closed before,
Would grieve thy patient love no more.

title: Be still! be still! for all around

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Be still! be still! for all around,
On either hand, is holy ground:
Here in his house, the Lord to-day
Will listen, while his people pray.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou, tossed upon the waves of care
Ready to sink with deep despair,
Here ask relief, with heart sincere,
And thou shalt find that God is here.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou who hast laid within the grave
Those whom thou hadst no power to save,
Now to the mercy-seat draw near,
With all thy woes, for God is here.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou who hast dear ones far away,
In foreign lands, ’mid ocean’s spray,
Pray for them now, and dry the tear,
And trust the God who listens here.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou who art mourning o’er thy sin,
Deploring guilt that reigns within,
The God of peace is ever near;
The troubled spirit meets him here.

title: O blest the souls, for ever blest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O blest the souls, for ever blest,
Where God as sovereign is confest;
O happy hearts, the blesséd homes
To which the King in glory comes!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Fling wide thy portals, O my heart!
Be thou a temple set apart;
So shall thy Sovereign enter in,
And new and nobler life begin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Deliverer, come! we open wide
Our hearts to thee; here, Lord, abide!
Let all thy glorious presence feel;
Thou—King of saints! thyself reveal.

title: How pleasant, how divinely fair

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How pleasant, how divinely fair,
Lord of hosts, thy dwellings are!
With long desire my spirit faints
To meet the assemblies of thy saints.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My soul would rest in thine abode,
My panting heart cries out for God;
My God! my King! why should I be
So far from all my joys and thee!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blest are the souls who find a place
Within the temple of thy grace;
There they behold thy gentler rays,
And seek thy face, and learn thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest are the men whose hearts are set
To find the way to Zion’s gate;
God is their strength, and through the road,
They lean upon their Helper, God.

title: O Father! with protecting care

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Father! with protecting care,
Meet us in this, our house of prayer;
Assembled in thy sacred name,
Thy promised blessing here we claim.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But chiefest in the cleanséd breast,
For ever let thy Spirit rest,
And make the contrite heart to be
A temple pure and worthy thee.

title: Look from on high, great God, and see

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Look from on high, great God, and see
Thy saints lamenting after thee:
We sigh, we languish, and complain;
Revive thy gracious work again.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To-day thy cheering grace impart,
Bind up and heal the broken heart;
Our sins subdue, our souls restore,
And let our foes prevail no more.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy presence in thy house afford,
And bless the preaching of thy word,
That sinners may their danger see,
And now begin to mourn for thee.

title: With sacred joy we lift our eyes
author: The sacrifice we bring

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With sacred joy we lift our eyes
To those bright realms above,
That glorious temple in the skies,
Where dwells eternal Love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Before the gracious throne we bow
Of heaven’s almighty King;
Here we present the solemn vow,
And hymns of praise we sing.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Lord, while in thy house we kneel,
With trust and holy fear,
Thy mercy and thy truth reveal,
And lend a gracious ear.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Within thy house, O Lord, our God
author: In realms beyond the skies

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Within thy house, O Lord, our God,
In glory now appear;
Make this a place of thine abode,
And shed thy blessings here.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When we thy mercy-seat surround,
Thy Spirit, Lord, impart;
And let thy gospel’s joyful sound,
With power, reach every heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Here let the voice of sacred joy
And humble prayer arise,
Till higher strains our tongues employ

title: My soul! how lovely is the place
author: And sing thy praises still

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My soul! how lovely is the place,
To which thy God resorts!
’Tis heaven to see his smiling face,
Though in his earthly courts.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There the great Monarch of the skies
His saving power displays,
And light breaks in upon our eyes,
With kind and quickening rays.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: What shall I render to my God
author: If I forsake the Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What shall I render to my God
For all his kindness shown?
My feet shall visit thine abode,
My songs address thy throne.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Among the saints that fill thy house,
My offerings shall be paid;
There shall my zeal perform the vows
My soul in anguish made.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How happy all thy servants are,
How great thy grace to me!
My life, which thou hast made thy care,
Lord, I devote to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now I am thine, for ever thine,
Nor shall my purpose move;
Thy hand hath loosed my bonds of pain,
And bound me with thy love.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Come, O thou King of all thy saints
author: A heaven on earth appear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, O thou King of all thy saints,
Our humble tribute own,
While, with our praises and complaints,
We bow before thy throne.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How should our songs, like those above,
With warm devotion rise!
How should our souls on wings of love,
Mount upward to the skies!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But, ah, the song, how faint it flows!
How languid our desire!
How dim the sacred passion glows,
Till thou the heart inspire!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest Saviour, let thy glory shine,
And fill thy dwellings here,
Till life, and love, and joy divine,

title: Again the Lord of light and life
author: To nations yet unborn

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Again the Lord of light and life
Awakes the kindling ray,
Unseals the eyelids of the morn,
And pours increasing day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O what a night was that which wrapt
The heathen world in gloom!
O what a Sun which rose this day
Triumphant from the tomb!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This day be grateful homage paid
And loud hosannas sung;
Let gladness dwell in every heart,
And praise on every tongue.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ten thousand different lips shall join
To hail this welcome morn,
Which scatters blessings from its wings

title: The offerings to thy throne which rise
author: Some rays from heaven above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The offerings to thy throne which rise,
Of mingled praise and prayer,
Are but a worthless sacrifice
Unless the heart is there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Upon thine all-discerning ear
Let no vain words intrude;
No tribute but the vow sincere—
The tribute of the good.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My offerings will indeed be blest,
If sanctified by thee—
If thy pure Spirit touch my breast
With its own purity.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O, may that Spirit warm my heart
To piety and love,
And to life’s lowly vale impart

title: Again our earthly cares we leave
author: That we may render praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Again our earthly cares we leave,
And to thy courts repair;
Again, with joyful feet, we come
To meet our Saviour here.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Within these walls let holy peace,
And love, and concord dwell;
Here give the troubled conscience ease,
The wounded spirit heal.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The feeling heart, the melting eye,
The humble mind, bestow:
And shine upon us from on high,
To make our graces grow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
May we in faith receive thy word,
In faith present our prayers,
And in the presence of our Lord,
Unbosom all our cares.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Show us some token of thy love,
Our fainting hope to raise,
And pour thy blessings from above,

title: Come, Lord, and warm each languid heart
author: We join the heavenly choir

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Then to the shining realms of bliss
The wings of faith shall soar,
And all the charms of Paradise
Our raptured thoughts explore.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There shall the followers of the Lamb
Join in immortal songs,
And endless honors to his name
Employ their tuneful tongues.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Early, my God, without delay
author: And tune my lips to sing

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Early, my God, without delay,
I haste to seek thy face;
My thirsty spirit faints away
Without thy cheering grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
So pilgrims on the scorching sand,
Beneath a burning sky,
Long for a cooling stream at hand,
And they must drink or die.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Not life itself, with all its joys,
Can my best passions move,
Or raise so high my cheerful voice,
As thy forgiving love.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Blest day of God! most calm, most bright
author: And thus to make it mine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest day of God! most calm, most bright,
The first and best of days:
The laborer’s rest, the saint’s delight,
The day of prayer and praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Saviour’s face made thee to shine;
His rising thee did raise:
And made thee heavenly and divine
Beyond all other days.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The first-fruits oft a blessing prove
To all the sheaves behind:
And they who do the Lord’s day love,
A happy week shall find.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Stand up and bless the Lord
author: Henceforth for evermore

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Stand up and bless the Lord,
Ye people of his choice;
Stand up and bless the Lord your God,
With heart, and soul, and voice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O for the living flame,
From his own altar brought,
To touch our lips, our minds inspire,
And raise to heaven our thought!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God is our strength and song,
And his salvation ours;
Then be his love in Christ proclaimed
With all our ransomed powers.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Come, we that love the Lord
author: To fairer worlds on high

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, we that love the Lord,
And let our joys be known;
Join in a song with sweet accord,
And thus surround the throne.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The sorrows of the mind
Be banished from this place!
Religion never was designed
To make our pleasures less.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let those refuse to sing
Who never knew our God;
But children of the heavenly King
May speak their joys abroad.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The men of grace have found
Glory begun below;
Celestial fruits on earthly ground
From hope and faith may grow.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The hill of Zion yields
A thousand sacred sweets,
Before we reach the heavenly fields,
Or walk the golden streets.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Come, sound his praise abroad
author: And own your gracious God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, sound his praise abroad,
And hymns of glory sing;
Jehovah is the sovereign God,
The universal King.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Hungry, and faint, and poor

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hungry, and faint, and poor,
Behold us, Lord, again
Assembled at thy mercy’s door,
Thy bounty to obtain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy word invites us nigh,
Or we would starve indeed;
For we no money have to buy,
Nor righteousness to plead.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The food our spirits want,
Thy hand alone can give;
O! hear the prayer of faith, and grant
That we may eat and live!

title: My God, permit my tongue
author: And he supports my steps

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God, permit my tongue
This joy, to call thee mine;
And let my early cries prevail,
To taste thy love divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Within thy churches, Lord,
I long to find my place;
Thy power and glory to behold,
And feel thy quickening grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Since thou hast been my help,
To thee my spirit flies;
And on thy watchful providence,
My cheerful hope relies.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: And are we yet alive
author: Till we can sin no more

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And are we yet alive,
And see each other’s face?
Glory and praise to Jesus give,
For his preserving grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What troubles have we seen!
What conflicts have we past!
Fightings without, and fears within,
Since we assembled last.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But out of all, the Lord
Hath brought us by his love;
And still he doth his help afford,
And hides our life above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then let us make our boast
Of his redeeming power,
Which saves us to the uttermost,

title: To thy temple we repair

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
While thy glorious name is sung,
Tune our lips, inspire our tongue;
Then our joyful souls shall bless
Christ, the Lord, our Righteousness.

title: Father, hear our humble claim

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Build us in one spirit up,
Called in one high calling’s hope—
One the spirit, one the aim,
One the pure baptismal flame.

title: Lord, we come before thee now

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, we come before thee now;
At thy feet we humbly bow:
O do not our suit disdain,
Shall we seek thee, Lord, in vain?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
In thine own appointed way,
Now we seek thee; here we stay;
Lord, from hence we would not go,
Till a blessing thou bestow.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Far from mortal cares retreating
author: All our hope is from above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Far from mortal cares retreating,
Sordid hopes, and vain desires,
Here our willing footsteps meeting,
Every heart to heaven aspires.
From the Fount of glory beaming,
Light celestial cheers our eyes,
Mercy from above proclaiming
Peace and pardon from the skies.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Love divine, all love excelling

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Love divine, all love excelling,
Joy of heaven to earth come down!
Fix in us thy humble dwelling:
All thy faithful mercies crown;
Jesus, thou art all compassion,
Pure, unbounded love thou art,
Visit us with thy salvation,
Enter every trembling heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Breathe, O, breathe thy loving Spirit
Into every troubled breast:
Let us all in thee inherit,
Let us find thy promised rest.
Take away the love of sinning,
Take our load of guilt away;
End the work of thy beginning,
Bring us to eternal day.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: God is in his holy temple

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
God in Christ reveals his presence,
Throned upon the mercy-seat:
Saints, rejoice! and sinners, tremble!
Each prepare his God to meet:
Lowly, lowly,
Bow adoring at his feet.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Though the heaven, and heaven of heavens,
O thou Great Unsearchable!
Are too mean to comprehend thee,
Thou with man art pleased to dwell;
Welcome, welcome,
God with us, Immanuel.

title: Blest is the hour when cares depart
author: Blest through eternity

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest is the hour when cares depart,
And earthly scenes are far—
When tears of woe forget to start,
And gently dawns upon the heart
Devotion’s holy star.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Blest is the place where angels bend
To hear our worship rise,
Where kindred hearts their musings blend,
And all the soul’s affections tend
Beyond the vailing skies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blest are the hallowed vows that bind
Man to his work of love—
Bind him to cheer the humble mind,
Console the weeping, lead the blind,
And guide to joys above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sweet shall the song of glory swell,
Saviour divine, to thee,
When they whose work is finished well,
In thy own courts of rest shall dwell,

title: In thy name, O Lord, assembling
author: Holy bliss for evermore

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
While our days on earth are lengthened,
May we give them, Lord, to thee!
Cheered by hope, and daily strengthened,
We would run, nor weary be,
Till thy glory,
Without clouds, in heaven we see.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Lord of the worlds above
author: CLOSING HYMNS

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord of the worlds above,
How pleasant and how fair
The dwellings of thy love,
Thy earthly temples, are!
To thy abode my heart aspires,
With warm desires to see my God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, happy souls, who pray
Where God appoints to hear!
O, happy men, who pay
Their constant service there!
They praise thee still; and happy they
Who love the way to Zion’s hill.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
They go from strength to strength,
Through this dark vale of tears,
Till each arrives at length,
Till each in heaven appears:
O glorious seat, when God, our King
Shall thither bring our willing feet.

title: Now may the Lord our Shepherd lead

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Now may we hear our Shepherd’s voice,
And gladly answer to his call;
Now may our hearts for him rejoice,
Who knows, and names, and loves us all.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When the Chief Shepherd shall appear,
And small and great before him stand,
O, be the flock assembling here
Found with the sheep on his right hand!

title: Through all this life’s eventful road

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Through all this life’s eventful road,
Fain would I walk with thee, my God,
And find thy presence light around,
And every step on holy ground.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
And when the angel Death stands by,
Be this my strength, that thou art nigh;
And this my joy, that I shall be
With those who dwell in light with thee.

title: Ere to the world again we go

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ere to the world again we go,
Its pleasures, cares, and idle show,
Thy grace, once more, O God, we crave,
From folly and from sin to save.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
May the great truths we here have heard—
The lessons of thy holy Word—
Dwell in our inmost bosoms deep,
And all our souls from error keep.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, may the influence of this day
Long as our memory with us stay,
And as an angel guardian prove,
To guide us to our home above.

title: From all that dwell below the skies

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From all that dwell below the skies,
Let the Creator’s praise arise:
Let the Redeemer’s name be sung
Through every land, by every tongue.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Eternal are thy mercies, Lord;
Eternal truth attends thy word:
Thy praise shall sound from shore to shore,
Till suns shall rise and set no more.

title: Happy the saints whose lot is cast
author: Sweet earnests of the joys above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy the saints whose lot is cast
Where oft is heard the gospel sound;
The word is pleasing to their taste,
A healing balm for every wound.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With joy they hasten to the place
Where they their Saviour oft have met;
And while they feast upon his grace,
Their burdens and their griefs forget.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Come, Christian brethren, ere we part

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Christian brethren, ere we part,
Join every voice and every heart;
One solemn hymn to God we raise,
One final song of grateful praise.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Dismiss us with thy blessing, Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

title: Lord, how delightful ’tis to see

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, how delightful ’tis to see
A whole assembly worship thee,
At once they sing, at once they pray!
They hear of heaven, and learn the way.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O write upon my memory, Lord,
The text and doctrine of thy word;
That I may break thy laws no more,
But love thee better than before.

title: Lord, cause thy face on us to shine

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Bless all whose voice salvation brings,
Who minister in holy things;
Our pastors, rulers, deacons, bless;
Clothe them with zeal and righteousness:
Let many in the judgment day,
Turned from the error of their way,
Their hope, their joy, their crown, appear:
Save those who preach, and those who hear.

title: Lord, now we part in thy blest name

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, now we part in thy blest name,
In which we here together came;
Grant us our few remaining days,
To work thy will and spread thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Teach us, in life and death, to bless
Thee, Lord, our strength and righteousness;
And grant us all to meet above,
Where we shall better sing thy love!

title: O present still, though still unseen
author: A burning and a shining light

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O present still, though still unseen,
When brightly shines the prosperous day,
Be thoughts of thee a cloudy screen,
To temper the deceitful ray!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And, O, when gathers on our path
In shade and storm the frequent night,
Be thou, long-suffering, slow to wrath,

title: Up to the hills I lift mine eyes

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Up to the hills I lift mine eyes,
Th’ eternal hills beyond the skies;
Thence all her help my soul derives,
There my almighty Refuge lives.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He lives—the everlasting God
That built the world, that spread the flood;
The heavens with all their hosts he made,
And the dark regions of the dead.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Israel, a name divinely blest,
May rise secure, securely rest;
Thy holy Guardian’s wakeful eyes
Admit no slumber, nor surprise.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Should earth and hell with malice burn,
Still thou shalt go, and still return,
Safe in the Lord; his heavenly care
Defends thy life from every snare.

title: To God the great, the ever-blest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To God the great, the ever-blest,
Let songs of honor be addressed!
His mercy firm for ever stands;
Give him the thanks his love demands!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who knows the wonder of his ways?
Who can make known his boundless praise?
Blest are the souls that fear him still,
And learn submission to his will.

title: Praise God, ye heavenly hosts above

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Praise God, ye heavenly hosts above!
Praise him all creatures of his love!
Praise him each morning, noon and night,
Praise him with holy sweet delight!

title: Thou art our Shepherd, glorious God
author: The children of thy love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou art our Shepherd, glorious God!
Thy little flock behold,
And guide us by thy staff and rod,
The children of thy fold.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We praise thy name that we were brought
To this delightful place,
Where we are watched, and warned, and taught,
The children of thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
May all our friends, thy servants here,
Meet with us all above,
And we and they in heaven appear,

title: Internal Source of life and light

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Internal Source of life and light!
Supremely good and wise!
To thee we bring our grateful vows,
To thee lift up our eyes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our dark and erring minds illume
With truth’s celestial rays;
Inspire our hearts with sacred love,
And tune our lips to praise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Safely conduct us, by thy grace,
Through life’s perplexing road;
And place us, when that journey’s o’er,
At thy right hand, O God!

title: O God, by whom the seed is given
author: Shall ripen in the sky

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Preserve it from the passing feet,
And plunderers of the air;
The sultry’s sun’s intenser heat,
And weeds of worldly care!

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Lord, when together here we meet
author: Once interrupt our joy

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, when together here we meet,
And taste thy heavenly grace,
Thy smiles are so divinely sweet,
We’re loath to leave the place.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yet, Father, since it is thy will
That we must part again,
O let thy gracious presence still
With every one remain!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then let us all in Christ be one,
Bound with the cords of love,
Till we, around thy glorious throne,
Shall joyous meet above:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Where sin and sorrow from each heart
Shall then for ever fly,
And not one thought that we shall part

title: Almighty God, thy word is cast
author: To bring forth fruits of love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Almighty God, thy word is cast
Like seed into the ground;
Now let the dew of heaven descend,
And righteous fruits abound.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let not the foe of Christ and man
This holy seed remove:
But give it root in every heart,

title: Glory to God! who deigns to bless
author: And hears our hymn of praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glory to God! who deigns to bless
This consecrated day,
Unfolds his wondrous promises,
And makes it sweet to pray.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Glory to God! who deigns to hear
The humblest sigh we raise,
And answers every heartfelt prayer,

title: Lord, at this closing hour
author: Through Jesus Christ our Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, at this closing hour,
Establish every heart
Upon thy word of truth and power
To keep us when we part.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Through changes, bright or drear,
We would thy will pursue;
And toil to spread thy kingdom here
Till we its glory view.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: To God, the Only Wise
author: And everlasting song

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To God, the Only Wise,
Our Saviour and our King;
Let all the saints below the skies
Their humble praises bring.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
’Tis his almighty love,
His counsel and his care,
Preserve us safe from sin and death,
And every hurtful snare.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He will present our souls,
Unblemished and complete,
Before the glory of his face,
With joys divinely great.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then all the chosen seed
Shall meet around the throne,
Shall bless the conduct of his grace,
And make his wonders known.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To our Redeemer, God,
Wisdom and power belong,
Immortal crowns of majesty,

title: To bless thy chosen race
author: To praise thy glorious name

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To bless thy chosen race,
In mercy, Lord, incline;
And cause the brightness of thy face
On all thy saints to shine;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That so thy wondrous way
May through the world be known:
While distant lands their homage pay,
And thy salvation own.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Soon we shall meet again
author: Of thee in perfect peace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Soon we shall meet again
When all our toils are o’er,
Where sin, and death, and grief, and pain,
And parting are no more.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, happy, happy day
That calls thy exiles home;
The flaming heavens shall pass away,
The earth receive her doom.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Saviour, we wait the sound
That shall our souls release,
And labor that we may be found

title: And let our bodies part
author: Shall never part again

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And let our bodies part,
To different climes repair;
Still and for ever joined in heart
The friends of Jesus are.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O let us still proceed
In Jesus’ work below;
And following our triumphant Head,
To further conquests go.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O let our heart and mind,
Great God, to thee ascend,
That haven of repose to find,
Where all our labors end;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Where all our toils are o’er,
Our suffering and our pain:
Who meet on that eternal shore

title: Thy name, almighty Lord
author: Shall be exchanged no more

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy name, almighty Lord,
Shall sound through distant lands:
Great is thy grace, and sure thy word;
Thy truth for ever stands.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Far be thine honor spread,
And long thy praise endure,
Till morning light and evening shade

title: Blest are the pure in heart
author: Selects the pure in heart

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Still to the lowly soul
He doth himself impart,
And for his temple and his throne

title: Head of the Church triumphant
author: The praise of our salvation

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Head of the Church triumphant!
We joyfully adore thee;
Till thou appear, thy members here
Shall sing like those in glory.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We lift our hearts and voices
In blest anticipation,
And cry aloud, and give to God

title: All ye nations, praise the Lord
author: Like his own eternity

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
For his truth and mercy stand,
Past, and present, and to be,
Like the years of his right hand,

title: Thanks for mercies past receive
author: Take us to thy house above

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

title: Guide us, Lord! while, hand in hand

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Guide us while we onward move,
Linked in closest bonds of love,
Striving for the holy mind,
And the soul from sense refined;
That when life no longer burns,
And the dust to dust returns,
With the strength which thou hast given,
We may rise to thee and heaven.

title: Now may he, who from the dead
author: Loud thanksgiving unto God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now may he, who from the dead
Brought the Shepherd of the sheep,
Jesus Christ our King and Head,
All our souls in safety keep!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
May he teach us to fulfill
What is pleasing in his sight;
Perfect us in all his will,
And preserve us day and night.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Great Redeemer! thee we praise,
Who the covenant sealed with blood
While our hearts and voices raise

title: Glorious in thy saints appear

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
And, in every grace complete,
Make us, Lord, for glory meet;
Till we stand before thy sight,
Partners with the saints in light.

title: For a season called to part
author: Here to meet in peace again

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
For a season called to part,
Let us now ourselves commend
To the gracious eye and heart
Of our ever-present Friend.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, hear our humble prayer;
Tender Shepherd of thy sheep,
Let thy mercy and thy care
All our souls in safety keep.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Father! glory be to thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father! glory be to thee,
Source of all the good we see!
Glory for the blesséd Light
Rising on the ancient night!
Glory for the hopes that come
Streaming through the silent tomb!
Glory for thy Spirit given,
Guiding us in peace to heaven!

title: Peace be to this congregation

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Peace be to this congregation!
Peace to every heart therein!
Peace, the earnest of salvation,
Peace, the fruit of conquered sin;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Peace, that speaks the heavenly Giver,
Peace, to worldly minds unknown,
Peace, that floweth, as a river,
From the eternal Source alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O thou God of Peace! be near us,
Fix within our hearts thy home;
With thy bright appearing cheer us,
In thy blesséd freedom come.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, with all thy revelations,
Truth which we so long have sought;
Come with thy deep consolations,
Peace of God which passeth thought!

title: Israel’s Shepherd, guide me, feed me
author: Never wander from thee more

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Israel’s Shepherd, guide me, feed me,
Through my pilgrimage below,
And beside the waters lead me,
Where thy flock rejoicing go.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: May the grace of Christ, our Saviour
author: Joys which earth can not afford

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
May the grace of Christ, our Saviour,
And the Father’s boundless love,
With the Holy Spirit’s favor,
Rest upon us from above.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Worship, honor, glory, blessing

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Worship, honor, glory, blessing,
Be to him who reigns above!
Young and old thy Name confessing,
Saviour! let us share thy love!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As the saints in heaven adore thee,
We would bow before thy throne;
As thine angels bow before thee,
So on earth thy will be done!

title: Lord, dismiss us with thy blessing
author: Rise and reign in endless day

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
So, whene’er the signal’s given
Us from earth to call away;
Borne on angel’s wings to heaven
Glad the summons to obey,
May we ready,

title: Keep us, Lord, oh, keep us ever
author: May thy name our spirits cheer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Keep us, Lord, oh, keep us ever!
Vain our hope, if left by thee;
We are thine; oh, leave us never,
Till thy glorious face we see!
Then to praise thee
Through a bright eternity.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: God of our salvation, hear us
author: May thy presence cheer the gloom

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
As our steps are drawing nearer
To the place we call our home,
May our view of heaven grow clearer,
Hope more bright of joys to come;
And when dying,

title: To thee be praise for ever
author: Of thy redeeming love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To thee be praise for ever,
Thou glorious King of kings!
Thy wondrous love and favor
Each ransomed spirit sings.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We’ll celebrate thy glory,
With all thy saints above,
And shout the joyful story

title: To thee our wants are known

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To thee our wants are known,
From thee are all our powers;
Accept what is thine own,
And pardon what is ours:
Our praises, Lord, and prayers, receive,
And to thy words a blessing give.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, grant that each of us
Now met before thee here,
May meet together thus,
When thou and thine appear:
To thy blest presence may we come
And dwell in an eternal home.

title: Of thy love some gracious token

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text: THE NEW LIFE—TRUST AND JOY.

title: O peace of God, sweet peace of God
author: Guide to the endless peace of God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O peace of God, sweet peace of God!
Where broods on earth this gentle dove!
Where spread those pure and downy wings
To shelter him whom God doth love?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Whence comes this blessing of the soul,
This silent joy which can not fade?
This glory, tranquil, holy, bright,
Pervading sorrow’s deepest shade?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The peace of God, the peace of God!
It shines as clear ’mid cloud and storm
As in the calmest summer day,
’Mid chill as in the sunlight warm.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O peace of God! earth hath no power
To shed thine unction o’er the heart;
Its smile can never bring it here—
Its frown ne’er bid its light depart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Calm peace of God, in holy trust,
In love and faith, thy presence dwells—
In patient suffering and toil
Where mercy’s gentle tear-drop swells.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Is there a lone and dreary hour

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Is there a lone and dreary hour,
When worldly pleasures lose their power?
My Father! let me turn to thee,
And set each thought of darkness free.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Is there a time of rushing grief,
Which scorns the prospect of relief?
My Father! break the cheerless gloom,
And bid my heart its calm resume.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Is there an hour of peace and joy
When hope is all my soul’s employ?
My Father! still my hopes will roam,
Until they rest with thee, their home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The noontide blaze, the midnight scene,
The dawn, or twilight’s sweet serene,
The glow of life, the dying hour,
Shall own my Father’s grace and power.

title: O this is blessing, this is rest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O this is blessing, this is rest!
Into thine arms, O Lord! I flee;
I hide me in thy faithful breast,
And pour out all my soul to thee,
Now, hushing every adverse sound,
Songs of defense my soul surround,
As if all saints encamped about
One trusting heart, pursued by doubt.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And O, how solemn, yet how sweet,
Their one assured, persuasive strain!
“The Lord of hosts is thy retreat,
Still in his hands thy times remain.”
O tender word! O truth divine!
Lord, I am altogether thine;
I have bowed down, I need not flee;
Peace, peace is found in trusting thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And now I count supremely kind
The rule that once I thought severe;
And precious, to my altered mind,
At length thy kind reproofs appear.
I must be taught what I would know,
I must be led where I should go:
And all the rest ordained for me,
Is to be found in trusting thee.

title: O Father! gladly we repose
author: Through faith in thine encircling love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Father! gladly we repose
Our souls on thee, who dwellest above,
And bless thee for the peace which flows
From faith in thine encircling love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though every earthly trust may break,
Infinite might belongs to thee;
Though every earthly friend forsake,
Unchangeable thou still wilt be.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though griefs may gather darkly round,
They can not vail us from thy sight;
Though vain all human aid be found,
Thou every grief canst turn to light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
All things thy wise designs fulfill,
In earth beneath, and heaven above,
And good breaks out from every ill,

title: Fountain of light, and living breath

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Fountain of light, and living breath,
Whose mercies never fail nor fade,
Fill me with life that hath no death,
Fill me with light that hath no shade;
Appoint the remnant of my days
To see thy power, and sing thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O Lord, our God, before whose throne
Stand storms and fire, O what shall we
Return to heaven, that is our own,
When all the world belongs to thee?
We have no offering to impart,
But praises, and a broken heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O thou who sittest in heaven and seest
My deeds without, my thoughts within,
Be thou my prince, be thou my priest—
Command my soul, and cure my sin:
How bitter my afflictions be,
I care not, so I rise to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
What I possess, or what I crave,
Brings no content, great God, to me,
If what I would, or what I have,
Be not possessed and blest in thee:
What I enjoy, O, make it mine,
In making me—that have it—thine.

title: O Lord, thy heavenly grace impart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord, thy heavenly grace impart,
And fix my frail, inconstant heart;
Henceforth my chief delight shall be
To dedicate myself to thee,
To thee, my God, to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Whate’er pursuits my time employ,
One thought shall fill my soul with joy;
That silent, secret thought shall be,
That all my hopes are fixed on thee,
On thee, my God, on thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Renouncing every worldly thing,
And safe beneath thy sheltering wing,
My sweetest thought henceforth shall be,
That all I want I find in thee,
In thee, my God, in thee.

title: Do not I trust in thee, O Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Do not I trust in thee, O Lord?
Do I not rest in thee alone?
Is not the comfort of thy word
The sweetest cordial I have known?
When vexed with care, bowed down with grief,
Where else could I obtain relief?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And is it not my chief desire
To feel as if a stranger here?
Do not my hopes and thoughts aspire
Beyond this transitory sphere?
And art thou not, while here I roam,
My hope, my hiding-place, my home?

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
And now on thee I cast my soul,
Come life or death, come ease or pain;
Thy presence can each fear control,
Thy grace can to the end sustain:
Those whom thou lovest, heavenly Friend,
Thou lovest even to the end!

title: Whither, O whither should I fly
author: The heaven of loving thee alone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Whither, O whither should I fly,
But to my loving Father’s breast!
Secure within thine arms to lie,
And safe beneath thy wings to rest!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In all my ways thy hand I own,
Thy ruling providence I see:
Assist me still my course to run,
And still direct my paths to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: “He leadeth me!” O! blesséd thought
author: By his own hand he leadeth me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
“He leadeth me!” O! blesséd thought,
O! words with heavenly comfort fraught,
Whate’er I do, whate’er I be,
Still ’tis God’s hand that leadeth me!
He leadeth me! he leadeth me!
By his own hand he leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sometimes ’midst scenes of deepest gloom,
Sometimes where Eden’s bowers bloom;
By waters still, o’er troubled sea—
Still ’tis his hand that leadeth me!
He leadeth me! he leadeth me!
By his own hand he leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, I would clasp thy hands in mine,
Nor ever murmur nor repine—
Content, whatever lot I see,
Since ’tis my God that leadeth me!
He leadeth me! he leadeth me!
By his own hand he leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when my task on earth is done,
When, by thy grace, the victory’s won;
E’en death’s cold wave I will not flee,
Since God through Jordan leadeth me!
He leadeth me! he leadeth me!

title: My God, the spring of all my joys
author: To meet my dearest Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God, the spring of all my joys,
The life of my delights,
The glory of my brightest days,
The comfort of my nights!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In darkest shades, if thou appear,
My dawning is begun;
Thou art my soul’s bright morning star,
And thou my rising sun.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The opening heavens around me shine
With beams of sacred bliss,
While Jesus shows his mercy mine,
And whispers I am his.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My soul would leave this heavy clay
At that transporting word,
And run with joy the shining way

title: Rejoice, believers in the Lord
author: Shall triumph in him too

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rejoice, believers in the Lord,
Who makes your cause his own;
The hope that’s built upon his word,
Can ne’er be overthrown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though many foes beset your road,
And feeble is your arm,
Your life is hid in Christ your God
Beyond the reach of harm.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Weak as you are, you shall not faint,
Or fainting, shall not die;
Jesus, the strength of every saint,
Will aid you from on high.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: O not to fill the mouth of fame
author: Through all eternity

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O not to fill the mouth of fame,
My longing soul is stirred:
But give me a diviner name;
Call me thy servant, Lord!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No longer would my soul be known
As uncontrolled and free;
O, not mine own! O, not mine own!
Lord, I belong to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy servant—me thy servant choose,
Nought of thy claim abate!
The glorious name I would not lose,
Nor change the sweet estate.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Blest is the man who shuns the place
author: Down to the gates of hell

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest is the man who shuns the place
Where sinners love to meet,
Who fears to tread their wicked ways,
And hates the scoffer’s seat:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But in the statutes of the Lord,
Has placed his chief delight;
By day he reads or hears the word,
And meditates by night.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Green as the leaf, and ever fair,
Shall his profession shine:
While fruits of holiness appear
Like clusters on the vine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Not so the impious and unjust:
What vain designs they form!
Their hopes are blown away like dust,
Or chaff before the storm.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sinners in judgment shall not stand
Among the sons of grace,
When Christ the judge at his right hand
Appoints his saints a place.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Father of love, our Guide and Friend

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father of love, our Guide and Friend,
O, lead us gently on,
Until life’s trial-time shall end,
And heavenly peace be won!
We know not what the path may be
As yet by us untrod;
But we can trust our all to thee,
Our Father and our God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If called, like Abraham’s child, to climb
The hill of sacrifice,
Some angel may be there in time;
Deliverance shall arise:
Or, if some darker lot be good,
O, teach us to endure
The sorrow, pain, or solitude,
That make the spirit pure!

title: Thou art my portion, O my God
author: My hope is in thy word

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou art my portion, O my God;
Soon as I know thy way,
My heart makes haste t’ obey thy word,
And suffers no delay.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I choose the path of heavenly truth,
And glory in my choice;
Not all the riches of the earth
Could make me so rejoice.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The testimonies of thy grace
I set before mine eyes;
Thence I derive my daily strength,
And there my comfort lies.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
If once I wander from thy path,
I think upon my ways;
Then turn my feet to thy commands,
And trust thy pardoning grace.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Father, I know that all my life
author: For him on whom I wait

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, I know that all my life
Is portioned out for me;
The changes that will surely come,
I do not fear to see:
I ask thee for a present mind,
Intent on pleasing thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I ask thee for a thoughtful love,
Through constant watching wise,
To meet the glad with joyful smiles,
And wipe the weeping eyes;
A heart at leisure from itself,
To soothe and sympathize.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I would not have the restless will
That hurries to and fro,
That seeks for some great thing to do,
Or secret thing to know:
I would be treated as a child,
And guided where I go.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Wherever in the world I am,
In whatsoe’er estate,
I have a fellowship with hearts,
To keep and cultivate;
A work of lowly love to do

title: Jesus, these eyes have never seen

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, these eyes have never seen
That radiant form of thine!
The vail of sense hangs dark between
Thy blesséd face and mine!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I see thee not, I hear thee not,
Yet art thou oft with me;
And earth hath ne’er so dear a spot,
As where I meet with thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Like some bright dream that comes unsought,
When slumbers o’er me roll,
Thine image ever fills my thought,
And charms my ravished soul.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Yet though I have not seen, and still
Must rest in faith alone;
I love thee, dearest Lord! and will,
Unseen, but not unknown.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When death these mortal eyes shall seal,
And still this throbbing heart,
The rending vail shall thee reveal,
All glorious as thou art!

title: When I can trust my all with God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When I can trust my all with God,
In trial’s fearful hour—
Bow all resigned beneath his rod,
And bless his sparing power;
A joy springs up amid distress,
A fountain in the wilderness.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Israel the desert trod
author: We tread celestial ground

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Israel the desert trod,
Sustained by power divine,
While wondrous mercy marked the road
With many a mystic sign.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When Moses gave the stroke,
From Horeb’s flinty side
Issued a river, and the rock
The Hebrew’s thirst supplied.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But O! what nobler themes
Does gospel grace afford!
From Calvary spring superior streams—
There hung the smitten Lord!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Of every hope bereft,
Sinners to Jesus go;
Behold the Rock of Ages cleft,
And living currents flow.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Here may our spirits bathe,
Here may our joys abound!
Till (passed the wilderness and death)

title: My spirit on thy care
author: Of having all in thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My spirit on thy care,
Blest Saviour, I recline;
Thou wilt not leave me to despair,
For thou art love divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In thee I place my trust;
On thee I calmly rest:
I know thee good, I know thee just,
And count thy choice the best.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Whate’er events betide,
Thy will they all perform;
Safe in thy breast my head I hide,
Nor fear the coming storm.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let good or ill befall,
It must be good for me—
Secure of having thee in all

title: Jesus, cast a look on me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, cast a look on me!
Give me true simplicity:
Make me poor and keep me low,
Seeking only thee to know.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
All that feeds my busy pride,
Cast it evermore aside:
Bid my will to thine submit:
Lay me humbly at thy feet.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Leaning on thy loving breast,
Where a weary soul may rest;
Feeling well the peace of God
Flowing from thy precious blood!

title: My Shepherd’s mighty aid
author: Adore and love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Shepherd’s mighty aid,
His dear redeeming love,
His all-protecting power displayed,
I joy to prove.
Led onward by my Guide,
I tread the beauteous scene,
Where tranquil waters gently glide
Through pastures green.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In error’s maze my soul
Shall wander now no more;
His Spirit shall, with sweet control,
The lost restore.
My willing steps he’ll lead
In paths of righteousness;
His power defend, his bounty feed,
His mercy bless.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Affliction’s deepest gloom
Shall but his love display;
He will the vale of death illume
With living ray.
I lean upon his rod,
And thankfully adore;
My heart shall vindicate my God
For evermore.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His goodness ever nigh,
His mercy ever free,
Shall while I live, shall when I die
Still follow me.
For ever shall my soul
His boundless blessings prove,
And, while eternal ages roll,

title: ’Tis religion that can give

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
’Tis religion that can give
Sweetest pleasure while we live;
’Tis religion must supply
Solid comfort when we die.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
After death, its joys will be
Lasting as eternity!
Be the living God my friend,
Then my bliss shall never end.

title: Vainly through night’s weary hours
author: Who through Christ his prayer addressed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Vainly through night’s weary hours,
Keep we watch lest foes alarm;
Vain our bulwarks, and our towers,
But for God’s protecting arm.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Vain were all our toil and labor,
Did not God that labor bless;
Vain, without his grace and favor,
Every talent we possess.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Vainer still the hope of heaven
That on human strength relies;
But to him shall help be given
Who in humble faith applies.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Saviour! teach me, day by day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour! teach me, day by day,
Love’s sweet lessons to obey;
Sweeter lessons can not be,
Loving him who first loved me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With a child-like heart of love,
At thy bidding may I move;
Prompt to serve and follow thee,
Loving him who first loved me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Teach me all thy steps to trace,
Strong to follow in thy grace;
Learning how to love from thee,
Loving him who first loved me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Love in loving finds employ—
In obedience all her joy;
Ever new that joy will be,
Loving him who first loved me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thus may I rejoice to show
That I feel the love I owe;
Singing, till thy face I see,
Of his love who first loved me.

title: In heavenly love abiding
author: And he will walk with me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In heavenly love abiding,
No change my heart shall fear;
And safe is such confiding,
For nothing changes here.
The storm may roar without me,
My heart may low be laid,
But God is round about me,
And can I be dismayed?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Wherever he may guide me,
No want shall turn me back:
My Shepherd is beside me,
And nothing can I lack.
His wisdom ever waketh,
His sight is never dim;
He knows the way he taketh,
And I will walk with him.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Green pastures are before me,
Which yet I have not seen;
Bright skies will soon be o’er me,
Where the dark clouds have been.
My hope I can not measure,
My path to life is free,
My Saviour has my treasure,

title: O strong to save and bless

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O strong to save and bless,
My Rock and Righteousness,
Draw near to me;
Blessing, and joy, and might,
Wisdom, and love, and light,
Are all with thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Refuge and my Rest,
As child on mother’s breast
I lean on thee;
From faintness and from fear,
When foes and ill are near,
Deliver me.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Through the love of God our Saviour
author: All must be well

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Though we pass through tribulation,
All will be well:
Ours is such a full salvation;
All, all is well:
Happy, still in God confiding,
Fruitful, if in Christ abiding,
Holy, through the Spirit’s guiding,
All must be well.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: In time of fear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In time of fear,
When trouble’s near,
I look to thine abode;
Though helpers fail,
And foes prevail,
I’ll put my trust in God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And what is life
But toil and strife?
What terror has the grave?
Thine arm of power,
In peril’s hour,
The trembling soul will save.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In darkest skies,
Though storms arise,
I will not be dismayed:
O God of light,
And boundless might,
My soul on thee is stayed!

title: Acquaint thee, O mortal, acquaint thee with God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Acquaint thee, O mortal, acquaint thee with God,
And joy, like the sunshine, shall beam on thy road;
And peace, like the dewdrop, shall fall on thy head,
And sleep, like an angel, shall visit thy bed.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: O eyes that are weary, and hearts that are sore

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O eyes that are weary, and hearts that are sore,
Look off unto Jesus; now sorrow no more:
The light of his countenance shineth so bright,
That here, as in heaven, there need be no night.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Still looking to Jesus, O, may I be found,
When Jordan’s dark waters encompass me round:
They bear me away in his presence to be;
I see him still nearer whom always I see.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then, then shall I know the full beauty and grace
Of Jesus, my Lord, when I stand face to face;
Shall know how his love went before me each day,
And wonder that ever my eyes turned away.

title: Long did I toil, and knew no earthly rest

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Yes! he is mine! and nought of earthly things,
Not all the charms of pleasure, wealth, or power,
The fame of heroes, or the pomp of kings,
Could tempt me to forego his love an hour.
Go, worthless world, I cry, with all that’s thine!
Go! I my Saviour’s am, and he is mine.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: How firm a foundation, you saints of the Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How firm a foundation, you saints of the Lord,
Is laid for your faith in his excellent word!
What more can he say than to you he has said,
You who unto Jesus for refuge have fled?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In every condition, in sickness, in health,
In poverty’s vale, or abounding in wealth;
At home and abroad, on the land, on the sea,
As your days may demand, so your succor shall be.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fear not—I am with you; O be not dismayed!
I, I am your God, and will still give you aid;
I’ll strengthen you, help you, and cause you to stand,
Upheld by my righteous, omnipotent hand.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When through the deep waters I cause you to go,
The rivers of sorrow shall not you o’erflow;
For I will be with you, your troubles to bless,
And sanctify to you your deepest distress.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When through fiery trials your pathway shall lie,
My grace, all-sufficient, shall be your supply:
The flame shall not hurt you: I only design
Your dross to consume, and your gold to refine.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
E’en down to old age all my people shall prove
My sovereign, eternal, unchangeable love;
And when hoary hairs shall their temples adorn,
Like lambs they shall still in my bosom be borne.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
The soul that on Jesus has leaned for repose,
I will not, I can not, desert to his foes;
That soul, though all hell should endeavor to shake,
I’ll never—no, never—no, never forsake!

title: Joyfully, joyfully, onward I move

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Joyfully, joyfully, onward I move,
Bound to the land of bright spirits above;
Angelic choristers, sing as I come—
Joyfully, joyfully, haste to thy home!
Soon, with my pilgrimage ended below,
Home to the land of bright spirits I go;
Pilgrim and stranger, no more shall I roam:
Joyfully, joyfully, resting at home.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3

title: The child leans on its parent’s breast

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The child leans on its parent’s breast,
Leaves there its cares, and is at rest;
The bird sits singing by his nest,
And tells aloud
His trust in God, and so is blest
’Neath every cloud.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
The heart that trusts for ever sings,
And feels as light as it had wings;
A well of peace within it springs:
Come good or ill,
Whate’er to-day, to-morrow brings,
It is his will!

title: He bids us come; his voice we know
author: Till all the storm is o’er

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
He bids us come; his voice we know,
And boldly on the waters go,
To him our Christ and Lord;
We walk on life’s tempestuous sea,
For he who died to set us free
Hath called us by his word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Secure from troubled waves we tread,
Nor all the storms around us heed,
While to our Lord we look;
O’er every fierce temptation bound—
The billows yield a solid ground,
The wave is firm as rock.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But if from him we turn our eye,
And see the raging floods run high,
And feel our fears within;
Our foes so strong, our flesh so frail,
Reason and unbelief prevail,
And sink us into sin.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Rest, weary heart

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Rest, weary head!
Lie down to slumber in the peaceful tomb;
Light from above has broken through its gloom;
Here, in the place where once thy Saviour lay,
Where he shall wake thee on a future day,
Like a tired child upon its mother’s breast,
Rest, sweetly rest!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Rest, spirit free!
In the green pastures of the heavenly shore,
Where sin and sorrow can approach no more;
With all the flock by the Good Shepherd fed,
Beside the streams of life eternal led,
For ever with thy God and Saviour blest,
Rest, sweetly rest!

title: Star of morn and even

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Star of morn and even,
Sun of Heaven’s heaven,
Saviour high and dear,
Toward us turn thine ear;
Through whate’er may come,
Thou canst lead us home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though the gloom be grievous,
Those we leant on leave us,
Though the coward heart
Quit its proper part,
Though the tempter come,
Thou wilt lead us home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Saviour pure and holy,
Lover of the lowly,
Sign us with thy sign,
Take our hands in thine;
Take our hands and come,
Lead thy children home!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Star of morn and even,
Shine on us from heaven;
From thy glory-throne
Hear thy very own!
Lord and Saviour, come,
Lead us to our home!

title: I will not let thee go; thou help in time of need

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I will not let thee go; thou help in time of need,
Heap ill on ill,
I trust thee still,
E’en when it seems as thou wouldst slay indeed!
Do as thou wilt with me,
I yet will cling to thee,
Hide thou thy face; yet, help in time of need,
I will not let thee go!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I will not let thee go; should I forsake my bliss?
No, Lord, thou’rt mine,
And I am thine:
Thee will I hold when all things else I miss;
Though dark and sad the night,
Joy cometh with thy light,
O thou my Sun; should I forsake my bliss?
I will not let thee go!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I will not let thee go, my God, my Life, my Lord!
Not death can tear
Me from his care,
Who for my sake his soul in death outpoured.
Thou diedst for love to me,
I say in love to thee,
E’en when my heart shall break, my God, my Life, my Lord,
I will not let thee go!

title: Now as long as here I roam
author: Can not perish in the end

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now as long as here I roam,
On this earth have house and home,
Shall the light of love from thee
Shine through all my memory,
To my God I yet will cling,
All my life the praises sing
That from thankful hearts outspring.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Every sorrow, every smart,
That the Father’s loving heart
Hath appointed me of yore,
Or hath yet for me in store,
As my life flows on I’ll take
Calmly, gladly for his sake,
No more faithless murmurs make.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I will meet distress and pain,
I will greet e’en death’s dark reign,
I will lay me in the grave,
With a heart still glad and brave,
Whom the strongest doth defend,
Whom the highest counts his friend,

title: My days are gliding swiftly by

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My days are gliding swiftly by,
And I a pilgrim stranger,
Would not detain them as they fly—
Those hours of toil and danger.
CHORUS.
For O! we stand on Jordan’s strand,
Our friends are passing over;
And just before, the shining shore
We may almost discover.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We’ll gird our loins, my brethren dear,
Our distant home discerning;
Our absent Lord has left us word,
Let every lamp be burning.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Should coming days be cold and dark,
We need not cease our singing;
That perfect rest nought can molest,
Where golden harps are ringing.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let sorrow’s rudest tempest blow,
Each cord on earth to sever;
Our King says, “Come,” and there’s our home,
For ever, O! for ever.

title: Still will we trust, tho’ earth seem dark and dreary

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Still will we trust, tho’ earth seem dark and dreary,
And the heart faint beneath his chastening rod;
Though rough and steep our pathway, worn and weary,
Still will we trust in God!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our eyes see dimly till by faith anointed,
And our blind choosing brings us grief and pain;
Through him alone who hath our way appointed,
We find our peace again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Choose for us, God! nor let our weak preferring
Cheat our poor souls of good thou hast designed;
Choose for us, God! thy wisdom is unerring,
And we are fools and blind.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
So from our sky, the night shall furl her shadows,
And day pour gladness through his golden gates;
Our rough path leads to flower-enameled meadows
Where joy our coming waits.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Let us press on in patient self-denial,
Accept the hardship, shrinking not from loss—
Our guerdon lies beyond the hour of trial;
Our crown, beyond the Cross.

title: God doth not leave his own
author: God doth not leave his own

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
God doth not leave his own!
Though “few and evil” all their days appear,
Though grief and fear
Come in the train of earth and hell’s dark crowd,
The trusting heart says, even in the cloud,
God doth not leave his own.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God doth not leave his own!
This sorrow in their life he doth permit,
Yea, useth it
To speed his children on their heavenward way.
He guides the winds—Faith, Hope and Love all say

title: I know not if or dark or bright
author: I hear my Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I know not if or dark or bright
Shall be my lot;
If that wherein my hopes delight
Be best, or not.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It may be mine to drag for years
Toil’s heavy chain;
Or day and night my meat be tears
On bed of pain.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Dear faces may surround my hearth
With smiles and glee;
Or I may dwell alone, and mirth
Be strange to me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My bark is wafted to the strand
By breath divine;
And on the helm there rests a hand
Other than mine.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: We are too far from thee, our Saviour
author: Thou drawest us to thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We are too far from thee, our Saviour,
Too far from thee,
Before our eyes
Dark mists arise,
And vail the glories from the skies:
We are too far from thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We are too far from thee, our Saviour,
Too far from thee.
Fierce pains oppress,
Dark cares distress,
Made darker by our loneliness:
We are too far from thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We are too far from thee, our Saviour,
Too far from thee,
Dark waters roll
Above the soul;
Striving to reach the heavenly goal,
We are too far from thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We are too far from thee, our Saviour,
Too far from thee,
Alone, afraid,
Our path is laid
In darkness; send thy heavenly aid;
We are too far from thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
We are too far from thee, our Saviour,
Too far from thee,
E’en if thy rod
Bring us to God,
In meekness be the pathway trod,
If it but lead to God.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Draw us more close to thee, our Saviour,
More close to thee,
Let come what will
Of good or ill,
’Tis one to us, well knowing still

title: Jesus! guide our way
author: ASPIRATIONS

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus! guide our way
To eternal day!
So shall we, no more delaying,
Follow thee, thy voice obeying;
Lead us by the hand
To our Father’s land!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When we danger meet,
Steadfast make our feet!
Lord, preserve us uncomplaining
’Mid the darkness round us reigning!
Through adversity
Lies our way to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Now let our souls, on wings sublime

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now let our souls, on wings sublime,
Rise from the vanities of time,
Draw back the parting vail, and see
The glories of eternity.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Born by new, celestial birth,
Why should we grovel here on earth?
Why grasp at vain and fleeting toys,
So near to heaven’s eternal joys?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Shall aught beguile us on the road,
While we are walking back to God?
For strangers into life we come,
And dying is but going home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Welcome, sweet hour of full discharge,
That sets our longing souls at large,
Unbinds our chains, breaks up our cell,
And gives us with our God to dwell.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To dwell with God, to feel his love,
Is the full heaven enjoyed above;
And the sweet expectation now
Is the young dawn of heaven below.

title: Jesus, my love, my chief delight
author: Nor envy the rich sinner’s state

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, my love, my chief delight,
For thee I long, for thee I pray,
Amid the shadows of the night,
Amid the business of the day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When shall I see thy smiling face,
That face which I have often seen?
Arise, thou Sun of Righteousness!
Scatter the clouds that intervene.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou art the glorious gift of God,
To sinners weary and distressed;
The first of all his gifts bestowed,
And certain pledge of all the rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Since I can say this gift is mine,
I’ll tread the world beneath my feet,
No more at poverty repine,

title: What sinners value I resign

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What sinners value I resign,
Lord! ’tis enough that thou art mine;
I shall behold thy blissful face,
And stand complete in righteousness.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This life’s a dream, an empty show;
But the bright world to which I go
Has joys substantial and sincere:
When shall I wake and find me there?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O glorious hour! O blest abode!
I shall be near and like my God!
And flesh and sin no more control
The sacred pleasures of the soul.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My flesh shall slumber in the ground
Till the last trumpet’s joyful sound;
Then burst the chains with sweet surprise,
And in my Saviour’s image rise.

title: O thou, to whose all-searching sight

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou, to whose all-searching sight
The darkness shineth as the light,
Search, prove my heart, it pants for thee;
O, burst these bonds, and set it free.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
If in this darksome wild I stray,
Be thou my light, be thou my way;
No foes, no violence I fear,
No fraud, while thou, my God, art near.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When rising floods my soul o’erflow,
When sinks my heart in waves of woe—
Jesus, thy timely aid impart,
And raise my head and cheer my heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Saviour, where’er thy steps I see,
Dauntless, untired, I follow thee;
O, let thy hand support me still,
And lead me to thy holy hill.

title: Let me be with thee where thou art

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let me be with thee where thou art,
My Saviour, my eternal Rest!
Then only will this longing heart
Be fully and for ever blest!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let me be with thee where thou art,
Where spotless saints thy name adore;
Then only will this sinful heart
Be evil and defiled no more!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let me be with thee where thou art,
Where none can die, where none remove;
There neither death nor life will part
Me from thy presence and thy love!

title: O for a heart to praise my God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O for a heart to praise my God,
A heart from sin set free,
A heart that always feels the blood
So freely shed for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A heart resigned, submissive, meek,
My great Redeemer’s throne,
Where only Christ is heard to speak
Where Jesus reigns alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O for a lowly, contrite heart,
Confiding, true, and clean,
Which neither life nor death can part
From him that dwells within.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A heart in ev’ry thought renewed,
And full of love divine,
Perfect and right, and pure and good,
A copy, Lord, of thine.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Sweet land of rest, for thee I sigh
author: And dwell with Christ at home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet land of rest, for thee I sigh,
When will the moment come,
When I shall lay my armor by,
And dwell in peace at home?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
O, this is not my home,
O, this is not my home:
This world’s a wilderness of woe,
This world is not my home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No tranquil joy on earth I know,
No peaceful, sheltering dome;
This world’s a wilderness of woe,
This world is not my home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When by affliction sharply tried,
I view the gaping tomb,
Although I dread death’s chilling tide,
Yet still I sigh for home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Weary of wandering round and round
This vale of sin and gloom,
I long to quit the unhallowed ground,

title: You glittering toys of earth, adieu

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
You glittering toys of earth, adieu,
A nobler choice be mine;
A real prize attracts my view—
A treasure all divine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Away, unworthy of my cares,
You specious baits of sense;
Inestimable worth appears,
The pearl of price immense!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus to multitudes unknown—
O name divinely sweet!
Jesus, in thee, in thee alone,
Wealth, honor, pleasure meet.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Should both the Indies, at my call,
Their boasted stores resign,
With joy I would renounce them all,
For leave to call thee mine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Should earth’s vain treasures all depart
Of this dear gift possessed,
I’d clasp it to my joyful heart,
And be for ever blest.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Blest Sovereign of my soul’s desires,
Thy love is bliss divine;
Accept the praise that love inspires,
Since I can call thee mine!

title: Jesus hath died that I might live

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus hath died that I might live,
Might live to God alone;
In him eternal life receive,
And be in spirit one,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My soul breaks out in strong desire
The perfect bliss to prove;
My longing heart is all on fire
To be dissolved in love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Give me thyself. From every boast
From every wish, set free,
Let all I am in thee be lost;
But give thyself to me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy gifts, alas! can not suffice,
Unless thyself be given;
Thy presence makes my Paradise,
And where thou art, is heaven!

title: Awake, you saints, and raise your eyes
author: You bring eternal day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, you saints, and raise your eyes,
And raise your voices high;
Awake, and praise that sovereign love
That shows salvation nigh.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Not many years their round shall run,
Not many mornings rise,
Ere all its glories stand revealed
To our admiring eyes.
