sections.label: Verse 4

title: I am thy workmanship, O Lord
author: Who bears a Saviour’s name

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I am thy workmanship, O Lord!
And unto thee belong;
Thou art my shield, my Great Reward,
My Glory, and my song.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Make me a weapon of thy power,
An angel of thy will;
To thee devoted, let each hour
Its happy task fulfill.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Yet dare not I, a child of dust
Thus plead my filial claim,
But as in him is all my trust,

title: Give me the wings of faith, to rise
author: Shows the same path to heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Give me the wings of faith, to rise
Within the vail, and see
The saints above, how great their joys
How bright their glories be.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Once they were mourning here below,
And bathed their couch with tears;
They wrestled hard, as we do now,
With sins, and doubts, and fears.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I ask them whence their victory came;
They, with united breath,
Ascribe their conquest to the Lamb,
Their triumph to his death.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: The dove, let loose in eastern skies
author: Thy freedom on her wings

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The dove, let loose in eastern skies,
Returning fondly home,
Ne’er stoops to earth her wing, nor flies
Where idle warblers roam;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But high she shoots through air and light
Above all low delay,
Where nothing earthly bounds her flight,
Nor shadow dims her way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So grant me, Lord, from every snare
And stain of passion free,
Aloft, through faith’s serener air,
To urge my course to thee;—

sections.label: Verse 4

title: I have no resting-place on earth

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I have no resting-place on earth
On which to fix my love;
But O! my heart is yearning for
The promised rest above.
’Tis true, this earth is passing fair,
O’er which I sadly roam;
But yet it hath no charms for me,
For heavén is my home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A pilgrim long I’ve wandered here;
But, with a steadfast eye,
I see a rest reserved for me,
At God’s right hand on high,
Then all the joys of earth in vain
Shall tempt my feet to roam,
To seek a dwelling-place below,
Since heavén is my home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, were this earth as fair as when
Primeval Eden smiled,
I would not by its glowing charms
Be from my hope beguiled;
But I would seek a brighter world,
Where God has bid me come:
Then seek no more to bind me here,
For heavén is my home.

title: Jerusalem, my happy home
author: Will soon come after me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jerusalem, my happy home,
O how I long for thee!
When will my sorrows have an end?
Thy joys when shall I see?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy walls are all of precious stones,
Most glorious to behold!
Thy gates are richly set with pearl,
Thy streets are paved with gold.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy gardens and thy pleasant greens
My study long have been;
Such sparkling gems by human sight
Have never yet been seen.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
If heavén be thus glorious, Lord,
Why should I stay from thence?
What folly ’tis that I should dread
To die and go from hence!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Reach down, reach down thine arms of grace
And cause me to ascend,
Where congregations ne’er break up,
And Sabbaths never end.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Jerusalem! my glorious home
author: When I thy joys shall see

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jerusalem! my glorious home,
Name ever dear to me!
When shall my labors have an end,
In joy, and peace, and thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When shall these eyes thy heaven-built walls
And pearly gates behold?
Thy bulwarks with salvation strong,
And streets of shining gold?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There happier bowers than Eden’s bloom,
Nor sin nor sorrow know:
Blessed seats! through rude and stormy scenes
I onward press to you!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Why should I shrink at pain and woe?
Or feel, at death, dismay?
I’ve Canaan’s goodly land in view,
And realms of endless day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Apostles, martyrs, prophets there,
Around my Saviour stand;
And soon my friends in Christ below
Will join the glorious band.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Lord, we expect a day
author: And all thy truth record

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, we expect a day
Still brighter far than this,
When death shall bear our souls away,
To realms of light and bliss.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There rapturous scenes of joy
Shall burst upon our sight;
And every pain, and tear, and sigh,
Be drowned in endless night.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Beneath thy balmy wing,
O Sun of Righteousness!
Our happy souls shall sit and sing
The wonders of thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Nor shall that radiant day,
So joyfully begun,
In evening shadows die away
Beneath the setting sun.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
How various and how new
Are thy compassions, Lord!
Eternity thy love shall show,

title: As the hart, with eager looks

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As the hart, with eager looks,
Panteth for the water-brooks,
So my soul, athirst for thee,
Pants the living God to see:
When, O when, with filial fear,
Lord, shall I to thee draw near?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Why art thou cast down, my soul?
God, thy God, shall make thee whole:
Why art thou disquieted?
God shall lift thy fallen head,
And his countenance benign
Be the saving health of thine.

title: Come, my Christian brethren, come

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, my Christian brethren, come,
Let us onward to our home;
Though we many trials meet,
Jesus makes our trials sweet.
CHORUS.
We with Jesus soon shall be
Happy in eternity:
By our Father’s side sit down:
They that conquer shall wear the crown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Brother Christian, doubt no more,
Christ your Saviour’s gone before;
He himself has marked the way,
Leading to eternal day.
We with Jesus, etc.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let us never be afraid,
’Tis on Christ our help is laid;
He will all our foes o’ercome,
He will take his exiles home.
We with Jesus, etc.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though the world revile and mock,
We are built upon the Rock;
And while thus we dwell secure,
Christ will make our goings sure.
We with Jesus, etc.

title: Let me go; my soul is weary
author: Finds at last its long sought rest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let me go; my soul is weary
Of the chain which binds me here;
Let my spirit bend its pinion
To a brighter, holier sphere.
Earth, ’tis true hath friends that bless me
With their fond and faithful love;
But the hands of angels beckon
Onward to the climes above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let me go; for earth hath sorrow,
Sin, and pain, and bitter tears;
All its paths are dark and dreary,
All its hopes are fraught with fears;
Short-lived are its brightest flowers,
Soon its cherished joys decay:—
Let me go; I fain would leave it
For the realms of endless day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let me go; my heart hath tasted
Of my Saviour’s wondrous grace;
Let me go, where I shall ever
See and know him face to face.
Let me go; the trees of heavén
Rise before me, waving bright,
And the distant, crystal waters
Flash upon my failing sight.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let me go; for songs seraphic
Now seem calling from the sky—
’Tis the welcome of the angels,
Which e’en now are hovering nigh:
Let me go: they wait to bear me
To the mansions of the blest;
Where the spirit, worn and weary,

title: O that I had wings like a dove
author: Shall be the one theme of my song

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The clouds that now hang o’er my soul,
Make dark all the pathway of life;
While thunders unceasingly roll
In storms of deep anger and strife;
I hope for some bright ray to beam
From clouds where there yet may be light,
But only the lightning’s red gleam
Is seen through the darkness of night.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I try to be humble and meek,
Leave all to my Saviour’s own will;
For, He to the tempest can speak,
The winds will obey and be still;
But now my soul flutters and cries,
And longs to be soaring away,
From darkness and gloom, to the skies,
The regions of bright, endless day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Dear Saviour, O, let me come home,
And rest on thy bosom in peace;
No more from thy presence to roam—
Then tempests and storms shall all cease.
I’ll sing of thy wonderful ways,
With all of the glorified throng—
For ever and ever, thy praise,

title: To Jesus, the crown of my hope
author: Intrude on my blissful repose

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Dissolve thou those bands that detain
My soul from her portion in thee,
Ah! strike off this adamant chain,
And make me eternally free.
When that happy era begins,
When arrayed in thy glories I shine,
Nor grieve any more, by my sins,
The bosom on which I recline;

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O then shall the vail be removed!
And round me thy brightness be poured;
I shall meet him, whom absent I loved;
I shall see, whom unseen I adored.
And then, never more shall the fears,
The trials, temptations, and woes,
Which darken this valley of tears,

title: A few more years shall roll
author: And take my sins away

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A few more years shall roll,
A few more seasons come;
And we shall be with those that rest,
Asleep within the tomb.
Then, O my Lord, prepare
My soul for that great day;
O wash me in thy precious blood,
And take my sins away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A few more suns shall set
O’er these dark hills of time;
And we shall be where suns are not,
A far serener clime.
Then, O my Lord, prepare
My soul for that blest day;
O wash me in thy precious blood,
And take my sins away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A few more storms shall beat
On this wild rocky shore;
And we shall be where tempests cease,
And surges swell no more.
Then, O my Lord, prepare
My soul for that calm day,
O wash me in thy precious blood,
And take my sins away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A few more struggles here,
A few more partings o’er,
A few more toils, a few more tears,
And we shall weep no more.
Then, O my Lord, prepare
My soul for that blest day;
O wash me in thy precious blood,
And take my sins away.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
A few more meetings here,
Shall cheer us on our way;
And we shall reach the endless rest,
The eternal Sabbath day.
Then, O my Lord, prepare
My soul for that sweet day,
O wash me in thy precious blood,

title: Here, we are but straying pilgrims

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Here, we are but straying pilgrims,
Here, our path is often dim,
But to cheer us on our journey,
Still we sing this way-side hymn.
CHORUS.
Yonder, over the rolling river,
Where the shining mansions rise,
Soon will be our home for ever,
And the smile of the blesséd Giver
Gladdens all our longing eyes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here, our feet are often weary,
On the hills that throng our way;
Here, the tempest darkly gathers,
But our hearts within us say—
Yonder, over the rolling river, etc.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here, our souls are often fearful,
Of the pilgrim’s lurking foe;
But the Lord is our defender,
And he tells us we may know,
Yonder, over the rolling river, etc.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here, our shadowed homes are transient,
And we meet the stranger’s frown;
So we’ll sing with joy while going.
E’en to death’s dark billow down—
Yonder, over the rolling river, etc.

title: O when shall I see Jesus
author: And take you home to rest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O when shall I see Jesus,
And dwell with him above,
To drink the flowing fountain
Of everlasting love?
When shall I be delivered
From this vain world of sin,
And with my blesséd Jesus
Drink endless pleasures in?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But now I am a soldier,
My Captain’s gone before:
He’s given me my orders,
And tells me not to fear.
And if I hold out faithful,
A crown of life he’ll give,
And all his valiant soldiers
Eternal life shall have.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Through grace I am determined
To conquer though I die;
And then away to Jesus
On wings of love I’ll fly.
Farewell to sin and sorrow,
I bid them both adieu:
And you, my friends, prove faithful,
And on your way pursue.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And if you meet with troubles
And trials on the way,
Then cast your care on Jesus,
And don’t forget to pray.
Gird on the heavenly armor
Of faith, and hope, and love,
And when your warfare’s ended,
You’ll reign with him above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O! do not be discouraged,
For Jesus is your Friend,
And if you long for knowledge,
On him you may depend;
Neither will he upbraid you,
Though often you request;
He’ll give you grace to conquer,

title: How long, O Lord, our Saviour
author: With joy thy face to see

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How long, O Lord, our Saviour,
Wilt thou remain away?
Our hearts are growing weary
Of thy so long delay;
O when shall come the moment,
When brighter far than morn,
The sunshine of thy glory,
Shall on thy people dawn.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How long, O gracious Master,
Wilt thou thy household leave?
So long hast thou now tarried,
Few thy return believe.
Immersed in sloth and folly,
Thy servants, Lord, we see,
And few of us stand ready
With joy to welcome thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How long, O heavenly Bridegroom,
How long wilt thou delay?
And yet how few are grieving
That thou dost absent stay:
Thy very bride, her portion
And calling hath forgot,
And seeks for ease and glory
Where thou, her Lord, art not.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O wake thy slumbering virgins,
Send forth the solemn cry—
Let all thy saints repeat it—
The Bridegroom draweth nigh;
May all our lamps be burning,
Our loins well girded be,
Each longing heart preparing

title: Rise, my soul, and stretch thy wings
author: And earth exchanged for heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Rivers to the ocean run,
Nor stay in all their course;
Fire ascending seeks the sun;
Both speed them to their source:
So a soul that’s born of God
Pants to view his glorious face,
Upward tends to his abode,
To rest in his embrace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Cease, ye pilgrims, cease to mourn;
Press onward to the prize;
Soon your Saviour will return
Triumphant in the skies:
Yet a season, and you know
Happy entrance will be given,
All your sorrows left below,

title: Go up, go up, my heart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Go up, go up, my heart,
Dwell with thy God above;
For here thou canst not rest,
Nor here give out thy love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Go up, go up, my heart,
Be not a trifler here;
Ascend above these clouds,
Dwell in a higher sphere.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let not thy love flow out
To things so soiled and dim;
Go up to heaven and God,
Take up thy love to him.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Waste not thy precious stores
On creature-love below;
To God that wealth belongs,
On him that wealth bestow.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: My spirit longs for thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My spirit longs for thee
Within my troubled breast,
Through I unworthy be
Of so divine a Guest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Of so divine a Guest
Unworthy though I be,
Yet has my heart no rest
Unless it come from thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Unless it come from thee,
In vain I look around;
In all that I can see,
No rest is to be found.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No rest is to be found,
But in thy blesséd love:
O let my wish be crowned,
And send it from above!

title: Purer yet and purer
author: Ne’er can be expressed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Purer yet and purer
I would be in mind,
Dearer yet and dearer
Every duty find:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hoping still, and trusting
God without a fear
Patiently believing
He will make all clear:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Calmer yet and calmer
Trial bear and pain,
Surer yet and surer
Peace at last to gain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Suffering still and doing,
To his will resigned,
And to God subduing
Heart, and will, and mind:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Higher yet and higher,
Out of clouds and night,
Nearer yet and nearer
Rising to the light—

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Oft these earnest longings
Swell within my breast,
Yet their inner meaning

title: I would not live alway: I ask not to stay

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I would not live alway: I ask not to stay
Where storm after storm rises dark o’er the way;
The few cloudy mornings that dawn on us here
Are enough for life’s woes, full enough for its cheer.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Who, who would live alway, away from his God,
Away from yon heaven, that blissful abode,
Where the rivers of pleasure flow o’er the bright plains,
And the noontide of glory eternally reigns;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Where the saints of all ages in harmony meet,
Their Saviour and brethren transported to greet,
While the anthems of rapture unceasingly roll,
And the smile of the Lord is the feast of the soul!

title: I am weary of straying; O fain would I rest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I am weary of straying; O fain would I rest,
In that far distant land of the pure and the blest;
Where sin can no longer her blandishment spread,
And tears and temptations for ever are fled.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I am weary of hoping, where hope is untrue,
As fair but as fleeting, as morning’s bright dew;
I long for the land whose blest promise alone
Is as changeless and sure as eternity’s throne.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I am weary of sighing o’er sorrows of earth,
O’er joy’s glowing visions, that fade at their birth,
O’er pangs of the loved, which we can not assuage,
O’er the blightings of youth, and the weakness of age.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I am weary of loving what passes away—
The sweetest and dearest, alas, may not stay!
I long for that land where those partings are o’er,
And death and the tomb can divide hearts no more.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: My rest is in heaven—my home is not here

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My rest is in heaven—my home is not here;
Then why should I murmur when trials appear?
Be hushed, my sad spirit, the worst that may come
But shortens thy journey and hastens thee home.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Though foes and temptations my progress oppose,
They only make heaven more sweet at the close;
Come joy or come sorrow—the worst may befall,
One moment in heaven will make up for all.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The thorn and the thistle around me may grow,
I would not repose upon roses below;
I ask not my portion, I seek not my rest,
Till, seated with Jesus, I lean on his breast.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
A scrip for the way and a staff in my hand,
I march on in haste through the enemy’s land:
The road may be rough, but it can not be long:
So I’ll smooth it with hope, and I’ll cheer it with song.

title: Not here! not here! not where the sparkling waters

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Not here! not here! not where the sparkling waters
Fade into mocking sands as we draw near;
Where in the wilderness each footstep falters—
“I shall be satisfied;” but, O! not here!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not here—where all the dreams of bliss deceive us,
Where the worn spirit never gains its goal;
Where, haunted ever by the thought that grieves us,
Across us floods of bitter memory roll.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is a land where every pulse is thrilling
With rapture earth’s sojourners may not know,
Where heaven’s repose the weary heart is stilling,
And peacefully life’s time-tossed currents flow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Far out of sight, while yet the flesh enfolds us,
Lies the fair country where our hearts abide,
And of its bliss is nought more wondrous told us
Than these few words—“I shall be satisfied.”

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Satisfied! satisfied! The spirit’s yearning
For sweet companionship with kindred minds—
The silent love that here meets no returning—
The inspiration which no language finds—

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Shall they be satisfied? The soul’s vague longing—
The aching void which nothing earthly fills?
O! what desires upon my soul are thronging
As I look upward to the heavenly hills.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Thither my weak and weary steps are tending—
Saviour and Lord! with thy frail child abide!
Guide me toward home, where, all my wanderings ending,
I shall see thee, and “shall be satisfied.”

title: Beyond the smiling and the weeping

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Beyond the smiling and the weeping,
I shall be soon;
Beyond the waking and the sleeping,
Beyond the sowing and the reaping,
I shall be soon.
Love, rest, and home!
Sweet home!
Lord, tarry not, but come.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Beyond the blooming and the fading,
I shall be soon;
Beyond the shining and the shading,
Beyond the hoping and the dreading
I shall be soon.
Love, rest, and home!
Sweet home!
Lord, tarry not, but come.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Beyond the rising and the setting,
I shall be soon;
Beyond the calming and the fretting,
Beyond remembering and forgetting,
I shall be soon.
Love, rest, and home!
Sweet home!
Lord, tarry not, but come.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Beyond the parting and the meeting,
I shall be soon;
Beyond the farewell and the greeting,
Beyond the pulse’s fever beating,
I shall be soon.
Love, rest, and home!
Sweet home!
Lord, tarry not, but come.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Beyond the frost-chain and the fever,
I shall be soon;
Beyond the rock-waste and the river,
Beyond the ever and the never
I shall be soon.
Love, rest, and home!
Sweet home!
Lord, tarry not, but come.

title: O tell me no more of this world’s vain store

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The souls that believe, in glory shall live,
And me in that number will Jesus receive;
My soul, don’t delay, he calls thee away,
Rise, follow the Saviour, and bless the glad day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No mortal doth know what he can bestow,
What light, strength and comfort—go after him, go;
Lo, onward I move to a city above,
None guesses how wondrous my journey will prove.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Great spoils I shall win, from death, hell, and sin,
’Midst outward afflictions, I feel Christ within;
And when I’m to die, receive me, I’ll cry,
For Jesus has loved me—I can not tell why.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But this I do find, we two are so joined,
He’ll not live in glory, and leave me behind,
So this is the race I’m running, through grace,
Henceforth, till admitted to see my Lord’s face.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Now this is my care, that my neighbors may share
These blessings: to seek them will none of you dare?
In bondage, O why, and death, will you lie,
When Jesus assures you free grace is so nigh?

title: Lead us, heavenly Father! lead us
author: Nothing can our peace destroy

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lead us, heavenly Father! lead us
O’er the world’s tempestuous sea;
Guard us, guide us, keep us, feed us,
For we have no help but thee.
Yet possessing
Every blessing,
If our God our Father be.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Saviour! breathe forgiveness o’er us;
All our weakness thou dost know;
Thou didst tread this earth before us,
Thou didst feel its keenest woe.
Lone and dreary,
Faint and weary
Through the desert thou didst go.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Spirit of our God descending!
Fill our hearts with heavenly joy;
Love with every passion blending,
Pleasure that can never cloy.
Thus provided,
Pardoned, guided,

title: My feet are worn and weary with the march

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My feet are worn and weary with the march
O’er the rough road and up the steep hill-side;
O city of our God! I fain would see
Thy pastures green, where peaceful waters glide.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My hands are worn and weary, toiling on,
Day after day, for perishable meat;
O city of our God! I fain would rest—
I sigh to gain thy glorious mercy-seat.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My garments, travel-worn and stained with dust,
Oft rent by briers and thorns that crowd my way,
Would fain be made, O Lord, my righteousness!
Spotless and white in heaven’s unclouded ray.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My eyes are weary looking at the sin,
Impiety, and scorn upon the earth;
O city of our God! within thy walls
All—all are clothed again with thy new birth.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
My heart is weary of its own deep sin—
Sinning, repenting, sinning still again;
When shall my soul thy glorious presence feel,
And find, dear Saviour, it is free from stain?

sections.label: Verse 6
Verse 7
sections.text:
Love thou the path of sorrow that he trod;
Toil on, and wait in patience for thy rest:
O city of our God! we soon shall see
Thy glorious walls—home of the loved and blest.

title: Soon and for ever the breaking of day
author: TEMPTATIONS AND CONFLICTS

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Soon and for ever the breaking of day
Shall chase all the night-clouds of sorrow away;
Soon and for ever we’ll see as we’re seen,
And know the deep meaning of things that have been,
Where fightings without and conflicts within
Shall weary no more in the warfare with sin—
Where tears, and where fears, and where death shall be never,
Christians with Christ shall be soon and for ever.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon and for ever—such promise our trust—
Though ashes to ashes, and dust be to dust,
Soon and for ever our union shall be
Made perfect, our glorious Redeemer, in thee:
When the cares and the sorrows of time shall be o’er,
Its pangs and its partings remembered no more;
Where life can not fail and where death can not sever,
Christians with Christ shall be soon and for ever.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Soon and for ever the work shall be done,
The warfare accomplished, the victory won;
Soon and for ever the soldier lay down
The sword for a harp, the cross for a crown:
Then droop not in sorrow, despond not in fear,
A glorious to-morrow is brightening and near,
When—blesséd reward for each faithful endeavor—
Christians with Christ shall be soon and for ever!

title: In thee, O Lord, I put my trust
author: Then will I give thee all the praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In thee, O Lord, I put my trust,
Thou art my portion and my song;
Thy ways, with me, are always just,
But mine, with thee, are often wrong.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I can not do the things I would,
For sin is in my flesh concealed;
So evil takes the place of good,
And all my weakness stands revealed.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But thou, O Lord, canst make me clean,
And give me strength to do the right;
While on thy promises I lean,
All darkness changes into light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O give me grace the wrong to shun,
The right to follow all my days,
And when life’s victory is won,

title: The Christian warrior, see him stand

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Christian warrior, see him stand
In the whole armor of his God;
The Spirit’s sword is in his hand,
His feet are with the gospel shod.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In panoply of truth complete,
Salvation’s helmet on his head,
With righteousness, a breastplate meet;
And faith’s broad shield before him spread.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus, strong in his Redeemer’s strength,
Sin, death, and hell he tramples down,
Fights the good fight, and wins at length,
Through mercy, an immortal crown.

title: Awake, my soul! lift up thine eyes

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
See where rebellious passions rage,
And fierce desires and lust engage;
The meanest foe of all the train
Has thousands and ten thousands slain.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, then, my soul! now learn to wield
The weight of thine immortal shield;
Put on the armor from above,
Of heavenly truth, and heavenly love.

title: Silent, like men in solemn haste

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Silent, like men in solemn haste,
Girded wayfarers of the waste,
We press along the narrow road
That leads to life, to bliss, to God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We fling aside the weight and sin,
Resolved the victory to win;
We know the peril, but our eyes
Rest on the splendor of the prize.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
No love of present gain nor ease,
No seeking man nor self to please.—
With the brave heart and steady eye,
We onward march to victory.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Night is far spent, and morn is near—
Morn of the cloudless and the clear;
’Tis but a little and we come
To our reward, our crown, our home.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Another year—it may be less—
And we have crossed the wilderness,
Finished the toil, the rest begun,
The battle fought, the triumph won.

title: When Israel, of the Lord beloved
author: A burning and a shining light

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When Israel, of the Lord beloved,
Out from the land of bondage came,
Her father’s God before her moved,
An awful Guide, in smoke and flame.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
By day, along th’ astonished lands
The cloudy pillar glided slow;
By night Arabia’s crimsoned sands
Returned the fiery column’s glow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thus present still, though now unseen,
O Lord, when shines the prosperous day,
Be thoughts of thee a cloudy screen,
To temper the deceitful ray.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And O, when gathers on our path,
In shade and storm, the frequent night,
Be thou long-suffering, slow to wrath,

title: O Israel, to thy tents repair

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Israel, to thy tents repair:
Why thus secure on hostile ground?
Thy King commands thee to beware
For many foes thy camp surround.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The trumpet gives a martial strain:
O Israel, gird thee for the fight!
Arise, the combat to maintain,
And put thine enemies to flight!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou shouldst not sleep, as others do;
Awake; be vigilant; be brave!
The coward, and the sluggard too,
Must wear the fetters of the slave.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A nobler lot is cast for thee;
A kingdom waits thee in the skies:
With such a hope, shall Israel flee,
Or yield, through weariness, the prize?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
No! let a careless world repose
And slumber on through life’s short day,
While Israel to the conflict goes,
And bears the glorious prize away!

title: The tempter to my soul hath said
author: His presence guards his people’s path

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The tempter to my soul hath said—
“There is no help in God for thee;”
Lord! lift thou up thy servant’s head,
My glory, shield, and solace be.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
I laid me down and slept—I woke—
Thou, Lord! my spirit didst sustain;
Bright from the east the morning broke—
Thy comforts rose on me again.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: When, in the hour of lonely woe

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When, in the hour of lonely woe,
I give my sorrows leave to flow,
And anxious fear and dark distrust
Weigh down my spirit to the dust;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When not e’en friendship’s gentle aid
Can heal the wounds the world has made,
O this shall check each rising sigh—
My Saviour is for ever nigh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His counsels and upholding care
My safety and my comfort are:
And he shall guide me all my days,
Till glory crown the work of grace.

title: Lord! I have foes without, within

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord! I have foes without, within,
The world, the flesh, indwelling sin,
Life’s daily ills, temptation’s power,
The tempted spirit’s weaker hour.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yet, in the gloom of silent thought,
I call to mind what God hath wrought—
Thy wonders in the days of old,
Thy mercies great and manifold.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, then to thee I stretch my hands,
Like failing streams through desert sands;
I thirst for thee, as harvest plains,
Parched by the summer, thirst for rains!

sections.label: Verse 4

title: When darkness long has vailed my mind
author: And thy rebellious child is still

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When darkness long has vailed my mind,
And smiling day once more appears;
Then, my Creator! then I find
The folly of my doubts and fears.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Straight I upbraid my wandering heart,
And blush that I should ever be
Thus prone to act so base a part,
Or harbor one hard thought of thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, let me then at length be taught
What I am still so slow to learn—
That God is love, and changes not,
Nor knows the shadow of a turn.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sweet truth, and easy to repeat!
But, when my faith is sharply tried,
I find myself a learner yet,
Unskillful, weak, and apt to slide.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: By faith in Christ I walk with God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
By faith in Christ I walk with God,
With heaven, my journey’s end, in view;
Supported by his staff and rod,
My road is safe and pleasant too.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I travel through a desert wide,
Where many round me blindly stray;
But he vouchsafes to be my Guide,
And keeps me in the narrow way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The wilderness affords no food,
But God for my support prepares,
Provides me every needful good,
And frees my soul from wants and cares.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
I pity all that worldlings talk
Of pleasures that will quickly end;
Be this my choice, O Lord! to walk
With thee, my Guide, my Guard, my Friend.

title: Awake, our souls; away, our fears
author: Nor tire amid the heavenly road

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
The mighty God, whose matchless power
Is ever new and ever young,
And firm endures, while endless years
Their everlasting circles run.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
From thee, the overflowing spring,
Our souls shall drink a full supply;
While those who trust their native strength,
Shall melt away, and droop, and die.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: The billows swell, the winds are high

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
O Lord, the pilot’s part perform,
And guide and guard me through the storm;
Defend me from each threatening ill:
Control the waves; say, “Peace! be still.”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Amid the roaring of the sea,
My soul still hangs her hope on thee;
Thy constant love, thy faithful care,
Is all that saves me from despair.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though tempest-tossed and half a wreck,
My Saviour through the floods I seek:
Let neither winds nor stormy main
Force back my shattered bark again.

title: O where is now that glowing love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O where is now that glowing love
That marked our union with the Lord?
Our hearts were fixed on things above.
Nor could the world a joy afford.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Where is the zeal that led us then
To make our Saviour’s glory known;
That freed us from the fear of men,
And kept our eyes on him alone?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Where are the happy seasons spent
In fellowship with him we loved?
The sacred joy, the sweet content,
The blessédness that then we proved?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Behold, again we turn to thee,
O cast us not away, though vile!
No peace we have, no joy we see,
O Lord, our God, but in thy smile.

title: Thou hidden love of God, whose hight

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou hidden love of God, whose hight,
Whose depth, unfathomed, no man knows,
I see from far thy beauteous light:
Inly I sigh for thy repose;
My heart is pained; nor can it be
At rest till it find rest in thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
’Tis mercy all, that thou hast brought
My mind to seek her peace in thee;
Yet, while I seek, but find thee not,
No peace my wandering soul shall see.
O, when shall all my wanderings end,
And all my steps to thee-ward tend?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Is there a thing beneath the sun
That strives with thee my heart to share?
Ah, tear it thence, and reign alone,
The Lord of every motion there:
Then shall my heart from earth be free,
When it hath found repose in thee.

title: Rise, O my soul! pursue the path
author: Which led them safe to heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rise, O my soul! pursue the path
By ancient heroes trod;
Ambitious view those holy men
Who lived and walked with God.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
’Twas through the Lamb’s most precious blood
They conquered every foe:
And to his power and matchless grace,
Their crowns and honor owe.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord, may we ever keep in view
The patterns thou hast given,
And ne’er forsake the blessed road

title: Christians, keep your armor bright
author: The victory is ours

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Christians, keep your armor bright,
Rejoice, give thanks, and sing;
In union strong together fight;
Hosanna to our King!
Come, laud and magnify his name,
Nor let his praises cease;
His ways are ways of pleasantness
And all his paths are peace.
CHORUS.
O it will be glorious.
With crowns and palms victorious,
And Jesus reigning over us,
When our sad warfare’s o’er.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We will not act the coward’s part,
But onward all proceed:
Our Captain shall his grace impart
In every time of need.
Great peace have they who love his cause,
And on his word rely;
From such as keep his holy laws,
The enemy will fly.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The world and sin may grieve us sore,
And rouse our weakest fears;
Our march is but a few days more
Through this dark vale of tears.
Death may assail, and Satan too,
With his opposing powers;
But let us prove our valor true,

title: O thou, from whom all goodness flows

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou, from whom all goodness flows,
I lift my soul to thee;
In all my sorrows, conflicts, woes,
O Lord, remember me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If for thy sake, upon my name
Reproach and shame shall be,
I’ll hail reproach and welcome shame;
O Lord remember me!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
When, in the solemn hour of death,
I wait thy just decree,
Be this the prayer of my last breath—
O Lord, remember me!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And when before thy throne I stand,
And lift my soul to thee,
Then with the saints at thy right hand,
O Lord, remember me!

title: Am I a soldier of the cross
author: The glory shall be thine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Am I a soldier of the cross,
A follower of the Lamb?
And shall I fear to own his cause,
Or blush to speak his name?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Must I be carried to the skies
On flowery beds of ease,
While others fought to win the prize,
And sailed through bloody seas?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Are there no foes for me to face?
Must I not stem the flood?
Is this vile world a friend to grace,
To help me on to God?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sure I must fight, if I would reign;
Increase my courage, Lord!
I’ll bear the toil, endure the pain,
Supported by thy word.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy saints, in all this glorious war,
Shall conquer, though they die;
They see the triumph from afar,
With Hope’s exulting eye.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
When that illustrious day shall rise,
And all thine armies shine
In robes of victory through the skies,

title: Kind Father, look with pity now
author: His love my endless song

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Kind Father, look with pity now
On one by sin defiled;
While at the mercy-seat I bow,
O bless thy erring child.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My struggles, Lord, to do thy will,
How poor and weak they are!
But thou art gracious to me still,
Then hear my humble prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let love upon my broken heart
Pour out its healing balm;
Bid all my trembling fears depart—
My troubled spirit calm.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And now my hope new courage takes,
My faith grows strong and sure;
The cloud from off my vision breaks,
Again my heart is pure.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
My soul mounts up on wings of light
And soars to climes above—
The regions where all things are bright,
The home of Peace and Love.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
There, soon I’ll sing of love divine,
With all the ransomed throng,
There, Jesus shall be ever mine,

title: I’m not ashamed to own my Lord
author: Appoint for me a place

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I’m not ashamed to own my Lord,
Nor to defend his cause,
Maintain the honors of his word,
The glory of his cross.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, my Lord, I know his name,
His name is all my trust;
Nor will he put my soul to shame,
Nor let my hope be lost.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Firm as his throne his promise stands,
And he can well secure
What I’ve committed to his hands
Till the decisive hour.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then will he own my worthless name
Before his Father’s face,
And in the new Jerusalem

title: Awake, my soul, stretch every nerve
author: We’ll lay our honors down

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, my soul, stretch every nerve,
And press with vigor on;
A heavenly race demands your zeal,
And an immortal crown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
’Tis God’s all-animating voice
That calls thee from on high:
’Tis his own hand presents the prize
To thy aspiring eye.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A cloud of witnesses around
Holds thee in full survey:
Forget the steps already trod,
And onward urge the way.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest Saviour, introduced by thee,
Have we our race begun!
And crowned with victory at thy feet

title: Nay, tell us not of dangers dire
author: We rest upon his arm

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Nay, tell us not of dangers dire
That lie in duty’s path;
A warrior of the cross can feel
No fear of human wrath.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Where’er the prince of darkness holds
His earthly reign abhorred,
Sword of the Spirit, thee we draw,
And battle for the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We go! we go, to break the chains
That bind the erring mind,
And give the freedom that we feel
To all of human kind.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But, O, we wear no burnished steel,
And seek no gory field;
Our weapon is the word of God,
His promise is our shield.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: How oft, alas! this wretched heart
author: And let me rove no more

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How oft, alas! this wretched heart
Has wandered from the Lord!
How oft my roving thoughts depart—
Forgetful of his word!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yet sovereign mercy calls—“Return!”
Dear Lord! and may I come?
My vile ingratitude I mourn;
O! take the wanderer home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And canst thou—wilt thou yet forgive,
And bid my crimes remove!
And shall a pardoned rebel live
To speak thy wondrous love?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Almighty grace! thy healing power,
How glorious—how divine!
That can to life and bliss restore
A heart so vile as mine!

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Father, when o’er our trembling hearts
author: Help thou our unbelief

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, when o’er our trembling hearts
Doubt’s shadows gathering brood,
When faith in thee almost departs,
And gloomiest fears intrude,
Forsake us not, O God of grace,
But send those fears relief;
Grant us again to see thy face;
Lord, help our unbelief.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When sorrow comes, and joys are flown,
And fondest hopes be dead,
And blessings, long esteemed our own,
Are now for ever fled—
When the bright promise of our spring
Is but a withering leaf—
Lord, to thy truth still let us cling,
Help thou our unbelief.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And when the powers of nature fail
Upon the couch of pain,
Nor love, nor friendship can avail
The spirit to detain;
Then, Father, be our closing eyes
Undimmed by tears of grief,
And if a trembling doubt arise,

title: The Saviour bids us watch and pray
author: To heaven’s eternal joys

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Saviour bids us watch and pray,
Through life’s brief, fleeting hour,
And gives the Spirit’s quickening ray
To those who seek his power.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
The Saviour bids us watch and pray;
For soon the hour will come
That calls us from the earth away,
To our eternal home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O Saviour, we would watch and pray,
And hear thy sacred voice,
And walk, as thou hast marked the way,

title: As o’er the past my memory strays

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As o’er the past my memory strays,
Why heaves the secret sigh?
’Tis that I mourn departed days,
Still unprepared to die.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The world and worldly things beloved,
My anxious thoughts employed;
And time, unhallowed, unimproved,
Presents a fearful void.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yet, Holy Father, wild despair
Chase from my laboring breast;
Thy grace it is which prompts the prayer,
That grace can do the rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My life’s brief remnant all be thine;
And when thy sure decree
Bids me this fleeting breath resign,
O, speed my soul to thee.

title: Alas, what hourly dangers rise
author: From happiness and thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Alas, what hourly dangers rise!
What snares beset my way!
To heaven, O, let me lift mine eyes,
And hourly watch and pray.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How oft my mournful thoughts complain,
And melt in flowing tears!
My weak resistance, ah, how vain!
How strong my foes and fears!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O gracious God! in whom I live,
My feeble efforts aid;
Help me to watch, and pray, and strive,
Though trembling and afraid.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Increase my faith, increase my hope,
When foes and fears prevail;
And bear my fainting spirit up,
Or soon my strength will fail.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O, keep me in thy heavenly way,
And bid the tempter flee!
And let me never, never stray

title: “For ever with the Lord,”
author: Expands the bow of peace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
“For ever with the Lord,”
Amen, so let it be;
Life from the dead is in that word,
’Tis immortality.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here in the body pent,
Absent from him I roam,
Yet nightly pitch my moving tent
A day’s march nearer home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My Father’s house on high,
Home of my soul, how near
At times, to faith’s aspiring eye,
Thy golden gates appear!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ah, then my spirit faints,
To reach the land I love,
The bright inheritance of saints,
Jerusalem above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yet doubts still intervene,
And all my comfort flies;
Like Noah’s dove, I flit between
Rough seas and stormy skies.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: This world is poor from shore to shore
author: I’m on my way to heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
This world is poor from shore to shore,
And, like a baseless vision,
Its lofty domes and brilliant ore,
Its gems and crowns are vain and poor;
There’s nothing rich but heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Creation’s mighty fabric all
Shall be to atoms riven—
The skies consume, the planets fall,
Convulsions rock this earthly ball;
There’s nothing firm but heaven.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
The clouds disperse—the light appears,
My sins are all forgiven;
Triumphant grace has quelled my fears:
Roll on, thou sun! fly swift, my years!

title: My soul, be on thy guard
author: To his divine abode

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Ne’er think the victory won,
Nor lay thine armor down:
Thy arduous work will not be done
Till thou obtain thy crown.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: A charge to keep I have
author: I shall for ever die

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A charge to keep I have,
A God to glorify,
A never-dying soul to save,
And fit it for the sky.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To serve the present age,
My calling to fulfill;
O, may it all my powers engage
To do my Master’s will.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Arm me with jealous care
As in thy sight to live;
And O, thy servant, Lord, prepare
A strict account to give.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Help me to watch and pray,
And on thyself rely,
Assured, if I my trust betray,

title: Arise, ye saints, arise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Arise, ye saints, arise!
The Lord our Leader is;
The foe before his banner flies,
For victory is his.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lead on, almighty Lord,
Lead on, to victory!
Encouraged by the bright reward:
With joy we’ll follow thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We’ll follow thee, our Guide,
Our Saviour and our King;
We’ll follow thee, through grace supplied
From heaven’s eternal spring.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We hope to see the day
When all our toils shall cease;
When we shall cast our arms away,
And dwell in endless peace.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Till, of the prize possessed,
We hear of war no more,
And O, sweet thought! for ever rest
On yonder peaceful shore!

title: Hark, how the watchmen cry
author: Are all in Jesus’ name

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark, how the watchmen cry!
Attend the trumpet’s sound;
Stand to your arms: the foe is nigh—
The powers of hell surround.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who bow to Christ’s command,
Your arms and hearts prepare;
The day of battle is at hand—
Go forth to glorious war.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See on the mountain top
The standard of your God;
In Jesus’ name ’tis lifted up,
All stained with hallowed blood.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His standard-bearers, now
To all the nations call:
To Jesus’ cross, ye nations bow;
He bore the cross for all.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6

title: Soldiers of Christ, arise
author: And stand entire at last

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Soldiers of Christ, arise!
And put your armor on,
Strong in the strength which God supplies
Through his belovéd Son.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Strong in the Lord of Hosts,
And in his mighty power;
Who in the strength of Jesus trusts,
Is more than conqueror.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Stand, then, in his great might,
With all his strength endued;
But take, to arm you for the fight,
The panoply of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Leave no unguarded place,
No weakness of the soul;
Take every virtue, every grace,
And fortify the whole.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
That having all things done,
And all your conflicts past,
You may o’ercome through Christ alone,

title: Give to the winds thy fears

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Give to the winds thy fears,
Hope, and be undismayed;
God hears thy sighs, and counts thy tears,
God shall lift up thy head.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Through waves, through clouds and storms,
He gently clears thy way;
Wait thou his time; so shall this night
Soon end in joyous day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Still heavy is thy heart!
Still sink thy spirits down!
Cast off the weight, let fear depart,
Bid every care be gone.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Far, far above thy thought
His counsel shall appear,
When fully he the work hath wrought,
That caused thy needless fear.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
What, though thou rulest not!
Yet heaven, and earth, and hell
Proclaim, God sitteth on the throne,
And ruleth all things well!

title: My soul, it is thy God
author: In everlasting light

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My soul, it is thy God
Who calls thee by his grace;
Now loose thee from each cumbering load,
And bend thee to the race.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: God of mercy! God of love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of mercy! God of love!
Hear our sad, repentant songs;
Listen to thy suppliant ones,
Thou, to whom all grace belongs!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
These, and every secret fault,
Filled with grief and shame we own;
Humbled at thy feet we bow,
Seeking strength from thee alone.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
God of mercy! God of love!
Hear our sad repentant songs;
O, restore thy suppliant ones,
Thou to whom all grace belongs!

title: Oft in sorrow, oft in woe

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oft in sorrow, oft in woe,
Onward, Christian, onward go;
Fight the fight, maintain the strife,
Strengthened with the bread of life.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Sleep not, soldier of the cross
author: Makes more sweet thy coming rest

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Up! and take thy shield and sword;
Up! it is the call of heaven:
Shrink not faithless from the Lord:
Nobly strive as he hath striven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Break through all the force of ill;
Tread the might of passion down—
Struggling onward, onward still,
To the conquering Saviour’s crown!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Through the midst of toil and pain,
Let this thought ne’er leave thy breast:
Every triumph thou dost gain

title: Onward, Christian, though the region

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Onward, Christian, though the region
Where thou art be drear and lone,
God hath set a guardian legion
Very near thee—press thou on!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Listen, Christian, their hosanna
Rolleth o’er thee—“God is love,”
Write upon thy red-cross banner,
“Upward ever—heaven’s above.”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By the thorn-road, and none other,
Is the mount of vision won;
Tread it without shrinking, brother!
Jesus trod it—press thou on!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By thy trustful, calm endeavor,
Guiding, cheering, like the sun,
Earth-bound hearts thou shalt deliver;
O, for their sake, press thou on!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Be this world the wiser, stronger,
For thy life of pain and peace;
While it needs thee, O no longer
Pray thou for thy quick release:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Pray thou, Christian, daily, rather,
That thou be a faithful son;
By the prayer of Jesus—“Father,
Not my will, but thine, be done!”

title: Whither goest thou, pilgrim stranger
author: Then my pilgrimage will end

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Whither goest thou, pilgrim stranger,
Passing through this darksome vale?
Knowest thou not ’tis full of danger,
And will not thy courage fail?
CHORUS.
I am bound for the kingdom,
Will you go to glory with me?
Hallelujah! praise you the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Pilgrim, thou dost justly call me,
Wandering o’er this waste so wide;
Yet no harm will e’er befall me,
While I’m blest with such a guide.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Such a guide—no guide attends thee:
Hence for thee my fears arise;
If some guardian power befriend thee,
’Tis unseen by mortal eyes.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Yes, unseen—but still believe me,
Such a guide my steps attends;
He’ll in every strait relieve me,
He from every harm defends.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Pilgrim! see that stream before thee!
Darkly winding through the vale;
Should its deadly waves roll o’er thee,
Would not then thy courage fail?

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Holy Father, thou hast taught me
author: Keep me ever at thy side

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
In the world will foes assail me,
Craftier, stronger far than I;
And the strife may never fail me,
Well I know, before I die.
Therefore, Lord, I come, believing
Thou canst give the power I need;
Through the prayer of faith receiving
Strength—the Spirit’s strength, indeed.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I would trust in thy protecting,
Wholly rest upon thine arm;
Follow wholly thy directing,
Thou, mine only guard from harm!
Keep me from mine own undoing,
Help me turn to thee when tried,
Still my footsteps, Father, viewing,

title: Dark and thorny is the desert

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Dark and thorny is the desert
Through which pilgrims make their way;
But beyond this vale of sorrow
Lie the realms of endless day.
Dear young soldiers, do not murmur
At the troubles of the way;
Meet the tempest—fight with courage—
Never faint, but often pray.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
There on flowery fields of pleasure,
And the hills of endless rest,
Joy, and peace, and love, shall ever,
Reign and triumph in your breast.
There ten thousand flaming seraphs
Fly across the heavenly plain;
There they sing immortal praises!
Glory, glory is their theme.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But, methinks, a sweeter concert
Makes the crystal arches ring,
And a song is heard in Zion
Which the angels can not sing:
Who can paint those sons of glory,
Ransomed souls that dwell on high,
Who, with golden harps, for ever
Sound redemption through the sky.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
See the heavenly host in rapture
Gazing on these shining bands;
Wondering at their costly garments,
And the laurels in their hands;
There upon the golden pavement,
See the ransomed march along!
While the splendid courts of glory
Sweetly echo with their song!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Here I see the under shepherds,
And the flocks they fed below,
Here with joy they dwell together,
Jesus is their shepherd now.
Hail! you happy, happy spirits!
Welcome to the blissful plain—
Glory, honor, and salvation;
Reign, sweet Shepherd, ever reign.

title: Must Simon bear the cross alone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Must Simon bear the cross alone,
And all the world go free?
No, there’s a cross for every one,
And there’s a cross for me.
Yes, there’s a cross on Calvary,
Through which by faith the crown I see;
To me ’tis pardon bringing;
O that’s the cross for me!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How happy are the saints above,
Who once went mourning here!
But now they taste unmingled love,
And joy without a tear.
For perfect love will dry the tear,
And cast out all tormenting fear,
Which round my heart is clinging;
O that’s the love for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We’ll bear the consecrated cross,
Till from the cross we’re free;
And then go home to wear the crown,
For there’s a crown for me.
Yes, there’s a crown in heaven above,
The purchase of my Saviour’s love,
For me at his appearing;
O that’s the crown for me!

sections.label: Verse 4

title: O my soul! what means this sadness

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
What though Satan’s strong temptations
Vex and grieve thee day by day
And thy sinful inclinations
Often fill thee with dismay;
Thou shalt conquer,
Through the Lamb’s redeeming blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though ten thousand ills beset thee,
From without and from within,
Jesus saith he’ll ne’er forget thee,
But will save from hell and sin.
He is faithful
To perform his gracious word.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
O that I could now adore him
Like the heavenly host above,
Who for ever bow before him,
And unceasing sing his love,
Happy songsters!
When shall I your chorus join?

title: Here behold me, as I cast me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Here behold me, as I cast me
At thy throne, O glorious King!
Tears fast thronging, child-like longing,
Son of man to thee I bring.
Let me find thee—
Me, a poor and worthless thing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Look upon me, Lord, I pray thee;
Let thy Spirit dwell in mine:
Thou hast sought me, thou hast bought me,
Only thee to know I pine:
Let me find thee—
Take my heart and grant me thine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Nought I ask for, nought I strive for,
But thy grace, so rich and free,
That thou givest whom thou lovest,
And who truly cleave to thee;
Let me find thee—
He hath all things who hath thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Earthly treasure, mirth and pleasure,
Glorious name or richest hoard
Are but weary, void, and dreary,
To the heart that longs for God:
Let me find thee—
I am ready, mighty Lord.

title: The sun above us gleaming
author: O that’s the land for me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The sun above us gleaming
Is not the sun for me;
Though joyful be his beaming,
And beautiful to see;
There is a Sun of Righteousness
Who cheers and saves me by his grace,
All copious on me streaming,
O that’s the Sun for me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The kings and lords of nations,
Are not the kings for me;
Too low their highest stations;
Too mean their dignity:
The King of kings and Lord of lords,
Almighty in his ways and words,
The word of his salvation,
O that’s the king for me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This house of death and mourning
Is not the house for me,
Where all to dust are turning,
In tears and agony;
But there’s a house not made with hands,
It ever stood and ever stands,
Beyond the world’s last burning;
O that’s the house for me.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
This land of sin and sorrow,
Is not the land for me,
Where anguish oft I borrow
From dying company;
Th’ immortal land is far away,
I’ll enter it on some bright day,
That day may be to-morrow—

title: O Saviour whose mercy, severe in its kindness

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Saviour whose mercy, severe in its kindness,
Hath chastened my wanderings and guided my way,
Adored be the power that hath pitied my blindness,
And weaned me from phantoms that smiled to betray.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Enchanted with all that was dazzling and fair,
I followed the rainbow—I caught at the toy;
And still in displeasure thy goodness was there,
Disappointing the hope, and defeating the joy.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
So, cured of my folly, yet cured but in part,
I turned to the refuge thy pity displayed;
And still did this eager and credulous heart
Weave visions of promise, that bloomed but to fade.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
I dreamed of celestial reward and renown,
I grasped at the triumph that blesses the brave;
I asked for the palm branch, the robe, and the crown,
I asked, and thou showedst me the cross and a grave!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Subdued and instructed, at length to thy will,
My hopes, and my wishes, my all I resign;
O give me a heart that can wait and be still,
Nor know of a wish or a pleasure but thine.

sections.label: Verse 8

title: The captive’s oar may pause upon the galley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The captive’s oar may pause upon the galley,
The soldier sleep beneath his pluméd crest,
And peace may fold her wing o’er hill and valley,
But thou, O Christian! must not take thy rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Wilt thou find rest of soul in thy returning
To that old path thou hast so vainly trod?
Hast thou forgotten all thy weary yearning
To walk among the children of thy God?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Canst thou forget thy Christian superscription—
Behold we count them happy which endure?
What treasure wouldst thou, in the land Egyptian,
Repass the stormy waters to secure?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And God will come in his own time and power,
To set his earnest-hearted children free;
Watch only through this dark and painful hour,
And the bright morning yet will break for thee!

title: Breast the wave, Christian, when it is strongest

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Shall we grow weary in our watch

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Shall we grow weary in our watch,
And murmur at the long delay,
Impatient of our Father’s time
And his appointéd way?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, oft a deeper test of faith
Than prison-cell, or martyr’s stake,
The self-renouncing watchfulness
Of silent prayer may make.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We gird us bravely to rebuke
Our erring brother in the wrong;
And in the ear of pride and power
Our warning voice is strong.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Easier to smite with Peter’s sword,
Than watch one hour in humbling prayer;
Life’s great things, like the Syrian lord,
Our hearts can do and dare.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But, O, we shrink from Jordan’s side,
From waters which alone can save;
And murmur for Abana’s banks
And Pharpar’s brighter wave.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O thou, who in the garden’s shade
Didst wake thy weary ones again,
Who slumbered at that fearful hour,
Forgetful of thy pain—

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Bend o’er us now, as over them,
And set our sleep-bound spirits free,
Nor leave us slumbering in the watch
Our souls should keep with thee!

title: God of our salvation
author: SUBMISSION AND DELIVERANCE

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God of our salvation!
Unto thee we pray;
Hear our supplication,
Be our strength and stay.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Wretchéd and unworthy,
Poor, and sick, and blind,
Prostrate we adore thee,
Call thy grace to mind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He that dwelleth near thee,
Safely shall abide;
Ever love and fear thee,
In thy strength confide.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sure is thy protection,
Safe is thy defense,
While in deep affliction,
Woe, or pestilence.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
God of our salvation!
Saviour, Prince of Peace,
Boundless thy compassion,
Infinite thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Be still, my heart! these anxious cares

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Be still, my heart! these anxious cares,
To thee are burdens, thorns, and snares;
They cast dishonor on thy Lord,
And contradict his gracious word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Brought safely by his hand thus far,
Why wilt thou now give place to fear?
How canst thou want if he provide,
Or lose thy way with such a guide?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Did ever trouble yet befall,
And he refuse to hear thy call?
And has he not his promise passed,
That thou shalt overcome at last?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He who has helped me hitherto
Will help me all my journey through,
And give me daily cause to raise
New trophies to his endless praise.

title: O Lord, thy counsels and thy care

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord, thy counsels and thy care,
My safety and my comfort are;
And thou shalt guide me all my days,
Till glory crown the work of grace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In whom but thee, in heaven above,
Can I repose my trust, my love?
And shall an earthly object be
Loved in comparison with thee?

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: My God, my Father, while I stray

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God, my Father, while I stray
Far from my home, on life’s rough way,
O, teach me from my heart to say,
“Thy will be done!”

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What though in lonely grief I sigh
For friends beloved no longer nigh;
Submissive still would I reply,
“Thy will be done!”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If thou shouldst call me to resign
What most I prize—it ne’er was mine;
I only yield thee what was thine:
“Thy will be done!”

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
If but my fainting heart be blest
With thy sweet Spirit for its guest,
My God, to thee I leave the rest:
“Thy will be done!”

title: To weary hearts, to mourning homes

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Angel of patience! sent to calm
Our feverish brows with cooling balm,
To lay with hope the storms of fear,
And reconcile life’s smile and tear,
The throbs of wounded pride to still,
And make our own our Father’s will!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O thou, who mournest on thy way,
With longings for the close of day,
He walks with thee, that angel kind,
And gently whispers, “Be resigned!
Bear up, bear on, the end shall tell,
The dear Lord ordereth all things well.”

title: O let my trembling soul be still

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
So trusting in thy love, I tread
The narrow path of duty on;
What though some cherished joys are fled?
What though some flattering dreams are gone?
Yet purer, nobler joys remain,
And peace is won through conquered pain.

title: When adverse winds and waves arise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When adverse winds and waves arise,
And in my heart despondence sighs;
When life her throng of cares reveals,
And weakness o’er my spirit steals,
Grateful I hear the kind decree,
That “as my day, my strength shall be.”

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When, with sad footsteps, memory roves
’Mid smitten joys and buried loves,
When sleep my tearful pillow flies,
And dewy morning drinks my sighs,
Still to thy promise, Lord! I flee,
That “as my day, my strength shall be.”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One trial more must yet be past:
One pang—the keenest and the last;
And when, with brow convulsed and pale,
My feeble, quivering heart-strings fail,
Redeemer! grant my soul to see,
That “as my day, my strength shall be.”

title: All as God wills! who wisely heeds
author: I open to the day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All as God wills! who wisely heeds
To give or to withhold,
And knoweth more of all my needs
Than all my prayers have told.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Enough that blessings undeserved
Have marked my erring track—
That wheresoe’er my feet have swerved,
His chastening turned me back—

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
That more and more a Providence,
Of love is understood,
Making the springs of time and sense
Sweet with eternal good—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
That death seems but a covered way
Which opens into light,
Wherein no blinded child can stray
Beyond the Father’s sight—

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
That care and trial seem at last,
Through memory’s sunset air,
Like mountain ranges overpast,
In purple distance fair—

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
That all the jarring notes of life,
Seem blending in a psalm,
And all the angles of its strife
Slow rounding into calm.

sections.label: Verse 7

title: We wait in faith, in prayer we wait

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We wait in faith, in prayer we wait,
Until the happy hour
When God shall ope the morning gate,
By his almighty power.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We wait in faith, and turn our face
To where the day-light springs;
Till he shall come, earth’s gloom to chase,
With healing on his wings.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And even now, amid the gray,
The east is brightening fast,
And kindling to that perfect day
Which never shall be past.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We wait in faith, we wait in prayer,
Till that blest day shall shine,
When earth shall fruits of Eden bear,
And all, O God, be thine!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O guide us till our night is done!
Until from shore to shore,
Thou, Lord, our everlasting sun,
Art shining evermore!

title: It is the Lord—enthroned in light
author: To thee I all resign

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
It is the Lord—enthroned in light,
Whose claims are all divine,
Who has an undisputed right
To govern me and mine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It is the Lord—who gives me all,
My wealth, my friends my ease;
And of his bounties may recall
Whatever part he please.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It is the Lord—my covenant God—
Thrice blesséd be his name—
Whose gracious promise, sealed with blood,
Must ever be the same.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Our souls are in the Saviour’s hand

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our souls are in the Saviour’s hand;
And he will keep them still,
And you and I shall surely stand
With him on Zion’s hill.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Him eye to eye we there shall see,
Our face like his shall shine;
O! what a glorious company,
When saints and angels join!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O! what a joyful meeting there,
In robes of white array!
Palms in our hands we all shall bear,
And crowns that ne’er decay!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When we’ve been there ten thousand years,
Bright shining as the sun,
We’ve no less days to sing God’s praise,
Than when we first begun!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then let us hasten to the day
When all shall be brought home:
Come, O Redeemer! come away!
O Jesus! quickly come!

title: Father, I know thy ways are just

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, I know thy ways are just,
Although to me unknown;
O, grant me grace thy love to trust,
And cry, “Thy will be done.”

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If thou shouldst hedge with thorns my path,
Should wealth and friends be gone,
Still, with a firm and lively faith,
I’ll cry, “Thy will be done.”

sections.label: Verse 3

title: How bright these glorious spirits shine
author: Shall wipe off every tear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How bright these glorious spirits shine!
Whence all their bright array?
How came they to the blissful seats
Of everlasting day?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lo! these are they from sufferings great
Who came to realms of light,
And in the blood of Christ have washed
Those robes which shine so bright.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Now with triumphant palms they stand
Before the throne on high,
And serve the God they love, amidst
The glories of the sky.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His presence fills each heart with joy,
Tunes every mouth to sing;
By day, by night, the sacred courts
With glad hosannas ring.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Hunger and thirst are felt no more,
Nor sun with scorching ray;
God is their sun, whose cheering beams
Diffuse eternal day.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The Lamb that sits upon the throne,
Shall o’er them still preside,
Feed them with nourishment divine,
And all their footsteps guide.

sections.label: Verse 7

title: In trouble and in grief, O God
author: That brings me near to thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In trouble and in grief, O God,
Thy smile hath cheered my way;
And joy hath budded from each thorn
That round my footsteps lay.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The hours of pain have yielded good
Which prosperous days refused;
As herbs, though scentless when entire,
Spread fragrance when they’re bruised.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The oak strikes deeper as its boughs
By furious blasts are driven;
So life’s tempestuous storms the more
Have fixed my heart in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
All-gracious Lord, whate’er my lot
In other times may be,
I’ll welcome still the heaviest grief

title: Through all the changing scenes of life
author: Who on his succor trust

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Through all the changing scenes of life,
In trouble and in joy,
The praises of my God shall still
My heart and tongue employ.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Of his deliverance I will boast,
Till all that are distressed,
From my example, comfort take,
And charm their griefs to rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, magnify the Lord with me,
With me exalt his name;
When in distress to him I called,
He to my rescue came.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: I look to thee in every need

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I look to thee in every need,
And never look in vain;
I feel thy strong and tender love,
And all is well again:
The thought of thee is mightier far
Than sin and pain and sorrow are.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Discouraged in the work of life,
Disheartened by its load,
Shamed by its failures or its fears,
I sink beside the road;
But let me only think of thee,
And then new heart springs up in me.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Thy way, not mine, O Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Smooth let it be, or rough,
It will be still the best;
Winding or straight, it matters not,
It leads me to thy rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I dare not choose my lot,
I would not if I might;
But choose thou for me, O my God!
So shall I walk aright.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The kingdom that I seek
Is thine; so let the way
That leads to it, O Lord! be thine,
Else I must surely stray.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
My portion thou! my cup
With joy or sorrow fill;
As ever best to thee may seem,
Choose thou my good and ill.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Choose thou for me my friends,
My sickness or my health;
Choose thou my joys and cares for me,
My poverty or wealth.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Not mine, not mine the choice,
In things or great or small;
Be thou my Guide, my Guard, my Strength,
My Wisdom, and my All.

title: “My times are in thy hand,”
author: His child a needless tear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
“My times are in thy hand,”
My God, I’d have them there;
My life, my friends, my soul I leave
Entirely to thy care.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
“My times are in thy hand,”
Whatever they may be;
Pleasing or painful, dark or bright,
As best may seem to thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
“My times are in thy hand,”
Why should I doubt or fear?
My Father’s hand will never cause

title: My God, my Strength, my Hope
author: Into thy perfect love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God, my Strength, my Hope,
On thee I cast my care,
With humble confidence look up,
And know thou hearest my prayer.
Give me on thee to wait,
Till I can all things do—
On thee, almighty to create,
Almighty to renew.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I want a Godly fear,
A quick-discerning eye,
That looks to thee when sin is near,
And bids the tempter fly;
A spirit still prepared,
And armed with jealous care,
For ever standing on its guard,
And watching unto prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I rest upon thy word;
The promise is for me;
My succor and salvation, Lord,
Shall surely come from thee:
