But let me still abide,
Nor from my hope remove,
Till thou my patient spirit guide

title: Blest be thy love, dear Lord
author: If thine in death we be

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest be thy love, dear Lord,
That taught us this sweet way,
Only to love thee for thyself,
And for that love obey.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O thou, our souls’ chief hope!
We to thy mercy fly;
Where’er we are, thou canst protect,
Whate’er we need, supply.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Whether we sleep or wake,
To thee we both resign;
By night we see, as well as day,
If thy light on us shine.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Your harps, ye trembling saints
author: Shall thy salvation see

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Your harps, ye trembling saints!
Down from the willows take;
Loud to the praise of love divine,
Bid every string awake.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though in a foreign land,
We are not far from home,
And, nearer to our house above,
We every moment come.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His grace will, to the end,
Stronger and brighter shine;
Nor present things, nor things to come,
Shall quench this spark divine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When we in darkness walk,
Nor feel the heavenly flame
Then will we trust our gracious God,
And rest upon his name.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Blest is the man, O God!
That stays himself on thee:
Who waits for thy salvation, Lord!

title: Jesus, take me for thine own
author: Having all in having thee

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Making thus the Lord my choice,
I have nothing more to choose,
But to listen to thy voice,
And my will in thine to lose.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Sovereign Ruler of the skies

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sovereign Ruler of the skies,
Ever gracious, ever wise!
All my times are in thy hand;
All events at thy command.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Times of sickness, times of health,
Times of penury and wealth—
All must come, and last, and end,
As shall please my heavenly Friend.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O thou gracious, wise and just!
In thy hands my life I trust;
Have I somewhat dearer still?—
I resign it to thy will.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thee at all times will I bless;
Having thee, I all possess:
Ne’er can I bereavéd be,
While I do not part with thee.

title: Quiet, Lord, my froward heart

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Quiet, Lord, my froward heart,
Make me teachable and mild,
Upright, simple, free from art,
Make me as a weanéd child;
From distrust and envy free,
Pleased with all that pleases thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What thou shalt to-day provide,
Let me as a child receive:
What to-morrow may betide,
Calmly to thy wisdom leave;
’Tis enough that thou wilt care—
Why should I the burden bear?

sections.label: Verse 3

title: My Jesus, as thou wilt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Jesus, as thou wilt!
O may thy will be mine!
Into thy hand of love
I would my all resign.
Through sorrow, or through joy,
Conduct me as thine own,
And help me still to say,
My Lord, thy will be done!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Jesus, as thou wilt!
If needy here and poor,
Give me thy people’s bread,
Their portion rich and sure.
The manna of thy word
Let my soul feed upon;
And if all else should fail—
My Lord, thy will be done!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My Jesus, as thou wilt:
If among thorns I go,
Still sometimes here and there,
Let a few roses blow.
But thou on earth, along
The thorny pain hast gone;
Then lead me after thee;
My Lord, thy will be done!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My Jesus, as thou wilt!
Though seen through many a tear,
Let not my star of hope
Grow dim or disappear.
Since thou on earth hast wept
And sorrowed oft alone,
If I must weep with thee,
My Lord, thy will be done!

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
My Jesus, as thou wilt!
When death itself draws nigh,
To thy dear wounded side
I would for refuge fly.
Leaning on thee, to go
Where thou before hast gone;
The rest as thou shalt please,
My Lord, thy will be done.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
My Jesus, as thou wilt!
All shall be well for me;
Each changing future scene,
I gladly trust with thee.
Straight to my home above
I travel calmly on,
And sing, in life or death,
My Lord, thy will be done!

title: O how kindly hast thou led me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O how kindly hast thou led me,
Heavenly Father, day by day!
Found my dwelling, clothed and fed me,
Furnished friends to cheer my way!
Didst thou bless me, didst thou chasten,
With thy smile, or with thy rod,
’Twas that still my step might hasten
Homeward, heavenward, to my God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O how slowly have I often
Followed where thy hand would draw!
How thy kindness failed to soften!
How thy chastening failed to awe!
Make me for thy rest more ready,
As thy path is longer trod;
Keep me in thy friendship steady,
Till thou call me home, my God!

title: Jesus, I my cross have taken

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, I my cross have taken,
All to leave and follow thee;
I am poor, despised, forsaken—
Thou henceforth my all shalt be:
Perish every fond ambition—
All I’ve sought, or hoped, or known;
Yet how rich is my condition—
God and heaven are still my own!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let the world despise and leave me,
It has left my Saviour too;
Human hearts and looks deceive me,
Thou art not like them, untrue;
Whilst thy graces shall adorn me,
God of wisdom, love, and might—
Foes may hate, and friends may scorn me,
Show thy face, and all is bright.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Go then—earthly fame and treasure,
Come, disaster, scorn, and pain;
In thy service, pain is pleasure—
With thy favor, loss is gain.
I have called thee, Abba Father!
I have set my heart on thee;
Storms may howl, and clouds may gather,
All will work for good to me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Man may trouble and distress me,
’Twill but drive me to thy breast,
Life with trials hard may press me,
Heaven will bring me sweeter rest.
O, ’tis not in grief to harm me
While thy love is left to me;
O, ’twere not in joy to charm me,
Were that joy unmixed with thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
Verse 6
sections.text:
Haste thee on from grace to glory,
Armed by faith, and winged by prayer,
Heaven’s eternal day’s before thee,
God’s own hand shall guide thee there.
Soon shall close thy earthly mission;
Soon shall pass thy pilgrim’s days;
Hope shall change to glad fruition,
Faith to sight, and prayer to praise!

title: Hallelujah! best and sweetest
author: Ours at length this strain shall be

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hallelujah! best and sweetest
Of the hymns of praise above!
Hallelujah! thou repeatest,
Angel-host, these notes of love;
This ye utter,
While your golden harps ye move.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hallelujah! Church victorious,
Join the concert of the sky:
Hallelujah! bright and glorious!
Lift, ye saints, this strain on high!
We, poor exiles,
Join not yet your melody.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
But our earnest supplication,
Holy God! we raise to thee;
Visit us with thy salvation,
Make us all thy peace to see!
Hallelujah!

title: Father, O hear me now

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father, O hear me now!
Father divine!
Thou, only thou, canst see
The heart’s deep agony:
Help me to say to thee
“Thy will, not mine!”

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O God! be thou my stay
In this dark hour;
Kindly each sorrow hear,
Hush every troubled fear,
Thee let me still revere,
Still own thy power.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In thee alone I trust,
Thou Holy One!
Humbly to thee I pray
That through each troubled day
Of life, I still may say,
“Thy will be done!”

title: I did thee wrong, my God

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Less wayward let me be,
More pliable and mild;
In glad simplicity
More like a trustful child.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Less, less of self each day,
And more, my God, of thee;
O, keep me in the way,
However rough it be.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Less of the flesh each day,
Less of the world and sin;
More of thy Son, I pray,
More of thyself within.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
More molded to thy will,
Lord, let thy servant be;
Higher and higher still,
More, and still more, like thee!

title: Come, all ye saints of God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, all ye saints of God,
Wide through the earth abroad,
Spread Jesus’ fame:
Tell what his love hath done;
Trust in his name alone;
Shout to his lofty throne,
“Worthy the Lamb!”

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hence, gloomy doubts and fears!
Dry up your mournful tears;
Swell the glad theme:
To Christ, our gracious King,
Strike each melodious string;
Join heart and voice to sing,
“Worthy the Lamb!”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hark! how the choirs above,
Filled with the Saviour’s love,
Dwell on his name!
There, too, may we be found,
With light and glory crowned;
While all the heavens resound,
“Worthy the Lamb!”

title: Nearer, my God, to thee
author: Nearer to thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Nearer, my God, to thee,
Nearer to thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to thee,
Nearer to thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though like the wanderer,
Daylight all gone,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to thee—
Nearer to thee!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven;
All that thou sendest me,
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to thee!
Nearer to thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs,
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer my God, to thee—
Nearer to thee!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Or, if on joyful wing,
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upward I fly;
Still all my song shall be
Nearer, my God, to thee,

title: While thou, O my God, art my help and defender

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
While thou, O my God, art my help and defender,
No cares can o’erwhelm me, no terrors appall:
The wiles and the snares of this world will but render
More lively my hope in my God and my all.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
To thee, dearest Lord, will I turn without ceasing,
Though grief may oppress me or sorrow befall;
And love thee, till death, my blest spirit releasing,
Secures to me Jesus, my God and my all.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when thou demandest the life thou hast given,
With joy will I answer thy merciful call;
And quit thee on earth, but to find thee in heaven—
My portion for ever, my God and my all.

title: O for the peace that floweth as a river
author: Will light the shadows of earth’s Little While

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O for the peace that floweth as a river,
Making life’s desert places bloom and smile;
O for that faith to grasp the glad For ever,
Amid the shadows of earth’s Little While!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A little while for patient vigil keeping,
To face the storm, to wrestle with the strong;
A little while to sow the seed with weeping,
Then bind the sheaves and sing the harvest-song.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A little while to wear the vail of sadness,
To toil with weary step through miry ways,
Then to pour forth the fragrant oil of gladness,
And clasp the girdle round the robe of Praise!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A little while, ’mid shadow and illusion,
To strive by faith love’s mysteries to spell,
Then read each dark enigma’s bright solution,
Then hail sight’s verdict—He doth all things well.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And he who is himself the Gift and Giver,
The future glory and the present smile,
With the bright promise of the glad For ever,

title: A little longer still—patience belovéd

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A little longer still—patience belovéd;
A little longer still, ere heaven unroll
The glory, and the brightness, and the wonder,
Eternal and divine, that waits thy soul.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A little longer ere life, true, immortal,
(Not this our shadowy life) will be thine own,
And thou shalt stand where winged archangels worship,
And trembling bow before the great white throne.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A little longer still, and heaven awaits thee,
And fills thy spirit with a great delight;
Then our pale joys will seem a dream forgotten,
Our sun a darkness, and our day a night.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A little longer, and thy heart, belovéd,
Shall beat for ever with a love divine;
And joy so pure, so mighty, so eternal,
No mortal knows, and lives, shall then be thine.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Through cross to crown! and though thy spirit’s life

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Through cross to crown! and though thy spirit’s life
Trials untold assail with giant strength,
Good cheer! good cheer! Soon ends the bitter strife,
And thou shalt reign in peace with Christ at length.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Through woe to joy! and though at morn thou weep,
And though the midnight finds thee weeping still,
Good cheer! good cheer! The shepherd loves his sheep;
Resign thee to the watchful Father’s will.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Through death to life! and through this vale of tears,
And through this thistle-field of life, ascend
To the great supper in that world whose years
Of bliss unfading, cloudless, know no end.

title: “After the toil,” when the morning breaks
author: All its glorified dream of the Infinite Day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
“After the toil,” when the morning breaks
On the bloom-crowned hills of the heavenly land;
“After the toil,” when each slumberer wakes,
’Neath the glorified touch of the Infinite Hand.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
“After the toil,” when the dim earth sinks,
Like a worn-out pebble in eternity’s sea;
“After the toil,” when each thirsty soul drinks
Of the River that flows through Immensity.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
“After the toil,” O shadowing cloud
Of time o’er the face of the Infinite;
When thou shalt be dropped like a worm-eaten shroud,
What a morning will dawn on us after the night!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
“After the toil,” and the cross that we bear
Way-worn and weary through life’s creeping years;
Angels will smile on the crown we shall wear,
And the songs of salvation will follow our tears.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
“After the toil,” O! thou who art faint,
Rise from the shadows that darken thy way—
Rise while thy faith’s raptured pencil shall paint

title: Christian, the morn breaks sweetly o’er thee
author: Where thy Redeemer reigns alone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Christian, the morn breaks sweetly o’er thee,
And all the midnight shadows flee;
Tinged are the distant skies with glory,
A beacon-light hung out for thee;
Arise, arise! the light breaks o’er thee,
Thy name is graven on the throne,
Thy home is in the world of glory,
Where thy Redeemer reigns alone.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Cheer up! cheer up! the day breaks o’er thee,
Bright as the summer’s noontide ray,
The star-gemmed crowns and realms of glory
Invite thy happy soul away;
Away! away! leave all for glory,
Thy name is graven on the throne;
Thy home is in that world of glory,

title: Whate’er my God ordains is right

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3

title: Their hearts shall not be moved

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
One like the Son of God
Is walking at their side,
When by the fervid flame
And fiery furnace tried;
And ’tis enough that he is near,
To strengthen them in every fear.

title: To heaven I lift mine eye
author: With his almighty arm

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To heaven I lift mine eye,
To heaven, Jehovah’s throne,
For there my Saviour sits on high,
And thence shall strength and aid supply
To all he calls his own.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He will not faint nor fail,
Nor cause thy feet to stray;
For him no weary hours assail,
Nor evening darkness spreads her vail
O’er his eternal day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Beneath that light divine,
Securely shalt thou move;
The sun with milder beams shall shine,
And eve’s still queen her lamp incline
Benignant from above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For he, thy God and Friend,
Shall keep thy soul from harm,
In each sad scene of doubt attend,
And guide thy life, and bless thine end,

title: When our purest delights are nipt in the blossom
author: RELAPSE AND RECOVERY

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When our purest delights are nipt in the blossom,
When those we love best are laid low;
When grief plants in secret her thorn in the bosom,
Deserted—“to whom shall we go?”

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When, with error bewildered, our path becomes dreary,
And tears of despondency flow:
When the whole head is sick, and the whole heart is weary,
Despairing—“to whom shall we go?”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Where the sad, thirsty soul turns away from the springs
Of pleasure this world can bestow,
And sighs for another, and flatters its wings,
Impatient—“to whom shall we go?”

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O blest be that light which has parted the clouds,
And a path to the pilgrim can show;
That pierces the vail which the future enshrouds,
And tells us to whom we shall go!

title: O Thou that hearest when sinners cry

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Thou that hearest when sinners cry,
Though all my sins before thee lie,
Behold me not with angry look,
But blot their memory from thy book.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Create my nature pure within,
And form my soul averse to sin;
Let thy good Spirit ne’er depart,
Nor hide thy presence from my heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I can not live without thy light,
Cast out and banished from thy sight;
Thy holy joys, my God, restore,
And guard me that I fall no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though I have grieved thy Spirit, Lord,
His help and comfort still afford;
And let a sinner seek thy throne,
To plead the merits of the Son.

title: Weary of wandering from my God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Weary of wandering from my God,
And now made willing to return,
I hear, and bow beneath the rod;
For thee, for thee alone, I mourn:
I have an Advocate above,
A Friend before the throne of love.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou knowest the way to bring me back,
My fallen spirit to restore;
O, for thy truth and mercy’s sake,
Forgive, and bid me sin no more!
The ruins of my soul repair,
And make my heart a house of prayer.

title: Before thy throne with tearful eyes
author: Then endless songs my thanks shall tell

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Before thy throne with tearful eyes,
My gracious Lord, I humbly fall;
To thee my weary spirit flies,
For thy forgiving love I call.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How free thy mercy overflows,
When sinners on thy grace rely!
Thy tender love no limit knows;
O, save me—justly doomed to die!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yes! thou wilt save; my soul is free!
The gloom of sin is fled away;
My tongue breaks forth in praise to thee,
And all my powers thy word obey.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hence while I wrestle with my foes—
The world, the flesh, the hosts of hell—
Sustain thou me till conflicts close,

title: O thou, whose tender mercy hears
author: A taste of joy divine

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
See Lord, before thy throne of grace,
A wretched wanderer mourn:
Hast thou not bid me seek thy face?
Hast thou not said—“Return?”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And shall my guilty fears prevail
To drive me from thy feet?
O, let not this dear refuge fail,
This only safe retreat!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Absent from thee, my Guide! my Light!
Without one cheering ray,
Through dangers, fears, and gloomy night,
How desolate my way.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O, shine on this benighted heart,
With beams of mercy shine!
And let thy healing voice impart

title: O for a closer walk with God
author: That leads me to the Lamb

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O for a closer walk with God!
A calm and heavenly frame!
A light to shine upon the road
That leads me to the Lamb!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Where is the blessedness I knew
When first I saw the Lord?
Where is the soul-refreshing view
Of Jesus and his word?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
What peaceful hours I once enjoyed!
How sweet their memory still!
But they have left an aching void
The world can never fill.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Return, O holy Dove, return,
Sweet messenger of rest;
I hate the sins that made thee mourn,
And drove thee from my breast.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The dearest idol I have known,
Whate’er that idol be,
Help me to tear it from thy throne,
And worship only thee.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Sweet was the time when first I felt
author: Let me that mercy share

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet was the time when first I felt
The Saviour’s pardoning blood
Applied to cleanse my soul from guilt,
And bring me home to God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon as the morn the light revealed,
His praises tuned my tongue;
And, when the evening shade prevailed,
His love was all my song.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In prayer, my soul drew near the Lord,
And saw his glory shine;
And when I read his holy word,
I called each promise mine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But now, when evening shade prevails,
My soul in darkness mourns;
And when the morn the light reveals,
No light to me returns.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: O Saviour, lend a listening ear
author: I raise my ardent cry

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Saviour, lend a listening ear,
And answer my request!
Forgive, and wipe the falling tear,
Now with thy love my spirit cheer,
And set my heart at rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I mourn the hidings of thy face;
The absence of that smile,
Which led me to a throne of grace,
And gave my soul a resting-place
From earthly care and toil.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
’Tis sin that separates from thee
This poor benighted soul;
My folly and my guilt I see,
And now upon the bended knee,
I yield to thy control.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Up to the place of thine abode
I lift my waiting eye;
To thee, O holy Lamb of God!
Whose blood for me so freely flowed,

title: Weeping soul, no longer mourn

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

title: Pity, Lord! this child of clay

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Pity, Lord! this child of clay,
Who can only weep and pray—
Only on thy love depend:
Thou who art the sinner’s Friend;
Thou the sinner’s only plea—
Jesus, Saviour, pity me!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
From thy flock, a straying Lamb,
Tender Shepherd, though I am;
Now, upon the mountain cold,
Lost, I long to gain the fold,
And within thine arms to be:
Jesus, Saviour, pity me!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, where stillest streams are poured,
In green pastures lead me, Lord!
Bring me back, where angels sound
Joy to the poor wanderer found:
Evermore my Shepherd be:
Jesus, Saviour, pity me!

title: Brother, hast thou wandered far

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Brother, hast thou wandered far
From the Father’s happy home,
With thyself and God at war?
Turn thee, brother—homeward come.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hast thou wasted all the powers
God for noble uses gave?
Squandered life’s most golden hours?
Turn thee, brother—God can save.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Take me, O my Father! take me
author: I must be for ever blest

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Long from thee my footsteps straying,
Thorny proved the way I trod;
Weary come I now, and praying—
Take me to thy love my God!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fruitless years with grief recalling,
Humbly I confess my sin!
At thy feet, O Father, falling,
To thy household take me in.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Freely now to thee I proffer
This relenting heart of mine;
Freely, life and soul I offer,
Gift unworthy love like thine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Once the world’s Redeemer, dying,
Bore our sins upon the tree;
On that sacrifice relying,
Now I look in hope to thee.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: A weak and weary dove, with drooping wing
author: SYMPATHIES AND ACTIVITIES

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A weak and weary dove, with drooping wing,
And tired of wandering o’er this watery waste,
Jesus, my ark! once more a worthless thing,
To thee I fly, thy pardoning love to taste.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For since I left thy sweet, secure retreat,
In search of pleasures fair, though false and vain,
My peace—my joy have flown; no rest my feet
Have found; and now I turn to thee again!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
I’ve sought to find a place to rest my feet
In fame’s alluring temple, bright and gay;
In health, and competence, and pleasures sweet,
But short and transient as the passing day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yet all in vain: o’er all this dreary waste
Of sin and sorrow, toil and care, and pain,
No spot I’ve found, my weary feet to rest;
And now, sweet ark, I fly to thee again.

title: Thy footsteps, Lord, with joy we trace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy footsteps, Lord, with joy we trace,
And mark the conquests of thy grace;
Complete the work thou hast begun,
And let thy will on earth be done.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou good and wise, and righteous Lord,
All move subservient to thy word;
O, soon let every nation prove
The perfect joy of Christian love!

title: While others pray for grace to die
author: The more I long thy face to see

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
E’en if the darkness should appear
Too deep for faith as well as sight,
If I am thine, thou wilt be near,
And take me to thy heavenly light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But O! my Lord, in life’s highway
I crave the sunshine of thy face;
And every moment of the day
I need thy strong supporting grace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I dare not—will not—Lord, deny
That heart and feet both go astray;
Therefore the more to thee I cry
To keep me in the chosen way.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The more my sin and unbelief
Keep me from walking near to thee,
The more, Lord Jesus, is my grief—

title: Blest is the man whose softening heart
author: His trembling soul shall live

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Whose breast expands with generous warmth
A stranger’s woes to feel;
And bleeds in pity o’er the wound
He wants the power to heal.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He spreads his kind supporting arms,
To every child of grief;
His secret bounty largely flows,
And brings unasked relief.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To gentle offices of love,
His feet are never slow;
He views, through mercy’s melting eye,
A brother in a foe.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Bright Source of everlasting love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Bright Source of everlasting love,
To thee our souls we raise;
And to thy sovereign bounty rear
A monument of praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy mercy gilds the path of life
With every cheering ray,
Kindly restrains the rising tear,
Or wipes that tear away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To tents of woe, to beds of pain,
Our cheerful feet repair,
And with the gifts thy hand bestows,
Relieve the mourners there.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Lord, lead the way the Saviour went
author: They lose not their reward

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, lead the way the Saviour went,
By lane and cell obscure,
And let our treasures still be spent
Like his, upon the poor.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Like him, through scenes of deep distress,
Who bore the world’s sad weight,
We, in their gloomy loneliness,
Would seek the desolate.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For thou hast placed us side by side
In this wide world of ill;
And, that thy followers may be tried,
The poor are with us still.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Beneath the shadow of the cross
author: And the sweet tasks of love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Beneath the shadow of the cross,
As earthly hopes remove,
His new commandment Jesus gives,
His blesséd word of love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, bond of union, strong and deep!
O, bond of perfect peace!
Not e’en the lifted cross can harm,
If we but hold to this.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then, Jesus, be thy Spirit ours!
And swift our feet shall move
To deeds of pure self-sacrifice,

title: Scorn not the slightest word or deed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Scorn not the slightest word or deed,
Nor deem it void of power;
There’s fruit in each wind-wafted seed,
That waits its natal hour.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A whispered word may touch the heart,
And call it back to life;
A look of love bid sin depart,
And still unholy strife.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No act falls fruitless, none can tell
How vast its power may be,
Nor what results infolded dwell
Within it silently.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Work on, despair not, bring thy mite,
Nor care how small it be,
God is with all that serve the right,
The holy, true, and free.

title: Make channels for the streams of love
author: Such is the law of love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Make channels for the streams of love,
Where they may broadly run;
And love has overflowing streams,
To fill them every one.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But if at any time we cease
Such channels to provide,
The very founts of love for us
Will soon be parched and dried.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: O be not faithless! with the morn

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O be not faithless! with the morn
Cast thou abroad thy grain!
At noontide faint not thou forlorn,
At evening sow again!
Blessed are they, whate’er betide,
Who thus all waters sow beside.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou knowest not which seed shall grow,
Or which may die, or live;
In faith, and hope, and patience, sow!
The increase God shall give
According to his gracious will—
As best his purpose may fulfill.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, could our inward eye but view,
Our hearts but feel aright,
What faith, and love, and hope can do,
By their celestial might,
We should not say, till these be dead,
The power that marvels wrought is fled.

title: She loved her Saviour, and to him
author: And so give all to him

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
She loved her Saviour, and to him
Her costliest present brought;
To crown his head, or grace his name,
No gift too rare she thought.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
So let the Saviour be adored,
And not the poor despised,
Give to the hungry from your hoard,
But all, give all to Christ.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: What grace, O Lord, and beauty shone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What grace, O Lord, and beauty shone
Around thy steps below;
What patient love was seen in all
Thy life and death of woe!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For, ever on thy burdened heart
A weight of sorrow hung;
Yet no ungentle, murmuring word
Escaped thy silent tongue.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy foes might hate, despise, revile,
Thy friends unfaithful prove;
Unwearied in forgiveness still,
Thy heart could only love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O give us hearts to love like thee!
Like thee, O Lord, to grieve
Far more for others’ sins than all
The wrongs that we receive.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
One with thyself, may every eye,
In us, thy brethren, see
The gentleness and grace that spring
From union, Lord! with thee.

title: O gracious Lord, whose mercies rise
author: The orphan’s cup of woe

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O gracious Lord, whose mercies rise
Above our utmost need,
Incline thine ear unto our cry,
And hear the orphan plead.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Bereft of all a mother’s love,
And all a mother’s care,
Lord, whither shall we flee for help?
To whom direct our prayer?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To thee we flee, to thee we pray;
Thou shalt our Father be:
More than the fondest parent’s care
We find, O Lord, in thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Already Thou hast heard our cry,
And wiped away our tears:
Thy mercy has a refuge found
To guard our helpless years.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Where shall the child of sorrow find
author: Pity the orphan’s woes

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Where shall the child of sorrow find
A place for calm repose?
Thou! Father of the fatherless,
Pity the orphan’s woes!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What friend have I in heaven or earth,
What friend to trust but thee?
My father’s dead, my mother’s dead,
My God! “remember me.”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy gracious promise now fulfill,
And bid my troubles cease;
In thee the fatherless shall find
Pure mercy, grace, and peace.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Help us, O Lord, thy yoke to wear
author: More blest than to receive

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Help us, O Lord, thy yoke to wear,
Delighting in thy will;
Each other’s burdens learn to bear,
The law of love fulfill.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He that hath pity on the poor,
Doth lend unto the Lord:
And, lo! his recompense is sure;
For more shall be restored.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
And while we thus obey thy word,
And every want relieve,
O may we find it, gracious Lord!

title: Hush the loud cannon’s roar
author: And men be brothers all

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hush the loud cannon’s roar,
The frantic warrior’s call,
Why should the earth be drenched with gore?
Are we not brothers all?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Churches and sects, strike down
Each mean partition wall;
Let love each harsher feeling drown:
Christians are brothers all.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Let love and truth alone
Hold human hearts in thrall,
That heaven its work at length may own,

title: O praise our God to-day
author: And weep with them that weep

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O praise our God to-day,
His constant mercy bless,
Whose love hath helped us on our way,
And granted us success.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O happiest work below,
Earnest of joy above,
To sweeten many a cup of woe,
By deeds of holy love!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord! may it be our choice
This blesséd rule to keep:
Rejoice with them that do rejoice,

title: Sow in the morn thy seed

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
And duly shall appear,
In verdure, beauty, strength,
The tender blade, the stalk, the ear,
And the full corn at length.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou canst not toil in vain;
Cold, heat, the moist and dry,
Shall foster and mature the grain
For garners in the sky.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Thence, when the glorious end—
The day of God—is come,
The angel-reapers shall descend,
And heaven cry, Harvest-home.

title: What though earthly friends may frown

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What though earthly friends may frown,
Why should I dejected be?
Father, let thy will be known,
Let me find my all in thee.
Never let my soul despair,
God will hear the orphan’s prayer;
God will hear,
God will hear the orphan’s prayer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sorrow’s child I long have been,
Often for unkindness mourned;
Friendless orphan, poor and mean,
By the proud and wealthy scorned.
Still to God will I repair,
God will hear the orphan’s prayer;
God will hear,
God will hear the orphan’s prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Earthly comforts fade and die,
Sorrows oft our joys attend;
But if we on God rely,
He will prove a constant friend.
On him I’ll cast every care,
He regards the orphan’s prayer;
He regards,
He regards the orphan’s prayer.

title: He that goeth forth with weeping
author: For the harvest time is near

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
He that goeth forth with weeping,
Bearing precious seed in love,
Never tiring, never sleeping,
Findeth mercy from above.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: All around us, fair with flowers
author: Shall have left our work undone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All around us, fair with flowers,
Fields of beauty sleeping lie;
All around us clarion voices
Call to duty stern and high.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Following every voice of mercy
With a trusting, loving heart;
Let us in life’s earnest labor
Still be sure to do our part.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Now, to-day, and not to-morrow,
Let us work with all our might,
Lest the wretched faint and perish
In the coming stormy night.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now, to-day, and not to-morrow,
Lest, before to-morrow’s sun,
We, too, mournfully departing,

title: With my substance I will honor
author: By this gift our love we’ll prove

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With my substance I will honor
My Redeemer and my Lord;
Were ten thousand worlds my manor,
All were nothing to his word:
Hallelujah!
Now we offer to the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
While the heralds of salvation
His abounding grace proclaim,
Let his saints of every station
Gladly join to spread his fame:
Hallelujah!
Gifts we offer to his name.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: One whom Jesus loved has truly spoken
author: And in its ashes plant the tree of peace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
One whom Jesus loved has truly spoken!
The holier worship which God deigns to bless,
Restores the lost, and heals the spirit broken,
And feeds the widow and the fatherless.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Follow, with reverent steps, the great example
Of him whose holy work was doing good;
So shall the wide earth seem our Father’s temple,
Each loving life a psalm of gratitude.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Down the dark future, through long generations
author: The holy melodies of love arise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Down the dark future, through long generations,
The sounds of war grow fainter, and then cease;
And like a bell with solemn, sweet vibrations,
I hear once more the voice of Christ say, “Peace!”

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Peace, peace on earth! the heart of man for ever
author: And peace on earth fulfill the angels’ joy

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Peace, peace on earth! the heart of man for ever,
Through all these weary strifes, foretells the day;
Blesséd be God, the hope forsakes him never,
That war shall end, and swords be sheathed for aye.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Breathe thoughts of pity o’er a brother’s fall
author: And mighty and eternal is thy gain

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Breathe thoughts of pity o’er a brother’s fall,
But dwell not with stern anger on his fault:
The grace of God alone holds thee, holds all;
Were that withdrawn, thou too wouldst swerve and halt.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Send back the wanderer to the Saviour’s fold—
That were an action worthy of a saint;
But not in malice let the crime be told,
Nor publish to the world the evil taint.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Saviour suffers when his children slide;
Then is his holy name by men blasphemed!
And he afresh is mocked and crucified,
Even by those his bitter death redeemed.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Every day hath toil and trouble
author: PRIVATE DEVOTIONS

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Every day hath toil and trouble,
Every heart hath care;
Meekly bear thine own full measure,
And thy brother’s share,
Fear not, shrink not, though the burden
Heavy to thee prove;
God shall fill thy mouth with gladness,
And thy heart with love.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Patiently enduring, ever
Let thy spirit be
Bound, by links that can not sever,
To humanity.
Labor, wait! thy master labored
Till his task was done;
Count not lost thy fleeting moments—
Life hath but begun.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Labor! wait! though midnight shadows
Gather round thee here,
And the storm above thee lowering
Fill thy heart with fear—
Wait in hope! the morning dawneth
When the night is gone,
And a peaceful rest awaits thee

title: Far from my thoughts, vain world! begone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Far from my thoughts, vain world! begone,
Let my religious hours alone:
Fain would mine eyes my Saviour see;
I wait a visit, Lord! from thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My heart grows warm with holy fire,
And kindles with a pure desire;
Come, my dear Jesus! from above,
And feed my soul with heavenly love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blest Saviour, what delicious fare—
How sweet thine entertainments are!
Never did angels taste above
Redeeming grace and dying love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hail, great Immanuel, all-divine!
In thee thy Father’s glories shine:
Thou brightest, sweetest, fairest One,
That eyes have seen, or angels known!

title: Sun of my soul! thou Saviour dear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sun of my soul! thou Saviour dear,
It is not night if thou be near:
O, may no earth-born cloud arise
To hide thee from thy servant’s eyes!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When soft the dews of kindly sleep
My wearied eyelids gently steep,
Be my last thought—how sweet to rest
For ever on my Saviour’s breast!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Abide with me from morn till eve,
For without thee I can not live;
Abide with me when night is nigh,
For without thee I dare not die.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Be near to bless me when I wake,
Ere through the world my way I take;
Abide with me till in thy love
I lose myself in heaven above.

title: My God, my heart with love inflame

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God, my heart with love inflame,
That I may in thy holy name
Aloud in songs of praise rejoice,
While I have breath to raise my voice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No more let my ungrateful heart
One moment from thy praise depart;
But live and sing in sweet accord,
The glories of my sovereign Lord.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus! thou hope of glory, come,
And make my heart thy constant home:
Through all the remnant of my days,
O let me speak and live thy praise!

title: In silence of the voiceless night

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In silence of the voiceless night,
When chased by dreams, the slumbers flee,
Whom, in the darkness, do I seek,
O God, but thee?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And if there weigh upon my breast,
Vague memories of the day foregone,
Scarce knowing why, I fly to thee,
And lay them down.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Or, if it be the gloom that comes,
In token of impending ill,
My bosom heeds not what it is,
Since ’tis thy will.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For, O! in spite of constant care,
Or aught beside, how joyfully
I pass that solitary hour,
My God, with thee!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
More tranquil than the stilly night,
More peaceful than that voiceless hour,
Supremely blest, my bosom lies
Beneath thy power.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
For what on earth can I desire,
Of all it hath to offer me?
Or whom in heaven do I seek,
O God, but thee?

title: O that I could for ever dwell

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O that I could for ever dwell,
Delighted, at the Saviour’s feet;
Behold the form I love so well,
And all his tender words repeat!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The world shut out from all my soul,
And heaven brought in with all its bliss,
O! is there aught from pole to pole,
One moment to compare with this?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
This is the hidden life I prize—
A life of penitential love;
When I my follies most despise,
And raise my highest thoughts above?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When all I am I clearly see,
And freely own with deepest shame;
When the Redeemer’s love to me
Kindles within a deathless flame.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thus would I live till nature fail,
And all my former sins forsake;
Then rise to God within the vail,
And of eternal joys partake.

title: Return, my roving heart, return
author: That God has fixed his dwelling there

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Return, my roving heart, return,
And chase these shadowy forms no more;
Seek out some solitude to mourn,
And thy forsaken God implore.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O thou, great God, whose piercing eye
Distinctly marks each deep recess;
In these sequestered hours draw nigh,
And with thy presence fill the place.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Through all the windings of my heart,
My search let heavenly wisdom guide;
And still its radiant beams impart
Till all be searched and purified.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Our Father God! not face to face

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our Father God! not face to face
May mortal sense commune with thee,
Nor lift the curtains of that place
Where dwells thy secret Majesty:
Yet wheresoe’er our spirits bend
In reverent faith and humble prayer,
Thy promised blessing will descend,
And we shall find thy Spirit there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord! be the spot where now we meet
An open gateway into heaven;
Here may we sit at Jesus’ feet,
And feel our deepest sins forgiven.
Here may desponding care look up;
And sorrow lay its burden down,
Or learn of him to drink the cup,
To bear the cross and win the crown.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here may the sick and wandering soul,
To truth still blind, to sin a slave,
Find better than Bethesda’s pool,
Or than Siloam’s healing wave;
And may we learn, while here, apart
From the world’s passion and its strife,
That thy true shrine’s a loving heart,
And thy best praise a holy life!

title: Sweet is the prayer whose holy stream
author: And God accepts the prayer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sweet is the prayer whose holy stream
In earnest pleading flows;
Devotion dwells upon the theme,
And warm and warmer glows.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Faith grasps the blessing she desires,
Hope points the upward gaze;
And love, untrembling love inspires
The eloquence of praise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But sweeter far the still, small voice,
Heard by the human ear,
When God hath made the heart rejoice,
And dried the bitter tear.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Far from the world, O Lord, I flee
author: When time shall be no more

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Far from the world, O Lord, I flee,
From strife and tumult far;
From scenes where Satan wages still
His most successful war.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The calm retreat, the silent shade,
With prayer and praise agree;
And seem by thy sweet bounty made
For those who follow thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There, if thy Spirit touch the soul,
And grace her mean abode,
O, with what peace, and joy, and love,
She then communes with God!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There, like the nightingale she pours
Her solitary lays;
Nor asks a witness of her song,
Nor thirsts for human praise.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Author and Guardian of my life!
Sweet Source of light divine,
And all harmonious names in one—
My Saviour!—thou art mine!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
What thanks I owe thee, and what love—
A boundless, endless store—
Shall echo through the realms above,

title: Father divine, thy piercing eye
author: Thy suppliant to confess

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father divine, thy piercing eye
Sees through the darkest night,
In deep retirement thou art nigh,
With heart-discerning sight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There may that piercing eye survey,
My duteous homage paid,
With every morning’s dawning ray
And every evening’s shade.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O let thy own celestial fire
The incense still inflame;
While my warm vows to thee aspire,
Through my Redeemer’s name.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: O could I find, from day to day
author: My soul shall love thee more

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O could I find, from day to day,
A nearness to my God,
Then would my hours glide sweet away
While leaning on his word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord, I desire with thee to live
Anew from day to day,
In joys the world can never give,
Nor ever take away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blest Jesus, come and rule my heart,
And make me wholly thine,
That I may never more depart,
Nor grieve thy love divine.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Still with thee, O my God
author: I would be still with thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Still with thee, O my God,
I would desire to be;
By day, by night, at home, abroad,
I would be still with thee;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With thee, when dawn comes in,
And calls me back to care;
Each day returning to begin
With thee, my God, in prayer;—

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With thee, amid the crowd
That throngs the busy mart,
To hear thy voice, ’mid clamor loud,
Speak softly to my heart;—

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
With thee, when day is done,
And evening calms the mind:
The setting as the rising sun,
With thee my heart would find.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
With thee, when darkness brings
The signal of repose,
Calm in the shadow of thy wings,
Mine eyelids I would close.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Let my life be hid in thee
author: In my dying hour prevail

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let my life be hid in thee,
Life of life, and Light of light!
Love’s illimitable Sea!
Depth of peace, of power the Hight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let my life be hid in thee,
When my foes are gathering round;
Covered with thy panoply,
Safe within thy holy ground.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let my life be hid in thee,
From vexation and annoy;
Calm in thy tranquillity,
All my mourning turned to joy.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Jesus, Saviour all divine

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, Saviour all divine,
Hast thou made me truly thine?
Hast thou bought me by thy blood?
Reconciled my heart to God?
Hearken to my tender prayer,
Let me thine own image bear;
Let me love thee more and more,
Till I reach heaven’s blissful shore.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou canst fit me by thy grace
For the heavenly dwelling-place;
All thy promises are sure,
Ever shall thy love endure;
Then what more could I desire,
How to greater bliss aspire?
All I need, in thee I see,
Thou art all in all to me.

title: God is in the loneliest spot

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God is in the loneliest spot
Present, though thou know it not;
Morning vows and evening prayer
Make a Bethel everywhere.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: When far from the hearts where our fondest thoughts center
author: AFFLICTIONS

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When far from the hearts where our fondest thoughts center,
Denied for a time their loved presence to share;
In spirit we meet, when the closet we enter,
And hold sweet communion together in prayer!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O! fondly I think, as night’s curtains surround them,
The Shepherd of Israel tenderly keeps,
The angels of light are encamping around them,
They are watched by the eye that ne’er slumbers nor sleeps,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When the voice of the morning once more shall awake them,
And summon them forth to the calls of the day,
I will think of that God who will never forsake them,
The Friend ever near though all else be away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then why should one thought of anxiety seize us,
Though distance divide us from those whom we love?
They rest in the covenant mercy of Jesus,
Their prayers meet with ours in the mansions above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O! sweet bond of friendship, whate’er may betide us,
Though on life’s stormy billows our barks may be driven,
Though distance, or trial, or death may divide us,

title: Thy will be done! I will not fear
author: To drink the bitter cup I go

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy will be done! I will not fear
The fate provided by thy love;
Though clouds and darkness shroud me here,
I know that all is bright above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The stars of heaven are shining on,
Though these frail eyes are dimmed with tears;
The hopes of earth indeed are gone,
But are not ours the immortal years?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Father! forgive the heart that clings,
Thus trembling, to the things of time;
And bid my soul, on angel wings,
Ascend into a purer clime.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There shall no doubts disturb its trust,
No sorrows dim celestial love;
But these afflictions of the dust,
Like shadows of the night, remove.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Deem not that they are blest alone
author: For all his children suffer here

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Deem not that they are blest alone
Whose days a peaceful tenor keep;
The God who loves our race has shown
A blessing for the eyes that weep.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The light of smiles shall fill again
The lids that overflow with tears,
And weary hours of woe and pain
Are earnests of serener years.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, there are days of hope and rest
For every dark and troubled night!
And grief may bide an evening guest,
But joy shall come with early light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And thou who o’er thy friend’s low bier
Dost shed the bitter drops like rain,
Hope that a brighter, happier sphere
Will give him to thy arms again.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Nor let the good man’s trust depart,
Though life its common gifts deny;
Though with a pierced and broken heart,
And spurned of men, he goes to die.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: God of my life, to thee I call

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Friend of the friendless and the faint,
Where should I lodge my deep complaint?
Where, but with thee, whose open door
Invites the helpless and the poor?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He who has helped me hitherto,
Will help me all the journey through,
And give me daily cause to raise
New trophies to his endless praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though rough and thorny be the road,
It leads thee home, apace, to God;
Then count thy present trials small,
For heaven will make amends for all.

title: My spirit looks to God alone

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2

title: As oft, with worn and weary feet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As oft, with worn and weary feet,
We tread earth’s rugged valley o’er,
The thought—how comforting and sweet!
Christ took this very path before!
Our wants and weaknesses he knows,
From life’s first dawning to its close.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Do sickness, feebleness, or pain,
Or sorrow, in our path appear?
The recollection will remain,
More deeply did he suffer here!
His life, how truly sad and brief,
Filled up with suffering and with grief!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If Satan tempt our hearts to stray,
And whisper evil things within,
So did he, in the desert way,
Assail our Lord with thoughts of sin;
When worn, and in a feeble hour,
The tempter came with all his power.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Just such as I, this earth he trod,
With every human ill but sin;
And, though indeed the Son of God,
As I am now, so he has been.
My God, my Saviour, look on me
With pity, love and sympathy.

title: Saviour! though my rebellious will

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour! though my rebellious will
Has been, by thy blest power, renewed;
Yet in its secret workings still
How much remains to be subdued!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oft I recall, with grief and shame,
How many years their course had run
Ere grace my murmuring heart o’ercame,
Ere I could say, “Thy will be done!”

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
At length thy patient, wondrous love,
Unchanging, tender, pitying, strong,
Availed that stony heart to move,
Which had rebelled, alas! so long.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then was I taught by thee to say,
“Do with me what to thee seems best,
Give—take, whate’er thou wilt away,
Health, comfort, usefulness, or rest.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
“Be my whole life in suffering spent,
But let me be in suffering thine;
Still, O my Lord, I am content,
Thou now hast made thy pleasure mine.”

title: When gathering clouds around I view

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When gathering clouds around I view,
And days are dark and friends are few;
On him I lean, who, not in vain,
Experienced every human pain.
He sees my wants, allays my fears,
And counts and treasures up my tears.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If aught should tempt my soul to stray
From heavenly wisdom’s narrow way,
To fly the good I would pursue,
Or do the ill I would not do;
Still he who felt temptation’s power,
Will guard me in that dangerous hour.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When, sorrowing, o’er some stone I bend,
Which covers all that was a friend;
And from his hand, his voice, his smile,
Divides me for a little while—
My Saviour marks the tears I shed,
For “Jesus wept” o’er Lazarus dead.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And, O! when I have safely passed
Through every conflict but the last,
Still, Lord, unchanging, watch beside
My dying bed, for thou hast died;
Then point to realms of cloudless day,
And wipe the latest tear away.

title: I will extol thee, Lord on high

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I will extol thee, Lord on high:
At thy command diseases fly;
Who, but a God can speak and save
From the dark borders of the grave?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thine anger but a moment stays,
Thy love is life and length of days:
Though grief and tears the night employ,
The morning star restores our joy.

title: Great Source of boundless power and grace
author: And I shall never fall

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Great Source of boundless power and grace!
Attend my mournful cry;
In hours of dark and deep distress,
To thee alone I fly.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Fain would I call thy grace to mind,
And trust thy glorious name:
Jehovah, powerful, wise, and kind,
For ever is the same.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy presence, Lord, can cheer my heart,
When earthly comforts die;
Thy voice can bid my pains depart,
And raise my pleasures high.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: To thee, my God, whose presence fills
author: The pillars of thy throne

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To thee, my God, whose presence fills
The earth, and seas, and skies,
To thee, whose name, whose heart is Love,
With all my powers I rise.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O bid the roaring tempest cease;
Or give me strength to bear
Whate’er thy holy will appoints,
And save me from despair!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To thee, my God, alone I look,
On thee alone confide;
Thou never hast deceived the soul
That on thy grace relied.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Though oft thy ways are wrapt in clouds
Mysterious and unknown,
Truth, righteousness, and mercy stand,

title: Christ leads me through no darker rooms
author: That sing Jehovah’s praise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Christ leads me through no darker rooms
Than he went through before:
He that into God’s kingdom comes
Must enter by this door.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Come, Lord, when grace hath made me meet
Thy blesséd face to see;
For if thy work on earth be sweet,
What must thy glory be?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then I shall end my sad complaints,
And weary, sinful days,
And join with those triumphant saints

title: Affliction is a stormy deep

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Affliction is a stormy deep,
Where wave resounds to wave;
Though o’er our heads the billows roll,
We know the Lord can save.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When darkness, and when sorrows rose,
And pressed on every side,
The Lord hath still sustained our steps,
And still hath been our guide.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Perhaps, before the morning dawn,
He will restore our peace;
For he who bade the tempest roar
Can bid the tempest cease.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here will we rest, here build our hopes,
Nor murmur at his rod;
He’s more to us than all the world—
Our Health, our Life, our God.

title: O thou who driest the mourner’s tear
author: We never saw by day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou who driest the mourner’s tear,
How dark this world would be,
If, when deceived and wounded here,
We could not fly to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But thou wilt heal the broken heart,
Which, like the plants that throw
Their fragrance from the wounded part,
Breathes sweetness out of woe.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When joy no longer soothes or cheers,
And e’en the hope that threw
A moment’s sparkle o’er our tears
Is dimmed and vanished too;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O, who would bear life’s stormy doom,
Did not thy wing of love
Come brightly wafting through the gloom,
Our peace-branch from above?

sections.label: Verse 5

title: My times of sorrow and of joy

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My times of sorrow and of joy,
Great God! are in thy hand;
My choicest comforts come from thee,
And go at thy command.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If thou shouldst take them all away,
Yet would I not repine;
Before they were possessed by me,
They were entirely thine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Nor would I drop a murmuring word,
Though all the world were gone,
But seek enduring happiness
In thee, and thee alone.

title: Happy are they who learn in thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy are they who learn in thee,
Though patient suffering teach,
The secret of enduring strength,
And praise too deep for speech;
Peace that no pleasure from without,
Nor strife within, can reach.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Safe in thy sanctifying grace,
Almighty to restore,
Borne onward—sin and death behind,
And love and life before—
O let my soul abound in hope,
And praise thee evermore!

title: When languor and disease invade
author: My spirit flies away

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When languor and disease invade
This trembling house of clay,
’Tis sweet to look beyond my pains,
And long to fly away:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sweet to look inward, and attend
The whispers of his love;
Sweet to look upward to the place
Where Jesus pleads above:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sweet to look back, and see my name
In life’s fair book set down;
Sweet to look forward, and behold
Eternal joys my own:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sweet to rejoice in lively hope,
That when my change shall come,
Angels shall hover round my bed,
And waft my spirit home:

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sweet in his faithfulness to rest,
Whose love can never end;
Sweet on his covenant of grace
For all things to depend.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
If such the sweetness of the streams,
What must the fountain be,
Where saints and angels draw their bliss
Immediately from thee!

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
O may the unction of these truths
For ever with me stay,
Till, from her sin-worn cage dismissed,

title: My God, thy service well demands
author: To my celestial home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My God, thy service well demands
The remnant of my days:
Why was this fleeting breath renewed,
But to renew thy praise?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thine arms of everlasting love
Did this weak frame sustain;
When life was hovering o’er the grave,
And nature sunk with pain.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou, when the pains of death were felt,
Didst chase the fears of hell,
And teach my pale and quivering lips
Thy matchless grace to tell.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Calmly I bowed my fainting head
On thy dear, faithful breast;
Pleased to obey my Father’s call
To his eternal rest.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Into thy hands, my Saviour God,
Did I my soul resign,
In firm dependence on that truth
Which made salvation mine.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Back from the borders of the grave,
At thy command I come,
Nor will I urge a speedier flight

title: In every trouble, sharp and strong
author: His love is still the same

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In every trouble, sharp and strong,
My soul to Jesus flies;
My anchor-hold is firm in him,
When swelling billows rise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
His comforts bear my spirits up,
I trust a faithful God;
The sure foundation of my hope
Is in a Saviour’s blood.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: And can my heart aspire so high
author: In my Redeemer’s name

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And can my heart aspire so high,
To say—“My Father God!”
Lord, at thy feet I long to lie,
And learn to kiss the rod.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I would submit to all thy will,
For thou art good and wise;
Let every anxious thought be still,
Nor one faint murmur rise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy love can cheer the darksome gloom,
And bid me wait serene;
Till hopes and joys immortal bloom,
And brighten all the scene.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: O thou! who, in the olive shade
author: Hallow this whelming grief

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou! who, in the olive shade,
When the dark hour came on,
Didst, with a breath of heavenly aid,
Strengthen thy suffering Son;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, by the anguish of that night,
Send us now blest relief;
Or to the chastened, let thy might
Hallow this whelming grief.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And thou, that, when the starry sky,
Saw the dread strife begun,
Didst teach adoring faith to cry,
Father! thy will be done;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By thy meek Spirit, thou, of all
That e’er have mourned the chief,
Blest Saviour! if the stroke must fall,

title: With earnest longings of the mind
author: And sing restoring love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
With earnest longings of the mind,
My God, to thee I look;
So pants the hunted hart to find
And taste the cooling brook.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When shall I see thy courts of grace,
And meet my God again?
So long an absence from thy face,
My heart endures with pain.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
’Tis with a mournful pleasure now,
I think on ancient days;
Then to thy house did numbers go,
And all our work was praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
But why, my soul, sunk down so far,
Beneath this heavy load?
Why do my thoughts indulge despair;
And sin against my God?

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Now to thy heavenly Father’s praise
author: Has bound me with thy love

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now to thy heavenly Father’s praise,
My heart, thy tribute bring;
That goodness which prolongs my days,
With grateful pleasure sing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Whene’er he sends afflicting pains,
His mercy holds the rod;
His powerful word the heart sustains,
And speaks a faithful God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A faithful God is ever nigh
When humble grief implores;
His ear attends each plaintive sigh,
He pities and restores.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: How tender is thy hand
author: For there is none beside

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How tender is thy hand,
O thou most gracious Lord!
Afflictions come at thy command,
And leave us at thy word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
How gentle was the rod
That chastened us for sin!
How soon we found a smiling God,
Where deep distress had been!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A Father’s hand we felt,
A Father’s heart we knew;
’Mid tears of penitence we knelt,
And found his word was true.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: When overwhelmed with grief
author: The refuge where I hide

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When overwhelmed with grief,
My heart within me dies,
Helpless, and far from all relief,
To heaven I lift mine eyes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O lead me to the Rock
That’s high above my head,
And make the covert of thy wings
My shelter and my shade.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Out of the depths of woe

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Out of the depths of woe,
To thee, O Lord! I cry;
Darkness surrounds thee, but I know
That thou art ever nigh.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Like them I watch and pray,
Who for the morning long;
Catch the first gleam of welcome day,
Then burst into a song.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Glory to God above!
The waters soon will cease;
For, lo! the swift returning dove
Brings home the sign of peace!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though storms thy face obscure,
And dangers threaten loud,
Thy holy covenant is sure;
Thy bow is in the cloud!

title: How gracious and how wise
author: And every frailty cease

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How gracious and how wise
Is our chastising God;
And, O! how rich the blessings are
Which blossom from his rod!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He lifts it up on high
With pity in his heart,
That every stroke his children feel,
May grace and peace impart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Instructed thus, they bow
And own his sovereign sway;
They turn their erring footsteps back
To his forsaken way.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His covenant love they seek,
And seek the happy bands
That closer still engage their hearts
To honor his commands.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Our Father, we consent
To discipline divine;
And bless the pain that makes our souls
Still more completely thine.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Supported by thy love,
We tend to realms of peace,
Where every pain shall far remove,

title: We love this outward world

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We love this outward world,
Its fair sky overhead,
Its morning’s soft, gray mist unfurled,
Its sunsets rich and red.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But there’s a world within,
That higher glory hath;
A life the struggling soul must win—
The life of joy and faith.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For this the Father’s love
Doth shade the world of sense,
The bounding play of health remove,
And dim the sparkling glance;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
That, though the earth grows dull,
And earthly pleasures few,
The spirit gain its wisdom full
To suffer and to do.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Holy this world within,
Unknown to sound or sight—
The world of victory over sin,
Of faith, and love, and light.

title: Thou very present aid
author: And heaven in Christ begun

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou very present aid
In suffering and distress,
The soul which still on thee is stayed,
Is kept in perfect peace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The soul, by faith reclined
On the Redeemer’s breast,
’Mid raging storms exults to find
An everlasting rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Sorrow and fear are gone
Whene’er thy face appears:
It stills the sighing orphan’s moan,
And dries the widow’s tears:

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Jesus, to whom I fly,
Doth all my wishes fill:
What though created streams are dry,
I have the fountain still.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Prince of Peace! control my will

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou hast bought me with thy blood,
Opened wide the gate to God;
Peace I ask—but peace must be,
Lord, in being one with thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Saviour, at thy feet I fall;
Thou my Life, my God, my All,
Let thy happy servant be
One for evermore with thee.

title: Gently, gently lay thy rod

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Gently, gently lay thy rod
On my sinful head, O God!
Stay thy wrath, in mercy stay,
Lest I sink beneath its sway.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Who, within the silent grave,
Shall proclaim thy power to save?
Lord! my sinking soul reprieve;
Speak, and I shall rise and live.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lo! he comes—he heeds my plea!
Lo! he comes—the shadows flee;
Glory round me dawns once more!
Rise, my spirit, and adore!

title: ’Tis my happiness below

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
’Tis my happiness below,
Not to live without the cross,
But the Saviour’s power to know,
Sanctifying every loss.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Trials must and will befall;
But with humble faith to see
Love inscribed upon them all—
This is happiness to me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Did I meet no trials here,
No chastisement by the way;
Might I not, with reason, fear
I should prove a castaway?

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Full of trembling expectation
author: Keep me faithful to the end

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Full of trembling expectation,
Feeling much and fearing more,
Mighty God of my salvation!
I thy timely aid implore;
Suffering Son of Man, be near me,
All my sufferings to sustain;
By thy sorer griefs to cheer me,
By thy more than mortal pain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Call to mind that unknown anguish,
In thy days of flesh below;
When thy troubled soul did languish
Under a whole world of woe;
When thou didst our curse inherit,
Groan beneath our guilty load,
Burdened with a wounded spirit,
Bruised by all the wrath of God.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By thy most severe temptation,
In that dark, Satanic hour;
By thy last, mysterious passion,
Screen me from the adverse power;
By thy fainting in the garden,
By thy bloody sweat I pray,
Write upon my heart the pardon,
Take my sins and fears away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By the travail of thy spirit,
By thine outcry on the tree,
By thine agonizing merit,
In my pangs, remember me!
By thy pangs of crucifixion,
My weak, dying soul befriend;
Make me patient in affliction,

title: Why should I, in vain repining

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why should I, in vain repining,
Mourn the clouds that cross my way;
Since my Saviour’s presence, shining,
Turns my darkness into day?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Earthly honor, earthly treasure,
All the warmest passions win,
And the silken wings of pleasure
Only waft us on to sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But, within the vale of sorrow,
All with tempests overblown,
Purer light and joy we borrow
From the face of God alone.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Welcome, then, each darker token!
Mercy sent it from above!
So the heart, subdued, not broken,
Bends in fear, and melts with love.

title: In the floods of tribulation
author: Which has brought me to his feet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In the floods of tribulation,
While the billows o’er me roll,
Jesus whispers consolation,
And supports my sinking soul;
Sweet affliction!
Bringing Jesus to my soul.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In the darkest dispensations
Doth my faithful Lord appear,
With his richest consolations,
To reanimate and cheer.
Sweet affliction!
Thus to bring my Saviour near.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
All I meet shall still befriend me
In my path to heavenly joy,
Where, though trials now attend me,
Trials never more annoy.
Sweet affliction!
Every promise gives me joy.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Wearing there a weight of glory,
Still the path I’ll ne’er forget;
But, exulting, cry, It led me
To my blesséd Saviour’s seat.
Sweet affliction!

title: How vast is the tribute I owe

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How vast is the tribute I owe,
Of gratitude, homage and praise,
To the giver of all I possess,
The life and the length of my days!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When the sorrows I boded were come,
I poured out my sighs and my tears;
And to him, who alone can relieve,
My soul breathed her vows and her prayers.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When my heart throbbed with pain and alarm,
When paleness my cheek overspread,
When sickness pervaded my frame—
Then my soul on my Maker was stayed.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When death’s awful image was nigh,
And no mortal was able to save,
Thou didst brighten the valley of death,
And illumine the gloom of the grave.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In mercy thy presence dispels
The shades of adversity’s night,
And turns the sad scene of despair
To a morning of joy and delight.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Great source of my comforts restored,
Thou healer and balm of my woes!
Thou hope and desire of my soul!
On thy mercy I’ll ever repose.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
How boundless the gratitude due
To thee, O thou God of my praise!
The fountain of all I possess,
The life and the light of my days!

title: O why this disconsolate frame
author: And Jesus to welcome me home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O why this disconsolate frame!
Though earthly enjoyments decay,
My Jesus is ever the same—
My Sun in the gloomiest day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though molten awhile in the fire,
’Tis only the gold to refine;
And be this my simple desire,
Though suffering, not to repine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O what are the pleasures to me
Which earth in its fullness can boast?
Delusive, its vanities flee—
A flash of enjoyment at most.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And if my Redeemer could part,
For me, with his throne in the skies,
O why is so dear to my heart
What he in his wisdom denies?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then let the rude tempest assail,
Let blasts of adversity blow,
The heavens, though distant, I hail,
Beyond this rough ocean of woe.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: ’Tis not a lonely night watch
author: Till we thine image bear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
’Tis not a lonely night watch
Which by the couch I spend:
Jesus is close beside us,
Our Saviour and our Friend.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Often I strive all vainly,
To ease the aching head,
Then, silently and gently,
Himself he makes thy bed.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Do we not hear him saying,
“Your guilt on me was laid,”
“Ye are my blood-bought jewels;”
“Fear not, be not dismayed.”

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
