“I sit beside the furnace,”
“The gold will soon be pure,”
“And blesséd are those servants
Who to the end endure.”

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Amen! O blessed Saviour,
Dwell with us, in us, here,
And let us welcome trials,

title: O thou in whose presence my soul takes delight
author: Re-echoes the praise of her Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O thou in whose presence my soul takes delight,
On whom in affliction I call;
My comfort by day and my song in the night,
My hope, my salvation, my all!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Where dost thou at noontide resort with thy sheep
To feed on the pastures of love?
For why in the valley of death should I weep,
Or alone in the wilderness rove?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O why should I wander an alien from thee,
And cry in the desert for bread?
Thy foes will rejoice when my sorrows they see,
And smile at the tears I have shed.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
You daughters of Zion, declare have you seen
The star that on Israel shone?
Say if your tents my belovéd has been,
And where with his flock he is gone?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
This is my belovéd; his form is divine,
His vestments shed odors around,
The locks on his head are as grapes on the vine
When autumn with plenty is crowned.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
The roses of Sharon, the lilies that grow
In the vales, on the banks of the streams,
On his cheeks in the beauty of excellence glow,
And his eyes are as quivers of beams.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
His voice, as the sound of the dulcimer sweet,
Is heard through the shadows of death;
The cedars of Lebanon bow at his feet,
The air is perfumed with his breath.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
His lips as a fountain of righteousness flow
That water the garden of grace;
From which their salvation the Gentiles shall know,
And bask in the smiles of his face.

sections.label: Verse 9
sections.text:
Love sits on his eyelids, and scatters delight
Through all the bright mansions on high;
Their faces the cherubim vail in his sight,
And tremble with fullness of joy.

sections.label: Verse 10

title: We will not weep, for God is standing by us

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We will not weep, for God is standing by us,
And tears will blind us to the blesséd sight;
We will not doubt, if darkness still doth try us:
Our souls have promise of serenest light.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O not in doubt shall be our journey’s ending:
Sin with its fears, shall leave us at the last;
All its best hopes in glad fulfillment blending,
Life shall be with us more when death is past.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Help us, O Father! when the world is pressing
On our frail hearts, that faint without their Friend;
Help us, O Father! let thy constant blessing
Strengthen our weakness, till the joyful end.

title: As down in the sunless retreats of the ocean

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As down in the sunless retreats of the ocean,
Sweet flowers are springing no mortal can see,
So deep in my heart, the still prayer of devotion
Unheard by the world, rises silent to thee—
My God! silent to thee—
Pure, warm, silent to thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As still to the star of its worship, though clouded,
The needle points faithfully o’er the dim sea,
So, dark as I roam thro’ this wintery world shrouded,
The hope of my spirit turns trembling to thee—
My God! trembling to thee—
True, fond, trembling to thee.

title: The spring-tide hour

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The spring-tide hour
Brings leaf and flower,
With songs of life and love;
And many a lay
Wears out the day
In many a leafy grove.
Bird, flower, and tree,
Seem to agree
Their choicest gifts to bring;
But this poor heart
Bears not its part,
In it there is no spring.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Dews fall apace,
The dews of grace,
Upon this soul of sin;
And love divine
Delights to shine
Upon the waste within:
Yet year by year,
Fruits, flowers, appear,
And birds their praises sing;
But this poor heart
Bears not its part,
Its winter has no spring.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, let thy love,
Fresh from above,
Soft as the south-wind blow!
Call forth its bloom,
Wake its perfume,
And bid its spices flow!
And when thy voice
Makes earth rejoice,
And the hills laugh and sing,
Lord! make this heart
To bear its part,
And join the praise of spring!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: PRESENT AND FUTURE: LIFE AND DEATH.

title: Gently, my Saviour, let me down

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Gently, my Saviour, let me down,
To slumber in the arms of death;
I rest my soul on thee alone,
E’en till my last, expiring breath.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon will the storm of life be o’er,
And I shall enter endless rest;
There I shall live to sin no more,
And bless thy name, for ever blest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Bid me possess sweet peace within;
Let childlike patience keep my heart,
Then shall I feel my heaven begin,
Before my spirit hence depart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O, speed thy chariot, God of love,
And take me from this world of woe;
I long to reach those joys above,
And bid farewell to all below.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
There shall my raptured spirit raise
Still louder notes than angels sing,
High glories to Immanuel’s grace,
My God, my Saviour, and my King!

title: The morning flowers display their sweets
author: If firm the word of God remains

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The morning flowers display their sweets,
And gay their silken leaves unfold,
As careless of the noon-day heats
And fearless of the evening cold.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Nipt by the wind’s untimely blast,
Parched by the sun’s directer ray,
The momentary glories waste,
The short-lived beauties die away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So blooms the human face divine,
When youth its pride and beauty shows;
Fairer than spring the colors shine,
And sweeter than the virgin rose.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Or worn by slowly rolling years,
Or broke by sickness in a day,
The fading glory disappears,
The short-lived beauties die away.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yet these, new-rising from the tomb,
With luster brighter far shall shine;
Revive with ever-during bloom,
Safe from diseases and decline.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: The God of mercy will indulge

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The God of mercy will indulge
The flowing tear, the heaving sigh,
When honored parents fall around,
When friends beloved and kindred die.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yet not one anxious murmuring thought
Should with our mourning passion blend;
Nor should our bleeding hearts forget
Their mighty, ever-living Friend.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Parent, Protector, Guardian, Guide,
Thou art each tender name in one;
On thee we cast our every care,
And comfort seek from thee alone.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To thee, our Father, would we look,
Our Rock, our Portion, and our Friend,
And on thy covenant love and truth,
With humble, steadfast hope depend.

title: Dear is the spot where Christians sleep

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Dear is the spot where Christians sleep,
And sweet the strains their spirits pour;
O, why should we in anguish weep?
They are not lost, but gone before.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Secure from every mortal care,
By sin and sorrow vexed no more,
Eternal happiness they share
Who are not lost, but gone before.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To Zion’s peaceful courts above
In faith triumphant may we soar,
Embracing, in the arms of love,
The friends not lost, but gone before.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To Jordan’s bank whene’er we come,
And hear the swelling waters roar;
Jesus! convey us safely home,
To friends not lost, but gone before.

title: Asleep in Jesus! Blesséd sleep

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! Blesséd sleep
From which none ever wakes to weep;
A calm and undisturbed repose,
Unbroken by the last of foes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! O how sweet
To be for such a slumber meet!
With holy confidence to sing,
That death has lost its venomed sting.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! peaceful rest,
Whose waking is supremely blest:
No fear, no woe, shall dim the hour
That manifests the Saviour’s power.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! O for me
May such a blissful refuge be:
Securely shall my ashes lie,
And wait the summons from on high.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! time nor space
Affects this precious hiding-place:
On Indian plains, or Lapland snows,
Believers find the same repose.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Asleep in Jesus! far from thee
Thy kindred and their graves may be:
But thine is still a blesséd sleep,
which none ever wake to weep.

title: How blest the righteous when he dies

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How blest the righteous when he dies!
When sinks a weary soul to rest!
How mildly beam the closing eyes!
How gently heaves the expiring breast!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
A holy quiet reigns around,
A calm which life nor death destroys;
And nought disturbs that peace profound
Which his unfettered soul enjoys.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Life’s labor done, as sinks the clay,
Light from its load the spirit flies,
While heaven and earth combine to say,
“How blest the righteous when he dies!”

title: As the sweet flower that scents the morn

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As the sweet flower that scents the morn,
But withers in the rising day—
Thus lovely seemed the infant’s dawn;
Thus swiftly fled his life away!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ere sin could blight or sorrow fade,
Death timely came with friendly care;
The opening bud to heaven conveyed,
And bade it bloom for ever there.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He died to sin, and all its woes,
But for a moment felt the rod—
On love’s triumphant wing he rose,
To rest for ever with his God!

title: So fades the lovely, blooming flower

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
So fades the lovely, blooming flower,
Frail, smiling solace of an hour;
So soon our transient comforts fly,
And pleasure only blooms to die.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Is there no kind, no healing art,
To soothe the anguish of the heart?
Spirit of grace, be ever nigh;
Thy comforts are not made to die.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let gentle patience smile on pain,
Till dying hope revives again;
Hope wipes the tear from sorrow’s eye,
And faith points upward to the sky.

title: How blest are they whose transient years

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How blest are they whose transient years
Pass like an evening meteor’s flight;
Not dark with guilt, nor dim with tears:
Whose course is short, unclouded, bright.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, cheerless were our lengthened way:
But heaven’s own light dispels the gloom,
Streams downward from eternal day,
And casts a glory round the tomb.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O, stay thy tears; the blest above
Have hailed a spirit’s heavenly birth,
And sung a song of joy and love;
Then why should anguish reign on earth?

title: Why should we start and fear to die
author: And breathe my life out sweetly there

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why should we start and fear to die?
What timorous worms we mortals are!
Death is the gate of endless joy,
And yet we dread to enter there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The pains, the groans, and dying strife,
Fright our approaching souls away;
Still we shrink back again to life,
Fond of our prison and our clay.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O if my Lord would come and meet,
My soul would stretch her wings in haste,
Fly fearless through death’s iron gate,
Nor feel the terrors as she passed!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus can make a dying bed
Feel soft as downy pillows are,
While on his breast I lean my head,

title: The glories of our birth and state

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Princes and magistrates must fall,
And in the dust be equal made;
The high and mighty with the small,
Scepter and crown with scythe and spade.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: Almighty Maker of my frame
author: And fix my hope on thee alone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Almighty Maker of my frame,
Teach me the measure of my days;
Teach me to know how frail I am,
And spend the remnant to thy praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Vain his ambition, noise, and show,
Vain are the cares which rack his mind;
He heaps up treasures mixed with woe,
And dies, and leaves them all behind.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: O God, thy grace and blessing give

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O God, thy grace and blessing give
To us, who on thy name attend,
That we this mortal life may live
Regardful of our journey’s end.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Teach us to know that Jesus died,
And rose again, our souls to save;
Teach us to take him as our Guide,
Our Help from childhood to the grave.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then shall not death with terror come,
But welcome as a bidden guest—
The herald of a better home,
The messenger of peace and rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And, when the awful signs appear
Of judgment, and the throne above,
Our hearts still fixed, we shall not fear,
God is our trust; and God is Love.

title: Though I walk through the gloomy vale
author: Thy rod directs my doubtful way

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Though I walk through the gloomy vale,
Where death and all its terrors are,
My heart and hope shall never fail,
For God my Shepherd’s with me there.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: O mourner! who with tender love
author: And thou shalt meet thy child in heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O mourner! who with tender love,
Hast wept beside some infant grave,
Hast thou not sought a Friend above,
Who died thy little one to save?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Then lift thy weary, weeping eye
Above the waves that round thee dwell;
Is not thy darling safe on high?
Canst thou not whisper—It is well?

sections.label: Verse 3

title: No bitter tears for thee be shed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
No bitter tears for thee be shed,
Blossom of being! seen and gone!
With flowers alone we strew thy bed,
O blest departed one!
Whose all of life, a rosy ray,
Blushed into dawn, and passed away.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yes! thou art fled, ere guilt had power
To stain thy cherub-soul and form,
Closed is the soft ephemeral flower
That never felt a storm!
The sunbeam’s smile, the zephyr’s breath,
All that it knew from birth to death.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh! hadst thou still on earth remained,
Vision of beauty! fair as brief!
How soon thy brightness had been stained
With passion or with grief!
Now, not a sullying breath can rise,
To dim thy glory in the skies.

title: Unvail thy bosom, faithful tomb
author: Shall then arise to meet the Lord

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Unvail thy bosom, faithful tomb;
Take this new treasure to thy trust,
And give these sacred relics room
To slumber in the silent dust.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Nor pain, nor grief, nor anxious fear,
Invade thy bounds; no mortal woes
Can reach the peaceful sleeper here,
While angels watch the soft repose.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So Jesus slept; God’s dying Son
Passed through the grave, and blessed the bed:
Rest here, blest saint, till from his throne
The morning break, and pierce the shade.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: The hour of my departure’s come

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The race appointed I have run,
The combat’s o’er, the prize is won;
And now my witness is on high,
And now my record’s in the sky.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: How short and hasty is our life
author: And see salvation nigh

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How short and hasty is our life:
How vast our soul’s affairs!
Yet foolish mortals vainly strive
To lavish out their years.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our days run thoughtlessly along,
Without a moment’s stay;
We, like a story, or a song,
Do pass our lives away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God from on high invites us home;
But we march heedless on,
And, ever hastening to the tomb,
Stoop downward as we run.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Draw us, O God, with thy rich grace,
And lift our thoughts on high,
That we may end this mortal race,

title: Ye golden lamps of heaven, farewell
author: With infinite delight

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ye golden lamps of heaven, farewell,
With all your feeble light:
Farewell, thou ever-changing moon,
Pale empress of the night.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And thou, refulgent orb of day,
In brighter flames arrayed;
My soul, that springs beyond thy sphere,
No more demands thine aid.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye stars are but the shining dust
Of my divine abode,
The pavement of those heavenly courts
Where I shall reign with God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The Father of eternal light
Shall there his beams display,
Nor shall one moment’s darkness mix
With that unvaried day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
No more the drops of piercing grief
Shall swell into mine eyes;
Nor the meridian sun decline
Amid those brighter skies.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
There all the millions of his saints
Shall in one song unite,
And each the bliss of all shall view

title: Death can not make our souls afraid
author: Of so divine a death

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Death can not make our souls afraid,
If God be with us there;
We may walk through its darkest shade,
And never yield to fear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I could renounce my all below,
If my Redeemer bid;
And run, if I were called to go,
And die as Moses did.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Might I but climb to Pisgah’s top,
And view the promised land,
My flesh itself would long to drop,
And welcome the command.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Clasped in my heavenly Father’s arms,
I would forget my breath,
And lose my life among the charms

title: Life is a span—a fleeting hour
author: And joys that can not die

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Life is a span—a fleeting hour;
How soon the vapor flies!
Man is a tender, transient flower,
That, even in blooming, dies.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The once-loved form, now cold and dead,
Each mournful thought employs;
And nature weeps her comforts fled,
And withered all her joys.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hope looks beyond the bounds of time,
When what we now deplore
Shall rise in full, immortal prime,
And bloom to fade no more.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Dear as thou wast, and justly dear

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Dear as thou wast, and justly dear
We would not weep for thee:
One thought shall check the starting tear,
It is that thou art free.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And thus shall faith’s consoling power
The tears of love restrain;
O, who that saw thy parting hour,
Could wish thee here again!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Gently the passing spirit fled,
Sustained by grace divine;
O, may such grace on us be shed,
And make our end like thine!

title: Why do we mourn departing friends

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Why do we mourn departing friends,
Or shake at death’s alarms?
’Tis but the voice that Jesus sends
To call them to his arms.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Are we not tending upward, too,
As fast as time can move?
Nor would we wish the time more slow
To keep us from our Love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Why should we tremble to convey
Their bodies to the tomb?
’Twas there the flesh of Jesus lay,
Amid its silent gloom.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The graves of all the saints he blest,
And softened every bed;
Where should the dying members rest,
But with their dying Head?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thence he arose, ascending high,
And showed our feet the way;
Up to the Lord our souls shall fly,
At the great rising day.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Then let the last loud trumpet sound,
And bid our kindred rise:
Awake, ye nations under ground;
Ye saints, ascend the skies.

title: When blooming youth is snatched away
author: For death’s approaching hour

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When blooming youth is snatched away
By death’s resistless hand,
Our hearts the mournful tribute pay,
Which pity must demand.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
While pity prompts the rising sigh,
O may this truth, impressed
With awful power, “I too must die,”
Sink deep in every breast.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let this vain world engage no more;
Behold the opening tomb:
It bids us seize the present hour:
To-morrow death may come.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O let us fly—to Jesus fly,
Whose powerful arm can save;
Then shall our hopes ascend on high,
And triumph o’er the grave.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Not for the pious dead we weep
author: Then follow to the tomb

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Their peace is sealed, their rest is sure,
Within that better home:
Awhile we weep and linger here,

title: Let not your hearts with anxious thoughts
author: Shall see my Father’s face

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let not your hearts with anxious thoughts
Be troubled or dismayed:
But trust in God your Father’s care,
And trust my gracious aid.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I to my Father’s house return;
There numerous mansions stand,
And glory manifold abounds
Through all the happy land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I go your entrance to secure,
And your abode prepare;
Regions unknown are safe to you,
When I, your Friend, am there.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thence shall I come when ages close,
To take you home with me;
There shall we meet to part no more,
Where sorrows ne’er shall be.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: How happy is the pilgrim’s lot

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How happy is the pilgrim’s lot!
How free from every anxious thought,
From worldly hope and fear!
Confined to neither court nor cell,
His soul disdains on earth to dwell—
He only sojourns here.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This happiness in part is mine,
Already saved from low design,
From every creature-love;
Blest with the scorn of finite good,
My soul is lightened of its load,
And seeks the things above.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: She was the music of our home
author: On the immortal shore

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
She was the music of our home,
A day that knew no night,
The fragrance of our garden bower,
A thing all smiles and light.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Above the couch we bent and prayed
In the half-lighted room,
As the bright hues of infant life
Sank slowly into gloom.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The form remained; but there was now
No soul our love to share;
Farewell, with weeping hearts, we said,
Child of our love and care.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: O for an overcoming faith
author: Through Christ our living Head

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O for an overcoming faith
To cheer my dying hours,
To triumph o’er the monster death,
And all his frightful powers.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Joyful, with all the strength I have,
My quivering lips shall sing,
Where is thy boasted victory, grave?
And where the monster’s sting?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If sin be pardoned, I’m secure—
Death has no sting beside;
The law gives sin its damning power,
But Christ my ransom died.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now to the God of victory
Immortal thanks be paid,
Who makes us conquerors while we die,

title: What though the arm of conquering death
author: Who lives for evermore

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What though the arm of conquering death
Does God’s own house invade;
What though our teacher and our friend
Is numbered with the dead;—

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though earthly shepherds dwell in dust,
The agéd and the young;
The watchful eye in darkness closed,
And dumb the instructive tongue?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The eternal Shepherd still survives,
His teachings to impart:
Lord, be our Leader and our Guide,
And rule and keep our heart.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Yes, while the dear Redeemer lives,
We have a boundless store,
And shall be fed with what he gives,

title: O where shall rest be found
author: And evermore undone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O where shall rest be found—
Rest for the weary soul?
’Twere vain the ocean-depths to sound,
Or pierce to either pole.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The world can never give
The bliss for which we sigh:
’Tis not the whole of life to live,
Nor all of death to die.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Beyond this vale of tears
There is a life above,
Unmeasured by the flight of years;
And all that life is love.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There is a death whose pang
Outlasts the fleeting breath:
O what eternal horrors hang
Around the second death!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord God of truth and grace,
Teach us that death to shun,
Lest we be banished from thy face,

title: It is not death to die
author: To reign with thee on high

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
It is not death to die—
To leave this weary road,
And, ’mid the brotherhood on high,
To be at home with God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It is not death to close
The eye long dimmed by tears,
And wake, in glorious repose,
To spend eternal years.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It is not death to bear
The wrench that sets us free
From dungeon chain—to breathe the air
Of boundless liberty.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
It is not death to fling
Aside this sinful dust,
And rise, on strong, exulting wing,
To live among the just.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Our fathers! where are they
author: Our souls to thee commend

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our fathers! where are they,
With all they called their own?
Their joys and griefs, their hopes and cares,
Their wealth and honor, gone!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But joy or grief succeeds,
Beyond our mortal thought,
While still the remnant of their dust
Lies in the grave forgot.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God of our fathers, hear,
Thou everlasting Friend,
While we, as on life’s utmost verge,

title: Far from my heavenly home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Far from my heavenly home,
Far from my Father’s breast,
Fainting, I cry, Blest Saviour! come,
And speed me to my rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My spirit homeward turns,
And fain would thither flee;
My heart, O Zion! droops and yearns,
When I remember thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To thee, to thee, I press,
A dark and toilsome road;
When shall I pass the wilderness
And reach the saints’ abode.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Go to thy rest, fair child
author: Amid the cherub train

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Go to thy rest, fair child!
Go to thy dreamless bed,
While yet so gentle, undefiled,
With blessings on thy head.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Fresh roses in thy hand,
Buds on thy pillow laid,
Haste from this dark and fearful land,
Where flowers so quickly fade.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Ere sin had seared the breast,
Or sorrow woke the tear;
Rise to thy throne of changeless rest,
In yon celestial sphere!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Because thy smile was fair,
Thy lip and eye so bright,
Because thy loving cradle care
Was such a dear delight;

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Shall love, with weak embrace,
Thy upward wing detain?
No! gentle angel, seek thy place

title: Servant of God, well done
author: His soul is found in peace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Servant of God, well done!
Rest from thy loved employ;
The battle fought, the victory won,
Enter thy Master’s joy.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Tranquil amid alarms,
It found him on the field,
A veteran slumbering on his arms,
Beneath his red-cross shield.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
At midnight came the cry,
“To meet thy God, prepare!”
He woke—and caught his Captain’s eye;
Then, strong in faith and prayer,

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
His spirit, with a bound,
Left its encumbering clay;
His tent, at sunrise, on the ground,
A darkened ruin lay.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: Though I walk the downward shade
author: In his presence I shall rest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Though I walk the downward shade,
Deepening through the vail of death,
Yet I will not be afraid,
But, with my departing breath,
I will glory in my God,
In my Saviour I will trust,
Strengthened by his staff and rod,
While this body falls to dust.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon on wings, on wings of love,
My transported soul shall rise,
Like the home-returning dove,
Vanishing through boundless skies:
Then, where death shall be no more,
Sin nor suffering e’er molest,
All my days of mourning o’er,

title: Deathless spirit, now arise

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Deathless spirit, now arise!
Soar, thou native of the skies!
Pearl of price, by Jesus bought,
To his glorious likeness wrought,
Go, to shine before his throne,
Deck his mediatorial crown;
Go, his triumph to adorn;
Made for God, to God return.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lo! he beckons from on high!
Fearless to his presence fly;
Thine the merit of his blood,
Thine the righteousness of God!
Angels, joyful to attend,
Hovering round thy pillow bend,
Wait, to catch the signal given,
And escort thee quick to heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Is thy earthly house distressed,
Willing to retain its guest?
’Tis not thou, but it, must die—
Fly, celestial tenant, fly!
Burst thy shackles, drop thy clay,
Sweetly breathe thyself away,
Singing, to thy crown remove,
Swift of wing, and fired with love.

title: Fallen—on Zion’s battle-field

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Fallen—on Zion’s battle-field,
A soldier of renown,
Armed in the panoply of God,
In conflict cloven down!
His helmet on his armor bright,
His cheek unblanched with fear—
While round his head there gleamed a light,
His dying hour to cheer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Fallen—while cheering with his voice
The sacramental host,
With banners floating on the air—
Death found him at his post;
In life’s high prime the warfare closed,
But not ingloriously;
He fell beyond the outer wall,
And shouted, victory!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
[3 Fallen—a holy man of God,
An Israelite indeed,
A standard bearer of the cross,
Mighty in word and deed—
A master spirit of the age,
A bright and burning light,
Whose beams across the firmament
Scattered the clouds of night.]

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fallen—as sets the sun at eve,
To rise in splendor where
His kindred luminaries shine,
Their heaven of bliss to share;
Beyond the stormy battle-field
He reigns in triumph now,
Sweeping a harp of wondrous song,
With glory on his brow!

title: They are going—only going
author: Suffer and forbid them not

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
They are going—only going—
Jesus called them long ago;
All the wintery time they’re passing,
Softly as the falling snow.
When the violets in the spring-time
Catch the azure of the sky,
They are carried out to slumber
Sweetly where the violets lie.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
They are going—only going—
When with summer earth is dressed,
In their cold hands holding roses
Folded to each silent breast;
When the autumn hangs red banners
Out above the harvest sheaves,
They are going—ever going—
Thick and fast, like falling leaves.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
All along the mighty ages,
All adown the solemn time,
They have taken up their homeward
March to that serener clime,
Where the watching, waiting angels
Lead them from the shadow dim,
To the brightness of his presence
Who has called them unto him.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
They are going—only going—
Out of pain and into bliss—
Out of sad and sinful weakness
Into perfect holiness.
Snowy brows—no care shall shade them;
Bright eyes—tears shall never dim;
Rosy lips—no time shall fade them:
Jesus called them unto him.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Little hearts for ever stainless—
Little hands as pure as they—
Little feet by angels guided,
Never a forbidden way!
They are going—ever going—
Leaving many a lonely spot;
But ’tis Jesus who has called them—

title: Dropping down the troubled river
author: At the Father’s own right hand

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Dropping down the troubled river
To the tranquil, tranquil shore,
Where the sweet light shineth ever,
And the sun goes down no more.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Dropping down the winding river
To the wide and welcome sea,
Where no tempest wrecketh ever,
Where the sky is fair and free.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Dropping down the rapid river,
To the dear and deathless land,
Where the living live for ever

title: Sister, thou wast mild and lovely
author: Where no farewell tear is shed

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sister, thou wast mild and lovely,
Gentle as the summer breeze,
Pleasant as the air of evening,
When it floats among the trees.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Peaceful be thy silent slumber—
Peaceful in the grave so low:
Thou no more wilt join our number;
Thou no more our songs shalt know.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Yet again we hope to meet thee,
When the day of life is fled,
Then in heaven with joy to greet thee,

title: Happy soul! thy days are ended

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy soul! thy days are ended,
All thy mourning days below;
Go, by angel guards attended,
To the sight of Jesus go!
Waiting to receive thy spirit,
Lo! the Saviour stands above;
Shows the purchase of his merit,
Reaches out the crown of love.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: What is life? ’tis but a vapor

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What is life? ’tis but a vapor,
Soon it vanishes away:
Life is but a dying taper—
O, my soul, why wish to stay!
Why not spread thy wings and fly
Straight to yonder world of joy!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See that glory, how resplendent!
Brighter far than fancy paints;
There, in majesty transcendent,
Jesus reigns the King of saints,
Why not spread thy wings and fly
Straight to yonder world of joy!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Joyful crowds his throne surrounding,
Sing with rapture of his love;
Through the heavens his praise resounding,
Filling all the courts above.
Why not spread thy wings and fly
Straight to yonder world of joy!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Go, and share his people’s glory,
’Midst the ransomed crowd appear;
Thine a joyful, wondrous story,
One that angels love to hear.
Why not spread thy wings and fly
Straight to yonder world of joy!

title: Tossed no more on life’s rough billow

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Tossed no more on life’s rough billow,
All the storms of sorrow fled,
Death hath found a quiet pillow
For the agéd Christian’s head,
Peaceful slumbers
Guarding now his lowly bed.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, may we be reunited
To the spirits of the just,
Leaving all that sin has blighted
With corruption, in the dust;
Hear us, Jesus,
Thou our Lord, our Life, our Trust.

title: When the vale of death appears
author: I will join the immortal choir

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When the vale of death appears,
Faint and cold this mortal clay,
Blest Redeemer, soothe my fears,
Light me through the gloomy way;
Break the shadows,
Usher in eternal day.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: Time is winging us away
author: Secure in Jesus’ love

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Time is winging us away
To our eternal home;
Life is but a winter’s day—
A journey to the tomb!
But the Christian shall enjoy
Health and beauty soon above,
Far beyond the world’s alloy,

title: Go to the grave in all thy glorious prime
author: And open vision for the written word

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Go to the grave; for thee thy Saviour lay
In death’s embrace, ere he arose on high;
And all the ransomed, by that narrow way,
Pass to eternal life beyond the sky.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Weep not for the saint that ascends
author: Still must wait till the day-spring appears

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Weep not for the saint that ascends
To partake of the joys of the sky,
Weep not for the seraph that bends
With the worshiping chorus on high.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Weep not for the spirit now crowned
With the garland to martyrdom given,
O weep not for him; he has found
His reward and his refuge in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But weep for their sorrows, who stand
And lament o’er the dead by his grave—
Who sigh when they muse on the land
Of their home, far away o’er the wave.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And weep for the nations that dwell
Where the light of the truth never shone,
Where anthems of praise never swell,
And the love of the Lamb is unknown.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Weep not for the saint that ascends
To partake of the joys of the sky;
Weep not for the seraph that bends
With the worshiping chorus on high:

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
But weep for the mourners who stand
By the grave of their brother, in tears,
And weep for the people whose land

title: What’s this that steals upon my frame
author: All is well

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What’s this that steals upon my frame?
Is it death?
That soon will quench this vital flame?
Is it death?
If this be death, I soon shall be
From every pain and sorrow free,
I shall my Lord in glory see—
All is well!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Weep not, my friends, weep not for me,
All is well!
My sins are pardoned, I am free;
All is well.
There’s not a cloud that doth arise,
To hide my Saviour from my eyes;
I soon shall mount the upper skies—
All is well.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Tune, tune your harps, ye saints in glory,
All is well;
I will rehearse the pleasing story,
All is well.
Bright angels have from glory come,
They’re round my bed, they’re in my room,
They wait to waft my spirit home—
All is well.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hark, hark, my Lord and Master calls me,
All is well;
I soon shall see his face in glory,
All is well.
Farewell, dear friends, adieu, adieu,
I can no longer stay with you—
My glittering crown appears in view;
All is well.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Hail, hail, all hail, ye blood-washed throng,
Saved by grace;
I’ve come to join your rapturous song,
Saved by grace.
All, all is peace and joy divine,
All heaven and glory now are mine;
O, hallelujah to the Lamb!

title: O think that, while you’re weeping here

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O think that, while you’re weeping here,
His hand a golden harp is stringing;
And with a voice serene and clear,
His ransomed soul, without a tear,
His Saviour’s praise is singing!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And think that all his pains are fled,
His toils and sorrows closed for ever;
While he, whose blood for man was shed,
Has placed upon his servant’s head
A crown that fadeth never!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For thus, while round your lowly bier
Surviving friends are sadly bending,
Your souls, like his, to Jesus dear,
Shall wing their flight to yonder sphere,
Faith lightest pinions lending.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And thus, when to the silent tomb,
Your lifeless dust like his is given,
Like faith shall whisper, ’midst the gloom,
That yet again in faithful bloom,
That dust shall smile in heaven!

title: There is a calm for those who weep
author: A quiet home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a calm for those who weep,
A rest for weary pilgrims found;
They softly lie, and sweetly sleep,
Low in the ground.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The storm that racks the wintery sky
No more disturbs their deep repose,
Than summer evening’s latest sigh,
That shuts the rose.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou traveler in this vale of tears,
To realms of everlasting light,
Through time’s dark wilderness of years,
Pursue thy flight.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Whate’er thy lot—whate’er thou be—
Confess thy folly—kiss the rod;
And in thy chastening sorrows see
The hand of God.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Though long of winds and waves the sport,
Condemned in wretchedness to roam,
Thou soon shalt reach a sheltering port,

title: Lowly and solemn be

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lowly and solemn be
Thy children’s cry to thee,
Father divine;
A hymn of suppliant breath,
Owning that life and death
Alike are thine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O Father, in that hour,
When earthly help and power
Are all in vain,
When spears, and shield, and crown,
In faintness are cast down,
Do thou sustain.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By him who bowed to take
The death-cup for our sake,
The thorn, the rod—
From whom the last dismay
Was not to pass away—
Aid us, O God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Trembling beside the grave,
We call on thee to save,
Father divine:
Hear, hear our suppliant breath;
Keep us, in life and death,
Thine, only thine.

title: As flows the rapid river
author: The ruin of thy soul

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As flows the rapid river,
With channel broad and free,
Its waters rippling ever,
And hastening to the sea;
So life is onward flowing,
And days of offered peace,
And man is swiftly going
Where calls of mercy cease.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As moons are ever waning,
As hastes the sun away,
As stormy winds, complaining,
Bring on the wintery day:
So fast the night comes o’er us—
The darkness of the grave;
The death is just before us;
God takes the life he gave.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Say, hath thy heart its treasure
Laid up in worlds above?
And is it all thy pleasure
Thy God to praise and love?
Beware lest death’s dark river
Its billows o’er thee roll,
And thou lament for ever

title: Alas! how poor and little worth
author: Come stealing on

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Alas! how poor and little worth
Are all those glittering toys of earth
That lure us here!
Dreams of a sleep that death must break:
Alas! before it bids us wake,
They disappear.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Where is the strength that spurned decay,
The step that rolled so light and gay,
The heart’s blithe tone?
The strength is gone, the step is slow,
And joy grows weariness and woe
When age comes on.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
O, let the soul its slumbers break,
Arouse its senses, and awake
To see how soon
Life, like its glories, glides away,
And the stern footsteps of decay

title: Friend after friend departs

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Friend after friend departs;
Who hath not lost a friend?
There is no union here of hearts,
That finds not here an end?
Were this frail world our only rest,
Living or dying, none were blest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Beyond the flight of time,
Beyond this vale of death,
There surely is some blesséd clime,
Where life is not a breath,
Nor life’s affections transient fire,
Whose sparks fly upward to expire,

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4

title: When the spark of life is waning
author: Weep not for me

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When the spark of life is waning,
Weep not for me;
When the languid eye is streaming,
Weep not for me;
When the feeble pulse is ceasing,
Start not at its swift decreasing,
’Tis the fettered soul’s releasing,
Weep not for me.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: No, no, it is not dying

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
No, no, it is not dying
To go unto our God,
This gloomy earth forsaking,
Our journey homeward taking
Along the starry road.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No, no, it is not dying
Heaven’s citizen to be,
A crown immortal wearing,
And rest unbroken sharing,
From care and conflict free.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No, no, it is not dying
The Shepherd’s voice to know;
His sheep he ever leadeth,
His peaceful flock he feedeth,
Where living pastures grow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No, no, it is not dying
To wear a heavenly crown,
Among God’s people dwelling,
The glorious triumph swelling,
Of him whose sway we own.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Thou God of love! beneath thy sheltering wings

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou God of love! beneath thy sheltering wings
We leave our holy dead,
To rest in hope! From this world’s sufferings
Their souls have fled!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O! when our souls are burdened with the weight
Of life, and all its woes,
Let us remember them, and calmly wait
For our life’s close!

title: Go to thy rest in peace
author: We meet to part no more

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Go to thy peaceful rest;
For thee we need not weep,
Since thou art now among the blest—
No more by sin and sorrow pressed,
But hushed in quiet sleep.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Go to thy rest; and while
Thy absence we deplore,
One thought our sorrow shall beguile;
For soon, with a celestial smile,

title: Away from his home and the friends of his youth

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Away from his home and the friends of his youth,
He hasted, the herald of mercy and truth,
For the love of his Lord, and to seek for the lost:
Soon, alas! was his fall—but he died at his post.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The stranger’s eye wept, that, in life’s brightest bloom,
One gifted so highly should sink to the tomb;
For in ardor he led in the van of the host,
And he fell like a soldier—he died at his post.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He wept not himself that his warfare was done—
The battle was fought, and the victory won;
But he whispered of those whom his heart clung to most,
“Tell my brethren, for me, that I died at my post.”

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Victorious his fall—for he rose as he fell,
With Jesus, his Master, in glory to dwell:
He has passed o’er the stream, and has reached the bright coast,
For he fell like a martyr—he died at his post.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
And can we the words of his exit forget?
O! no; they are fresh in our memory yet:
An example so worthy shall never be lost,
We will fall in the work—we will die at our post.

title: Thou art gone to the grave; but we will not deplore thee

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou art gone to the grave; but we will not deplore thee,
Though sorrows and darkness encompass the tomb:
The Saviour has passed through its portals before thee,
And the lamp of his love is thy guide thro’ the gloom.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou art gone to the grave; we no longer behold thee,
Nor tread the rough paths of the world by thy side;
But the wide arms of mercy are spread to enfold thee,
And sinners may hope, since the Saviour has died.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou art gone to the grave; and its mansion forsaking,
Perchance thy weak spirit in doubt lingered long;
But the sunshine of heaven beamed bright on thy waking,
And the sound thou didst hear was the seraphim’s song.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Christian, the vision before thee is glorious

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Christian, the vision before thee is glorious,
The earth shall allure thy tried spirit no more:
Thou wast in the day of thy trial victorious,
Secure now at last, thy temptations are o’er.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hard was the strife, but the strong one in battle,
Has been thy defender, and vanquished thy foes;
And heaven stood by thee to help thee in trouble,
And joyed when the sound of thy triumph arose.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
High was the anthem those raptures revealing,
Ten thousand celestials the chorus prolong;
But louder the strains of the ransomed are pealing,
And glory is swelling the conqueror’s song.

title: Far, far o’er hill and dale, on the winds stealing
author: SECOND ADVENT

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Far, far o’er hill and dale, on the winds stealing,
List to the tolling bell, mournfully pealing,
Hark, hark, it seems to say, as melt those sounds away,
So earthly joys decay, while new their feeling!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now through the charméd air, on the winds stealing,
List to the mourner’s prayer, solemnly bending:
Hark, hark, it seems to say, turn from those joys away,
To those which ne’er decay, for life is ending.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So when our mortal ties death shall dissever,
Lord, may we reach the skies where care comes never,
And in eternal day, joining the angels’ lay,
To our Creator pay homage for ever.

title: Hope of our hearts, O Lord, appear
author: Who died to make her free

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hope of our hearts, O Lord, appear,
Thou glorious star of day!
Shine forth, and chase the dreary night,
With all our tears, away.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O bid the bright archangel now
The trump of God prepare,
To call thy saints—the quick, the dead,
To meet thee in the air.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No resting-place we seek on earth,
No loveliness we see;
Our eye is on the royal crown,
Prepared for us and thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But, dearest Lord, however bright
That crown of joy above,
What is it to the brighter hope
Of dwelling in thy love?

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
What to the joy, the deeper joy,
Unmingled, pure and free,
Of union with our living Head,
Of fellowship with thee?

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
This joy e’en now on earth is ours;
But only, Lord, above
Our heart without a pang shall know
The fullness of thy love.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
There, near thy heart, upon the throne,
Thy ransomed Bride shall see
What grace was in the bleeding Lamb,

title: The Church has waited long

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Church has waited long
Her absent Lord to see;
And still in loneliness she waits,
A friendless stranger she.
Age after age has gone,
Sun after sun has set,
And still in weeds of widowhood
She weeps a mourner yet.
Come, then, Lord Jesus, come!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
The whole creation groans,
And waits to hear that voice
That shall restore her comeliness,
And make her wastes rejoice.
Come, Lord, and wipe away
The curse, the sin, the stain,
And make this blighted world of ours
Thine own fair world again.
Come, then, Lord Jesus, come!

title: When the King of kings comes
author: When the King of kings comes

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When the King of kings comes,
When the Lord of lords comes;
We shall have a joyful day,
When the King of kings comes:
To see the nations broken down,
And kingdoms once of great renown,
And saints now suffering wear the crown,
When the King of kings comes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When the trump of God calls,
When the last of foes falls;
We shall have a joyful day,
When the King of kings comes:
To see the saints raised from the dead,
And all together gatheréd,
And made like to their glorious Head,
When the King of kings comes.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When the foe’s distress comes,
When the church’s rest comes;
We shall have a joyful day,
When the King of kings comes:
To see the New Jerusalem,
Its fullness and its matchless frame,
Surpassing all report and fame,
When the King of kings comes.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When the world’s course is run,
When the judgment is begun;
We shall have a joyful day,
When the King of kings comes:
To see the sons of God well known,
All spotless to their Father shown,
And Jesus all his brethren own,
When the King of kings comes.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When our Lord in clouds comes,
When he with great power comes;
We shall have a joyful day,
When the King of kings comes:
To see all things by him restored,
And God himself alone adored,
By all the saints with one accord,

title: Saviour, haste: our souls are waiting
author: We shall have supreme delight

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Saviour, haste: our souls are waiting
For the long expected day,
When, new heavens and earth creating,
Thou shalt banish grief away;
All the sorrow
Caused by sin and Satan’s sway.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Haste, O hasten thine appearing,
Take thy mourning people home;
’Tis this hope our spirits cheering,
While we in the desert roam,
Makes thy people
Strangers here till thou dost come.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, how long shall the creation
Groan and travail sore in pain,
Waiting for its sure salvation
When thou shalt in glory reign,
And like Eden
This sad earth shall bloom again?

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Lo! he cometh—countless trumpets

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lo! he cometh—countless trumpets
Wake to life the slumbering dead;
’Mid ten thousand saints and angels,
See their great exalted Head:
Hallelujah!—
Welcome, welcome, Son of God!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
“Come, ye blesséd of my Father!
Enter into life and joy:
Banish all your fears and sorrows;
Endless praise be your employ;”
Hallelujah!—
Welcome, welcome, to the skies.

title: Lo! he comes, with clouds descending

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lo! he comes, with clouds descending,
Once for favored sinners slain,
Thousand thousand saints attending,
Swell the triumph of his train!
Hallelujah!
Jesus now shall ever reign!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Every eye shall now behold him,
Robed in dreadful majesty;
Those who set at naught and sold him,
Pierced and nailed him to the tree,
Deeply wailing,
Shall the true Messiah see.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Every island, sea, and mountain,
Heaven and earth, shall flee away;
All who hate him, must, confounded,
Hear the trump proclaim the day,
Come to judgment!
Come to judgment! come away!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now redemption, long expected,
See in solemn pomp appear!
All his saints by man rejected,
Now shall meet him in the air,
Hallelujah!
See the day of God appear!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord, thy Bride says by thy Spirit,
Hasten thou the general doom!
Promised glory to inherit,
Take thy weary pilgrims home!
All creation
Travails, groans, and bids thee come.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Yes—Amen! Let all adore thee,
High on thy exalted throne;
Saviour, take the power and glory,
Claim the kingdoms for thy own!
O! come quickly!
Hallelujah, come, Lord, come!

title: We wait for thee, all-glorious One
author: THE RESURRECTION

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We wait for thee, all-glorious One;
We look for thine appearing;
We bear thy name, and on the throne,
We see thy presence cheering.
Faith even now
Uplifts its brow,
And sees the Lord descending,
And with him bliss unending.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We wait for thee, through days forlorn,
In patient self-denial;
We know that thou our grief hast borne
Upon thy cross of trial.
And well may we
Submit with thee
To bear the cross and love it,
Until thy hand remove it.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We wait for thee; already thou
Hast all our heart’s submission;
And though the spirit sees thee now,
We long for open vision;
When ours shall be
Sweet rest with thee,
And pure, unfading pleasure,
And life in endless measure.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We wait for thee in certain hope—
The time will soon be over;
With child-like longing we look up,
The glory to discover.
O, bliss! to share
Thy triumph there,
When home with joy and singing,
The Lord his saints is bringing!

title: The Lord will come, the earth shall quake

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord will come, the earth shall quake,
The hills their fixéd seat forsake;
And withering, from the vault of night,
The stars withdraw their feeble light.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The Lord will come, but not the same
As once in lowly form he came;
A silent Lamb to slaughter led,
The bruised, the suffering, and the dead.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Lord will come—a dreadful form,
With wreath of flame, and robe of storm,
On cherub wings, and wings of wind,
Anointed Judge of human kind.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
While sinners in despair shall call,
“Rocks, hide us! mountains, on us fall!”
The saints, ascending from the tomb,
Shall joyful sing—“The Lord is come!”

title: That day of wrath! that dreadful day

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
That day of wrath! that dreadful day,
When heaven and earth shall pass away!
What power shall be the sinner’s stay?
How shall he meet that dreadful day?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
O, on that day, that dreadful day,
When man to judgment wakes from clay,
Be thou, O God, the sinner’s stay,
Though heaven and earth shall pass away.

title: When, downward, to the darksome tomb
author: Who died from death to save

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When, downward, to the darksome tomb,
I thoughtful turn my eyes,
Frail nature trembles at the gloom,
And anxious fears arise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Why shrinks my soul? in death’s embrace
Once Jesus captive slept;
And angels hovering o’er the place,
His lowly pillow kept.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thus shall they guard my sleeping dust,
And, as the Saviour rose,
The grave again shall yield her trust,
And end my deep repose.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My Lord, before to glory gone,
Shall bid me come away;
And calm and bright shall break the dawn
Of heaven’s eternal day.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: In expectation sweet
author: Upon its perfect bliss

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In expectation sweet,
We wait, and sing, and pray,
Till Christ’s triumphal car we meet,
And see an endless day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He comes! the Conqueror comes!
Death falls beneath his sword;
The joyful prisoners burst their tombs,
And rise to meet their Lord.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The trumpet sounds—Awake!
Ye dead, to judgment come!
The pillars of creation shake,
While hell receives her doom.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Rest for the toiling hand
author: Shall rise a heavenly flower

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rest for the toiling hand,
Rest for the anxious brow,
Rest for the weary, way-worn feet,
Rest from all labor now;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soon shall the trump of God
Give out the welcome sound
That shakes thy silent chamber-walls,
And breaks the turf-sealed ground.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye dwellers in the dust,
Awake! come forth and sing;
Sharp has your frost of winter been,
But bright shall be your spring.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: The chariot! the chariot! its wheels roll in fire

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
The glory! the glory! around him are poured
Mighty hosts of the angels that wait on the Lord;
And the glorified saints, and the martyrs are there,
And there, all who the palm-wreaths of victory wear!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The trumpet! the trumpet! the dead have all heard;
Lo! the depths of the stone-covered charnel are stirred!
From the sea, from the earth, from the south, from the north,
All the vast generations of men are come forth.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The judgment! the judgment! the thrones are all set,
Where the lamb and the bright-crownéd elders are met!
There all flesh is at once in the sight of the Lord,
And the doom of eternity hangs on his word.

title: Lo! the seal of death is breaking
author: Over all the golden shore

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
There, no more at eve declining,
Suns without a cloud are shining
O’er the land of life and love;
There the founts of life are flowing,
Flowers unknown to time, are blowing
In that radiant scene above.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: The last lovely morning
author: FINAL JUDGMENT

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The last lovely morning,
All blooming and fair,
Is fast onward fleeting,
And soon will appear.
CHORUS.
While the mighty, mighty, mighty trump
Sounds, Come, come away,
O, let us be ready to hail the glad day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And when that bright morning
In splendor shall dawn,
Our tears shall be ended,
Our sorrows all gone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Bridegroom from glory
To earth shall descend,
Ten thousand bright angels
Around him attend.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The grave shall be opened,
The dead shall arise,
And with the Redeemer
Mount up to the skies.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The saints then immortal
In glory shall reign,
The Bride with the Bridegroom

title: When thou, my righteous Judge, shalt come
author: With praise of sovereign grace

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When thou, my righteous Judge, shalt come
To take thy ransomed people home,
Shall I among them stand?
Shall such a worthless worm as I,
Who sometimes am afraid to die,
Be found at thy right hand?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love to meet thy people now,
Before thy feet with them to bow,
Though vilest of them all;
But—can I bear the piercing thought—
What if my name should be left out
When thou for them shalt call?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Lord, prevent it by thy grace:
Be thou my only hiding-place,
In this, the accepted day;
Thy pardoning voice, O, let me hear,
To still my unbelieving fear,
Nor let me fall, I pray.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when the final trump shall sound,
Among thy saints let me be found,
To bow before thy face;
Then in triumphant strains I’ll sing,
While heaven’s resounding mansions ring

title: Behold the day is come
author: And he their God and King

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Angels, in bright attire,
Conduct him through the skies;
Darkness and tempest, smoke and fire,
Attend him as he flies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How awful is the sight!
How loud the thunders roar!
The sun forbears to give his light,
And stars are seen no more.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Hark, ye mortals, hear the trumpet
author: Now your solemn close appears

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark, ye mortals, hear the trumpet
Sounding loud, the mighty roar!
Hark! the archangel’s voice proclaiming,
Thou, old Time, shalt be no more.
Rolling ages,

title: Day of judgment, day of wonders

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Day of judgment, day of wonders!
Hark! the trumpet’s awful sound,
Louder than a thousand thunders,
Shakes the vast creation round;
How the summons
Will the sinner’s heart confound!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See the Judge our nature wearing,
Clothed in majesty divine!
You who long for his appearing,
Then shall say, “This Lord is mine!”
Gracious Saviour,
Own me in that day for thine!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
At his call the dead awaken,
Rise to life from earth and sea:
All the powers of nature, shaken
By his looks, prepare to flee:
Careless sinner,
What will then become of thee?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Horrors past imagination
Will surprise your trembling heart,
When you hear your condemnation,
“Hence, accurséd wretch, depart!
Hence, with Satan
And his angels have your part.”

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But to those who have confesséd,
Loved and served the Lord below,
He will say, “Come near, you blesséd,
See the kingdom I bestow:
You for ever
Shall my love and glory know.”

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Under sorrows and reproaches,
May this thought our courage raise!
Swiftly God’s great day approaches,
Sighs shall then be changed to praise:
May we triumph,
When the world is in a blaze!

title: Ah, guilty sinner, ruined by transgression
author: HEAVEN

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ah, guilty sinner, ruined by transgression,
What shall thy doom be, when, arrayed in terror,
God shall command thee, covered with pollution,
Up to the judgement?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Stop, thoughtless sinner, stop awhile and ponder,
Ere death arrest thee, and the Judge, in vengeance
Hurl from his presence thy affrighted spirit,
Swift to perdition.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oft has he called thee, but thou wouldst not hear him,
Mercies and judgments have alike been slighted;
Yet he is gracious, and with arms unfolded,
Waits to embrace thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, then, poor sinner, come away this moment,
Just as you are, come, filthy and polluted,
Come to the fountain open for the guilty;
Jesus invites you.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But, if you trifle with his gracious message,
Cleave to the world and love its guilty pleasures,
Mercy, grown weary, shall, in righteous judgment,
Leave you for ever.

sections.label: Verse 6

title: There is a land mine eye hath seen
author: Within the paradise of God

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a land mine eye hath seen,
In visions of enraptured thought,
So bright that all which spreads between
Is with its radiant glory fraught;

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A land upon whose blissful shore
There rests no shadow, falls no stain;
There those who meet shall part no more,
And those long parted, meet again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Its skies are not like earthly skies,
With varying hues of shade and light;
It hath no need of suns to rise
To dissipate the gloom of night.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: On Zion’s glorious summit stood

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
On Zion’s glorious summit stood
A numerous host redeemed by blood;
They hymned their King in strains divine:
I heard the song, and strove to join.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here all who suffered sword or flame
For truth, or Jesus’ lovely name,
Shout victory now, and hail the Lamb,
And bow before the great I AM.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While everlasting ages roll,
Eternal love shall feast their soul,
And scenes of bliss for ever new
Rise in succession to their view.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O sweet employ, to sing and trace
The amazing hights and depths of grace;
And spend from sin and sorrow free,
A blissful, vast eternity!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O what a sweet, exalted song,
When every tribe and every tongue,
Redeemed by blood, with Christ appear,
And join in one full chorus there!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
My soul anticipates the day—
Would stretch her wings and soar away,
To aid the song, the palm to bear,
And praise my great Redeemer there.

title: Lo! round the throne, a glorious band

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lo! round the throne, a glorious band,
The saints in countless myriads stand;
Of every tongue redeemed to God,
Arrayed in garments washed in blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
O, may we tread the sacred road
That holy saints and martyrs trod;
Wage to the end the glorious strife,
And win, like them, a crown of life.

title: Return, my soul, and sweetly rest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Return, my soul, and sweetly rest,
On thy almighty Father’s breast;
The bounties of his grace adore,
And count his wondrous mercies o’er.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy mercy, Lord, preserved my breath,
And snatched my fainting soul from death;
Removed my sorrows, dried my tears,
And saved me from surrounding snares.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
What shall I render to thee, Lord?
Or how his wondrous grace record?
To him my grateful voice I’ll raise,
With just thanksgiving to his praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O Zion! in thy sacred courts,
Where glory dwells, and joy resorts,
To notes divine I’ll tune the song,
And praise shall flow from every tongue.

title: Thy Father’s house! thine own bright home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thy Father’s house! thine own bright home,
And thou hast there a place for me!
Though yet an exile here I roam,
That distant home by faith I see.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I see its domes resplendent glow,
Where beams of God’s own glory fall;
And trees of life immortal grow,
Whose fruits o’erhang the sapphire wall.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I know that thou, who on the tree
Didst deign our mortal guilt to bear,
Wilt bring thine own to dwell with thee,
And waitest to receive me there!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy love will there array my soul
In thine own robe of spotless hue;
And I shall gaze while ages roll,
On thee, with raptures ever new!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O, welcome day! when thou my feet
Shalt bring the shining threshold o’er;
A Father’s warm embrace to meet,
And dwell at home for evermore!

title: My heavenly home is bright and fair
author: We’ll be gathered home

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My heavenly home is bright and fair,
We’ll be gathered home;
Nor death nor sighing visit there,
We’ll be gathered home:
CHORUS.
We’ll wait till Jesus comes,
We’ll wait till Jesus comes,
We’ll wait till Jesus comes,
And we’ll be gathered home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Its glittering towers the sun outshine,
We’ll be gathered home;
That heavenly mansion shall be mine,
We’ll be gathered home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My Father’s house is built on high,
We’ll be gathered home;
Above the arched and starry sky,
We’ll be gathered home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When from this earthly prison free,
We’ll be gathered home;
That heavenly mansion mine shall be,
We’ll be gathered home.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
While here, a stranger far from home,
We’ll be gathered home;
Affliction’s waves may round me foam,
We’ll be gathered home.

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
Let others seek a home below,
We’ll be gathered home,
Which flames devour or waves o’erthrow,
We’ll be gathered home.

sections.label: Verse 7
sections.text:
Be mine the happier lot to own,
We’ll be gathered home;
A heavenly mansion near the throne,
We’ll be gathered home.

sections.label: Verse 8
sections.text:
Then, fail this earth, let stars decline,
We’ll be gathered home;
And sun and moon refuse to shine,
We’ll be gathered home.

sections.label: Verse 9

title: There is a region lovelier far
author: There not a tear of sorrow flows

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a region lovelier far
Than sages tell or poets sing—
Brighter than summer’s beauties are,
And softer than the tints of spring.
CHORUS.
I’m going home, I’m going home,
I’m going home to die no more,
To die no more, to die no more,
I’m going home to die no more.

sections.label: Verse 2

title: There is an hour of hallowed peace
author: Shall reap again in joy

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is an hour of hallowed peace
For those with care oppressed,
When sighs and sorrowing tears shall cease,
And all be hushed to rest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
’Tis then the soul is freed from fears
And doubts which here annoy;
Then they that oft had sown in tears,
Shall reap again in joy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is a home of sweet repose,
Where storms assail no more;
The stream of endless pleasure flows,
On that celestial shore.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: There’s music in the upper heaven
author: In glorious might around

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There’s music in the upper heaven—
The choral notes that swell,
Are sweeter, fuller, richer far,
Than human lips can tell;
When rings the gush of golden harps,
And heavenly lutes are swept,
To tell the quenchless love of him
Who o’er a lost world wept.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The gliding rush of countless wings,
Borne on the swelling breeze,
That wafts the rustling music by,
Amid embowered trees;
The echo of the myriad feet,
That fall on pavements fair,
Of glittering dazzling gold that gleams
In untold brightness there.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The music of the pearly gates,
When back by angels flung,
Admitting there a ransomed soul,
Their sinless bands among;
The silvery sound that’s swelling up,
When flows the stream of life;
The rustle of the emerald leaf,
With healing virtues rife:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And then the tide of melody
That swells and bursts, when rings
The new song in that far-off world,
That thrilling rapture brings:
But, awed, we may not note its power,
Its depths we may not sound;
Unfathomed, fathomless it rolls

title: O could our thoughts and wishes fly
author: Immortal to the skies

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O could our thoughts and wishes fly
Above these gloomy shades,
To those bright worlds beyond the sky,
Which sorrow ne’er invades!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There joys, unseen by mortal eyes,
Or reason’s feeble ray,
In ever-blooming prospect rise,
Unconscious of decay.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, send a beam of light divine,
To guide our upward aim!
With one reviving touch of thine,
Our languid hearts inflame.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then shall, on faith’s sublimest wing,
Our ardent wishes rise
To those bright scenes where pleasures spring,

title: There is a land, a happy land
author: And every burden light

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a land, a happy land
Where tears are wiped away
From every eye, by God’s own hand,
And night is turned to day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There is a home, a happy home,
Where way-worn travelers rest,
Where toil and languor never come,
And every mourner’s blest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is a port, a peaceful port,
A safe and quiet shore,
Where weary mariners resort
And fear the storms no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There is a crown, a dazzling crown,
Bedecked with jewels fair;
And priests and kings of high renown,
That crown of glory wear.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: There is an hour of peaceful rest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is an hour of peaceful rest,
To mourning wanderers given;
There is a tear for souls distressed,
A balm for every wounded breast—
’Tis found above—in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There is a home for weary souls,
By sins and sorrows driven;
When tossed on life’s tempestuous shoals,
Where storms arise and ocean rolls,
And all is drear—but heaven.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There faith lifts up the tearless eye,
The heart with anguish riven;
It views the tempest passing by,
Sees evening shadows quickly fly,
And all serene—in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: Hark! hark! the voice of ceaseless praise
author: And swell the immortal song

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark! hark! the voice of ceaseless praise,
Around Jehovah’s throne;
Songs of celestial joy they raise,
To mortal lips unknown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Upon the sea of glass they stand
In shining robes of light;
The harps of God are in their hand,
They rest not day or night.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O! for an angel’s perfect love,
A seraph’s soaring wing,
To sing with thousand saints above,
The triumphs of our King.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
On earth our feeble voice we try,
In weakness and in shame,
We bless, we laud, we magnify,
We conquer in his name.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But, O! with pure and sinless heart,
His mercies to adore,
My God, to know thee as thou art,
Nor grieve thy Spirit more!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
O! blessed hope! a “little while,”
And we, amidst that throng,
Shall live in our Redeemer’s smile,

title: There is a fold where none can stray

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There is a fold where none can stray,
And pastures ever green,
Where sultry sun, or stormy day,
Or night, is never seen.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Far up the everlasting hills,
In God’s own light it lies;
His smile its vast dominion fills
With joy that never dies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One narrow vale, one darksome wave,
Divides that land from this;
I have a Shepherd pledged to save,
And bear me home to bliss.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Soon at his feet my soul shall lie,
In life’s last struggling breath;
But I shall only seem to die,
I shall not taste of death.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Far from this guilty world to be
Exempt from toil and strife;
To spend eternity with thee—
My Saviour, this is life!

title: And is there, Lord, a rest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And is there, Lord, a rest
For weary souls designed,
Where not a care shall stir the breast,
Or sorrow entrance find?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Is there a blissful home,
Where kindred minds shall meet,
And live, and love, nor ever roam
From that serene retreat?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Are their bright, happy fields,
Where nought that blooms shall die;
Where each new scene fresh pleasure yields,
And healthful breezes sigh?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Are there celestial streams,
Where living waters glide,
With murmurs sweet as angel dreams,
And flowery banks beside?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
For ever blesséd they
Whose joyful feet shall stand,
While endless ages waste away,
Amid that glorious land!

sections.label: Verse 6
sections.text:
My soul would thither tend
While toilsome years are given;
Then let me, gracious Lord, ascend
To sweet repose in heaven!

title: I love to think of heaven
author: To be for ever there

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I love to think of heaven,
Where white-robed angels are,
Where many a friend is gathered safe,
From fear, and toil, and care.
CHORUS.
There will be no more parting there,
There will be no more parting there,
In heaven above, where all is love,
There will be no more parting there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I love to think of heaven,
Where my Redeemer reigns,
Where rapturous songs of triumph rise,
In endless, joyous strains.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I love to think of heaven,
The saints’ eternal home,
Where palms, and robes, and crowns ne’er fade,
And all our joys are one.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I love to think of heaven,
The greetings there we’ll meet,
The harps—the songs for ever ours—
The walks—the golden streets.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Come, sing to me of heaven

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, sing to me of heaven,
When I’m about to die;
